upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following heart sounds are best heard with the bell of stethoscope? 1 Opening snap II. Systolic click III. Third heart sound IV. Mid diastolic murmur
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Low-pitched sounds such as the third heart sound (S3) and the mid-diastolic rumble of mitral stenosis are best auscultated with the bell of the stethoscope lightly applied to the apex.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements for diagnosing ventricular aneurysm in a patient with recent myocardial infarction :
1. Paradoxical impulse on chest wall II. Persistent ST elevation on ECG III. Unusual bulge from cardiac silhouette on X-ray IV. Presence of pulsus paradoxsus
Which of the above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Left ventricular aneurysm post-MI presents with a paradoxical apical impulse (I), persistent ST-segment elevation on ECG (II), and an abnormal bulge on the cardiac silhouette on chest X-ray (III); pulsus paradoxus is not a feature.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is correct for subcutancous nodules in Rheumatic fever?
options: They are present over flexor aspect of forearm
The usual size of these nodules is 3-5 cm
They typically appear more than 3 weeks after onset of other clinical manifestations
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (d) — They typically appear more than 3 weeks after onset of other clinical manifestations.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is correct with regard to Carey Coombs murmur ?
options: Soft systolic murmur due to mitral regurgitation
Soft mid-diastolic murmur due to mitral valvulitis
Harsh early diastolic murmur due to sortic regurgitation
Blowing late systolic murmur due to aortic stenosis
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Carey Coombs murmur is a soft, short, mid-diastolic murmur heard at the apex in acute rheumatic fever due to mitral valvulitis.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Opening Snap (OS) in a patient of mitral stenosis?
options: OS is best heard with the bell of stethoscope
Intensity of OS becomes louder when the valve is calcified
OS moves closer to the second sound (S2) as the stenosis becomes more severe
OS is best heard at the second left intercostal space
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (c) — OS moves closer to the second sound (S2) as the stenosis becomes more severe.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following responses to intravenous adenosine is correctly matched ? Arrhythmia Response
options: Ventricular - Termination tachycardia and complete recovery
Atrial flutter - Termination and complete recovery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Intravenous adenosine transiently blocks AV nodal conduction and terminates AV nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT) and AVRT, whereas it only transiently slows ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation/flutter and has no effect on most VT.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Consider the following steps for using a metered dose inhaler (MDI) : I. Incline the head backward to minimize oropharyngeal depos tion II. Remove the cap and shake the inhaler III. Breathe out gently and place the mouthpiece into the mouth IV. Hold the breath for 10 seconds V. Simultaneously, begin a slow deep inspiration, depress the canister and continue to inhale Which one of the following is the correct sequence of using MDI?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Correct MDI technique: remove cap and shake (II) → breathe out gently and seal lips around mouthpiece (III) → tilt head slightly back (I) → begin slow deep inspiration while actuating canister (V) → hold breath for 10 seconds (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Under the Stepwise Approach to the management of Bronchial Asthma, which one of the following is the correct initial treatment at Step 1 for a patient diagnosed with Asthma?
options: Low dose inhaled corticosteroid plus aral corticosteroid
Low dose inhaled corticosteroid plus long acting anti-muscarinic agents
Low dose inhaled corticosteroid plus leukotriene antagonist
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: GINA stepwise asthma management recommends a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) as the core controller foundation starting at Step 1.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 62-year old male chronic smoker has been diagnosed with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). On pulmonary function testing, the ratio of Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1) to Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) was 0-6 and FEVI was 70% of predicted. What is the severity of airflow obstruction in this patient as per GOLD criteria?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: With FEV1/FVC < 0.70 confirming COPD, an FEV1 between 50% and 79% of predicted (70%) corresponds to GOLD Stage II (Moderate) airflow limitation.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following correctly denotes the inheritance pattern of cystic fibrosis ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cystic fibrosis is inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the CFTR gene on chromosome 7.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following conditions are contraindications for noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation in patients with respiratory failure? I. Craniofacial abnormalities II. Significant burns III. Respiratory failure with PaCO, of 60 mm Hg IV. Cardiovascular instability
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Contraindications to NIV include craniofacial trauma/abnormalities preventing mask seal (I), significant facial burns (II), and haemodynamic/cardiovascular instability (IV); hypercapnic respiratory failure (PaCO2 60 mmHg) is a primary indication.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following terms denotes the extensive sclerosis of the skin of the chest wall which restricts chest wall movement and is seen as a rare complication of systemic sclerosis ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Extensive cutaneous sclerosis of the chest wall restricting thoracic expansion in systemic sclerosis is termed 'hidebound chest'.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Consider the following pleural fluid analysis : pH-7-6 Pleural fluid protein-0-5 g/dL Serum total protein 6-5 g/dL Pleural fluid LDH 100 U/L Serum LDH-300 U/L
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pleural fluid protein 0.5 g/dL vs serum 6.5 g/dL (ratio < 0.5) and LDH 100 U/L vs serum 300 U/L (ratio < 0.6) indicate a transudative effusion, which can occur in myxoedema (unlike exudative pancreatitis, sarcoidosis, or RA).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: 'Masson Bodies" formed due to proliferation of immature collagen are a characteristic histopathological finding seen in which of the following conditions ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Masson bodies (intra-alveolar fibroblastic plugs of immature collagen) are the characteristic histopathological hallmark of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding respiratory function in old age : I. There is increasing ventilatio perfusion mismatch II. There is increased ventilatory response to hypoxia and hype capnia III. There is a decline in maximum S oxygen uptake leading to redu tion in cardiorespiratory reserve IV. There is decline in the Forced Expiratory Volume to Forced Vital Capacity ratio (FEV1/FVC) by around 0-2% per year after the forties
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ageing lungs show increased V/Q mismatch (I), reduced VO2max and cardiorespiratory reserve (III), and a gradual decline in FEV1/FVC (~0.2%/year after age 40; IV), whereas ventilatory responses to hypoxia/hypercapnia decrease rather than increase.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is correct in respect of pulmonary involvement in rheumatoid disease ?
options: Rheumatoid pulmonary nodules are usually asymptomatic and detected incidentally on imaging
Rheumatoid pulmonary nodules are often solitary and located near
Pleural effusion in these patients is transudative and usually bilateral
Combination of pleural effusion and pneumoconiosis in these patients is known as Caplan syndrome
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (a) — Rheumatoid pulmonary nodules are usually asymptomatic and detected incidentally on imaging.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following conditions is a complication of bacterial phary gitis involving extension of infection into the internal jugular veins leading to thrombosis and metastatic dispersal of the organism?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lemierre syndrome (postanginal sepsis) is septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein (usually due to Fusobacterium necrophorum) following acute pharyngitis, causing septic pulmonary emboli.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 42-year old man with history of alcohol dependency presents with progressive abdominal distension. Abdominal examination reveals a shifting dullness. Which one of the following is the most appropriate drug to relieve this abdominal distension ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Spironolactone (an aldosterone antagonist) is the first-line diuretic of choice for cirrhotic ascites because secondary hyperaldosteronism drives sodium and water retention.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the investigation of choice for diagnosing the presence of stones in the gal bladder ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Transabdominal ultrasonography is the initial investigation of choice for diagnosing cholelithiasis (gallstones), with >95% sensitivity.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following biologic agents used in the treatment of inflammatory Bowel Disease acts by inhibiting the enzyme 'Janus Kinase"?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tofacitinib is an oral small-molecule Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor used in ulcerative colitis, whereas infliximab, adalimumab (anti-TNF), and vedolizumab (anti-integrin) are monoclonal antibodies.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Melanosis coli, which occurs due to long term consumption of stimulant laxatives, presents as brown di colouration of colonic mucosa due to deposition of which one of the following pigments ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Melanosis coli results from accumulation of lipofuscin pigment in macrophages of the colonic lamina propria after chronic anthraquinone stimulant laxative use.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following with regard to Gilbert Syndrome: I. Autosomal recessive trait of a mutation in gene for UD glucuronyl transferase enzyme II. Elevation of unconjugated bil rubin III. No stigmata of chronic liver disease other than jaundice IV. Early Liver biopsy recommended in patients with possible Gilbert Syndrome
Which of the above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Gilbert syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder of UGT1A1 (I) causing mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia (II) without stigmata of chronic liver disease (III); liver biopsy is not indicated.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: The single most important treatment and prognostic factor in alcohol-related liver disease is
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Strict alcohol abstinence is the single most important therapeutic and prognostic intervention in alcohol-related liver disease.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 40 year old man with a known case of chronic pancreatitis presents to the OPD with complaint of skin pigmentation over the abdomen. The patient gives a history of chronic use of a hot water bottle to relieve the abdominal discomfort. Which one of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Erythema ab igne is a reticulated, hyperpigmented, telangiectatic skin eruption caused by chronic localized heat exposure (such as repeated hot water bottle use for chronic pancreatitis pain).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is correct regarding arginine vasopressin antag nist Tolvaptan ?
options: It is useful in hypovolemic hyp natremia
It should be used for at least 1 year
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tolvaptan is an oral selective vasopressin V2-receptor antagonist used for euvolaemic or hypervolaemic hyponatraemia (contraindicated in hypovolaemic hyponatraemia and generally limited to short-term use).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following conditions is caused by matations in the gene that encodes the sodium-potassiu 2-chloride cotransporter (NKCC2), and presents with sodium wasting, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia and hypercalciuria ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Bartter syndrome is caused by loss-of-function mutations in thick ascending limb transporters (such as NKCC2), producing renal salt wasting, hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis, and hypercalciuria.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 52 year old male has uncontrolled diabetes. Which one of the following tests will help in early detection of nephropathy ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Urine albumin (albumin-to-creatinine ratio / microalbuminuria) is the earliest screening marker for diabetic nephropathy, preceding rises in serum creatinine or urea.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Autosomal dominant mutations in which one of the following genes may cause focal segmental glomeruloscler sis associated with abnormal genitalia, Wilm's tumour and mental retard tion ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Autosomal dominant WT1 mutations cause Denys-Drash and Frasier syndromes, characterized by FSGS/diffuse mesangial sclerosis, ambiguous/abnormal genitalia, and Wilms' tumour.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Kidney damage and Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) value between 15-29 mL/min/1-73 m are found in which stage of Chronic Kidney Discase ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: KDIGO CKD Stage 4 (severely decreased kidney function) corresponds to an eGFR of 15–29 mL/min/1.73 m².

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following hereditary tubulo-interstitial kidney diseases has an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance ?
options: Medullary cystic kidney disease type I
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Nephronophthisis is an autosomal recessive tubulo-interstitial cystic kidney disease, whereas medullary cystic kidney disease types 1 and 2 and juvenile hyperuricaemic nephropathy are autosomal dominant.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following findings in a patient are suggestive of acute nephritis ? L Hematuria II. Oliguria III. Reduced size of both kidneys IV. Edema
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute nephritic syndrome classically presents with haematuria (I), oliguria (II), and periorbital/peripheral oedema (IV) with normal-to-enlarged kidneys.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
A 35 year old male presents with increased urine output. On evaluation, his urinary output was around 4L/day; urinary osmolality was 200 mosmol/L. Which of the following are various differential diagnosis ? I. Psychogenic polydipsia II. Solute diuresis III. Central diabetes insipidus IV. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Polyuria (4 L/day) with hypotonic urine (osmolality 200 mOsm/L) is caused by water diuresis—namely psychogenic polydipsia (I), central DI (III), and nephrogenic DI (IV)—not hyperosmolar solute diuresis.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Contralateral Homonymous upper quadrantanopia is the type of visual loss seen when the lesion is located at which one of the following anatomical locations ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Temporal lobe lesions damage Meyer's loop (inferior optic radiation fibres), producing a contralateral homonymous superior (upper) quadrantanopia ('pie in the sky').

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are clinical features of migraine?
I. It is associated with dilatation of extracranial vessels
II. Common migraine is seen without Aura
III. Aura is most often visual
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Migraine involves cranial vasodilatation/trigeminovascular activation (I), occurs without aura in ~75–80% as common migraine (II), and has visual aura as the most frequent aura type (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 50 year old man presents with brief episodes of lancinating unilateral facial pain, involving the buccal distribution. Pain is triggered by washing face with cold water. What is the most likely aiagnosis ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Brief, recurrent, electric-shock-like unilateral facial pain in a trigeminal distribution triggered by cold water or touch is classic for trigeminal neuralgia.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following are trigger factors for seizures ? I. Sleep deprivation II. Missed doses of antiepileptic drugs III. Recreational drug misuse IV. Physical exhaustion Select the correct aaswer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sleep deprivation, missed anti-epileptic drug doses, recreational drug/alcohol misuse, and severe physical exhaustion are all well-recognized seizure triggers (all four).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following childhood epileptic disorders often needs long term treatment with anti epileptic drugs ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) has a very high relapse rate (>80–90%) upon drug withdrawal and typically requires lifelong/long-term anti-epileptic therapy (valproate/levetiracetam).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are clinical features of Parkinson's disease?
1. Reduced eye blinking II. Drooling of saliva III. Soft voice IV. Macrographia
Select the correct answer using the code given below
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Parkinson's disease features hypomimia with reduced blinking (I), sialorrhoea/drooling (II), and hypophonic soft voice (III), along with micrographia (small handwriting, not macrographia).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 35 year female presents with easy fatigability. Investigations show that Hb is 6 g%; Red cell morphology is normocytic normochromic; and reticulocyte production index is 5-5. Which one of the following conditions favours this abnormality?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Severe normocytic normochromic anaemia (Hb 6 g%) with a markedly elevated reticulocyte production index (5.5) reflects appropriate bone marrow compensation to acute blood loss or haemolysis (intravascular haemolysis).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 46 year old lady on vegan diet for a decade presents with chief complaiats of tingling and numbness in lower limbs for two months and a history of swaying while walking through narrow corridors. Which one of the following blood tests is advisable for diagnosis in this patient?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A 10-year vegan diet with lower-limb paraesthesias and sensory ataxia (subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord) indicates vitamin B12 deficiency; serum vitamin B12 testing is diagnostic.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following causes low-volume erythrocytosis?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Gaisböck's syndrome (stress/spurious polycythaemia) causes relative erythrocytosis due to contracted plasma volume with a normal red cell mass.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: First line therapy in chronic phase of chronic myeloid leukemia is
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Imatinib mesylate (a BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor) is the standard first-line therapy for chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukaemia.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
With regard to management of idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, consider the following statements:
1. All patients with ITP with platelet count less than 100×10/L should receive high dose of glucocort coids II. For patient with spontaneous bleeding, 40 mg of dexameth sone daily is indicated for 4 days III. Intravenous immunoglobulin can raise the platelet count IV. Life threatening bleeding should be treated with platelet transfusion
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In ITP management, pulsed dexamethasone 40 mg/day × 4 days is used for active/spontaneous bleeding (II), IVIG rapidly raises platelets (III), and platelet transfusion is reserved for life-threatening bleeding (IV); asymptomatic patients with platelets > 30×10⁹/L generally do not need steroids.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following drugs can cause secondary weight gain? L. Insulin II. Propranolol III. Orlistat IV. Thyroxine Select the correct aaswer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Insulin (anabolic/lipogenic) and beta-blockers like propranolol cause weight gain (I and II), whereas orlistat and thyroxine cause weight loss.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Under which one of the following conditions, the HPA axis suppression is likely to result in crisis due to adrenal insufficiency following withdrawal of glucocorticoids ?
options: II glucocorticoids have been given by intravenous route for five days
II glucocorticoids have been administered orally for one week
II glucocorticoids have been prescribed repeatedly within the previous year
II the dose is less than equivalent of 5 mg prednisolone per day
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (c) — If glucocorticoids have been prescribed repeatedly within the previous year.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Wilson's disease has which of the following inheritance?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wilson's disease (hepatolenticular degeneration) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by ATP7B gene mutations on chromosome 13.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following can be used for the management of severe hype kalaemia ?
1. Intravenous calcitonin II. Intravenous sodium bicarbonate III. Oral sodium polystyrene sulphate IV. Intravenous calcium gluconate
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Severe hyperkalaemia management includes IV calcium gluconate for membrane stabilization (IV), IV sodium bicarbonate for intracellular shift in acidosis (II), and cation-exchange resins like polystyrene sulfonate for GI elimination (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following conditions can cause euvolaemic hyponatraemia ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypothyroidism causes euvolaemic hyponatraemia (via impaired free water excretion/SIADH-like physiology), whereas adrenocortical failure causes hypovolaemic and nephrotic syndrome causes hypervolaemic hyponatraemia.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one among the following vectors transmits the filaria Loa Loa?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Loa loa (African eye worm) is transmitted by day-biting Chrysops (deer/mango) flies.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is the most favourable prognostic parameter in Bell's palsy ?
options: Incomplete paralysis in the first week
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Incomplete facial nerve paralysis within the first week (partial paresis rather than complete paralysis) is the strongest clinical predictor of complete spontaneous recovery in Bell's palsy.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following groups of drugs is ineffective against gram positive bacteria ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Monobactams (aztreonam) bind PBP-3 exclusively in aerobic Gram-negative rods and have no activity against Gram-positive bacteria or anaerobes.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding leprosy?
options: Type 1 Leprosy Reaction is also called erythema nodosum lepr sum
Type 2 Leprosy Reaction is an immune complex mediated sy drome called arthus phenomenon
'Lion face" appearance is seen in tuberculoid leprosy
Nose is the last site of involv ment in lepromatous leprosy
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (b) — Type 2 Leprosy Reaction is an immune complex mediated sy drome called arthus phenomenon.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 56 year old gardener presents with an ulcerative nodule with purulent discharge on his right index finger. He had a prick with a thorn, at the same site around a month back. Which one of the following infections is most likely ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A gardener developing a chronic ulcerated nodule on a finger 1 month after a thorn prick is classic for lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 36 year old man presents with decreased apetite, mouth soreness, diarrhoca and irritability. On examin tion he has a bright red tongue with a pigmented scaly rash around the neck. Which one of the following food items in his diet has a bearing on his disease ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Diarrhoea, glossitis ('bright red tongue'), and a photosensitive pigmented collar rash (Casal's necklace) indicate pellagra (niacin deficiency), classically linked to maize/corn-staple diets.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Acrodermatitis enteropathica is an autosomal recessive metabolic disorder which affects the absorption of which one of the following micronutrients?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acrodermatitis enteropathica is an autosomal recessive disorder of the ZIP4 (SLC39A4) intestinal zinc transporter causing severe zinc deficiency.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to the treatment of vitamin A deficiency :
1. Repeated high doses of retinol can cause liver damage and terat genicity II. Acute overdose of vitamin A may lead to increased intracranial pressure and skin desquamation III. Regular vitamin A supplement tion is also recommended for pregnant women even in countries where vitamin A deficiency is not endemic IV. Excessive intake of carotene may cause harmless orange pigment tion of the skin
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic retinol toxicity causes hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity (I), acute overdose causes pseudotumour cerebri and skin desquamation (II), and excess dietary carotene causes benign carotenodermia (IV); routine vitamin A is not recommended in pregnancy in non-endemic areas.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Koehner phenomenon is seen in which one of the following conditions?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Koebner (isomorphic) phenomenon—development of characteristic lesions at sites of skin trauma—is classically seen in psoriasis (as well as lichen planus and vitiligo).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following regarding the human hair growth cycle:
I. Anagen is a phase of active hair growth
II. Telogen is a transitional phase
III. Catagen is a resting phase
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In the hair follicle cycle, anagen is the active growth phase (I correct), catagen is the brief involuting/transitional phase, and telogen is the resting phase (so II and III are swapped).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding oculocutaneous albinism :
1. The disease results from genetic abnormalities leading to destru tion of melanocytes II. Type 1 albinism is due to a defect in the tyrosinase gene III. Patients may present with poor vision, ratator nystagmus and alternating strabismus IV. Patients are at an increased risk of sunburn or developing skin cancer
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In oculocutaneous albinism, melanocytes are normal in number but melanin synthesis is defective (I is false); Type 1 is due to tyrosinase mutations (II), with nystagmus/strabismus (III) and high sunburn/skin cancer risk (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 42 year old man presented with recurrent oral ulcers since one year, episodes of redness of eye and genital ulcers. Which one of the following tests is of diagnostic value ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Recurrent oral aphthous ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis/eye redness indicate Behçet's disease, for which a positive pathergy test (pustule formation 24–48 h after needle prick) supports diagnosis.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following joints are commonly affected in osteoarthritis? I. First metatarsophalangeal joint II. Proximal interphalangeal joint III. Ankle joint IV. 5th and 6th cervical vertebrae joint
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Osteoarthritis commonly affects the 1st MTP joint (I), interphalangeal joints (II), and lower cervical spine C5–C6 (IV), while sparing the ankle joint unless secondary to trauma.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are causes of reversible dementia ? I Hypothyroidism II. Vitamin B12 deficiency III. Dementia with lewy body IV. Thiaaine deficiency
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypothyroidism (I), vitamin B12 deficiency (II), and thiamine deficiency (IV) are treatable/reversible causes of dementia, unlike Lewy body dementia which is progressive and neurodegenerative.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are clinical features of Fronto-Temporal dementia ? I. Personality change II. Language disturbance III. Memory may be preserved in early stages IV. Anti-cholinesterases are the drug of choice for treatment
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Frontotemporal dementia presents with early personality/behavioural changes (I) and progressive aphasia/language disturbance (II) with relative preservation of episodic memory early on (III); cholinesterase inhibitors are ineffective.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the myelinating cell of Central Nervous System ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oligodendrocytes produce myelin sheaths around axons in the central nervous system (whereas Schwann cells myelinate peripheral nerves).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the correct description of Mee's lines, seen in chronic arsenie poisoning ?
options: Transverse white lines on nails of fingers and toes
Transverse red lines on the skin of palms and soles
Transverse white lines on the skin of palms and soles
Transverse red lines on the nails of fingers and toes
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Mees' lines are transverse white bands across the fingernails and toenails classically seen in chronic arsenic (and thallium) poisoning.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Fomepizole is an antidote used to treat poisoning from which of the following substances ? I. Methanol II. Digoxin III. Cocaine IV. Ethylene glycol
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fomepizole inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase and is the antidote of choice for toxic alcohol poisoning with methanol (I) and ethylene glycol (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
The 4A Test is a screening tool for detection of delirium. Which of the following parameters are included in the 4AT tool ? 1 Alertness rsor II. Apnoca III. Abbreviated Mental Test (AMT4) IV. Attention
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The 4AT delirium screening tool assesses Alertness (I), AMT4 (Abbreviated Mental Test-4; III), Attention (IV), and Acute change or fluctuating course (not apnoea).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following combin tions of lab test results is indicative of heavy alcohol consumption, with more than 60% sensitivity and specificity ?
options: Gamma glutamyl transferase (GGT) > 35 U/L and alkaline phosphatase > 45 U/L
Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT) > 20 U/L and serum uric acid < 7 mg/dL
High normal MCV > 91 fL and CDT < 20 U/L
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Elevated GGT (> 35 U/L) combined with elevated carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT > 20 U/L) provides >60% sensitivity and specificity for heavy chronic alcohol consumption.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the antidote for belladonna poisoning ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Physostigmine (a tertiary-amine cholinesterase inhibitor that crosses the blood-brain barrier) is the specific antidote for central and peripheral anticholinergic toxicity in belladonna (atropine) poisoning.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following prevents gastrointestinal absorption of thallium?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oral Prussian blue (potassium ferric hexacyanoferrate) exchanges potassium for thallium ions in the gut lumen and prevents thallium absorption/enterohepatic recirculation.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 45 year old farmer came with accidental consumption of a pesticide. He complained of frequent urination and excessive salivation. Which one of the following toxidromes is most likely to be associated with this poisoning?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Organophosphate pesticide ingestion inhibits acetylcholinesterase, producing a cholinergic toxidrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diaphoresis, bronchorrhoea).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following regarding salicylate poisoning:
I. Arterial pH of 7.25, anion gap of 18 mmol/L
II. Arterial pH of 7.25, anion gap of 10 mmol/L
III. pCO2 of 20 mm Hg
IV. pCO2 of 48 mm Hg
Which disturbance is likely to be encountered?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a mixed respiratory alkalosis (hyperventilation with low PaCO2 ~20 mmHg; III) and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis (low pH 7.25, anion gap 18 mmol/L; I).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are typical for classic heat stroke? L. Older patient II. Normokalemia III. Hyponatremia IV. Marked lactic acidosis
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Classic (non-exertional) heat stroke typically affects elderly/debilitated patients during heat waves (I) and usually presents with normokalaemia (II), unlike exertional heat stroke which causes hyperkalaemia and marked lactic acidosis.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding Weil's disease? I. It is caused by a virus named leptospira II. Acute kidney injury can lead to oliguria in this discase III. Microscopic agglutination is the investigation of choice IV. Ceftriaxone given parenterally is effective treatment
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Weil's disease is caused by the spirochaete bacterium Leptospira (not a virus, so I is false), causes oliguric AKI (II), is diagnosed serologically by the microscopic agglutination test (III), and responds to IV ceftriaxone/penicillin (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are co ponents of SOFA scoring system ? L PaOy/FiO, ratio I1. Mean arterial pressure Perso III. Glasgow coma scale IV. Prothrombin Time with INR
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The SOFA (Sequential Organ Failure Assessment) score evaluates PaO2/FiO2 (I), MAP/vasopressors (II), GCS (III), platelets, bilirubin, and creatinine (not PT/INR).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
What are the components to establish the diagnosis of Brain Death ?
1. Absent brain stem reflexes II. Apnoea in presence of elevated PCO: III. Hypothermia IV. Irreversible and unresponsive coma
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Brain death diagnosis requires irreversible unresponsive coma (IV), absent brainstem reflexes (I), and a positive apnoea test with elevated PaCO2 (II), after excluding confounding hypothermia (III is an exclusion).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common cause for no traumatic sub-arachnoid haemorrhage
options: Extension from primary intr cerebral haemorrhage
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Rupture of an intracranial saccular (berry) aneurysm is the most common cause of non-traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage (~80–85%).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Peri-operative respiratory failure is an example of
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Type III (perioperative) respiratory failure results from postoperative atelectasis and decreased functional residual capacity following anaesthesia and surgery.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: The murmur of mitral regurgitation is best heard at
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The pansystolic murmur of mitral regurgitation is loudest at the cardiac apex and classically radiates to the left axilla.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 28 year female presented to eme gency with fever, agitation and delirium. She was on regular medic tion of Carbimazole 40 mg daily, but missed her doses for the last 2 days. Which of the following scoring systems would you like to do to assess severity of disease?
options: Sequential Organ Failure Asses ment Score
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fever, agitation, and delirium after missing carbimazole doses indicate thyroid storm; severity is scored using the Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Out of the following areas of brain, which area is most commonly affected on brain imaging in Wilson's disease?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Copper deposition in Wilson's disease predominantly affects the basal ganglia (putamen, globus pallidus), producing the characteristic 'face of the giant panda' or lenticular hyperintensities on brain MRI.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are secondary iron overload conditions?
I. Transfusion related iron load
II. Thalassemia
III. Hepatitis C associated liver disease
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Secondary iron overload occurs in repeated blood transfusions (I), thalassaemia major/intermedia (II), and chronic hepatitis C liver disease (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are features of Alzheimer's disease ? I. It is a disorder of cerebral cortical function II. Only short term memory is affected III. Patients deny that there is an thing wrong IV. Depression is commonly present
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a cortical dementia (I) often accompanied by anosognosia/denial of deficits (III) and comorbid depression (IV); it progressively impairs both short- and long-term memory (II is false).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Glymphatics is the lymphatic like structure of which system ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The glymphatic system is a glial-dependent perivascular waste-clearance pathway in the central nervous system.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is correct in the diagnosis of Giardiasis?
options: Stool sample at 2-3 days interval should be examined for cysts
String test is done to find out cysts of Giardia lamblia
Jejunal biopsy samples can show presence of larvae of Giardia lamblia
Cystic form of Giardia lamblia remains viable in water upto 1 week only
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Because Giardia lamblia cyst shedding is intermittent, examining three stool samples collected at 2–3 day intervals significantly improves diagnostic sensitivity.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: In clinical assessment of an elderly patient, 'the get up and go test' is used to evalaate which of the following ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The 'Get Up and Go' (or Timed Up and Go) test evaluates mobility, gait, balance, and fall risk in elderly patients.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Treatment of first choice in acute Gout
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oral colchicine (alongside NSAIDs or corticosteroids) is a first-line agent for acute gout flares, whereas allopurinol is urate-lowering therapy not started during an acute attack.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 56 year male came with acute onset breathlessness and found to have pneumothorax. The resident doctor decided to insert intercostals drain. Which one of the following sites is suitable for such a procedure?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Intercostal chest tube insertion for pneumothorax is performed in the 'triangle of safety' (bordered by the lateral edge of pectoralis major, anterior border of latissimus dorsi, and the 5th intercostal space).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is an antidote for Rivaroxaban and Apixaban, when reversal of anticoagulation is needed due to uncontrolled bleeding ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Andexanet alfa is a recombinant modified factor Xa decoy protein used to reverse life-threatening bleeding from direct factor Xa inhibitors (rivaroxaban and apixaban).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are included in common causes of mediastinal masses in superior and anterior mediastinum?
I. Goitre
II. Thymic tumour
III. Neurogenic tumour
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Superior and anterior mediastinal masses commonly include retrosternal thyroid goitre (I) and thymic tumours/thymoma (II), whereas neurogenic tumours arise in the posterior mediastinum.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is used to reverse the anticoagulant effects of Dabigatran ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Idarucizumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody fragment that specifically binds and reverses the direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is contr indication of doing a wireless capsule endoscopy ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Known or suspected small-bowel stricture/obstruction is an absolute contraindication to wireless capsule endoscopy due to the risk of capsule retention.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the causative organism of Erythrasma, a mild, localized and superficial skin infection ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Erythrasma (reddish-brown intertriginous patches showing coral-red fluorescence under Wood's lamp) is caused by Corynebacterium minutissimum.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is correctly matched regarding classification of portal hypertension according to site of vascular obstruction ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Portal vein thrombosis causes pre-hepatic presinusoidal portal hypertension (whereas cirrhosis is intrahepatic sinusoidal, veno-occlusive disease is post-sinusoidal, and schistosomiasis is intrahepatic presinusoidal).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is a secondary cause of headache?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Medication overuse headache is a secondary headache disorder, whereas migraine, tension-type headache, and trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias are primary headaches.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A 32 year old man presents with history of recurrent jaundice over the previous decade. Family gives history of the patient having episodes of facial grimacing. Which one of the following is a clinical clue to the diagnosis ?
options: Adenoma sebaceum in the mid face
Olser's nodes at the finger tips
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Recurrent jaundice and extrapyramidal facial grimacing/dystonia in a young adult point to Wilson's disease, where slit-lamp examination reveals corneal Kayser-Fleischer rings.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are causes of secondary immunodeficiency in children ? I. Diphenylhydantoin II. Severe malnutrition III. Post-varicella state IV. Nephrotic syndrome
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Secondary immunodeficiency in children can result from phenytoin/diphenylhydantoin (I), severe malnutrition (II), and nephrotic syndrome via urinary IgG loss (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding vaccination routes for children ? I. Hepatitis B vaccine given in de toid region has reduced efficacy II. Two vaccines may be given in the same thigh, but separated by 1 inch III. Separate sites are used when administering a vaccine and an immunoglobulin IV. Two intramuscular vaccines may be given on the same day but in separate limbs
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Multiple vaccines can be given in the same thigh if separated by at least 1 inch (II), and active vaccine and passive immunoglobulin must always be injected at separate anatomical sites (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A radiopaque density may be noticed in poisoning by which of the following agents ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chloral hydrate (along with heavy metals, iron, and sustained-release/enteric-coated tablets—CHIPES mnemonic) is radiopaque on abdominal X-ray.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following syndromes are caused due to genomie imprinting?
1. Rubinstein Taybi syndrome II. Prader-Willi syndrome III. Angelman syndrome IV. Edward syndrome
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Prader-Willi syndrome (paternal 15q11-13 loss; II) and Angelman syndrome (maternal 15q11-13 loss; III) are classic disorders of genomic imprinting.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
As per POCSO (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Act 2012, sexual assault is considered aggravated when I. the abuse involves use of physical violence II. the abused child is disabled III. the abuse is committed by staff of an educational institution IV. the abuse is committed by an immediate family member/first degree relative
Which of the above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (c) — POCSO Act 2012 Sec 5/9: Aggravated sexual assault includes assault on a child with mental/physical disability (II) and assault by staff/management of an educational/religious institution (III) [Forensic Medicine / POCSO Act].

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
The mother of a 14-month-old normally developing baby comes to you for feeding advice. Which of the following would be appropriate for her as per the IMNCI (Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness) Program ? I. Breastfeed as often as the child wants II. Keep the child in your lap and feed with your own hands III. Offer food from the family pot IV. Give 3 to 4 meals cach day
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: IMNCI feeding advice for a 14-month-old includes breastfeeding on demand (I), offering nutrient-dense food from the family pot (III), and giving 3–4 meals per day plus snacks (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
For a sick child aged 4 years, which of the following are signs of "severe pneumonia or very severe disease" as per IMNCI (Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness) Program ? I. Fast breathing (Greater than or equal to 40 breaths per minute) II. Child vomits everything III. Stridor in a calm child IV. Chest indrawing
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under IMNCI for a child aged 2 months–5 years, general danger signs (vomiting everything; II) and stridor in a calm child (III) classify as severe pneumonia or very severe disease.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: In a child aged 33 years with an ear problem which one of these situations merits urgent referral to hospital?
options: Pus seen draining from the ear, and discharge reported for less than 14 days
Pus seen draining from the ear, and discharge reported for more than or equal to 14 days
Pus seen draining from both ears, irrespective of duration
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A tender postauricular swelling behind the ear indicates acute mastoiditis, requiring urgent hospital referral and IV antibiotics.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Upto 10% of cases of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) may be caused by genetic conditions. Which of the following are known to be associated with ASD ? I. Tuberous sclerosis IL. Fragile X syndrome III. Prader-Willi syndrome Perso IV. Patau syndrome
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tuberous sclerosis complex (I) and Fragile X syndrome (II) are the most common single-gene/syndromic causes associated with Autism Spectrum Disorder.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are characteristic features of cerebral palsy?
I. Disorder of movement
II. Permanent nature
III. Progressive course
IV. Disorder of posture
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cerebral palsy is a permanent (II), non-progressive (III is false) disorder of movement (I) and posture (IV) caused by injury to the developing brain.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the tools used for classification of spasticity in a child with cerebral palsy? I. Gross Motor Function Classific tion System II. Medical Research Council System III. Modified Connors Scale (Connors-II) IV. Modified Ashworth Scale
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS; I) and the Modified Ashworth Scale (IV) are standard tools used to classify motor function and spasticity in cerebral palsy.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following medications may be used in a child diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder?
I. Carbamazepine
II. Methylphenidate
III. Atomoxetine
IV. Clonazepam
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Methylphenidate (stimulant; II) and atomoxetine (non-stimulant SNRI; III) are first-line pharmacotherapies for paediatric ADHD.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are included as a "Deficiencyt under the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) ? I. Hypothyroidism II. Vitamin A deficiency III. Anemia IV. Vitamin D deficiency
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under RBSK, the 'Deficiencies' category covers Vitamin A deficiency (II), Anaemia (III), Vitamin D deficiency/rickets (IV), and severe acute malnutrition/goitre (hypothyroidism is under Defects/Diseases).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding management of hyperkalemia in a child? I. Intravenous calcium (gluconate or chloride) is given to enhance cellular uptake of potassium II. Beta adrenergic agonists (salbut mol or terbutaline) are used to stabilize myocardial cell me brane III. Regular insulin and glucose given intravenously enhance cellular uptake of potassium IV. Sodium polystyrene sulfonate enhances total body potassium elimination Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In paediatric hyperkalaemia, IV regular insulin with glucose shifts potassium intracellularly (III) and sodium polystyrene sulfonate promotes GI potassium elimination (IV); IV calcium stabilizes the myocardium (not cellular uptake), and beta-agonists shift K+ intracellularly (not membrane stabilization).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct about oral rotavirus vaccines ?
1. The storage should be at 2-8°C II. The vaccine should be used within 2 hours of reconstitution or opening III. Past history of intussusception is a contraindication IV. The vaccine can be given if the baby has ongoing diarrhoea Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oral rotavirus vaccine is stored at 2–8°C (I) and is contraindicated in infants with a prior history of intussusception (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A child can make a tower of 3 blocks, runs, copies his mother while sweeping and has a vocabulary of 8-10 words. His developmental age is
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Building a tower of 3 blocks, running, imitating domestic tasks (sweeping), and speaking 8–10 words correspond to a developmental age of 18 months.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A child can ride a tricycle, copies a circle, knows name and gender. The developmental age of this child is
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Riding a tricycle, copying a circle, and knowing one's name and gender are classic 3-year (36-month) developmental milestones.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: A teen boy with birth weight of 2-8 kg is born to a primigravida mother through vaginal delivery and cried immediately after birth. Which of the following statements are correct regarding his initial care after birth? I. The baby should be initiated on breastfeeding within one hour of birth II. The baby should be kept in a separate area from the mother III. The baby should be administered with 0-5 mg of vitamin K intr muscularly IV. The baby should be thoroughly examined for congenital malfo mations from head to toe Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Essential newborn care for a vigorous 2.8 kg term infant includes initiating breastfeeding within 1 hour of birth (I) and rooming-in with the mother (IV); vitamin K dose for ≥1 kg babies is 1 mg IM (not 0.5 mg).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following oral drugs may be used in the management of super-refractory status epilepticus?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oral/enteral topiramate (via nasogastric tube) is used as an adjunctive antiseizure agent in the management of super-refractory status epilepticus.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the use of benz diazepines in the initial management of status epilepticus ? I. Upto two doses may be used 5 minutes apart, if seizures are not controlled II. For Lorazepam, only a single dose should be used, even if seizures are not controlled III. Dose of midazolam at this stage is 1-15 pg/kg/min infusion IV. Dose of both lorazepam and midazolam is 0-1 mg/kg Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In initial paediatric status epilepticus management, up to two doses of a benzodiazepine may be given 5 minutes apart (I), with IV lorazepam dosed at 0.1 mg/kg (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding hypernatremia in children ? L Diabetes insipidus due to a def ciency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) may cause hyperatremia II. Addison disease may be ass ciated with hypernatremia III. Use of boiled skimmed milk can lead to hypernatremia IV. Use of lactulose can lead to hypernatremia Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Paediatric hypernatraemia can result from diabetes insipidus (free water loss; I), feeding inappropriately concentrated boiled skimmed milk (high solute load; III), and osmotic diarrhoea from lactulose (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the management of gastrointestinal bleeding in children? I Somatostatin or octreotide inf sion should be given for at least 7 days after stoppage of initial bleeding to prevent rebleeding II. Endoscopic Sclerotherapy (EST) involves endoscopic injection of N-butyl-2-cyanoacrylate or is butyl-2-cyanoacrylate III. EST has upto 90% efficacy in controlling acute bleeding IV. Following an episode of acute variceal bleeding, all patients should receive secondary proph laxis to prevent rebleeding Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Endoscopic sclerotherapy (EST) achieves up to 90% efficacy in controlling acute variceal bleeding in children (III), and secondary prophylaxis/eradication follow-up is standard after acute bleeding (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are advantages of endotracheal intubation, in a child requiring pediatric advanced life support ? I. Inspiratory time can be controlled II. Positive end-expiratory pressure can be provided III. Peak expiratory pressure can be controlled IV. Reduced risk of aspiration of gastric contents
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Endotracheal intubation in paediatric resuscitation allows control of inspiratory time (I), delivery of PEEP (II), and airway protection against gastric aspiration (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are causes of hypocalcemia in a child? I. Hypoaagnesemia II. Hypophosphatemia III. Metabolic acidosis IV. Pseudohypoparathyroidism
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (d) — I and IV Person Your prepp repp Porsonal Exam Guide 27 A - TDSP-O-GMPK prepp TDSP-O-GMPK - A prepp Your Personal Exam Guide repp Your Personal Exam Guide A - TDSP-O-GMPK TDSP-O-GMPK - A prepp repp Your Personal Exam Guide prepp repp Your Personal Exam Guide 31 A - TDSP-O-GMPK prepp TDSP-O-GMPK - A prepp Your Personal Exam Guide.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Vibration white finger refers to :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Vibration white finger (hand-arm vibration syndrome) is a form of secondary Raynaud's phenomenon/syndrome caused by prolonged use of vibrating hand tools.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are criteria for cancer screening?
I. Screening test should be sensitive and specific
II. Screening test should be acceptable to the screened population
III. The disease should be an uncommon one for screening to be effective
IV. Disease should be recognisable at an early stage
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wilson and Jungner screening criteria require a sensitive/specific (I), acceptable test (II) for a recognizable early-stage condition (IV) that is an important/common health problem (III is false).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A 45-year-old lady presents with complaints of fatigue, muscle weakness alang with bilateral multiple renal calculi which were picked up on a routine ultrasound. Further workup revealed serum calcium levels of 11.4 mg%. What is the next best investigation required to arrive at a diagnosis?
options: NCCT head and neck ascive2 lecibeM benidmo asoS- noitenimexa
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hypercalcaemia (11.4 mg%) with bilateral renal calculi and fatigue indicates primary hyperparathyroidism; a Tc-99m sestamibi scan localizes the parathyroid adenoma.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the aetiological factors associated with a communicating hydrocephalus ? I. Post haemorrhagic II. Lesions within the ventricle III. CSF infection IV. Raised CSF protein
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Communicating hydrocephalus results from impaired CSF reabsorption at the arachnoid granulations due to subarachnoid haemorrhage (I), meningitis/CSF infection (III), or elevated CSF protein (IV); intraventricular lesions cause obstructive (non-communicating) hydrocephalus.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding a brain abscess?
I. Abscesses arise when the brain is exposed directly as a result of fracture or infection of air sinus.
II. Presenting features include low grade fever, confusion, seizures and focal deficits.
III. MRI with contrast is the initial imaging modality of choice.
IV. The aetiological agents include bacteria, fungi, protozoa and viruses.
Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Brain abscesses arise from contiguous sinus/ear infection or skull fracture (I), present with low-grade fever, seizures, confusion, and focal deficits (II), and can be caused by bacteria, fungi, protozoa, or viruses (IV); contrast CT or MRI is used, with MRI superior.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the most common type of tumour of Vermiform Appendix ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In contemporary surgical pathology (Bailey & Love), epithelial tumours (mucinous/adenocarcinoma) have surpassed neuroendocrine/carcinoid tumours as the most common appendiceal neoplasm overall.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The earliest specific cystoscopic appearance of Bilharzial cystitis is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The earliest specific cystoscopic finding in urinary schistosomiasis (bilharzial cystitis) is the presence of bilharzial pseudo-tubercles (granulomas around ova) before sandy patches develop.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following best describes craniosynostosis ?
options: It is delayed fusion of one or more cranial sutures preventing growth perpendicular to the suture.
It is the premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures, preventing growth perpendicular to the suture,
It is the premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures, facilitating growth perpendicular to the suture.
It is delayed fusion of one or more cranial sutures facilitating growth perpendicular to the suture.
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (b) — It is the premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures, preventing growth perpendicular to the suture,.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A 60 year-old female presents with pain in her back of recent onset, which has become severe of late. During the course of investigations, she was found to have lytic lesions in the vertebrae and ribs. Which of the following organs should be carefully screened now for detecting the primary cause of these lesions ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Multiple lytic bone metastases in the vertebrae and ribs of a 60-year-old woman most commonly originate from primary breast carcinoma.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Cauda equine syndrome ? Its presenting symptoms are perineal numbness, painless urinary retention and fecal incontinence. HI. Urgent investigation with MRI is required. III. It is present most commonly in the 45-60 year age group. IV. Confirmed cases require early surgical decompression. Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cauda equina syndrome presents with saddle/perineal numbness, urinary retention, and faecal incontinence (I), requires urgent MRI (II), and demands emergency surgical decompression (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The commonest site of pressure sore is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The ischial tuberosity (ischium) is the commonest site of pressure sores overall in wheelchair/seated patients (with sacrum and heel common in bedridden patients).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Resection of which part of intestine does not significantly affect fluid and electrolyte balance ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Proximal jejunal resection is generally well tolerated without severe fluid/electrolyte derangement because the ileum and colon can adapt and absorb fluids/bile salts.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Good measure of systemic perfusion by ABG is by measurement of :
options: Lactate and / or the base deficit
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Serum lactate and/or base deficit on ABG are the most reliable biochemical indicators of tissue hypoperfusion and shock severity.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are congenital abnormalities of the gall bladder?
I. The phrygian cap
II. Floating gall bladder
III. Absence of gall bladder
IV. Spigelian gall bladder
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Congenital gallbladder anomalies include the Phrygian cap (I), floating gallbladder (II), and gallbladder agenesis (III); 'Spigelian gallbladder' does not exist.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are functions of the gall bladder ? Reservoir for bile Production of bile III. Secretion of mucus IV. Concentration of bile
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The gallbladder stores (I), concentrates (IV), and secretes mucus (III) into bile, whereas bile is produced by hepatocytes in the liver (II is false).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of following statements is correct regarding Budd-Chiari Syndrome (BCS) ?
options: Venous drainage of the liver is occluded by IVC thrombus.
Abdominal discomfort and ascites are the main presenting features.
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Budd-Chiari syndrome (hepatic venous outflow obstruction) classically presents with abdominal pain/discomfort, hepatomegaly, and ascites (with caudate lobe—segment 1—hypertrophy).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is correct regarding splenic artery aneuryam?
options: It is twice as common in men.
It is usually situated in the main arterial trunk.
It is caused due to blunt trauma to the abdomen.
It is generally multiple in number.
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Splenic artery aneurysms are far more common in multiparous women, are usually saccular and located in the distal/main arterial trunk, and are typically solitary.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding primary survey/management of traumatic head injury patient?
I. Ensure adequate oxygenation and circulation
II. Exclude hypoglycaemia
III. Check for mechanism of injury
IV. Check pupil size and response
Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Primary survey in traumatic head injury includes ensuring oxygenation/circulation (I), excluding hypoglycaemia (II), and assessing pupillary size and light reactivity (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding ABCDE of trauma care?
I. A stands for Airway with cervical spine protection
II. B stands for Breathing and ventilation
III. C stands for Control of massive external haemorrhage
IV. D stands for Disability (Neurological status)
Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In ATLS ABCDE primary survey: A = Airway with C-spine protection (I), B = Breathing and ventilation (II), C = Circulation with haemorrhage control, and D = Disability/neurological status (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding Inguinal hernias in children?
I. It is more common in full-term boys.
II. It should be repaired promptly.
III. It is always indirect.
IV. It may frequently be transilluminant.
Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Paediatric inguinal hernias are more common in premature infants than full-term (I is false), require prompt repair to prevent incarceration (II), are almost always indirect (III), and may transilluminate in infants (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: 21 The most common site of urethral opening in cases of hypospadias is :
options: At the junction of penile shaft and scrotum
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Distal (subcoronal/glanular, just proximal to the glans) is the most common location of the ectopic urethral meatus in hypospadias.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following about Minimal Access Surgery are correct? L Decreased intraoperative heat loss II. Improved visualization III. Increased chances of herniation IV. Improved mobility Select the aaswer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Minimal access (laparoscopic) surgery reduces intraoperative heat loss (I), provides magnified visualization (II), and improves postoperative patient mobility (IV) while reducing incisional hernia risk.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The maximum safe dose for Lignocaine (without adrenaline) as a local anaesthetic drug is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The maximum safe dose of plain lignocaine without adrenaline is 3 mg/kg (7 mg/kg with adrenaline).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the symptoms commonly experienced by patients with lymphoedema ? L Swelling II. Burning sensation III. Intolerance to cold IV. Cramps
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Patients with chronic lymphoedema commonly experience limb swelling (I), burning/aching discomfort (II), and muscle cramps (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the malignancies associated with lymphoedema ? Kaposi Sarcoma II. Squamous cell carcinoma ers III. Malignant melanoma IV. Leukaemia
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
