upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Malignancies associated with chronic lymphoedema include lymphangiosarcoma/Kaposi sarcoma (I), squamous cell carcinoma (II), and malignant melanoma (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the techniques commonly used to close the raw area after excision of a pilonidal sinus in order to avoid a midline wound ? Limberg procedure II. Y-V plasty III. Z-plasty IV. Karydakis procedure
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Off-midline flap closures after pilonidal sinus excision include the Limberg rhomboid flap (I), Z-plasty (III), and Karydakis asymmetric closure (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A 45-year-old lady presents with history of a painlese lump in the right breast since 1 month. On examination, the lump is hard, 3×4 cm in size in the upper outer quadraat and is not fixed to the skin or the underlying structures. The axilla reveals firm mobile lymph nodes (level I). Rest of systemie examination is normal. The clinical stage of this disease is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A 3 × 4 cm breast lump (T2: 2–5 cm) with mobile ipsilateral level I axillary lymph nodes (N1) and no distant metastases (M0) corresponds to clinical stage cT2N1M0.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is considered the gold standard for the diagnosis of oesophageal motility disorders ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: High-resolution oesophageal manometry is the gold-standard diagnostic test for oesophageal motility disorders such as achalasia and diffuse oesophageal spasm.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are considered aetiological factors for Adenocarcinoma oesophagus ? Barrett's oesophagus II. Gastro-oesophageal reflux III. Obesity IV. Alcohol intake
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Risk factors for oesophageal adenocarcinoma include Barrett's oesophagus (I), chronic GERD (II), and obesity (III), whereas alcohol is primarily linked to squamous cell carcinoma.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Plummer-Vinson syndrome : L Findings include cervical oesophageal web, iron deficiency anaemia and dysphagia. II. It is a rare disease, mainly affecting middle-aged women. III. There is predisposition to postcricoid, cervical oesophageal cancer. IV. Treatment is usually surgical.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Plummer-Vinson (Paterson-Kelly) syndrome features dysphagia, iron-deficiency anaemia, and a postcricoid oesophageal web (I), predominantly affects middle-aged women (II), and predisposes to postcricoid carcinoma (III); first-line treatment is iron replacement and endoscopic dilatation.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following are correct regarding late dumping ? L It usually occurs during the second hour after meal. It lasts for 30-40 minutes. III. Major symptoms are tremer, faintness, prostration IV. It is relieved by lying down. Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Late dumping syndrome occurs 1–3 hours (second hour) postprandially due to reactive hypoglycaemia (I), lasts 30–40 minutes (II), and manifests with tremor, diaphoresis, faintness, and prostration (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct regarding Gastric outlet obstruction associated with long standing peptic ulcer disease ?
options: Hypochloraemic alkalosis is the usual metabolic abnormality in such cases.
Endoscopic biopsy is essential to exclude malignancy.
Medical therapy has no role in the treatment of this condition.
Operation is frequently required along with a drainage procedure.
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Medical therapy (nasogastric decompression, IV fluid/electrolyte correction, PPIs, and H. pylori eradication) plays an essential initial role in peptic-ulcer-related gastric outlet obstruction, making Statement (c) incorrect.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The commonly used muscle relaxant with quickest onset of action and spontaneous recovery is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Suxamethonium (succinylcholine) is a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker with the fastest onset (30–60 s) and briefest duration (~5–10 min) due to rapid plasma cholinesterase hydrolysis.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The first imaging modality of choice for a 35-year-old lady, presenting to surgical emergency with complaints of colicky pain in right lower quadrant of abdomen and vomiting since last 2 days is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a 35-year-old woman of reproductive age presenting with acute right lower quadrant pain and vomiting, abdominal/pelvic ultrasound is the preferred initial imaging modality to avoid ionizing radiation.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Mallampati test is used for the assessment of :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Mallampati classification assesses oropharyngeal visibility (uvula, faucial pillars, soft palate) to predict difficult airway/endotracheal intubation.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
I. Diabetes
II. Hypertension
III. Renal failure
IV. Jaundice
Which of the above are the risk factors for post-operative wound dehiscence?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Risk factors for postoperative wound dehiscence include diabetes mellitus (I), renal failure/uraemia (III), and jaundice (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: If faced with a surgical emergency in a child of 15 years for whom no consent is available for life-saving surgery and no time for seeking authority from someone, the next step should be :
options: Conservative management till lawyer is available
Consent arrangement through Hospital Social Worker
Go ahead with surgery without consent urd
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a life-threatening surgical emergency in a minor where no parent/guardian is reachable and delay endangers life, the surgeon must proceed immediately with life-saving surgery under the doctrine of emergency/necessity without waiting for consent.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following information needs to be disclosed in order to establish valid consent for surgical treatment?
I. Condition and reasons why it warrants surgery
II. Type of surgery proposed
III. Unexpected hazards of proposed surgery
IV. The surgical experience and expertise of the operating surgeon
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Valid informed consent requires disclosing the patient's condition and indication for surgery (I), the nature of the proposed procedure (II), and material/unexpected risks and alternatives (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A surgical department of a premier medical college conducted a study on rates of post-operative wound infection. The results of the study were negative for the proposed hypothesis. What should the department do with the results ?
options: Redo the study with a new hypothesis
Redesign the study and increase the sample size
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Good clinical research ethics require transparently reporting negative study results to prevent publication bias and wasted future research.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding sutures in surgery? Barbed sutures have the advantage of eliminating the need for knots. Vertical mattresa sutures help in eversion of wound edges. III. Aberdeen knot is used for continuous suturing. IV. Silk is preferred for subcuticular suturing. Select the answer using the code given below :
options: II, III and IV GYNAECOLOGY & OBSTETRICS
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Barbed sutures eliminate knot-tying (I), vertical mattress sutures evert wound edges (II), and the Aberdeen knot secures continuous subcuticular closures (III); silk is braided/reactive and avoided for subcuticular closure.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Chadwick's sign describes :
options: the dusky hue of the vestibule and anterior vaginal wall visible at about gth week of pregaaacy
softening of cervix at th week of pregnancy
the abdominal and vaginal fingers apposed below the body of the uterus during bimanual examination
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (a) — the dusky hue of the vestibule and anterior vaginal wall visible at about gth week of pregaaacy.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following treatments are recommended for a pregnant woman suffering from sickle cell disease? Folic acid 1 mg daily Azathioprine III. Penicillin prophylaxis IV. Thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pregnant women with sickle cell disease should receive daily folic acid (I), prophylactic penicillin (III), and LMWH thromboprophylaxis (IV) due to hypercoagulability and hyposplenism.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are contraindications to External Cephalic Version (ECV) in breech?
I. Pregnancy less than 36 weeks
II. Multiple pregnancy
III. Previous cesarean delivery
IV. Rhesus isoimmunization
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Contraindications to external cephalic version (ECV) include multiple gestation (II), previous caesarean/uterine scar (III), and Rh isoimmunization (IV); ECV is routinely scheduled at/after 36–37 weeks.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following hematological findings are seen in pregnant women with thalassemia trait ?
options: Low serum total iron binding capacity
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Beta-thalassaemia trait in pregnancy is characterized by microcytosis (low MCV) and an elevated HbA2 (> 3.5%) on haemoglobin electrophoresis.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The best drug for maintenance therapy of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) during pregnancy is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hydroxychloroquine is safe throughout pregnancy and is the cornerstone maintenance therapy for SLE during gestation, reducing flares and neonatal lupus.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following maternal complications can be seen in hyperemesis gravidarum? I. Wernicke's encephalopathy IL. Hepatic failure III. Hypoprothrombinemia IV. Convulsions
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Severe hyperemesis gravidarum can be complicated by Wernicke's encephalopathy from thiamine deficiency (I), hepatic dysfunction/failure (II), vitamin K-dependent hypoprothrombinaemia (III), and convulsions (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The commonest ovarian tumour seen during pregnancy is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Benign cystic teratoma (mature dermoid cyst) is the most common ovarian neoplasm encountered during pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding shoulder dystocia?
I. It can be predicted during early labour.
II. Anencephaly is a risk factor.
III. Turtle neck sign is present.
IV. Episiotomy should always be given.
Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In shoulder dystocia, anencephaly is a recognized risk factor (II), retraction of the delivered fetal head against the perineum is the 'turtle neck sign' (III), and an adequate episiotomy facilitates internal manoeuvres (IV); it cannot be reliably predicted early in labour.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A primigravida at 38 weeks pregnancy was put on oxytocin drip in view of slow labour at the rate of 30 mU/min by the newly appointed registrar. She complains of confusion and starts throwing fits. What electrolyte imbalance is expected to have happened in this case ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: High-dose IV oxytocin has an antidiuretic (vasopressin-like) effect that causes water intoxication and dilutional hyponatraemia, leading to confusion and seizures.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following factors favour posterior position of the vertex?
I. Anthropoid pelvis
II. Low inclination pelvis
III. Attachment of placenta on the anterior wall
IV. Primary brachycephaly
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Factors favouring occipitoposterior position include an anthropoid pelvis (I), anterior placental attachment (III), and primary fetal brachycephaly (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following factors are associated with cord prolapse during labour ? Malpresentations II. Contracted pelvis III. Stabilizing induction IV. Prematurity
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Umbilical cord prolapse is predisposed by malpresentations (I), contracted pelvis preventing engagement (II), stabilizing induction (III), and prematurity (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Detection of magnesium toxicity in a patient receiving magnesium sulphate is noticed by which of the following? Loss of tendon reflexes II. Increased respiratory rate III. Chest pain, heart block IV. Cardiac arrest
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Clinical signs of progressive magnesium sulphate toxicity include loss of deep tendon reflexes (I), chest pain/ECG heart block (III), and cardiac arrest (IV), accompanied by respiratory depression (decreased, not increased, RR).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is correct regarding postpartum psychosis?
options: There is often no family history of psychosis.
Its onset is usually within 4 days of delivery.
Recurrence rate in subsequent pregnancy is 60-70%.
Electro convulsive therapy is the first treatment of choice.
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Postpartum psychosis typically has an abrupt onset within the first 4–14 days after delivery, often with a strong family or personal history of bipolar disorder.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are correct in the treatment of cracked nipple?
I. Correct attachment (Latch on) will provide immediate relief from pain and rapid healing.
II. If pain, mother should use breast pump and the infant is fed with the expressed milk.
III. Miconazole lotion is applied over the nipple as well as in the baby's mouth if there is oral thrush.
Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cracked nipples are managed by correcting infant latch-on (I), temporary breast pumping/expressed milk if painful (II), and applying topical miconazole to nipples and oral miconazole to the infant if candidiasis is present (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are correct regarding puerperal blues?
I. Its incidence is around 50%.
II. There is no specific metabolic or endocrine derangement.
III. Treatment is reassurance and psychological support.
Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Puerperal ('baby') blues affect ~50% of postpartum women (I), have no specific metabolic/endocrine abnormality (II), and resolve spontaneously with reassurance and support (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The Matthews Duncan process has been described for :
options: marginal separation of placenta in normal labour
central separation of placenta in normal labour
controlled contraction in active management of third stage of labour
reposition of acute inversion of uterus following vaginal delivery
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Matthews Duncan mechanism describes marginal separation of the placenta from the lateral edge downward (sliding out sideways with more bleeding) during the third stage of labour.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A PILI lady after 4 hours of delivery is suffering from persistent, severe pain in the perineal region, rectal tenesmus, bearing down feeling and retention of urine. The probable diagnosis is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Persistent severe perineal pain, rectal tenesmus, bearing-down sensation, and urinary retention 4 hours postpartum are classic for a vulval/paravaginal haematoma.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: According to WHO Intrapartum Guidelines 2018, which one of the following is correct about duration of first stage labour ?
options: Duration of latent phase primigravida has not been established
Duration of active stage of multigravida should not exceed 6 hours
Duration of active stage of primigravida should not exceed 8 hours
Duration of active stage of primigravida should not exceed 18 hours
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO Intrapartum Care Guidelines (2018) state that the duration of the latent first stage of labour has not been definitively established and varies widely among women.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
According to WHO Intrapartum Care Guidelines 2018, which of the following are correct about birthing position?
I. For a woman without epidural analgesia, adoption of birthing position is individual woman's choice.
II. For a woman without epidural analgesia, upright birthing position may be adopted.
III. For a woman with epidural analgesia, lithotomy and supine position only are recommended.
Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO 2018 guidelines encourage women without epidural analgesia to adopt any birthing position of their choice (I), including upright positions (II).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Twin pregnancy should have ultrasound at 10-13 weeks to confirm which of the following?
1. Number of foetus Care Viability of foetus III. Chorionicity of twins of IV. Malforaation in either foetus
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A first-trimester ultrasound at 10–13 weeks in twin pregnancy confirms fetal number (I), viability (II), chorionicity/amnionicity via lambda/T sign (III), and major structural malformations (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are neonatal complications of maternal diabetes during pregnancy?
I. Hyperbilirubinemia
II. Hypercalcemia
III. Cardiomyopathy
IV. Hypoglycemia
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Neonatal complications of maternal diabetes include hyperbilirubinaemia (I), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (III), and hypoglycaemia (IV), along with hypocalcaemia (not hypercalcaemia).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the predictive factors for Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) ? Low level of maternal 1a trimester Beta hCG Abnormal uterine artery Doppler at 20-24 weeks of pregnancy III. Fetal echogenic bowel on ultrasound IV. Maternal medical disorder
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Predictors of fetal growth restriction include abnormal uterine artery Doppler (notching/high PI) at 20–24 weeks (II), fetal echogenic bowel (III), and maternal medical disorders such as chronic hypertension/APS (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is the primary surveillance tool in the Growth Restricted Fetus ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Umbilical artery Doppler velocimetry (assessing placental vascular resistance/absent or reversed end-diastolic flow) is the primary surveillance tool in growth-restricted fetuses.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Glands of Cloquet are :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The gland (lymph node) of Cloquet (Rosenmüller's node) is the deep inguinal sentinel lymph node draining the vulva and clitoris.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Causes of AUB are subdivided by the acronym PALM-COEIN. What are the characteristics of PALM causes?
I. Structural lesions
II. Diagnosed by ultrasound
III. Confirmed by histopathology
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In FIGO's PALM-COEIN classification of AUB, PALM (Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy/hyperplasia) represents structural causes (I) diagnosed by imaging/ultrasound (II) and confirmed by histopathology (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Daily suppressive therapy for HSV-1 and HSV-2 is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Daily suppressive therapy for recurrent genital herpes (HSV-1/HSV-2) can be given as oral valacyclovir 500 mg–1 g once daily.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the primary organisms involved in PID? I. N. gonorrhocae II. Chlamydia III. Mycoplasma hominis IV. Candida albicans
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pelvic inflammatory disease is primarily caused by ascending bacterial pathogens, notably Neisseria gonorrhoeae (I), Chlamydia trachomatis (II), and Mycoplasma hominis/genitalium (III), not Candida.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
What are the characteristics of dermoid cyst ? Germ cell ovarian tumour II. Bilateral in 15-20% cases III. Torsion is common IV. Rupture is common
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Dermoid cyst (mature cystic teratoma) is a germ cell tumour (I), bilateral in 15–20% of cases (II), and most commonly complicated by torsion (III) rather than rupture.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not differential diagnosis of chronic inversion of uterus ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chronic uterine inversion must be differentiated from a prolapsed fibroid polyp, fungating cervical cancer, and uterovaginal prolapse, whereas a Gartner's duct cyst is an anterolateral vaginal wall cyst.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A 28-year-old Pala presents to Gynaecology OPD with complaints of malodorous vaginal discharge. On examination, the discharge was found to be grayish-white in colour and adherent to vaginal walls. Which one of the following is a bedside diagnostic criterion for the causative organism ?
options: Presence of RBCs in vaginal smear
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Thin, grayish-white, malodorous discharge adherent to vaginal walls indicates bacterial vaginosis; a positive 10% KOH 'whiff test' (fishy amine odour) is a bedside Amsel criterion.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements about hysterosalpingography, as an operative procedure, are correct? L Tubal patency assessment following tuboplasty operation II. Diagnosis of uterine synechiae III. Detection of IUD IV. Diagnosis of subserosal fibroid Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hysterosalpingography (HSG) is useful to assess tubal patency post-tuboplasty (I), diagnose intrauterine synechiae/Asherman syndrome (II), and locate a lost IUCD (III), but cannot diagnose subserosal fibroids.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are indications of endometrial sampling? Endometrial tuberculosis IL. Endometrial polyp III. Postmenopausal bleeding IV. Abnormal uterine bleeding
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Endometrial sampling is indicated in suspected endometrial tuberculosis (I), postmenopausal bleeding (III), and abnormal uterine bleeding (IV) to rule out hyperplasia/carcinoma.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A 30-year-old Pala female presents in Gynaecology emergency with acute abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding of short duration (1 hour). She gives history of tubal ligation after birth of third child. On examination, right adnexal tenderness was found and os was closed. What is the probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Acute abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, closed cervical os, and adnexal tenderness in a woman with prior tubal ligation (a major risk factor) strongly indicate ectopic pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding audit in Obstetrics and Gynaecology ? L It can replace the out of date clinical practices with better ones. II. It is an efficient educational tool. III. It should be based on scientific evidences with facts and figures. IV. It is not labour-intensive. Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Clinical audit in obstetrics and gynaecology replaces outdated practices with evidence-based care (I), serves as an effective educational tool (II), and relies on scientific facts/figures (III), though it is labour-intensive.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are poor prognostic factors in endometrial adenocarcinoma? Estrogen and progesterone receptor positivity HER-2/neu gene expression III. Histologic types papillary serous clear cell carcinoma IV. Aneuploid tumours
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Poor prognostic factors in endometrial adenocarcinoma include HER-2/neu overexpression (II), high-risk serous/clear-cell histology (III), and DNA aneuploidy (IV), whereas ER/PR positivity predicts a favourable prognosis.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
For which of the following conditions, surgery is indicated in a case of Fibroid Uterus? I. Symptomatic and failed medical management II. Size > 12 weeks III. Pedunculated fibroid
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Surgical intervention for uterine fibroids is indicated when symptomatic and refractory to medical therapy (I), uterine size exceeds 12 weeks (II), or when a pedunculated fibroid risks torsion (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is measured without any straining while examination under POP-Q system ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In the POP-Q pelvic organ prolapse staging system, total vaginal length (TVL) is measured at rest without Valsalva/straining (whereas Aa, Ba, C, D, Ap, Bp are measured on maximum straining).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are criteria for opting Le Fort's operation for surgical correction of pelvic organ prolapse ? Procidentia in old age Unfit for long duration surgery III. Associated uterine pathology IV. Coital function no longer required
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Le Fort's colpocleisis is reserved for elderly women with procidentia (I) who are medically unfit for prolonged surgery (II) and no longer desire coital function (IV), provided uterine pathology is excluded.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Opening of Bartholin's duct is in the :
options: vestibule outside the hymen at the junction of the anterior 2/3rd and posterior 1/3rd
in the groove between the hymen and labium minus
groove between labia majora and labia minora / superficial perineal pouch
periurethral region in anterior 1/3rd of labia minora
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (a) — vestibule outside the hymen at the junction of the anterior 2/3rd and posterior 1/ard in the groove between the hymen and labium minus.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are Amsel's diagnostic criteria ? Vaginal pH > 4.5 IL Positive Whiff test III. Presence of clue cella > 20% IV. Positive bacterial vaginal culture
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
options: II, III and IV PREVENTIVE & SOCIAL MEDICINE
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Amsel's diagnostic criteria for bacterial vaginosis include vaginal pH > 4.5 (I), positive KOH whiff test (II), and >20% clue cells on wet mount (III), plus thin homogeneous discharge (not culture).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following indicators are considered for computing Physical Quality of Life Index" (PQLI) ? L Infant mortality II. Life expectancy at age one III. Literacy IV. Per capita income
Select the correct answer using the code given below : uid
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) combines three indicators: infant mortality rate (I), life expectancy at age 1 (II), and basic literacy rate (III), excluding per capita income.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following terms is an *all-or-none phenomenon" and is best described as termination of all transmission of infection by extermination of the infectious agent ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Disease eradication is an all-or-none phenomenon denoting permanent global termination of all transmission by complete extermination of the infectious agent.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: "Objectives are set forth for different units and subunits, each of which prepares its own plan of action, usually on a short-term basis." The definition best sums up which one among the following terms?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Management by Objectives (MBO) involves setting specific, time-bound objectives for each unit and subunit so each prepares its own short-term action plan.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
The Panchayati Raj is a three-tier structure of rural local self-government in India with the three levels being village, block and district. Consider the following bodies L Gram Sabha II. Gram Panchayat III. Nyaya Panchayat IV. Panchayat Samiti
Which of the above bodies are present at the village level ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: At the village tier of India's Panchayati Raj system, the Gram Sabha (I), Gram Panchayat (II), and Nyaya Panchayat (III) operate, whereas the Panchayat Samiti operates at the block level.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Many patients with unexplained rash and fever were reported from a village close to the Primary Health Centre (PHC). What is the first step in initiating the investigation of such an epidemic ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The very first step in investigating a suspected epidemic is verification of the diagnosis to ensure reported cases truly represent the disease.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: John Snow's discovery that cholera is a waterborne disease was the outcome of which type of study ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: John Snow's 1854 cholera investigation comparing households supplied by the Broad Street pump/Southwark & Vauxhall vs Lambeth water companies is the classic example of a natural experiment.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Given below is a table showing diagnosis of Myocardial infarction by ECG: Myocardial infarction ECG results Present Absent Positive 45 8,000 Negative 32,000 Total 50 40,000 Consider the following statements: Sensitivity is 90%. II. Specificity is 80%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sensitivity = TP / Total Diseased = 45 / 50 = 90% (Statement I true); Specificity = TN / Total Non-diseased = 32,000 / 40,000 = 80% (Statement II true).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Data obtained from hospital records is nof a representative sample of the popalation. What are the reasons for this? Mild cases and subclinical cases may be missed. Population served by a hospital usually cannot be defined. III. Cost of hospital care is not recorded. IV. Admission policy for cases can vary from hospital to hospital.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hospital data are unrepresentative of the general population because mild/subclinical cases are missed (I), the catchment population cannot be defined (II), and admission policies vary across hospitals (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Of the following ocular manifestations of Vitamin A deficiency, the first sign that can be clinically seen is :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Conjunctival xerosis (dry, dull, unwettable conjunctiva) is the earliest clinically visible ocular sign of vitamin A deficiency (nyctalopia/night blindness is a symptom).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The bony deformity of 'pigeon chest' in children occurs due to deficiency of :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pigeon chest (pectus carinatum) in children is a classic skeletal deformity of rickets caused by vitamin D deficiency.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one among the following essential amino acids is usually the "limiting amino acid in most of the pulses ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pulses (legumes) are rich in lysine but deficient in sulphur-containing amino acids, making methionine (and cysteine) their limiting amino acid.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which among the following are defence mechanisms adopted when an individual is faced with problems or failures?
I. Rationalization
II. Regression
III. Projection
IV. Replacement
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Rationalization (I), regression (II), and projection (III) are classic ego defence mechanisms described in psychology.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
What are the reasons for choosing coliform organisma as indicators of faecal pollution of water rather than the waterborne pathogens directly? They are present in great abundance in the human intestine and excreted in great numbers in faeces. They have lower resistance to forces of natural purification. III. They survive lesser than the pathogens. IV. They are easily detected by culture methods.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Coliforms are used as faecal indicator organisms because they are abundant in human intestines/faeces (I) and are easily detected by standard culture methods (IV), with greater survival than most enteric pathogens.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has launched a programme to meet the challenge of high prevalence of anaemia amongst adolescent boys and girls. Consider the following statements in relation to the key interventions being undertaken : L entails supervised weekly administration of 100 mg elemental iron and 500 ug folie acid. II. These weekly iron-folic acid supplements are administered by using a fixed day approach. III. It entails supervised administration of Albenâazole 400 mg every three months for control of helminth infestation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) programme, adolescents receive supervised weekly 100 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid (I) on a fixed-day approach (II).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination in India (2016-2030) has defined certain milestones and targets. Among the following, which is the specific target that has to be met by the year 2027 ?
options: All states and UTs must reduce API to less than 1 case per 1000 population at risk.
All states and UTs must establish fully functional malaria surveillance to track, investigate and respond to each case.
Entire country is to have no indigenous cases and no deaths due to malaria.
Entire country has to initiate the elimination phase.
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under India's National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016–2030), the 2027 milestone is achieving zero indigenous malaria cases and zero malaria deaths nationwide (followed by 3 years of surveillance to certify elimination by 2030).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan, the beneficiaries are being provided with a minimum package of antenatal care including certain investigations and drugs on a fixed day of every month. Which day of the month is specified for this purpose?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA), assured comprehensive antenatal checkups are provided on the 9th day of every month.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: "Small for Date" (SFD) babies, also known as *small for gestational age babies, weigh less than what percentile for the gestational age?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Small for gestational age / small for date (SFD) neonates are defined as having a birth weight below the 10th percentile for their gestational age.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: In the most widespread calculation of Stillbirth Rate, the numerator is defined as foetal deaths weighing over X gram at birth, during the year. Which one of the following is the correct value for X'?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: For international comparability, the standard stillbirth rate numerator counts late fetal deaths weighing > 1000 g (or ≥28 weeks gestation).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: While performing triage in response to a disaster emergency, commonly internationally accepted four-colour code system is used. Which one among the following four-colour categories represents the highest priority for emergency response?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In 4-colour disaster triage, Red indicates immediate/highest-priority patients with life-threatening but salvageable injuries.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to Ice-Lined Refrigerator (ILR) employed for storing vaccines at the sub-district level:
I. These types of refrigerators are top-opening.
II. Based on the temperature zone, the inside of ILRs can be divided into 3 parts.
III. The upper part of ILR is cooler compared to the lower part.
IV. Vaccines should never be kept directly on the floor of the ILR as they can get damaged.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ice-lined refrigerators (ILRs) are top-opening (I) and vaccines must never be placed directly on the floor of the cabinet where freezing can damage freeze-sensitive vaccines (IV); the bottom is colder than the top.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the aajar an contributor to the total energy intake, in terms of energy provided, in an average Indian diet ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Carbohydrates provide the largest share (~60–70%) of total dietary energy intake in an average Indian diet.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following with regard to Amino Acids:
I. Essential Amino Acids are those that the body cannot synthesize and they must be obtained from dietary proteins.
II. Not just the Essential Amino Acids, Non-essential Amino Acids are also needed by the body for synthesis of tissue proteins.
III. Unless a protein contains all the Essential Amino Acids in amounts corresponding to human needs, a protein is said to be biologically incomplete.
IV. Animal proteins are rated superior to vegetable proteins.
Of the above statements, how many are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: All four statements are correct: essential amino acids must come from diet, non-essential amino acids are still needed for tissue protein synthesis, complete proteins supply all EAAs, and animal proteins are superior to vegetable proteins in biological value.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following strategies were encouraged by the UNICEF under its 'GOBI Campaign'? G for growth charts to better monitor child development II. O for oral rehydration to treat all mild and moderate dehydration III. B for better and continuous evalaation of children up to 5 years of age IV. 1 for immunization against measles, diphtheria, polio, pertussis, tetanus and tuberculosis
Select the correct answer using the code given below
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: UNICEF's GOBI strategy stands for Growth monitoring (I), Oral rehydration therapy (II), Breastfeeding, and Immunization (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the limit of daily exposure of noise that people can tolerate without substantial damage to their hearing?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The maximum permissible daily 8-hour noise exposure limit without substantial risk of noise-induced hearing loss is 85 dB(A).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: How much illumination is recommended by the Illuminating Engineering Society for the general office work?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Illuminating Engineering Society recommends 400 lux of illumination for general office work.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Dietary fibres have :
options: sometimes anabolic and sometimes catabolic effect, depending on the type
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Dietary fibre is indigestible by human enzymes and provides essentially no net metabolic/anabolic fuel, classified in this standard PSM MCQ as having a catabolic effect (increasing faecal bulk/transit and lowering cholesterol/energy absorption).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Egg proteins are considered to be the best among food proteins because: of their biological value II. of their digestibility III. they contain all the essential amino acids IV. their calorie content is higher than in proteins of vegetable sources
Which of the statements given above is'are correct ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Egg protein is the reference protein because of its ~96% biological value (I), high digestibility (II), and complete essential amino acid profile (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: On a chest radiograph, which of the following occupational diseases is most likely to be mistaken as a case of tuberculosis of lungs?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Upper-lobe nodular opacities and cavitation/fibrosis in silicosis closely mimic pulmonary tuberculosis on chest radiography.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: With which variety of asbestos, Mesothelioma has been shown to have a strong association ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Crocidolite (blue asbestos) has the strongest association with malignant pleural and peritoneal mesothelioma.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016, human anatomical waste is to be carried in which colour plastic bags ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016, human anatomical waste is segregated into yellow-coloured non-chlorinated plastic bags for incineration.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
As an index of thermal comfort, the 'Corrected Effective Temperature' is considered to be an improvement over 'Effective Temperature'. It deals with which of the following factors? Air velocity HI. Humidity III. Mean radiant heat IV. Sweat rate
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Corrected Effective Temperature (CET) improves upon Effective Temperature by incorporating air velocity (I), humidity (II), and mean radiant heat (III) measured via a globe thermometer.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: In a child who has not received any dose of DPT and OPV immunization, up to what age can these vaccines be given under the Universal Immunization Programme?
options: DPT up to 7 years of age and OPV up to 5 years of age
DPT up to 8 years of age and OPV up to 6 years of age
DPT up to 10 years of age and OPV up to 7 years of age
DPT up to 12 years of age and OPV up to 10 years of age
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under India's Universal Immunization Programme, DPT can be given up to 7 years of age and OPV up to 5 years of age.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A traveller who has passed through a yellow fever endemic zone and does not possess a Certificate of Vaccination against yellow fever, enters a yellow fever 'receptive' area. For how long from the date of leaving the infected area must this traveller be placed on quarantine in a mosquito-proof ward ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Unvaccinated travellers arriving from a yellow fever endemic zone into a receptive area are quarantined in a mosquito-proof ward for 6 days from the date of leaving the infected area (matching the 6-day incubation period).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Under the Employees' State Insurance Act 1948, if the sickness of an insured person is duly certified by an Insurance Medical Officer, periodical cash payment benefit is payable for a maximum period of how many days in any continuous period of 365 days, as Sickness Benefit ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the ESI Act 1948, Sickness Benefit is payable for a maximum of 91 days in any two consecutive benefit periods (365 days).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Wernicke's encephalopathy : I. It is caused by niacin deficiency. II. It is often seen in alcoholics. III. Ophthalmoplegia, polyneuritis and ataxia are some of its characteristic features. IV. It occurs occasionally in people who fast.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wernicke's encephalopathy is caused by thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency (not niacin, so I is false), commonly in alcoholics (II) and prolonged fasting (IV), presenting with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and polyneuropathy/confusion (III).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: A housefly transmits any infectious agent by which of the following methods, most commonly ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The common housefly (Musca domestica) transmits enteric pathogens predominantly by mechanical carriage on its feet, body hairs, and vomitus.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: In the case of a 7-year-old school-going child, which would be the most appropriate indicator to measure the current nutritional status ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Weight-for-height (wasting) is a sensitive age-independent indicator of acute/current nutritional status in school-age children.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) : Early detection and special care of pre-term newborns is one of the majar objectives of HBNC. ANM is the main person involved in the delivery of HBNC. III. Supporting the family for adoption of healthy practices helps achieve the key objectives of HBNC. IV. The primary aim of HBNC is to improve newborn survival.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) is delivered primarily by ASHA workers (not ANMs, so II is false) to detect/care for preterm newborns (I), promote healthy practices (III), and improve newborn survival (IV).

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following conditions are transmitted as a recessive, sex-linked trait? Retinitis pigmentosa II. Colour blindness III. Cystic fibrosis IV. Duchenne muscular dystrophy
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Retinitis pigmentosa (X-linked forms; I), red-green colour blindness (II), and Duchenne muscular dystrophy (IV) are X-linked recessive traits, whereas cystic fibrosis is autosomal recessive.

upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.text: Under which name (brand) does the National AIDS Control Organisation provide the STI/RTI services ?
upsc-cms-2025-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2025 Answer Key: Option (d) — Suraksha Clinic prepp epp Your Personal Exam Guide prepp prepp Your Personal Exam Guide epp Your Personal Exam Guide prepp epp Your Personal Exam Guide.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: The height of the Jugular Venous Pulse is determined by :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The vertical height of the jugular venous pulse (JVP) above the sternal angle directly reflects right atrial (central venous) pressure.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: The SA node is situated at the junction of :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The sinoatrial (SA) node is located subepicardially at the junction of the superior vena cava (SVC) and the right atrium (RA).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
High output cardiac failure is caused by which of the following diseases?
1. Beri-beri
2. Severe anaemia
3. Thyrotoxicosis
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: All three listed conditions—including thyrotoxicosis, hypertension, and ischaemic/valvular heart disease—are recognized causes of atrial fibrillation.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Reverse splitting of second heart sound is most commonly seen in :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Left bundle branch block (LBBB) delays left ventricular activation and aortic valve closure (A2), causing A2 to follow P2 during expiration and merge on inspiration (paradoxical/reverse splitting of S2).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are major criteria under the Jones Criteria for Acute Rheumatic Fever ?
1. Chorea
2. Erythema Marginatum
3. Subcutaneous Nodules
4. Polyarthralgia
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (a) — Revised Jones Criteria (low-risk population): Major criteria are Carditis, Polyarthritis, Chorea (1), Erythema marginatum (2), and Subcutaneous nodules (3). Polyarthralgia (4) is a minor criterion [Harrison's / Ghai Pediatrics].

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: A 70-year-old man with dyspnoea on exertion has been found to have a single second heart sound and a loud diamond-shaped, rough quality systolic murmur best heard at the right 2nd intercostal space, radiating to the right carotid artery. Which one of the following is the likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Exertional dyspnoea, single S2, and a harsh crescendo-decrescendo (diamond-shaped) systolic murmur at the right 2nd intercostal space radiating to the carotids are classic for severe aortic stenosis.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the appropriate scoring system used to assess the risk of stroke in patients of non-valvular chronic atrial fibrillation on oral anticoagulation?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The CHA2DS2-VASc score estimates annual stroke risk in non-valvular atrial fibrillation to guide anticoagulation (HAS-BLED estimates bleeding risk).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to pulmonary embolism:
1. Unexplained breathlessness is the most common symptom.
2. When congestive heart failure or pneumonia fail to improve despite standard medical treatment, occult pulmonary embolism should be considered.
3. Patients with high clinical likelihood of venous thromboembolism should first undergo D-dimer testing alone without obligatory imaging tests.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Unexplained dyspnoea is the most common symptom of PE (1), and occult PE must be suspected when CHF/pneumonia fail to respond (2); high-probability patients proceed directly to CTPA rather than D-dimer testing (3 is false).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following criteria:
1. Pleural fluid protein : Serum protein ratio > 0-5
2. Pleural fluid LDH : Serum LDH ratio >
3. Pleural fluid LDH > Two-thirds of the upper limit of normal serum LDH
Which of the above criteria, if present in pleural fluid, will indicate an exudate?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Light's criteria classify a pleural effusion as an exudate if ANY of the following hold: pleural/serum protein > 0.5 (1), pleural/serum LDH > 0.6 (2), or pleural LDH > 2/3 upper limit of normal serum LDH (3).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct with regard to clubbing ?
1. It usually affects the fingers symmetrically.
2. It does not involve the toes.
3. It may be associated with malignant lung conditions.
4. It may recede following the lung transplantation in cystic fibrosis. Select the answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Digital clubbing is usually symmetric (1), affects both fingers and toes, is linked to bronchogenic carcinoma (3), and can regress after lung transplantation in cystic fibrosis (4).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Lofgren syndrome :
1. It is an acute illness and is more commonly seen in females.
2. It is a clinically distinct phenotype of sarcoidosis characterized by peripheral arthropathy and uveitis.
3. Clinical features include fever, lymphadenopathy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Löfgren syndrome is an acute, self-limiting presentation of sarcoidosis seen more often in young women (1), featuring fever, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (3), erythema nodosum, and peripheral arthropathy/uveitis (2).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following investigations may be used for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis ?
1. Nucleic acid amplification
2. Culture in Middlebrook medium
3. Light emitting diode fluorescent microscopy with auramine staining
4. Peripheral blood smear
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pulmonary tuberculosis is diagnosed using NAAT/CBNAAT (1), mycobacterial culture on Middlebrook/LJ medium (2), and LED fluorescence microscopy with auramine-rhodamine staining (3).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: The distance walked in 6 minutes is an indirect measure of which of the following variables of the 'BODE Index' which is used to assess the prognosis in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease ?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In the BODE index (BMI, Obstruction, Dyspnoea, Exercise capacity), the 6-minute walk distance measures Exercise capacity.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: A 65-year-old female, a stone-cutter by occupation had multiple well circumscribed nodular opacities in upper and middle zones of a chest X-ray along with mediastinal lymph nodes showing egg-shell calcification. Which one of the following is the most likely etiology ?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Upper- and mid-zone well-circumscribed nodular opacities with eggshell calcification of mediastinal lymph nodes in a stone-cutter are pathognomonic of silicosis.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are complications of acute pancreatitis? 1. Hypoxia
2. Hypercalcemia
3. Hyperglycemia
4. Reduced serum albumin
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute pancreatitis causes hypoxia (1), hyperglycaemia (3), hypoalbuminaemia (4), and hypocalcaemia (due to fat saponification, not hypercalcaemia).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: The most specific initial diagnostic test for Celiac disease is:
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Endoscopic distal duodenal/small-bowel biopsy (demonstrating villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and intraepithelial lymphocytosis) is the gold-standard confirmatory test for coeliac disease.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
With regard to Helicobacter pylori eradication in peptic ulcer disease, consider the following statements :
1. Proton-pump inhibitor is taken with two antibiotics.
2. Treatment is prescribed for at least 7 days.
3. Treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection leads to vitamin B12 deficiency.
4. Patients requiring long-term NSAIDs should undergo Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy to reduce ulcer risk.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: H. pylori eradication combines a PPI with two antibiotics (1) for at least 7–14 days (2) and reduces ulcer risk in patients starting long-term NSAIDs (4); it does not cause vitamin B12 deficiency.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are precipitating factors for hepatic encephalopathy ?
1. Hypokalemia
2. Septicemia
3. Increased dietary protein load
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypokalaemia (promoting renal ammoniagenesis; 1), septicaemia (2), and excess dietary protein load (3) all precipitate hepatic encephalopathy.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Upper Gastro Intestinal Bleeding (UGIB) ?
options: Esophageal varices are the most common cause.
Eradication of Helicobacter pylori in patients with bleeding ulcers decreases the rebleeding rates to less than 5%.
Patients with cardiovascular disease who are on aspirin for secondary prevention should not restart their aspirin.
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2024 Answer Key: Option (b) — Eradication of Helicobacter pylori in patients with bleeding ulcers decreases the rebleeding rates to less than 5%..

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Crigler-Najjar syndrome Type-I is inherited as an :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Crigler-Najjar syndrome Type I (complete absence of UGT1A1 activity) is inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Whipple's disease is characterized by the infiltration of small intestinal mucosa by foamy' macrophages. Which one of the following histological stains is characteristically used to stain them?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain highlights the diastase-resistant glycoprotein inclusions inside foamy macrophages in Whipple's disease.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Poorly absorbed antibiotics are often used as adjunctive therapies in patients with hepatic encephalopathy. These may include :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Poorly absorbed oral antibiotics such as rifaximin or neomycin reduce gut ammonia-producing bacteria in hepatic encephalopathy.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
When the serum ascites to albumin gradient (SAAG) is less than 1.1 gm/dL, then which of the following causes of ascites may be considered ?
1. Infection
2. Malignancy Cardiac ascites
4. Portal hypertension
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A low SAAG (< 1.1 g/dL) indicates non-portal-hypertension ascites, primarily due to peritoneal infection/tuberculosis (1) or peritoneal carcinomatosis/malignancy (2).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: A sigmoid configuration along with tapering beak-like deformity at the lower esophageal sphincter on barium swallow is a feature of :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A dilated sigmoid oesophagus with smooth distal tapering ('bird-beak' appearance) at the lower oesophageal sphincter on barium swallow is classic for achalasia cardia.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Consider the following findings in urine examination of suspected haematuria: Dipstick test is Urine Etiology positive for microscopy following component A : Myoglobinuria D: White G : Glomerular blood bleeding cells B : Hematuria E : No red H : Intravascular cells hemolysis C : Hemoglobinuria F : Red cell I : Rhabdomyolysis casts Which one of the following triplets is correctly matched?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Glomerular haematuria (B) produces red cell casts (F) on urine microscopy, indicating glomerular bleeding (G).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding anti-glomerular basement membrane disease?
1. It is a rare autoimmune disease which presents as rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.
2. Antibodies are formed against α3 chain of type 4 collagen GBM.
3. The α3 chain is expressed in basement membrane of glomerulus and the retina.
4. The disease may be associated with retinal hemorrhage when it is known as Goodpasture syndrome. Select the answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Anti-GBM disease causes rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (1) mediated by autoantibodies against the α3 chain of type IV collagen (2), which is expressed in glomerular and alveolar (not retinal) basement membranes.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are poor prognostic indictators in glomerular disease?
1. Female sex
2. Hypertension
3. Persistent and severe proteinuria
4. Elevated creatinine levels at presentation
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Poor prognostic indicators in glomerular disease include hypertension (2), persistent heavy proteinuria (3), and elevated serum creatinine at presentation (4) (male sex, not female, confers worse prognosis).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are indications for a renal biopsy ?
1. Chronic kidney disease of uncertain etiology
2. Nephritic syndrome
3. Uncontrolled severe hypertension
4. Renal transplant dysfunction
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Renal biopsy is indicated in unexplained CKD/AKI (1), nephritic syndrome (2), and renal transplant dysfunction (4); uncontrolled severe hypertension is a contraindication.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is the correct range of Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) for Stage 2 chronic kidney disease?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: KDIGO Stage 2 CKD (mildly decreased GFR) corresponds to an eGFR of 60–89 mL/min/1.73 m².

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
A diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome requires the presence of which of the following clinical features ?
1. Menstrual irregularity
2. Clinical or biochemical androgen excess
3. Multiple cysts in the ovaries
4. BMI < 18:5 kg/m2
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Rotterdam diagnostic criteria for PCOS require at least 2 of 3 features: oligo/anovulation (menstrual irregularity; 1), clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism (2), and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound (3).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: A young male presented with recent onset urethral discharge and dysuria. On examination, the discharge was profuse and purulent. Microscopy of smears from the discharge revealed Gram-negative diplococci. What is the likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Profuse purulent urethral discharge with dysuria and Gram-negative intracellular diplococci on smear is diagnostic of gonorrhoea.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
A 40-year-old female with nephritic range proteinuria is found to have low serum complement levels. Which of the following can be the likely etiology?
1. Systemic lupus erythematosus
2. Post-infectious glomerulonephritis 3- Infective endocarditis
4. Mesangio-capillary glomerulonephritis
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypocomplementaemic glomerulonephritis occurs in SLE (1), post-infectious GN (2), infective endocarditis-related GN (3), and membranoproliferative/mesangiocapillary GN (4).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following clinical features:
1. Hypomimia
2. Dysphonia
3. Festination gait
4. Cogwheel rigidity Which of the features given above are generally present in Parkinsonism?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Parkinsonism presents with hypomimia (mask-like face; 1), hypophonia/dysphonia (2), festinating gait (3), and cogwheel rigidity (4).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Circuits between the basal ganglia and the motor cortex constitute the extra pyramidal system which controls muscle tone, body posture and the initiation of movement. Lesions of the extra pyramidal system present clinically with :
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Extrapyramidal (basal ganglia) lesions classically produce movement and tone abnormalities such as resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, and chorea.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Transient Global Amnesia (TGA) :
1. TGA mainly affects middle aged persons who present with abrupt, discrete loss of anterograde memory lasting for few hours.
2. During the episode, the patients are unable to record new memories resulting in repetitive questioning.
3. Consciousness is impaired during the episode and the patient is unable to perform even simple motor functions.
4. After 4-6 hours, memory function and behaviour return to normal but the patient has complete and persistent amnesia for the duration of the episode.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Transient global amnesia affects middle-aged adults with abrupt anterograde amnesia (1), repetitive questioning (2), and spontaneous recovery within 4–6 hours (4), while consciousness and motor skills remain intact (3 is false).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Contralateral homonymous lower quadrantanopia is the type of visual loss seen when the lesion is located at which one of the following anatomical locations?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Parietal lobe lesions damage the superior optic radiation fibres (Baum's loop), causing contralateral homonymous inferior (lower) quadrantanopia ('pie on the floor').

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following correctly describes the primary position of the right eye in right 3rd cranial nerve palsy?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In a right CN III (oculomotor) palsy, unopposed lateral rectus (CN VI) and superior oblique (CN IV) pull the eye into a 'down and out' (downwards and outwards) position.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding cluster headache :
1. The headaches are periodic, beginning at the same time for weeks at a stretch.
2. Patients experience severe, unilateral periorbital pain which typically lasts from 30 - 90 minutes. The headache is accompanied with autonomic features such as ipsilateral tearing, nasal congestion and conjunctival injection.
4. Subcutaneous injection of Sumatriptan or inhalation of 100% oxygen may be beneficial in halting acute attacks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cluster headaches occur in cyclical bouts (1) with severe unilateral periorbital pain lasting 30–90 min (2), ipsilateral autonomic signs (3), and respond acutely to subcutaneous sumatriptan or 100% oxygen (4).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: A 22-year-old lady presented with complaint of chronic daily headache. She has prior history of migraine but increasingly unrelieved with analgesics. She has history of using Sumatriptan almost daily since the last three weeks. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic daily headache refractory to analgesics in a migraineur taking sumatriptan almost daily for weeks is classic for medication overuse headache.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following with regard to trigger factors for seizures :
1. Flickering lights
2. Recreational drug misuse
3. Non-compliance to treatment with antiepileptic drugs
4. Sleep deprivation Which of the factors given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Flickering lights (photic stimulation; 1), recreational drugs (2), AED non-compliance (3), and sleep deprivation (4) are all recognized seizure precipitants.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: A 75-year-old man presented with temporal headache, jaw pain, exacerbated by chewing . and talking. Which one of the following investigations will most likely help in diagnosis ?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Temporal headache and jaw claudication in a 75-year-old man strongly suggest giant cell (temporal) arteritis; temporal artery biopsy is the gold-standard confirmatory test.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: The Rai staging system and Binet staging system are the two widely used staging systems used for staging which of the following hematological malignancies ?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Rai (0–IV) and Binet (A–C) clinical staging systems are specifically used for chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL).

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Patients suffering from which of the following conditions commonly present for several years in the dermatology OPD with eczematous or dermatitis skin lesions before being finally diagnosed with a T-cell lymphoma?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) characteristically mimics chronic eczema or dermatitis for years before definitive biopsy diagnosis.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is an oral anticoagulant ?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Dabigatran is an oral direct thrombin inhibitor, whereas heparin, fondaparinux, and bivalirudin are parenteral anticoagulants.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: A 39-year-old female presents with severe autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Which of the following should be the initial step in its management?
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oral glucocorticoids (prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day) are the first-line initial treatment for warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.

upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2024-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is a cause of Secondary Hyperaldosteronism ?
options: Inadequate renal perfusion due to renal artery stenosis
