upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (a) — Contraceptive failure rates (Pearl Index per 100 woman-years): DMPA 0–1 (1), Norplant 0.1 (2), LNG-IUS 0.02–0.2 (3); Levonorgestrel POP is ~1–3/HWY (dropped by UPSC) [Park's PSM].

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following in respect of Ormeloxifene :
1. It is a research product of Central Drug Research Institute, Lucknow
2. It is a steroidal compound
3. It is a potent antiestrogen with weak estrogenic properties
4. It does not inhibit ovulation
Which of the above are correct?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ormeloxifene (centchroman) was developed by CDRI Lucknow (1), is a non-steroidal SERM with potent antioestrogenic/weak oestrogenic activity (3), and does not inhibit ovulation (4).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Steroidal contraceptives available in the basket of contraceptive choice from Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India are
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Government of India's family planning basket provides monophasic combined oral contraceptive pills (Mala-N/Mala-D).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are absolute contraindications of Combined Oral Contraceptive (COCs) ?
1. Arterial or venous thrombosis history
2. Severe hypertension
3. Gestational trophoblastic neopl sia
4. Diabetes with vascular complic tions
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Absolute (MEC Category 4) contraindications to COCs include history of arterial/venous thrombosis (1), severe hypertension ≥ 160/100 (2), and diabetes with vascular complications (4).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: After male sterilization, additional contraceptive protection is
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: After vasectomy, backup contraception is required for 2–3 months (and ~20 ejaculations) until semen analysis confirms azoospermia.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: The life expectancy at birth for a country A is 64 years. The minimum and maximum values of life expectancy are 20 years and 86 years respectively. As part of Human Development Index (HDI), what is the Life Expectancy Index for the country A ?

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following indicators stand consolidated in Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) ?
1. Infant mortality
2. Life expectancy at age one
3. Per capita income
4. Literacy
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: PQLI consolidates infant mortality (1), life expectancy at age 1 (2), and literacy (4) (excluding per capita income).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following staff :
1. Medical Officer
2. Pharmacist
3. Anaesthetist
4. Health Educator Of them, who are routinely posted to a PHC ?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Routine PHC staff include Medical Officer (1), Pharmacist (2), and Health Educator/LHV/ANM (4), whereas anaesthetists are posted at CHCs/FRUs.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following manag ment techniques helps in standardising the methods of performing jobs?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Work sampling is a quantitative management technique used to observe and standardize job methods and time allocation.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: STDs are transmitted by
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sexually transmitted diseases are transmitted primarily by direct sexual contact.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Under the International Health Regul tions which of the following diseases are notifiable by the National Health Authority to the World Health Organ sation ?
1. Cholera
2. Plague
3. Klebsiella pneumonia
4. Yellow fever
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the classic International Health Regulations, cholera (1), plague (2), and yellow fever (4) were the internationally notifiable quarantinable diseases.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: In which one of the following study designs, the unit of study involves populations rather than individuals?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ecological studies use entire populations or geographical groups rather than individuals as the unit of analysis.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: The following table shows the mortality figures among hazardous industry workers : Age National Hazardous Observed group death industry deaths rate per worker 1000 population 25-34 2-0 3000 35-44 3.5 2000 9 45-54 6-0 2000 13 What is the Standardized Mortality Ratio (SMR) for the hazardous industry workers (as compared to national pop lation) ?

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following best explains the relationship among Prevalence (P), Incidence (I) and Duration (D) of a disease given the assumption that the population is stable ?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a stable population, disease prevalence equals incidence multiplied by mean duration (P = I × D).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: A new test was developed for detection of COVID-19. Test Disease + Disease-Total Positive 60 40 100 Negative 100 1800 1900 160 1840 2000 What is the sensitivity of the test as per the information provided above?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: From the 2×2 table, Sensitivity = TP / Total Diseased = 60 / 160 = 37.5%.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
The blood glucose level of 5 individuals was 110, 94, 102, 98, 96 : Consider the following statements :
1. The range is 10
2. The median is 98
3. The standard deviation is v10
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sorted: 94, 96, 98, 102, 110. Median = 98 (2); Range = 110 − 94 = 16 (here 10 in text/official key marks 1 and 2 only).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are true about measles ?
1. It is highly infectious in the phase following the appearance of rash
2. Infection usually confers lifelong immunity
3. It has a low secondary attack rate
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Measles confers lifelong immunity (2) and is highly infectious during the prodromal and early rash stages (1) with a very high (>80%) secondary attack rate.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following drugs should be avoided in the first-line ART regimens because of its well recognized met bolic toxicities ?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Stavudine (d4T) is avoided in first-line ART due to severe mitochondrial toxicities (lipodystrophy, lactic acidosis, peripheral neuropathy).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: The recommended dose of cotrimox zole for treatment of pneumonia in a child weighing 16 kg is
options: One paediatric tablet twice a day
Two paediatric tablets twice a day
Three paediatric tablets twice a day
Four paediatric tablets twice a day
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under WHO/IMNCI ARI dosing, a child weighing 10–19 kg (16 kg) receives 2 paediatric tablets (or 3 per older weight band; official key marks 3 tablets BID).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Hepatitis B vaccine administered at birth is
options: A combined vaccine of inactivated Polio and Hepatitis B
A fixed combination vaccine of Hib, Hepatitis
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The birth dose of Hepatitis B vaccine given within 24 hours of delivery is a monovalent recombinant Hepatitis B vaccine.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
The classical triad of congenital defects in Congenital Rubella Syndrome i clude which of the following ?
1. Hydrocephalus
2. Deafness
3. Cardiac malformations
4. Cataract
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The classic triad of Congenital Rubella Syndrome comprises sensorineural deafness (2), cardiac malformations like PDA (3), and cataracts (4).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are correct in respect of Diphtheria?
1. The incubation period is 14 to 28 days
2. Diphtheria antitoxin is used in treatment of cases
3. It is one of the diseases protected from, by the Pentavalent vaccine given in National Program
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Diphtheria is treated with diphtheria antitoxin (2) and prevented by the Pentavalent vaccine (3) (incubation period is 2–5 days, not 14–28 days).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
A person has presented with history of dog-bite on the uncovered surface of his right leg. There is a minor abrasion without bleeding. Consider the follo ing statements about management:
1. The bite should be taken as a category I contact with suspect animal
2. The bite requires local treatment of the wound
3. The person requires immediate vaccination
4. The person requires immediate administration of rabies immun globulin
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A minor abrasion without bleeding from a dog bite is a WHO Category II rabies exposure requiring immediate wound washing (2) and rabies vaccination (3), without RIG.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following stages of modern sewage treatment plants :
1. Use of Grit chamber
2. Use of Primary sedimentation tank
3. Screening
4. Use of Sludge digester What would be the correct sequence of the above stages?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Modern sewage treatment proceeds sequentially: screening (3) → grit chamber (1) → primary sedimentation tank (2) → sludge digester (4).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: A vital layer, also known as Schmutzdecke" is seen in which one of the following ?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The 'Schmutzdecke' (biological gelatinous layer on the sand surface) is the active purifying layer in a slow sand filter.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: A 25 year old woman is a sedentary worker. She is a lactating mother with a 3 month old child. Which one among the following is the best approximation of her energy requirement in terms of kilocalories per day ?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: For a sedentary lactating woman (0–6 months postpartum), ICMR RDA is ~1900 + 600 = 2500 kcal/day.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: The amount of iron lost per 28 day cycle in menstruating women is
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Average menstrual iron loss per 28-day cycle is approximately 12.5 mg (~0.4–0.5 mg/day averaged over the cycle).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: The most sensitive indicator of enviro mental iodine deficiency is
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Prevalence of neonatal hypothyroidism (elevated neonatal TSH) is the most sensitive indicator of environmental iodine deficiency.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Insulin Resistance Syndrome (Sy drome X) is associated with which of the following ?
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
2. Hyperinsulinaemia
3. Dyslipidaemia
4. Hypercalcaemia
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Insulin resistance syndrome (Syndrome X) encompasses Type 2 diabetes (1), hyperinsulinaemia (2), and atherogenic dyslipidaemia (3) (not hypercalcaemia).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: The "DASH diet" is a lifestyle modif cation for management of which of these conditions?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet is a proven nutritional intervention for hypertension.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is a famous large prospective study that helped establish risk factors for coronary heart disease ?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Framingham Heart Study is the landmark prospective cohort study that identified major cardiovascular risk factors.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Most industrial workers are exposed to lead as an occupational hazard. Which of the following statements regarding lead poisoning are correct?
1. Lead poisoning is also called plumbism
2. Basophilic stippling of red blood cells is seen
3. Progressive massive fibrosis of lungs is seen
4. Coproporphyrin in urine (CPU) is a useful screening test
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Lead poisoning (plumbism; 1) causes basophilic stippling of RBCs (2) and elevated urinary coproporphyrin (4) (PMF occurs in silicosis/CWP).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Of the following international age cies, which agency has been assisting India in development of friendly models of sanitization ?
options: CARE (Cooperative for Assistance and Relief Everywhere)
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Ford Foundation assisted India in developing community sanitation and rural health models.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one among the following was used for measuring economic status of households, in the National Family Health Survey-III (NFHS-III) ?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: NFHS-III measured household economic status using the asset-based Wealth Index.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
In a town with one lakh population (1,00,000) there are a total of 2500 live births in a year. There were 75 total deaths of children before the age of one month, total 200 deaths before the age of one year, and a total 300 deaths before the age of three years. Which of the following statements regarding Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) of the town for the given year are correct?
1. The denominator is 1,00,000
2. The IMR of the town is higher than the current national average of IMR for India
3. The numerator is the number of children dying before the age of one month
4. The IMR of the town is 80 per 1000 live births
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: IMR = (200 / 2500) × 1000 = 80 per 1000 live births, which is higher than the national average (2) and uses live births (2500) as denominator (4).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: The voluntary scheme under which any obstetrics and gynaecology specialist, lady doctor/MBBS doctor can volu teer themselves for providing sate motherhood service is called
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Vande Mataram Scheme enlists voluntary obstetricians/MBBS doctors to provide free safe motherhood services.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
A 2 year old child has presented for vaccination, who has never been vacc nated earlier. As per the Universal Immunization Program, which among the following vaccines will be admini tered to the child on the first visit?
1. BCG vaccine
2. DPT-1 vaccine
3. Hepatitis B vaccine
4. Measles vaccine
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: For an unimmunized 2-year-old child, DPT-1 (2) and Measles/MR (4) are given on the first visit (BCG is not given above 1 year under UIP).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Consider the following statements: Statement-1: In the National Immun zation Program, BCG vaccine is given only on the left upper arm Statement-2: This is done to maintain uniformity and for hel ing surveyors in verif ing receipt of the vaccine Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Statements?
options: Both Statement-1 and Statement-2 are correct and Statement-2 is the correct explanation for Stat ment-1
Both Statement-1 and Statement-2 are correct and Statement-2 is not the correct explanation for Stat ment-1
Statement-1 is true but Statement-2 is false
Statement-1 is false but Stat ment-2 is true
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2021 Answer Key: Option (a) — Both Statement-1 and Statement-2 are correct and Statement-2 is the correct explanation for Stat ment-1.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
You visit an industry to audit whether the benefits under the Employees State Insurance Act are being properly pr vided. Which of the following benefits should be available to the insured persons, or other dependents as the case may be?
1. Medical benefit
2. Sickness benefit
3. Funeral expenses
4. Rehabilitation allowance
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: ESI Act 1948 provides medical benefit (1), sickness benefit (2), funeral expenses (3), and rehabilitation allowance (4) alongside maternity and disablement benefits.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Among the following intra-uterine contraceptive devices, which of the following are included in second generation IUDs ?
1. Lippes Loop
2. Copper T-200
3. LNG-20 (Mirena)
4. Copper-T-380 A Vacancies ond updates on one click
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Second-generation IUDs are copper-releasing devices such as Copper T-200 (2) and Copper T-380A (4).

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: DANIDA, the international aid agency of Denmark, is known for its assistance to which one of the India's National Health Programmes ?
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: DANIDA (Danish International Development Agency) notably supported India's National Programme for Control of Blindness.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: After attending a birthday party in a hostel around 50 students reported having loose stools, fever and few reported vomiting. This outbreak can be identified as what type of outbreak?
options: Both propagated and common point source
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An acute gastroenteritis cluster among 50 students after a single shared birthday meal is a classic common-point-source outbreak.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following vaccines are given through the intramuscular route?
1. BCG vaccine
2. Hepatitis B vaccine
3. Pentavalent vaccine
4. Inactivated Polio vaccine
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hepatitis B (2), Pentavalent (3), and IM IPV (4) are administered intramuscularly, whereas BCG is intradermal.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text: Covaxin is a/an
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Covaxin (BBV152) is an inactivated whole-virion SARS-CoV-2 vaccine.

upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following agencies are playing a key role in running of the COVAX" initiative against COVID-19 ?
1. GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance
2. World Health Organisation (WHO)
3. Ford Foundation
4. Coalition for Epidemic Prepare ness Innovations (CEPI)
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2021-paper-2-authentic.explanation: COVAX was co-led by Gavi (1), WHO (2), and CEPI (4) to accelerate global COVID-19 vaccine access.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A chronic alcoholic develops a paroxysm of pa lpitations after alcohol binge. Which of the following Arrhythmia is most likely?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: 'Holiday heart syndrome'—paroxysmal palpitations following an acute alcohol binge—is most commonly caused by atrial fibrillation.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: An elderly-man with history of Diabetes me llitus and Coronary Artery Disease comes for follow-up, with complaints of muscle pains. Which one of the following drugs could be the most likely cause?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Myalgia/myopathy in a diabetic CAD patient on secondary prevention is most commonly an adverse effect of statin therapy (atorvastatin).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 40-year old lady comes to outdoor clinic with complaints of sudden onset chest pain. The chest X-ray shows bilateral Pneumothorax. Examination reveals abnormalities of body habitus-including long arms, legs and finger (ar achnodactyly), scoliosis, high arched palate, joint hypermobility, and a pansystolic murmur at cardiac apex. Which one of the following diseases is most likely?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tall marfanoid habitus, arachnodactyly, scoliosis, high-arched palate, joint hypermobility, spontaneous pneumothorax, and mitral regurgitation murmur are classic for Marfan's syndrome.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are indications for treadmill testing/exercise-testing EXCEPT:
options: To confirm the diagnosis of angina
To assess outcome after coronary revascularization
To evaluate the treatment efficacy of antianginal drugs
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Exercise treadmill testing is used to diagnose CAD, risk-stratify stable angina, and assess revascularization outcomes, not routinely to titrate antianginal drug efficacy.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Kussmaul’s sign is present in all of the following conditions, EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Kussmaul's sign (paradoxical inspiratory rise in JVP) occurs in restrictive cardiomyopathy, RV infarction, constrictive pericarditis, and massive PE, but not in uncomplicated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a common cause of atrial fibrillation?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypothyroidism causes sinus bradycardia rather than atrial fibrillation (unlike thyrotoxicosis, mitral regurgitation, hypertension, and acute MI).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: In an ECG recording, P wave is produced by:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: On the surface ECG, the P wave represents atrial depolarization.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following modalities is NOT used in the treatment of ventricular tachycardia?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Adenosine acts on the AV node and is ineffective/contraindicated for ventricular tachycardia (unlike DC cardioversion, lignocaine, and amiodarone).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following drugs is a Direct Renin Inhibitor?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Aliskiren is an oral direct renin inhibitor that blocks conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are causes of systolic hypertension with wide pulse pressure EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Aortic stenosis causes a narrow pulse pressure (pulsus parvus et tardus), whereas aortic regurgitation, thyrotoxicosis, and PDA cause wide pulse pressure.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Signet-ring sign on CT-chest is suggestive of:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The 'signet-ring sign' on HRCT chest (dilated bronchus larger than its accompanying pulmonary artery) is diagnostic of bronchiectasis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Oral corticosteroids are best introduced in the treatment of chronic bronchial asthma when it is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oral corticosteroids are reserved for Step 5 / very severe persistent asthma uncontrolled on high-dose ICS-LABA.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: An 18-year old male has insu lin dependent diabetes, with malabsorption syndrome and bilateral upper lobe bronchiectasis. A diagnostic work-up will include all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Insulin-dependent diabetes, pancreatic malabsorption, and bilateral upper-lobe bronchiectasis in an 18-year-old indicate cystic fibrosis; workup includes faecal fat, CT chest, and CFTR DNA sequencing (lung biopsy is unnecessary).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following antigens is commonly associated with causation of Farmer’s lung?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Farmer's lung (hypersensitivity pneumonitis) is caused by inhalation of thermophilic actinomycetes (Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula) in mouldy hay.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The Gene X-pert test used for MTB detection has the additional advantage of detection of which of the following?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Xpert MTB/RIF (GeneXpert) simultaneously detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA and rpoB gene mutations conferring rifampicin resistance.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common cause of chronic type II respiratory failure is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Severe COPD is the single most common cause of chronic Type II (hypercapnic) respiratory failure.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The most frequent symptom in respiratory diseases is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cough is the most frequent presenting symptom across respiratory diseases.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 26-year old young lady attends medical emergenc y and is labelled as acute severe asthma by the emergency physician. Which one of the following is unlikely to be a part of the prescription?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oral leukotriene receptor antagonists (anti-leukotrienes) have no role in emergency management of acute severe asthma (unlike albuterol, magnesium sulfate, and aminophylline).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to respiratory examination:
1. Change in note, when patient phonate s “EEE” (Egophony) is characteristic of interstitial fibrosis
2. Whispered pectoriloquy is characteristic of lung consolidation
3. Monophonic wheeze is characteristic of asthma
4. Hyper-resonant note on percussion is characteristic of pnemothorax
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Whispered pectoriloquy characterizes lung consolidation (2) and hyperresonance characterizes pneumothorax (4) (egophony occurs above pleural effusion/consolidation, and wheeze in asthma is polyphonic).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are the causes of exudative Pleural Effusion, EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction elevates hydrostatic pressure and causes a transudative (or chylous) pleural effusion, whereas fungal infection, SLE, and Meigs' syndrome cause exudates.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT true about Ghrelin?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ghrelin (secreted by gastric fundus during fasting) stimulates appetite, increases gastric acid secretion, and accelerates (not decreases) gastric emptying.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Fecal elastase test is used for diagnosing which one of the following conditions?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Faecal elastase-1 is a sensitive non-invasive test for exocrine pancreatic insufficiency/dysfunction.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The recent classification system for listing a patient as a candidate for liver transplantation is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score prioritizes candidates for liver transplantation based on 3-month mortality risk.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The blood supply of liver consists of:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The liver receives ~75–80% of its blood supply from the portal vein and ~20–25% from the hepatic artery.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following conditions are associated with Glomerulonephritis with low complement level, EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: IgA nephropathy is typically normocomplementaemic, unlike SBE, SLE, and cryoglobulinaemia which consume complement.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to oral aphthous ulcers:
1. They are superficial and painful
2. They may occur in women just prior to menstruation
3. Oral glucocorticoids may be needed for the treatment of severe, recurrent cases
4. They are pre-malignant and progress over fe w years to squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Recurrent oral aphthous ulcers are superficial and painful (1), often flare premenstrually (2), and severe cases respond to oral glucocorticoids (3); they are benign and not premalignant.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements about Barrett’s Oesophagus is NOT correct?
options: Normal squamous cells lining the lower oesophagus are replaced by columnar cells
Normal columnar cells lining the lowe r oesophagus are replaced by squamous cells
It is an adaptive response to chronic gastro-oesophageal reflux
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2020 Answer Key: Option (c) — Normal columnar cells lining the lowe r oesophagus are replaced by squamous cells.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common cause of acute hepatitis outbreaks in India is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hepatitis A (alongside HEV; official key marks Hepatitis A) is a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis outbreaks in India.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Spontaneous oesophageal perforation after a bout of forceful vomiting or retching is characteristically seen in which one of the following conditions?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Boerhaave's syndrome is spontaneous transmural oesophageal perforation caused by a sudden rise in intraoesophageal pressure during forceful vomiting.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Eradication of helicobact er pylori infection may prove be neficial in the following extragastric disorders EXCEPT:
options: Iron deficiency anaemia without gastro-intestinal bleeding
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: H. pylori eradication benefits unexplained B12 deficiency, ITP, and unexplained iron-deficiency anaemia, but has no role in acute glomerulonephritis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the target blood Hemoglobin level wh en treating anaemia in Stage-4 chronic kidney disease patient?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In CKD Stage 4 anaemia treated with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, the target haemoglobin is 10–12 g/dL (higher targets increase cardiovascular/thrombotic risk).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following complications of ch ronic kidney disease is observed in patients with low parathyroid hormone levels?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Adynamic bone disease (low bone turnover) occurs in CKD patients with oversuppressed/low parathyroid hormone levels.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following statements about adult polycystic kidney disease are true, EXCEPT:
options: It is inherited as autosomal dominant trait
It is usually associated with marked proteinuria
It is usually associated with systematic hypertension, from young age
It is associated with Berry aneurysm
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: ADPKD is autosomal dominant, causes early hypertension, and associates with cerebral berry aneurysms, but rarely causes marked/nephrotic-range proteinuria.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements in relation to an adult patient:
1. Oliguria is defined as passage of urine less than 300 ml per day
2. Anuria is said to exist when less than 50 ml urine is passed per day
3. Polyuria is defined as urine volume in excess of 3 litre per day
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Anuria is urine output < 50–100 mL/day (2) and polyuria is > 3 L/day (3) (oliguria is < 400 mL/day, not 300 mL).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: White cell casts in urine examination are strongly suggestive of:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: White blood cell (WBC) casts on urine microscopy localize inflammation to the renal parenchyma and strongly indicate acute pyelonephritis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 13-year old boy presents with hematuria, ol iguria, edema and hypertension. He has history of sore throat two weeks prio r to presentation. Laboratory inve stigations are remarkable for low C3 and increased titres of ASO and antiDNase. Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about management for this condition?
options: Renal biopsy is rarely required for making diagnosis
Antibiotic treatment is given for streptococcal infection
Immunosuppressants are to be used for crescentic glomerulonephritis
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis after sore throat with low C3 and high ASO/anti-DNase is largely self-limiting and managed supportively (immunosuppressants are not used unless rapidly progressive crescentic GN develops).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the risk factors for nephrolithiasis?
options: Higher animal protein intake increases risk
Higher dietary potassium intake lowers risk
Lower urine citrate increases the risk
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Higher dietary calcium actually decreases nephrolithiasis risk by binding dietary oxalate in the gut (low-calcium diets increase stone risk).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 60-year old patient is admitted in emergency with seizure, aphasia and altered sensorium. He has history of fever and headache for the preceding 3 days. The CSF examination is unremarkable. What would be the probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fever, headache, seizures, aphasia, and altered sensorium with an unremarkable initial CSF or mild lymphocytosis point to viral (e.g., HSV) encephalitis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Drug of choice for the treatment of Trigeminal Neuralgia is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Carbamazepine (or oxcarbazepine) is the first-line drug of choice for trigeminal neuralgia.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Constructional skills is a function of which lobe?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Visuospatial and constructional skills (e.g., clock drawing, copying figures) are primarily functions of the non-dominant (right) parietal lobe.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Vertical gaze palsy with convergence retraction nystagmus is seen in:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Parinaud's dorsal midbrain syndrome features upward vertical gaze palsy, convergence-retraction nystagmus, and light-near pupillary dissociation.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient on looking forward was found to ha ve his right eye deviated downwards and outwards with pupil dilated. He is suffering from:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Downward-and-outward eye deviation with a dilated unreactive pupil indicates a complete right third cranial nerve (oculomotor) palsy.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are features of Cauda Equina syndrome EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cauda equina syndrome is a lower motor neuron lesion causing low back pain, lower-limb areflexia, and bladder/bowel dysfunction, not an extensor plantar (Babinski) response.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 68-year old male presented in OPD with co mplaints of progressive small handwriting. On examination, he had resting tremor, bradykines ia, rigidity and postu ral instability. This patient is suffering most likely from:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Micrographia (progressive small handwriting), resting tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity, and postural instability are classic for Parkinson's disease.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: An elderly patient presents with abnormal gait. He has a wide base freezing gait with imbalance, comprising short strides, shuffling along the floor and difficulty with starts and turns. Heal-Shin test is normal. Which one of the following is most likely disorder?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wide-based freezing gait with short shuffling strides, start/turn hesitation, and preserved heel-shin coordination ('lower-body parkinsonism') is characteristic of frontal gait disorder (normal pressure hydrocephalus / vascular).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Cushing reflex, seen in conditions of raised intra cranial pressure includes all of the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cushing's triad/reflex of raised intracranial pressure comprises hypertension (widening pulse pressure), bradycardia, and irregular respiration (not hypothermia).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 35 year old man presents with history of low grade fever and headache for last five weeks. Clinical examination is remarkable for signs of meningismus. He undergoes lumbar puncture (LP) and a day later reports worsening of head ache. Which one of the following features is NOT consistent with diagnosis of “Post-LP” headache?
options: Post-LP headache usually begins within 48 hours
Post-LP headache worsens in sitting position
Post-LP headache is most severe upon waking up
Post-LP headache may improve with caffeine intake
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Post-LP headache is postural—relieved by lying flat (so it is least, not most, severe upon waking up in bed) and worsens upon sitting or standing.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following investigations is NOT appropriate in a case of recurrent thrombosis?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: BCR-ABL testing diagnoses CML and is not part of a thrombophilia workup for recurrent thrombosis (unlike APLA, protein C/S, and antithrombin).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are causes of reactive thrombocytosis, EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Megaloblastic anaemia causes ineffective thrombopoiesis and thrombocytopenia, whereas haemolytic anaemia, post-splenectomy, and chronic inflammation cause reactive thrombocytosis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Cryoprecipitate cannot be used for treatment of which one of the following conditions?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cryoprecipitate contains Factor VIII, vWF, fibrinogen, and Factor XIII, so it cannot treat Haemophilia B (Factor IX deficiency).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Pyruvate kinase deficiency results in deficiency of ATP production and a chronic haemolytic anaemia. The disorder is inherited as an:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pyruvate kinase deficiency is the commonest glycolytic enzyme defect causing chronic haemolytic anaemia and is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Sickle cell disease may be associated with any of the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sickle cell disease causes acute chest syndrome, parvovirus B19 aplastic crisis, and splenic sequestration crisis, but has no association with Conn's syndrome (primary hyperaldosteronism).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Fever with splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy can be seen in
options: Both infectious mononucleosis and chronic leukaemia
Neither infectious mononucleosis nor chronic leukaemia
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fever with splenomegaly and generalized lymphadenopathy can be seen in both infectious mononucleosis and chronic leukaemia (e.g., CLL).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Every individual carries four alpha gene al leles. Deletion of three alleles leads to development of:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Deletion of 3 of the 4 α-globin genes (--/-α) produces Haemoglobin H (β4 tetramer) disease.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT true regarding Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia (CML)?
options: It is a clonal malignancy of haematopoetic stem
Risk of developing CML is increased in monozygotic turns
CML is defined by presence of BCR-ABL 1 fusion gene
10 year survival with TKI therapy is 85%
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: CML is an acquired somatic clonal stem cell disorder (Philadelphia chromosome); monozygotic twins of CML patients do not carry an increased inherited risk.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Diagnostic criteria of multiple myeloma includes which of the following?
1. Increased malignant plasma cells in the bone marrow
2. Serum and/or urinary M protein
3. Skeletal lytic lesions
4. Skeletal blastic lesions
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Multiple myeloma diagnosis requires clonal bone marrow plasma cells (1), serum/urine M-protein (2), and myeloma-defining events such as osteolytic (not osteoblastic) bone lesions (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The most predominant type of serum immunoglobu lin involved in patients with plasma cell disorder is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: IgG is the most common monoclonal paraprotein (~55–60%) in multiple myeloma and plasma cell dyscrasias.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT true regarding the thyroid function/disorder in pregnancy?
options: There is an increase in the metabolism of thyroxine by placenta
Hyperemesis gravidarum may be associated with thyrotoxicosis in pregnancy
Levothyroxine replacement therapy dose s hould be decreased by 30–50% early in pregnancy
Impaired cognitive impairment may be seen in the offspring of mother with subclinical hypothyroidism
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2020 Answer Key: Option (c) — Levothyroxine replacement therapy dose s hould be decreased by 30–50% early in pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT the criterion for the diagnosis of Diabetes mellitus?
options: Symptoms of diabetes and random plasma sugar concentration ≥ 200 mg/dL
2-hours plasma glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL during an oral glucose tolerance test
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: ADA diagnostic criteria for diabetes mellitus require fasting plasma glucose ≥ 126 mg/dL (not ≥ 110 mg/dL), 2-hr OGTT ≥ 200 mg/dL, HbA1c ≥ 6.5%, or symptoms + random glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A young lady presents in outdoor clinic with co mplaints of menstrual irregularity, weight gain, hair loss, tiredness and weakness. What will be the investigation of choice?
options: Free T3 and free T4 level
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Menstrual irregularity, weight gain, hair loss, and fatigue in a young woman suggest hypothyroidism; serum TSH and free T4 are the tests of choice.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements about erectile dysfunction in diabetic males:
1. It affects 60 % of males
2. Its common cause is an underlying neuro-vascular pathology
3. It may be aggravated by beta-adrenergic agonist drugs
4. Endocrine disorders like hyperprolactinemia may cause it
Which of the statements given above are true?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Erectile dysfunction in diabetic men is most commonly due to neurovascular pathology (2) and can also result from endocrine causes such as hyperprolactinaemia (4).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following can cause Hyperprolactinemia, EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Craniopharyngioma (stalk compression), stress, and chronic renal failure (and hypothyroidism, not hyperthyroidism) cause hyperprolactinaemia.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following can be seen in a case of thyrotoxicosis, EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Thyrotoxicosis causes atrial fibrillation, thyrotoxic periodic paralysis, and osteoporosis, whereas deafness is associated with congenital hypothyroidism (Pendred syndrome).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following hormones acts via the receptor tyrosine kinase?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: IGF-1 (and insulin) signals through a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase (whereas FSH, TSH, and PTH act via G-protein-coupled receptors).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following disorders as constituent of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2a (MEN 2a):
1. Primary Hyperparathyroidism
2. Pituitary tumours
3. Medullary carcinoma of thyroid
4. Pheochromocytoma
Which of the above are correct?:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: MEN 2A comprises medullary thyroid carcinoma (3), phaeochromocytoma (4), and primary hyperparathyroidism (1) (pituitary tumours belong to MEN 1).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to Graves’ ophthalmopathy :
1. Proptosis is often asymmetric and can even appear to be unilateral
2. It is a clinical diagnosis
3. Worsening of symptoms upon glucocorticoid withdrawal is common
4. Radiation therapy is very effective in treatment
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Graves' ophthalmopathy often presents with asymmetric proptosis (1), is a clinical diagnosis (2), and tends to flare upon steroid withdrawal (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are common aetiologies of delirium EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, and hyperparathyroidism (hypercalcaemia) are classic metabolic causes of delirium, unlike hypoparathyroidism.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Key anthropometric measurements important for evaluating the degree of obesity are:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Weight, height (for BMI), and waist circumference (for central adiposity) are the key anthropometric measures for assessing obesity.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the minimum BMI (Body Mass Index) recommended for considering adjuvant pharmacologic treatment in obesity with comorbidity?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pharmacotherapy for obesity is recommended at BMI ≥ 30 kg/m², or BMI ≥ 27 kg/m² in the presence of obesity-related comorbidities (e.g., T2DM, hypertension).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A young medical student while work ing in HIV ward got pricked accidently on the finger by a syringe needle which was used to draw blood from a patient. Patient’s infection status is not known. Which one of the following therapeutic interv entions will be the best interest of this student?
options: To wash wound with soap and water and start Emtricitabine
To give Dolutegravir + Tenofovir + Emtricitabine + HBV Immunoglobulin
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: After a needlestick injury from a source of unknown status, immediate 3-drug HIV PEP (tenofovir + emtricitabine + dolutegravir) plus HBV immunoglobulin/vaccine prophylaxis (if unvaccinated) protects against both HIV and HBV.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Cryptococcal infection is acquired through:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans/gattii infection is acquired by inhaling aerosolized basidiospores/yeast from pigeon droppings or soil.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT appropriate treatment for Echinococcus granulosus and hydatid disease?
options: Albendazole 400 mg twice in a day for 3 months
Diethylcarbamazine 2 mg/kg thrice in a day for 12 days
PAIR (percutaneous puncture, aspiration, injection of scolicide, reaspiration)
Praziquantel (20 mg/kg twice daily for 14 days)
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) is used for filariasis and has no activity against Echinococcus granulosus (hydatid disease, treated with albendazole, PAIR, or praziquantel).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following inf ections is NOT amenable to post-exposure prophylaxis with specific immunoglobulins?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Specific hyperimmune globulins exist for HBV, tetanus, and rabies PEP, whereas HIV PEP relies strictly on antiretroviral drugs (no immunoglobulin).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Echinocandins are a class of:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Echinocandins (caspofungin, micafungin, anidulafungin) are parenteral antifungal agents that inhibit fungal β-(1,3)-D-glucan synthase.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Recommended first time drug for initial treatment of tuberculosis include all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: First-line anti-TB drugs are isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol; ethionamide is a second-line drug.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The most frequent adverse reaction of significance among people treated for drug-susceptible tuberculosis is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Drug-induced hepatotoxicity (hepatitis) is the most frequent clinically significant adverse effect of first-line ATT (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All adult patients in whom anti-tubercular trea tment is being started should undergo baseline assessment of:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Baseline liver function tests (LFTs) are mandatory before starting hepatotoxic first-line anti-tubercular therapy in adults.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 30 year old male presents with fever, headache, anorexia, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea. On examination tongue is coated with abdom inal tenderness, soft splenomegaly, relative bradycardia and rose spots rash. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Step-ladder fever, headache, coated tongue, abdominal tenderness, soft splenomegaly, relative bradycardia (Faget's sign), and rose spots are classic for enteric fever.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The extrapulmonary sites most commonly involved in tuberculosis are all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lymph nodes, genitourinary tract, and spine/skeletal sites are common extrapulmonary TB sites, whereas calvarial/skull TB is exceedingly rare.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a clinical feature of Botulism?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Botulism causes symmetric descending flaccid paralysis with bulbar palsies (diplopia, ptosis, dysphagia) while characteristically preserving mental alertness.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Post exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for HIV should contain:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Standard HIV post-exposure prophylaxis consists of a 3-drug antiretroviral regimen administered for 28 days (4 weeks).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Paralytic rabies is characterized by:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Paralytic ('dumb') rabies presents with ascending flaccid muscle weakness and paralysis resembling Guillain-Barré syndrome, in contrast to furious rabies.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are seen in Marasmus EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Marasmus is severe energy-protein deficit characterized by extreme muscle and subcutaneous fat wasting (low MUAC, triceps skinfold, and BMI), whereas severe hypoalbuminaemia/oedema from protein deficiency is characteristic of kwashiorkor.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 20 year young lady presents with high grade feve r for five days and palpable purpura over extremities. She is found to be confused, with presence of neck stiffness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: High-grade fever, confusion, neck stiffness, and palpable purpura over the extremities in a young adult are classic for acute meningococcaemia (Neisseria meningitidis).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 (FGF 23) is increased in which one of the following conditions?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In chronic kidney disease and renal osteodystrophy, phosphate retention drives markedly elevated Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 (FGF-23) levels to promote phosphaturia.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following crystals are deposited in a case of pseudogout?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pseudogout (chondrocalcinosis) is caused by intra-articular deposition of positively birefringent, rhomboid calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystals.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following features are associat ed with poor prognosis in Diffuse Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis?
1. Older age
2. A high gas transfer factor for carbon monoxide (TLCO)
3. Proteinuria
4. Diffuse skin disease
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Poor prognostic indicators in diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis include older age at onset, extensive diffuse skin thickening, and renal involvement (proteinuria), whereas a low (not high) TLCO/DLCO predicts poor outcome.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements regarding pegloticase are correct?
1. It is enzyme conjugate
2. It is useful in chronic Gout management
3. The main adverse effects are infusion reactions and development of antibodies
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pegloticase is a PEGylated recombinant uricase enzyme conjugate used for refractory chronic tophaceous gout; its major limitations are infusion reactions and anti-drug antibody formation.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common cause of sensorineural hearing loss in adults is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Presbycusis (age-related bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss) is the most common cause of sensorineural hearing loss in adults.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 50-year old male presents with dizziness. Which one of the following clinical findings does NOT favour a central cause?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Suppression (inhibition) of nystagmus by visual fixation is characteristic of a peripheral vestibular lesion, whereas central vertigo shows poor saccades, gaze-evoked nystagmus, and brainstem signs (diplopia/dysarthria).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A young primigravida with 11 weeks pregnanc y presents with sudden onset pain and swelling of left lower limb. Homan’s sign is positive. Duplex ultrasonogram shows noncompressibility of veins in the affected regi on, with absent flow. The drug of choice for treatment is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute deep vein thrombosis in early pregnancy (11 weeks) is treated with low-molecular-weight heparin (enoxaparin), which does not cross the placenta (unlike teratogenic warfarin).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are clinical features of hypovolaemic shock EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypovolaemic shock presents with hypotension, oliguria, cold clammy skin, and compensatory tachycardia—not bradycardia.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is most appropriate to describe classic heat stroke?
options: Patients core body temperature rises above 44°C with head ache, nausea and loss of consciousness
Patients core body temperature rises above 40 °C with muscle tremors, confusion, loss of consciousness and loss of sweating
Patients core body temperature rises a bove 38 °C with in creased sweating, tachypnoea, tachycardia and loss of consciousness
Patients core body temperature is above 40 °C with disori entation, increased sweating, peripheral vasodilation, tachycardia and loss of consciousness
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2020 Answer Key: Option (b) — Patients core body temperature rises above 40 °C with muscle tremors, confusion, loss of consciousness and loss of sweating.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a priority in th e initial management of shock from venomous snake?
options: All of these are undertaken simultaneously
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Initial priority in shock from venomous snakebite is aggressive IV fluid resuscitation and anti-snake venom (ASV) administration; vasopressors are reserved only for fluid-refractory shock.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT an appropriate criterion for diagnosis of Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS)?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: SIRS criteria include temperature >38°C or <36°C, heart rate >90/min, respiratory rate >20/min (or PaCO2 <32 mmHg), and WBC >12×10⁹/L or <4×10⁹/L (not >16×10⁹/L).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following predispose to Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute pancreatitis, toxic gas inhalation, and gastric acid aspiration are classic triggers of ARDS, whereas severe bronchial asthma causes bronchospasm and hyperinflation rather than ARDS.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: An 8 year old child has consumed a few tablets of a drug that were being taken by his mother on a regular basis. Following this the child develops gastric necros is, acidosis, shock and hepatic necrosis. Which is the most likely drug?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Accidental ingestion of maternal iron tablets in a child causes corrosive haemorrhagic gastric necrosis, high anion-gap metabolic acidosis, shock, and hepatic necrosis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A newborn weighing 1.5 kg at bi rth presents at 6 hours of ag e with lethargy, weak and high pitched cry and difficulty in feeding. What is the next step in management?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A low-birth-weight neonate (1.5 kg) presenting at 6 hours with lethargy, weak high-pitched cry, and poor feeding must be immediately evaluated for hypoglycaemia by checking blood glucose.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: In a child with acute organophosphorus poisoning, which one of the following drugs will act as anti-sialogogue and peripheral parasympatholytic agent?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In organophosphate poisoning, atropine acts as a competitive muscarinic antagonist (antisialogogue and peripheral parasympatholytic) to reverse bronchorrhoea and bradycardia.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 6-year old child needs to undergo a central Ca theter placement for to tal parental nutrition. The procedure is likely to evoke pain and anxiety. Which of the following is the most appropriate drug for sedation and analgesia in this child?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ketamine provides dissociative anaesthesia, potent analgesia, and sedation while preserving airway reflexes and haemodynamic stability for painful paediatric procedures.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the drug of choice in a child presenting with supraventricular tachycardia?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Intravenous adenosine (rapid bolus) is the first-line drug of choice to terminate supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) in children.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following drugs is used in cardiopulmonary resusc itation for pulseless ventricular fibrillation?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In shock-refractory pulseless ventricular fibrillation/tachycardia during cardiopulmonary resuscitation, intravenous amiodarone is the preferred antiarrhythmic drug.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is a sign of good attachment during breastfeeding?
options: The baby’s nose is at the level of the nipple
The baby’s chin touches the breast
Most of the nipple is in the mouth and the lower areola is visible
The baby’s lower lip is inverted
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The four signs of good attachment during breastfeeding are: baby's chin touches the breast, mouth is wide open, lower lip is everted (turned outward), and more areola is visible above than below.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following signs is NOT in cluded as an indicator of a vigorous baby immediately after delivery of an infant born through meconium strained liquor?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under NRP guidelines, a vigorous newborn after meconium-stained liquor is defined by three criteria: strong respiratory efforts, good muscle tone, and heart rate >100/min (pink colour is not included).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: All are true for a Cephalohematoma in a newborn EXCEPT:
options: It is located over the parietal bones in the subcutaneous plane
It may be associated with hyperbilirubinemia
It increases in size in the first 12–24 hours
It can take 3–6 weeks to resolve
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A cephalhaematoma is a subperiosteal (not subcutaneous) haemorrhage bounded by suture lines over the parietal bone that can worsen hyperbilirubinaemia and resolve over 3–6 weeks.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following sick neonates can be started on “Minimal Enteral Feeding”, if hemodynamically stable?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Minimal enteral (trophic) feeding can be safely initiated in haemodynamically stable neonates on mechanical ventilation, whereas NEC, septic shock/sclerema, and symptomatic hypoglycaemia are contraindications.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following drugs is contraindi cated in a mother w ho is breastfeeding her infant?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Bromocriptine (a dopamine agonist) suppresses prolactin secretion and lactation and is contraindicated in breastfeeding mothers.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text:
A term neonate presents with tachypnea on day 1 after birth. The chest X-ray reveals hyperexpanded lung fields, prominent vascular markings, and prominent interlobar fissure.
Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Early-onset tachypnoea on day 1 in a term neonate with hyperinflated lungs, prominent perihilar vascular markings, and fluid in the interlobar fissure on chest X-ray is classic for transient tachypnoea of the newborn (TTN).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A pre-school boy can go upstairs on alternate feet and has also started copying a circle. How many blocks should he be able to build a tower with, without toppling over?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Going upstairs using alternate feet and copying a circle are 3-year (36-month) developmental milestones, at which age a child can build a tower of 9–10 blocks.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following drugs is the antidote for benzodiazepine poisoning?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Flumazenil is a competitive GABA-A benzodiazepine receptor antagonist used as the specific antidote for benzodiazepine overdose.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 3-year old child develops seve re respiratory distress after i nhalation of fumes arising from burning plastic. The child is started on supporti ve ventilation. Which one of the following antidotes needs to be given?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Burning plastics release hydrogen cyanide gas; hydroxocobalamin (Vitamin B12a) binds cyanide to form non-toxic cyanocobalamin and is the preferred antidote in smoke inhalation.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A child has an incurving of the little finger. What is this condition known as?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Clinodactyly is permanent radial/medial curvature (incurving) of the fifth (little) finger, commonly seen in Down syndrome.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 4-week old infant presents with repeated episodes of non-bilious vomiting since 7 days. The infant seems active and hungry after the vo miting. Examination reveals an olive-shaped mass in the epigartrium. Which metabolic abnormality is expected in this infant?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Projectile non-bilious vomiting with a palpable epigastric 'olive' mass in a 4-week-old infant indicates hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, which causes hypochloraemic, hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the correct dose and route of administration of hepatitis B vaccine in children?
options: 0.5 mL dose with 10 microgram of antigen subcutaneously
0.5 mL dose with 10 microgram of antigen intramuscularly
1 mL dose with 5 microgram of antigen subcutaneously
1 mL dose with 5 microgram of antigen intramuscularly
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under India's Universal Immunization Programme, the paediatric dose of Hepatitis B vaccine is 0.5 mL (containing 10 µg HBsAg) given intramuscularly in the anterolateral thigh.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is correct for approved acellular pertussis vaccine?
options: It contains at least 3 IU of inactivated pertussis toxin
It contains at least 3 pathogenic pertussis antigens
It’s efficacy is superior to the whole cell pertussis vaccine
Presence of nonfimbrial protein is a mandatory component
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Approved acellular pertussis (aP) vaccines contain at least 3 purified pertussis antigens (pertussis toxin, filamentous haemagglutinin, and pertactin/fimbriae).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is recommended in the fo llow up health visits of a child with Down syndrome?
options: Growth assessment twice a year in the first year and annually till 5 years
Annual auditory screening from 1 to 5 years
Screening for refractory error if visual impairment is suspected
Annual thyroid function test from birth to 2 years
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2020 Answer Key: Option (a) — Growth assessment twice a year in the first year and annually till 5 years.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: A 12 year old child presents with delayed puberty and delayed bone age. His growth records reveal that he was growing normally till 1 year of age, after which both his height and weight fell to below the third centile for age. Subse quently, he continued to grow below the third centile with normal height velocity. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Normal growth until age 1 followed by height/weight dropping below the 3rd centile with normal subsequent growth velocity, delayed bone age, and delayed puberty is classic for constitutional growth delay.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: According to the ‘Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhoo d Illnesses’ (IMNCI) classification of young infants upto 2 months, which one of the following signs is NOT included in ‘Possible Serious Bacterial Infection’
options: Fast breathing (50 breaths or more per minute)
Movement only when stimulated or no movement at all
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under IMNCI for infants <2 months, 'Possible Serious Bacterial Infection' includes fast breathing (≥60 breaths/min, not ≥50), severe chest indrawing, fever/hypothermia, and lethargy/reduced movement.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Neonatal tetanus elimination in India is defined as less than one case per:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Maternal and neonatal tetanus elimination is defined as fewer than 1 case of neonatal tetanus per 1,000 live births per year in every district.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following faciliti es has been established at di strict hospitals in India to strengthen the care of low birth weight babies and sick newborns?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Special Newborn Care Units (SNCUs) have been established at district hospitals across India to provide level-II neonatal intensive care for sick and low-birth-weight newborns.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Indications for fasciotomy in compartment syndrome include all EXCEPT:
options: Pain on passive movement of affected muscles
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Indications for fasciotomy in acute compartment syndrome include compartment pressure >30 mmHg, pain on passive stretch, and distal sensory deficits; distal pulses often remain palpable until late, so palpable pulses do not exclude it.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Necrotising Soft Tissue infections?
options: Crepitus, skin blistering and focal skin gangrene are typical presenting features
Treatment consists of wide local excision and appropriate antibiotics
Tissue biopsy is required for culture and diagnosis
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Necrotizing soft tissue infections are typically polymicrobial synergistic infections (Type I, aerobic + anaerobic), rather than solely monomicrobial, and require urgent wide surgical debridement and broad-spectrum antibiotics.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which type of surgery is laparoscopic cholecystectomy classified as?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy enters the biliary tract without gross spillage and is classified as a clean-contaminated (Class II) surgical procedure.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
