upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: A 22-year female has presented with a history of malaise, cough, alternating constipation and diarrhoea with interm ittent abdominal pain for last 6 months. She also complains of abdominal distension for last 2 days. On examination he r abdomen has a doughy feel along with an ill defined mass over the right lower quadrant. She is most likely suffering from:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chronic malaise, alternating bowel habits, abdominal distension, a 'doughy' abdomen, and an ill-defined right lower quadrant mass in a young Indian female are classic for ileocaecal tuberculosis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding needle stick injuries:
1. Injured part should be washed under running water
2. Dominant index finger is the commonest site for needle stick injury
3. All needle stick injuries should be reported
4. Hepatitis/HIV testing should be done after needle stick injury
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Immediate management of a needle-stick injury includes washing with soap and running water, reporting the incident, and baseline/follow-up HIV and Hepatitis B/C testing (the non-dominant index finger is the commonest site).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding claudication:
1. It is a marker for silent coronary disease
2. Structured exercise program ( 2 hours per week for 3 months) leads to improvement in symptoms
3. Diabetes mellitus increases the risk and severity of claudication
4. Beta blockers may exacerbate claudication
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intermittent claudication is a marker of systemic atherosclerosis (silent CAD); diabetes worsens it, non-selective beta-blockers can exacerbate it, and a supervised 3-month exercise programme significantly improves walking distance.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: A 50-year old lady underwent uneventful bariatri c surgery for morbid obesity. On the third post operative day, she develops breathless an d pulmonary embolism is suspected. The next investigation to confirm the diagnosis will be:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is the gold-standard confirmatory imaging modality for suspected postoperative pulmonary embolism.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Medical management of thyrotoxic crisis includes all of the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Management of thyroid storm (thyrotoxic crisis) includes IV fluids, beta-blockers (propranolol), antithyroid drugs, iodine, and IV hydrocortisone; IV antibiotics are not a routine component unless infection precipitated the storm.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: A patient operated for a paro tid gland tumour developed symptoms of sweating and erytherma (flushing) over the region of su rgical excision while eating. The probable diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Gustatory sweating and flushing over the parotid region while eating after parotidectomy is Frey's syndrome (auriculotemporal nerve aberrant regeneration).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: First line hormone therapy for post-menopausal woman with metastatic carcinoma breast is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Aromatase inhibitors such as anastrozole or letrozole are the first-line endocrine therapy for postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are major subtypes of breast cancer based on Gene array analysis EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Molecular classification of breast cancer by gene expression profiling defines four major subtypes: Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-enriched, and Basal-like (triple-negative)—not simply 'oestrogen receptor positive'.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are sequelae of peptic ulcer surgery EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Post-gastrectomy/peptic ulcer surgery sequelae include dumping syndrome, bile reflux (bilious vomiting), and post-vagotomy diarrhoea, whereas early satiety and reduced (not increased) appetite occur.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) score for quantif ying the severity of chronic liver disease includes all variables EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) score uses five variables: serum bilirubin, serum albumin, INR (prothrombin time), ascites, and hepatic encephalopathy—serum creatinine is used in MELD, not CTP.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: ‘Chain of Lakes’ appearance due to sacculation with intervening short strictures of pancreatic duct is seen on:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Alternating pancreatic ductal strictures and saccular dilatations ('chain of lakes' appearance) on ERCP or MRCP are pathognomonic of chronic pancreatitis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Pyogenic Liver Abscess?
options: Anorexia, fever, malaise and right uppe r quadrant abdominal discomfort are the most common presenting features
It is more common in elderly, diabetics and immunocompromised patients
Treatment is with oral antibiotics alone
Streptococcus milleri and escherichia coli are the most common causative organisms
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pyogenic liver abscess requires prolonged intravenous antibiotics combined with percutaneous aspiration or catheter drainage—oral antibiotics alone are inadequate.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: ‘Swiss cheese defects’ are seen during laparoscopic repair of:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Multiple small fascial defects ('Swiss-cheese defects') along a previous laparotomy scar are classically encountered during laparoscopic ventral/incisional hernia repair.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are correct regarding splenic artery aneurysm?
1. Main arterial trunk is the common site
2. Palpable thrill can be felt
3. It is symptomless unless it ruptures
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Splenic artery aneurysms most commonly involve the main arterial trunk and are typically asymptomatic until rupture (a thrill is rarely palpable).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Valentino’s syndrome is:
options: Pain on per-vaginal examination in pelvic abscess
Pain over left shoulder in left hypochondriac collection
Pain over left groin in perirenal collection
Pain in right iliac fossa in perforated peptic ulcer
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Valentino's syndrome refers to right iliac fossa pain caused by gastric/duodenal fluid tracking down the right paracolic gutter from a perforated peptic ulcer, mimicking acute appendicitis.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis occurs due to:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) is an acute bacterial infection of pre-existing ascitic fluid (typically in cirrhosis) without an identifiable intra-abdominal surgical source.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Structure not forming boundaries of the “Tri angle of doom” seen during laparoscopic inguinal hernia surgery dissection is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair, the 'triangle of doom' is bounded medially by the vas deferens, laterally by the gonadal/spermatic vessels, and inferiorly by the peritoneal reflection (containing external iliac vessels); the inferior epigastric artery lies superiorly.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The term mid-line shift is associated with:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Midline shift on CT brain is a radiological hallmark of raised intracranial pressure and mass effect following head injury.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following cranial nerves does NOT supply to the external ear?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sensory innervation of the external ear comes from CN V (auriculotemporal), CN VII, CN IX, CN X (Arnold's nerve), and C2–C3; CN VI (abducens) is purely motor to the lateral rectus.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Left Internal Mammary Artery (LIMA) has b ecome the conduit of choice for Left Anterior Descending (LAD) artery during coronary artery bypass grafting because:
options: Long term patency rates are more than 98%
Atherosclerosis is never seen in this vessel
It is very easy to harvest
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The left internal mammary artery (LIMA) is the conduit of choice for the LAD because it resists atherosclerosis and achieves >90–98% 10-year patency rates.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: A 50-year old male with significant smoking hi story presented in the surgical emergency with sudden severe breathlessness. Chest X-ray shows right side d Pneumothorax. The appropriate management requires:
options: Aspiration of air with 16-18 G cannula
Right chest drain of size 8-14 Fr
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A large or symptomatic spontaneous pneumothorax in a 50-year-old smoker is treated with tube thoracostomy using a small-bore (8–14 Fr) intercostal chest drain.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regarding Felon is NOT correct?
options: There is infection of the finger tip between specialised fibrous septa
Incision and drainage is the treatment of choice
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A felon is an acute pyogenic infection of the closed pulp space of the fingertip, causing intense throbbing pain (not painless) and requiring prompt incision and drainage.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The most common site for osteosarcoma is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Osteosarcoma most commonly arises in the metaphysis of long bones around the knee, with the distal femur being the single most frequent site.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Rapid Sequence Induction is indicated in:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Rapid sequence induction (RSI) is indicated in patients with a full stomach or high aspiration risk, such as emergency surgery for intestinal obstruction.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements about Compartment Syndrome is NOT correct?
options: It is commonest in a closed fracture
Pain is on active movement but not on passive movement of muscles
Fasciotomy is the treatment of choice
Volkmann’s Ischaemic contractive is a late complication
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In acute compartment syndrome, severe pain is classically elicited by passive stretching (not merely active movement) of the ischaemic muscles.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT the strength of ultrasound as a diagnostic modality?
options: Allows dynamic studies to be done
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ultrasound is radiation-free, inexpensive, and permits dynamic real-time imaging, but it is highly operator-dependent with a steep (not short) learning curve.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements regarding lymphoedema following breast cancer treatment are correct?
1. Incidence has decreased due to rarely combined therapy of axillary LN dissection and radiotherapy
2. Precipitating cause like LN metastasis is a major determinant
3. The condition is often painful
4. Oedematous limb is susceptible to bacterial infection
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Post-mastectomy lymphoedema is often painful, predisposes the limb to recurrent cellulitis, and has declined with sentinel lymph node biopsy avoiding combined axillary dissection and radiotherapy.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a risk fact or for development of venous thrombosis in surgical patients?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Advanced age (>60 years), pregnancy, and obesity (BMI >30 kg/m²) are established risk factors for perioperative venous thromboembolism, whereas diabetes alone is not a primary VTE risk factor.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a complication of massive blood transfusion?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Massive blood transfusion causes dilutional coagulopathy, citrate-induced hypocalcaemia, hyperkalaemia, and hypothermia (from cold stored blood)—not hyperthermia.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Stage III “Pressure sore” is full thickness skin loss extending:
options: into subcutaneous tissue but not through fascia
through subcutaneous tissue into fascia and muscles
through subcutaneous tissue into fascia, muscles and bone
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A Stage III pressure ulcer involves full-thickness skin loss extending into the subcutaneous tissue down to, but not through, the underlying fascia.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: During subclavian vein puncture in a surgical ward suddenly a patie nt developed severe breathlessness. On auscultation breath sound was absent and the ipsilateral chest was tympanitic on percussion. The probable diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sudden dyspnoea with absent breath sounds and tympanitic percussion immediately after attempted subclavian central venous cannulation indicates iatrogenic pneumothorax.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Kohler’s disease is avascular necrosis of :
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Köhler's disease is idiopathic avascular necrosis (osteochondritis) of the tarsal navicular bone in young children.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT true of Pyoderma gangrenosum?
options: It is characterized by cutaneous ulceration with purple undermined edges
It is often secondary to heightened immunological reac tivity from another disease process
Cultures often show Gram positive Staphylococci
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pyoderma gangrenosum is a sterile neutrophilic dermatosis with violaceous undermined borders associated with IBD/systemic disease that responds to steroids; bacterial cultures are typically negative.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a tissue repair surgery for inguinal hernia repair?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bassini, Shouldice, and Desarda repairs are pure tissue repairs for inguinal hernia, whereas Stoppa's repair (giant prosthetic reinforcement of the visceral sac) uses a synthetic mesh.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following type of meshes is recommended for intraperitoneal use in abdominal wall hernia?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: For intraperitoneal placement (e.g., IPOM ventral hernia repair), composite/tissue-separating meshes with an anti-adhesive barrier are required to prevent bowel adhesions and fistulae.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT correct regarding MEN-1 syndrome?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: MEN-1 (Wermer syndrome) involves the '3 Ps': Parathyroid glands, Pancreatic islet tumours, and Pituitary adenomas—not the pineal gland.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT an electronic information site in surgery?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library are major online biomedical databases, whereas the National Medical Library is a physical/institutional library (or portal) rather than a primary surgical search database.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements re garding pre-conceptiona l counseling is NOT correct?
options: It is needed only in selected complicated pregnancies
It helps in early detection of risk factors
It helps in reducing maternal morbidity and mortality
It is a part of preventive medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Preconception counselling is beneficial for all women of reproductive age—not only selected complicated pregnancies—to optimize health and reduce maternal-fetal morbidity.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Non Stress Test (NST):
1. Reactive NST indicates a healthy fetus
2. NST is an observed association of fetal breathing with fetal movements
3. NST has a low false negative rate (< 1%) but high false positive rate (>50%)
4. Testing should be started at 20 weeks Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wait: for cms19-p2-042, in Rh-isoimmunized pregnancy, maternal ICT is tested (1), methergine at anterior shoulder is withheld to prevent fetomaternal haemorrhage (2), and MCA PSV Doppler accurately predicts fetal anaemia (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is a protective factor for endometrial hyperplasia?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Multiparity (multiple full-term pregnancies) reduces lifelong unopposed oestrogen exposure and is protective against endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman who is not breast feeding her newbor n child is advised to use a contraceptive method by:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In non-breastfeeding women, ovulation can return as early as 3–4 weeks postpartum, so contraception should be initiated by the 3rd postpartum week.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Pearl index for contraceptive effectiveness is calculated in terms of which of the following?
1. Pregnancy rate
2. Abortion rate
3. Hundred woman years
4. Thousand woman years
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Pearl Index measures contraceptive failure as the pregnancy rate per 100 woman-years of use.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Indications for removal of IUDs are all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Uterine perforation, acute pelvic inflammatory disease/salpingitis, and pregnancy with an IUD are indications for IUD removal, whereas normal cyclical menstrual bleeding is not.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Contraindications for insertion of IUDs are all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Suspected pregnancy, gestational trophoblastic disease, and severe dysmenorrhoea (for copper IUDs) are contraindications to IUD insertion, whereas post-placental insertion during Caesarean section is safe and recommended.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a contraindication for use of Mini pill?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Breastfeeding is an ideal indication (not a contraindication) for the progestin-only minipill, as it does not impair lactation.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the most commonl y used surgical method/technique of female sterilization as recommended by Government of India?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Modified Pomeroy's tubal ligation is the most common and Government of India-recommended surgical method for female sterilization (minilaparotomy).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are required for a registered medical practitioner to qualify for performing Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP), as per revised rules of MTP Act?
1. Certified for assisting at least 15 MTP in an authorized centre
2. Diploma or degree in Obstetrics and Gynaecology
3. House surgeon training for 3 months in Obstetrics and Gynaecology
4. Certified training for 6 months in laparoscopic surgeries
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under India's MTP Act rules, a registered medical practitioner with a postgraduate degree or diploma in Obstetrics and Gynaecology is automatically qualified to perform MTPs.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a support of uterus, preventing its descent?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Uterine support against prolapse is provided by the endopelvic fascia, Mackenrodt's (cardinal) ligaments, and pubocervical ligaments, whereas the inguinal ligament does not support the uterus.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: As per ICMR guidelines, which one of the followi ng statements is true regarding effects of COVID-19 on fetus according to current evidence?
options: There is increased risk of early pregnancy loss
COVID-19 virus infection is an indication of MTP
There is increased risk of fetal growth restriction
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Per ICMR guidelines, SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) is not known to be teratogenic and is not an indication for medical termination of pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: As per ICMR guidelines, which one of the follo wing statements is true regarding COVID-19 infection in pregnancy?
options: Covid-19 pneumonia in pregnancy is more severe with poor recovery
Pregnant women with heart disease are at higher risk
Vaginal secretions always test positive for COVID-19 in pregnancy
COVID-19 virus is secreted in breast milk
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Per ICMR guidelines, pregnant women with underlying comorbidities such as heart disease are at higher risk of severe COVID-19 complications (SARS-CoV-2 is not routinely transmitted in breast milk or vaginal secretions).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a method of management of Deep Transverse Arrest with the living fetus?
options: Delivery by application of forceps to the unrotated head
Manual rotation and application of forceps
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Applying forceps directly to an unrotated head in deep transverse arrest causes severe maternal and fetal trauma and is contraindicated; options are Caesarean section, ventouse, or manual/Kielland rotation before forceps.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Successful version of breech presentation is likely in case all of the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A frank breech with extended legs often acts as a splint and is less likely to undergo successful external cephalic version than a complete, unengaged breech with adequate liquor.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Implantation of a fertilised ovum occurs on which day following fertilisation?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Implantation of the human blastocyst into the decidualized endometrium begins on Day 6 after fertilization.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: During total abdominal hysterectomy the ureter is likely to undergo inju ry or ligation during the following steps EXCEPT:
options: During division and ligation of the round ligaments
During division and ligation of infundibulopelvic ligaments
During division and ligation of mackenrodt’s and uterosacral ligaments
At the vaginal angles while incising the vagina to remove the cervix with the uterus
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: During total abdominal hysterectomy, the ureter is vulnerable near the infundibulopelvic ligaments, Mackenrodt's/uterosacral ligaments, and vaginal angles—not during division and ligation of the round ligaments.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The net effect of antenatal care has been the following EXCEPT:
options: Reduction in the incidence of institutional delivery
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Effective antenatal care reduces maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality and increases (not reduces) institutional deliveries.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a component of active phase in the partograph?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In the Friedman curve/partograph, the active phase comprises the acceleration phase, phase of maximum slope, and phase of deceleration; expulsion is the second stage of labour.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: From medicolegal point of view which one of the following is NOT a si gn of previous child birth?
options: Perineum is lax and there is evidence of scarring
Introitus is gaping and there is presence of carunculae myrtiformis
Abdomen is lax and loose with striae and linea alba
Conical cervix with round external os
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A conical cervix with a small, round, nulliparous external os indicates a nulliparous uterus rather than previous childbirth (parous women have a transverse slit-like os and carunculae myrtiformes).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The components of partograph are all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The WHO partograph records time, fetal heart rate, liquor colour, moulding, cervical dilatation, descent, uterine contractions, maternal pulse/BP/temperature, and urine output/ketones—not maternal respiratory rate.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following information are provided by partograph?
1. Colour of liquor
2. Uterine contractions with duration and frequency
3. Dilatation of cervix
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The partograph provides continuous documentation of liquor colour, uterine contraction frequency and duration, and cervical dilatation.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Intraoperative recognition of ureter is by which of the following features?
1. Transparent tubular appearance
2. Pale glistening appearance
3. Longitudinal vessels on surface
4. Circumferential vessels on surface
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intraoperatively, the ureter is recognized by its pale, glistening tubular appearance, peristalsis (vermicular motion), and longitudinal surface blood vessels.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Hysterosalpingography (HSG) is least helpful in detecting which of the following?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hysterosalpingography (HSG) evaluates tubal patency, intrauterine synechiae (Asherman syndrome), and Müllerian uterine anomalies, but cannot reliably visualize peritubal/pelvic adhesions (laparoscopy is required).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are characteristics of Trichomonas vaginitis?
1. Presence of greenish frothy discharge
2. Vaginal pH > 4.5
3. Presence of clue cells in microscopic examination
4. Strawberry spots on the vaginal mucosa
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis vaginitis presents with greenish-yellow frothy discharge, vaginal pH >4.5, and punctate 'strawberry' cervicovaginitis (clue cells are seen in bacterial vaginosis).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Tumor marker of epithelial ovarian carcinoma is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: CA-125 is the primary serum tumour marker for epithelial ovarian carcinoma.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The most common site of cervical cancer is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma most commonly originates at the squamocolumnar junction within the transformation zone.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The placenta synthesizes all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The placenta synthesizes oestriol (using fetal adrenal DHEA-S), CRH, and PAPP-A, but lacks 17-alpha-hydroxylase and therefore cannot synthesize dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) de novo.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Withdrawal bleeding following administration of progesterone in a case of secondary amenorrhea indicates all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A positive progesterone withdrawal bleed proves an intact outflow tract, non-pregnant state, adequate endogenous oestrogen priming, and responsive endometrium—it does not indicate a pituitary defect (rather excludes severe hypothalamic-pituitary failure).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Monilial vaginitis is commonly associated with all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Broad-spectrum antibiotics, diabetes mellitus, and pregnancy predispose to vulvovaginal candidiasis (monilial vaginitis), whereas chloroquine treatment for malaria does not.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a risk factor for the development of placenta previa?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Advanced maternal age, smoking, and prior Caesarean scar are established risk factors for placenta praevia, whereas maternal anaemia is not a causative risk factor.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Common clinical presentations of moderate to severe abruption are all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Moderate-to-severe placental abruption presents with uterine tenderness/hypertonus, fetal distress, and preterm labour, whereas prolonged labour is not a characteristic presentation.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Common trisomies resulting in spontaneous abortion are all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Trisomy 16 (most common), 18, and 21 are frequent causes of spontaneous miscarriage, whereas autosomal trisomy 1 is virtually never seen due to pre-implantation lethality.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
The initial prevention strategy for antiphospholipid syndrome will be:
1. Steroids
2. Heparin
3. Low dose aspirin
4. Progesterone support
Which of the above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Standard prophylaxis for obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) to prevent recurrent pregnancy loss is low-dose aspirin combined with prophylactic heparin (LMWH or UFH).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Diagnostic criteria for PCOD are:
1. Oligo/amenorrohoea
2. Hyperandrogenism
3. Polycystic ovaries on ultrasound
Which of the above are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the Rotterdam criteria, PCOS is diagnosed when at least two of three features are present: oligo-/anovulation, clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following symptoms can be associated with pelvic organ prolapse?
1. Difficulty in passing urine
2. Incomplete evacuation of urine
3. Urgency and frequency
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pelvic organ prolapse (especially cystocele) kinks the urethra and impairs bladder emptying, causing voiding difficulty, incomplete evacuation, urgency, and frequency.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
A 30 year old lady, P 2L2 presents with painful unilateral swelling in vulva for 3 days. Which of the following statements are true regarding the above case?
1. Bartholin’s abscess may be the likely diagnosis
2. It is to be managed by marsupialisation
3. Gonococcus is the most common pathogenic organism
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A painful unilateral vulvar swelling for 3 days suggests a Bartholin's abscess (often caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae or polymicrobial flora); acute abscesses are treated by incision and drainage or Word catheter (marsupialisation is done for cysts, though some texts also note it).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a sign of separation of placenta?
options: Uterus becomes globular, firm and ballotable
Slight bulging in the suprapubic region
Apparent lengthenic of the cord with slight gush of vaginal bleeding
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: During placental separation, the uterus becomes globular and firm, the cord lengthens, a gush of blood occurs, and the fundal height rises (not reduces) as the placenta descends into the lower segment.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following regarding examination of a rape victim:
1. Emergency pill is provided
2. Internal examination must be performed
3. HIV testing is done
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Post-rape medical care includes emergency contraception and HIV/STI testing and prophylaxis; routine forceful internal speculum/digital examination is avoided unless clinically indicated and consented.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following cardinal movements of mechanism of normal labor:
1. Engagement
2. Internal rotation
3. Flexion
4. Restitution 5. Crowning 6. External rotation What is the correct sequence of movements in labor in occipito-lateral position?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The correct sequence of cardinal movements in occipitoposterior/occipitolateral labour is: Engagement (1) → Flexion (3) → Internal rotation (2) → Crowning (5) → Restitution (4) → External rotation (6).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following represent the properties of an ideal disinfectant?
1. It is broad spectrum
2. It is fast acting
3. It is non-toxic
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An ideal disinfectant is broad-spectrum (1), fast-acting (2), and non-toxic/non-corrosive to tissues and surfaces (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following measures can help reduce the risk of systemic hypertension?
1. Reduction in dietary intake of common salt
2. Controlling weight for age
3. Increasing potassium rich foods in the diet
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Primary prevention of hypertension includes dietary salt reduction (1), maintaining healthy body weight (2), and increasing dietary potassium intake (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Keeping biological determinants in perspective, consider the following statements:
1. Presence of a normal karyotype is the first requisite for human health
2. Genetic screening can play an important role in prevention of wide spectrum of diseases
3. If an individual is allowed to live in heal thy relationship with the environment, the person’s genetic potentialities can transform into phenotypic realities
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A normal karyotype (1), genetic screening for prevention (2), and favourable gene-environment interaction (3) all underpin biological determinants of health.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: NITI Aayog has the following roles EXCEPT:
options: It provides critical directional and strategic input in the development process
It provides relevant technical advice with focus on technology upgradation
It focuses on the development of “Referral Service Complex”
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: NITI Aayog provides strategic policy direction, technical advice, and capacity building, whereas the 'Referral Service Complex' was part of the Kartar Singh/Shrivastav Committee health infrastructure model.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Poor hand hygiene of a mess worker in a univers ity college mess led to Hepatitis A cases in the hostel inmates. What type of epidemic will this exposure present with?
1. Propagated
2. Common source-continuous exposure
3. Common source-point exposure
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ongoing poor hand hygiene by a mess food handler causing sequential Hepatitis A cases among hostel inmates represents a common-source continuous-exposure epidemic.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the specificity of sputum microscopy in detection of Pulmona ry Tuberculosis (PTB) as per the information given below? PTB Total Sputum microscopy Present Absent Positive 270 20 290 Negative 30 180 210 Total 300 200 500
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Specificity = TN / (TN + FP) = 180 / 200 = 90%.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: In a cohort of 500 women attending antenatal clinic, 70 % had ultrasonography (USG). This cohort was followed up at delivery. Of the wo men who had USG, 70 delivered low birth weight (LBW) babies; whereas of the wome n, who did not undergo USG, 50 delivered LBW babies. The incidence of LBW babies among women who had USG is:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Of 500 women, 70% had USG = 350 women. Among these 350 women, 70 delivered LBW babies, giving an incidence of 70 / 350 = 20%.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Major source of vitamin K1 is:
options: Foods rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Vitamin K1 (phylloquinone) is obtained primarily from fresh dark green leafy vegetables (spinach, cabbage, kale).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a function of Epidemiology?
options: To study historically the rise and fall of disease in the population
Searching for the causes and risk factor
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Epidemiology studies disease distribution, determinants/risk factors, historical trends, and syndrome identification at the population level, whereas making an individual clinical diagnosis is clinical medicine.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a contagious disease?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Malaria is a vector-borne (Anopheles mosquito) disease and is not directly contagious from person to person, unlike scabies, trachoma, and leprosy.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: In primary immune response, how much more antigenic dose is required to induce IgG antibodies as against the induction of IgM antibodies?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a primary immune response, approximately 50 times more antigen is required to induce IgG production compared with IgM.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Pentavalent vaccine provides protection against which of the following diseases?
options: Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tuberculosis, Measles and Hepatitis B
Diphtheria, Pertussis, Measles, Hepatitis B and Hib
Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B and Rubella
Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B and Hib
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Pentavalent vaccine in India's UIP protects against Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Consider the following data for a country: Population in 0-14 years of age – 391,558,367 Population between 15–64 years of age – 856,076,200 Population above 65 years of age – 71,943,390 What shall be the dependency ratio of this country?

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regarding Rabies Immunoglobulin is NOT true?
options: It should be administered only once as s oon as possible after the initiation of post exposure prophylaxis
It should be administered all into or around the wound sites
There is no scientific ground for performing a skin test prior to administering equine immunoglobulin
It can be administered till 15 days after the first dose of anti-rabies vaccine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2020 Answer Key: Option (d) — It can be administered till 15 days after the first dose of anti-rabies vaccine.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are true about Bedaquiline (BDQ) EXCEPT:
options: It specifically targets mycobacterial ATP synthase
It has high volume of tissue distribution
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bedaquiline is a bactericidal (not bacteriostatic) diarylquinoline that inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase, with a long terminal half-life and high volume of distribution.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Visual inspection based screening test with 5 % acetic acid is used for the screening of which one of the following cancers?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Visual inspection with 5% acetic acid (VIA) is a low-cost, effective screening test for cervical cancer/precancerous lesions.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Predictive accuracy of a screening test depends on the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Positive and negative predictive values depend on disease prevalence, sensitivity, and specificity—not directly on disease incidence.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: How much of Zinc supplement is recommended by WHO and UNICEF for infants less than 6 months of age after an episode of acute diarrhoea?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO/UNICEF recommend oral zinc 10 mg/day for 10–14 days in infants < 6 months of age (and 20 mg/day for ≥6 months) during acute diarrhoea.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regard ing sequential administration of Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) and Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) is NOT correct?
options: It will be cost effective in developing countries for Polio prevention
The combined schedules of IPV and OPV appear to reduce or prevent Vaccine Associated Paralytic Polio (VAPP)
Intestinal mucosal immunity is lost due to IPV administration
IPV and OPV together may optimize both the humoral and mucosal immunogenicity of Polio vaccine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sequential IPV + OPV schedules reduce VAPP and optimize both humoral and mucosal immunity; IPV does not abolish intestinal mucosal immunity induced by OPV.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the recommended dose regimen of Vita min A for the treatment of early stages of Xerophthalmia?
options: Single massive dose of 2 lac International Units (IU)
2 lac IU on two successive days
2 doses of 1 lac IU in two successive days
2 doses of 1 lac IU at a gap of one week
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: For early xerophthalmia/Bitot's spots in children ≥1 year, WHO recommends 200,000 IU (2 lakh IU) oral Vitamin A on Day 1 and Day 2 (two successive days), plus a third dose 2–4 weeks later.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which is the most specific causative agent of Rabies?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Classical rabies is caused by Lyssavirus genotype/serotype 1 (rabies virus).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the antibiotic of choice for the preventio n of Rheumatic heart disease?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intramuscular benzathine benzylpenicillin every 3–4 weeks is the drug of choice for secondary prophylaxis of rheumatic fever/rheumatic heart disease.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are global targets for WHO Global Action Plan (2013–2020) for Prevention and Control of NCDs, EXCEPT:
options: A 10 % relative reduction in risk of premature mortality from cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes and chronic respiratory diseases
A 10 % relative reduction in prevalence of insufficient physical activity
A 10 % relative reduction in mean population intake of salt/sodium
At least 10 % relative reduction in the harmful use of alcohol
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2020 Answer Key: Option (a) — A 10 % relative reduction in risk of premature mortality from cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes and chronic respiratory diseases.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Under the Employees State Insurance (ESI) Scheme, extended sickness benefit is provided in which of the following infectious diseases?
1. Tuberculosis
2. Leprosy
3. Chronic empyema
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the ESI Scheme, Extended Sickness Benefit (up to 2 years) is granted for 34 specified long-term diseases including tuberculosis (1), leprosy (2), and chronic empyema (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: In the context of NCD prevention and control in India, the extent of relative reduction in household use of solid fuels as a primary source of energy for cooking by 2025 is targeted at:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: India's National NCD Monitoring Framework targets a 50% relative reduction in household use of solid fuels for cooking by 2025.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following criteria which may indicat e elimination of lymphatic filariasis in a community:
1. When lymphatic filariasis ceases to be a public health problem in the community
2. When the number of microfilaria carriers declines to 1.5 % within the community
3. When children born in the community after the initiation of elimination programme are free from circulating antigenaemia Which of the criteria stated above hold true?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO lymphatic filariasis elimination criteria require microfilaria prevalence < 1% (not 1.5%; 2 is false) and absence of antigenaemia in children born after MDA initiation (3), so LF ceases to be a public health problem (1).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Hold over time of cold chain equipment depends on all of the following factors EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cold chain equipment hold-over time depends on ambient temperature, icepack lining condition, and total vaccine load/thermal mass, not the specific types of vaccines stored.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements regarding Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) are correct?
1. It consolidates infant mortality, life expectancy at age one, and literacy
2. It does not measure economic growth but measures the result of economic policies
3. For each component, the performance of indi vidual countries is placed on a scale of
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: PQLI combines infant mortality, life expectancy at age 1, and literacy (1), measures social outcomes rather than economic growth (2), and scores each component on a 0–100 scale (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) include:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) equal the sum of Years of Life Lost due to premature mortality (YLL) and Years Lived with Disability (YLD).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are health care delivery indicators?
1. Population per trained birth attendant
2. Population per health/sub centre
3. Doctor-nurse ratio
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Healthcare delivery indicators include population per trained birth attendant (1), population per health/sub-centre (2), and doctor-to-nurse ratio (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following key action areas are incorporated in the Ottawa Charter?
1. Building healthy public policy
2. Strengthening community action for health
3. Reorienting health services
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The 1986 Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion defines five action areas, including building healthy public policy (1), strengthening community action (2), and reorienting health services (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Under Chapter XXI of the 10 th revision of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD-10 ), lifestyle-related problems fall under which of the following code range?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In ICD-10 Chapter XXI (Factors influencing health status), lifestyle-related problems (tobacco, alcohol, lack of exercise, diet) are coded under Z72.0–Z72.5.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following diseases are spread by airborne transmission?
1. Influenza
2. Chicken pox
3. Q-fever
4. Psittacosis
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Influenza (1), varicella/chickenpox (2), Coxiella burnetii/Q-fever (3), and Chlamydia psittaci/psittacosis (4) can all spread via airborne/aerosol transmission.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: DASH diet plan is advocated in the control of which one of the following diseases?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet is designed to prevent and control systemic hypertension.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Endemic ascitis occurs due to:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Endemic ascites in central India is caused by hepatotoxic pyrrolizidine alkaloids (naturally occurring plant toxins) from Crotalaria (Jhunjhunia) weeds contaminating millet.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The presence of which of the following bact eria in drinking water is an important confirmatory evidence of recent faecal pollution of water?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Faecal streptococci (Enterococci) confirm recent faecal contamination of drinking water (Clostridium perfringens indicates remote pollution).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
With regard to the Goals, Milestones and Targets for the Global Technical Strategy for Malaria (2016-2030), consider the following statements:
1. Compared to 2015, the target is to reduce the malaria mortality rates globally by at least 90% by year 2030
2. Compared to 2015, the target is to redu ce malaria case incidence by 90% by year
3. Eliminate malaria from at least 35 count ries, where malaria was transmitted in 2015, by year 2030
Which of the above statements hold true?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO's Global Technical Strategy for Malaria (2016–2030) aims by 2030 to cut global malaria mortality by ≥90% (1), reduce case incidence by ≥90% (2), and eliminate malaria in at least 35 countries (3).

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following IUDs is associated with a low pregnancy ra te (0.2 per 100), less number of ectopic pregnancies and lower menstrual blood loss?
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-20 / Mirena) has the lowest pregnancy failure rate (~0.2/100 woman-years), reduces ectopic pregnancy risk, and markedly decreases menstrual blood loss.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text: The incidence of diarrhoea is highest among infants in the age group of 6–11 months due to all of the following reasons EXCEPT:
options: Introduction of foods which may be contaminated
Direct contact with human or animal faeces
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Peak diarrhoea incidence at 6–11 months results from waning maternal antibodies, contaminated weaning foods, and crawling/hand-to-mouth contact with faeces—not teething/tooth eruption.

upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.text:
In the context of “Anti-Malaria Month Campaign”, consider the following statements:
1. It is observed every year in the month of June
2. It is planned during the Monsoon season
3. It aims to enhance the level of community awareness and participation
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2020-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Anti-Malaria Month is observed annually in June (1; pre-monsoon, not monsoon) to boost community awareness and participation before peak transmission (3).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Austin Flint Murmur occurs in:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Austin Flint murmur is an apical mid-diastolic rumble heard in severe chronic aortic regurgitation due to the regurgitant jet impinging on the anterior mitral leaflet.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which amongst the following should be considered in a patient with acute chest pain and ST segment elevation in the precordial leads?
1. Acute myocardial infarction
2. Acute hyperkalemia
3. Pericarditis
4. Hypocalcemia
5. Oesophagitis
6. Pneumothorax
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Precordial ST-segment elevation with acute chest pain occurs in acute myocardial infarction (1), acute hyperkalaemia (2), and acute pericarditis (3).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Which amongst the following is the most powerful independent risk factor for atherosclerosis?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Advancing age is the single most powerful non-modifiable independent risk factor for atherosclerosis.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text:
In which of the following SA node dysfunction conditions, permanent pacing may NOT be required?
1. Beta blocker drugs
2. Narcotic drugs
3. Iatrogenic–Post RT/Surgery
4. Hypothyroidism
5. Sick sinus syndrome
6. Raised Intracranial tension
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Reversible SA node dysfunction from beta-blockers (1), narcotics (2), hypothyroidism (4), or raised ICP (6) does not require permanent pacing (unlike intrinsic sick sinus syndrome or permanent surgical/RT injury).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Kartagener syndrome has the following features EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Kartagener syndrome (primary ciliary dyskinesia with situs inversus, bronchiectasis, and chronic sinusitis) is inherited as an autosomal recessive (not dominant) trait.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following pulmonary function set is characteristic of COPD?
options: FEV1 / FVC < 70% ; FEV1 ↓ ; FVC ↓ ; TLC ↑ DLCO Normal
FEV1 / FVC < 70% ; FEV1 ↑ ; FVC ↓ ; TLC ↓ DLCO ↓
FEV1 / FVC < 70% ; FEV1 ↓ ; FVC ↑ ; TLC ↑ DLCO ↑
FEV1 / FVC < 70% ; FEV1 ↓ ; FVC ↓ ; TLC ↓ DLCO ↓
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: COPD shows obstructive spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 70%, decreased FEV1 and FVC) with hyperinflation (increased TLC); note in pure chronic bronchitis DLCO may remain normal.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following drugs causes dry cough as a side effect?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: ACE inhibitors such as ramipril inhibit bradykinin breakdown, causing a persistent dry hacking cough in ~10–15% of patients.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: For Acid Fast Bacilli (AFB) to be detected in sputum by the direct microscopy, the bacillary burden in sputum typically is:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Direct sputum smear microscopy (Ziehl-Neelsen) requires approximately 5,000–10,000 acid-fast bacilli per mL of sputum for reliable detection.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: The pleural fluid is considered as empyema if following is present in it:
options: Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH) of more than 1000 U/L
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Complicated parapneumonic effusion/empyema is characterized by pleural fluid glucose < 60 mg/dL, LDH > 1000 U/L, and pH < 7.0–7.2 (all of these).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Airway secretions contain all of the following antimicrobial peptides EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Airway secretions contain innate antimicrobial peptides/proteins such as defensins, secretory IgA, and lysozyme (histidine is an amino acid, not an antimicrobial peptide).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: The respiratory motor neuron associated with origin of respiratory cycle is located in:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The dorsal respiratory group (inspiratory pacemaker/motor neurons) is located in the posterior/dorsal medulla oblongata (nucleus tractus solitarius).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Weight Loss:
1. 4.5 kg over 6-12 months
2. 10 kg over 6-12 months
3. More than 5 % over 6-12 months
4. More than 10 % over 6-12 months
Which of the above constitute significant or clinically important weight loss?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Clinically significant involuntary weight loss is defined as loss of > 4.5 kg (10 lb; 1) or > 5% of baseline body weight (3) over 6–12 months.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following Ascitic Fluid analysis is most compatible with a diagnosis of Ascites secondary to portal hypertension?
options: SAAG < 1.1 g/dl ; Ascitic Fluid Protein < 2.5 g/dl
SAAG < 1.1 g/dl ; Ascitic Fluid Protein > 2.5 g /dl
SAAG > 1.1 g/dl ; Ascitic Fluid Protein < 2.5 g /dl
SAAG > 1.1 g/dl ; Ascitic Fluid Protein > 2.5 g /dl
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Portal hypertension ascites (e.g., cirrhosis) classically exhibits a high SAAG (> 1.1 g/dL) with low ascitic fluid total protein (< 2.5 g/dL).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: All are the causes of Interstitial lung disease EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Bronchial asthma is a chronic obstructive airway disease, not an interstitial lung disease (unlike IPF, GPA, and sarcoidosis).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: The rhythmic activity recorded on scalp by EEG in a normal aw ake adult lying quietly with eyes closed is:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A normal awake adult resting quietly with eyes closed exhibits a posterior dominant alpha rhythm (8–13 Hz) on EEG.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Transient Monocular blindness may be due to small platelet emboli that occludes:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Transient monocular blindness (amaurosis fugax) results from cholesterol/platelet microemboli from carotid stenosis occluding the ophthalmic/central retinal artery.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: The phenomenon of sparing of macular vision is due to collateral circulation between:
options: anterior, middle and posterior cerebral artery
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Macular sparing in posterior cerebral artery stroke occurs because the occipital pole representing the macula receives dual collateral blood supply from both the middle and posterior cerebral arteries.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Characteristic features of Horner’s Syndrome are:
options: partial ptosis, enophthalmos, constricted pupil, decreased sweating
partial ptosis, exophthalmos, constricted pupil, decreased sweating
partial ptosis, enophthalmos, dilated pupil, decreased sweating
partial ptosis, enophthalmos, constricted pupil, increased sweating
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Horner's syndrome (oculosympathetic paresis) presents with the classic tetrad of partial ptosis, miosis (constricted pupil), enophthalmos (apparent), and ipsilateral anhidrosis (decreased sweating).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following statements are true EXCEPT:
options: Dorsal column fibres synapse at the cuneate and gracile nuclei
Pain and temperature sensations are carried by lateral spinothalamic tract
Spinal cord ends at lower level of 5th lumbar vertebrae
Dorsal spinocerebellar tract carries fibres from the same side of the body
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In adults, the spinal cord terminates as the conus medullaris at the lower border of the L1 (or L1–L2) vertebra, not L5.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: The following conditions usually present with proximal muscle weakness, EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Myotonic dystrophy (myotonia dystrophica) classically causes distal limb, facial, and neck flexor weakness, whereas FSHD, Duchenne, and Becker dystrophies cause proximal weakness.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Pel-Ebstein fever is seen in:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pel-Ebstein fever (cyclical bouts of high fever alternating with afebrile periods over 1–2 weeks) is classically associated with Hodgkin lymphoma.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are true regarding acute leukaemias, EXCEPT:
options: Promyelocytic leukaemia may present with DIC
Gum hypertrophy is a feature of monocytic leukaemia
Translocation is a common chromosomal abnormality in acute myeloid leukaemia
Auer rods suggest acute lymphocytic leukaemia
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Auer rods (azurophilic crystalline cytoplasmic inclusions) are pathognomonic of acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), never acute lymphocytic leukaemia (ALL).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are clinical features of Polycystic ovarian syndrome EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: PCOS presents with oligomenorrhoea/amenorrhoea (anovulation), hirsutism, insulin resistance/glucose intolerance, and infertility—not menorrhagia typically.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Clinical features of Turner syndrome include all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Turner syndrome (45,X) features short stature, webbed neck, coarctation of the aorta, and a wide (cubitus valgus)—not narrow—carrying angle of the elbow.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Pretibial myxedema is a clinical feature of:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pretibial myxoedema (thyroid dermopathy—non-pitting waxy plaques over the shins) is a specific extrathyroidal manifestation of Graves' disease.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match the
List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I
List II ( disease) ( signs)
A. Conn syndrome
1. Anosmia
B. Turner syndrome
2. Tetany
C. Kallman syndrome
3. Lymphoedema
D. Cushing syndrome
4. Avascular necrosis of hip
Code:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Conn syndrome causes hypokalaemic alkalosis/tetany (A-2); Turner syndrome causes neonatal lymphoedema (B-3); Kallmann syndrome causes anosmia (C-1); Cushing syndrome causes avascular necrosis of the femoral head (D-4).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of Koch’s postulates?
options: The same organism must be present in every case of the disease
The organism must be isolated from the diseased host and grown in culture
The isolate must cause the disease when incubated
The organism may not be reisolated from the incubated diseased host
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Koch's fourth postulate requires that the inoculated organism MUST be re-isolated in pure culture from the experimentally diseased host.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following cause dementia EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Huntington's disease, Alzheimer's disease, and thiamine deficiency (Wernicke-Korsakoff) cause dementia, whereas vitamin D toxicity causes hypercalcaemia/nephrocalcinosis rather than primary dementia.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: The therapeutic level of Digoxin in blood is:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The therapeutic serum digoxin concentration is narrow, typically 0.5–2.0 ng/mL (1–2 ng/mL).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: A 40-year old woman presents with sudden ons et palpitations. An ECG done reveals narrow- QRS complex tachycardia. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sudden-onset regular narrow-complex tachycardia in a 40-year-old woman is most commonly AV nodal/AV reentry tachycardia (AVNRT/AVRT).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements are true about management of acute pulmonary oedema?
1. Put the patient in relaxed, supine position
2. Give high flow, high concentration oxygen
3. Administer Furosemide intravenously
4. No role of Nitrates
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema management includes upright sitting (not supine), high-flow oxygen (2), IV furosemide (3), and IV nitrates.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following does NOT cause prolongation of QT interval?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hyperkalaemia causes peaked T waves, QRS widening, and shortened (not prolonged) QT interval, unlike hypomagnesaemia, erythromycin, and amiodarone.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: A 21-year young man presents in emergency w ith high grade fever with inflammation of knee and ankle joints which is fleeting in natu re. There is history of occasional palpitations. There is no history of antecedent sore throat. On examination, splenomegaly is present. The ECG shows prolongation of PR interval. What is the most likely diagnosis in India?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: High fever with fleeting migratory polyarthritis of large joints (knees, ankles) and PR interval prolongation (first-degree AV block) in a young Indian adult is classic for acute rheumatic fever.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: A 50-year gentleman with Type-2 Diabetes mellitus for 5 years presents in medical emergency with sudden onset of dyspnoea at rest, orthopnoea, and prostration. On examination, pulse is rapid and very weak in volume. His blood pressure is 100/70 mmHg. There are diffuse crepitations at lung bases. What is the most lik ely diagnosis of his conditions?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute dyspnoea at rest, orthopnoea, hypotension, and diffuse basal crepitations indicate acute left heart failure with pulmonary oedema.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: The ‘Y’ descent in JVP waveform represents:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The 'y' descent of the JVP waveform corresponds to passive rapid atrial emptying into the right ventricle immediately after tricuspid valve opening.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: While distinguishing a venous pulsation from the arterial pulsation in neck, which of the following is NOT correct?
options: The height of venous pulse varies with respiration
Abdominal pressure causes rise in venous pulse
Venous pulse has a single peak in each cardiac cycle
Venous pulse is not easily palpable
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The jugular venous pulse is biphasic (two positive peaks, a and v, per cardiac cycle), whereas arterial pulsation has a single peak.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following does NOT cause pulmonary infiltrates with eosinophilia?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Bronchial asthma (ABPA), radiation pneumonitis, and EGPA (Churg-Strauss) cause pulmonary infiltrates with eosinophilia, unlike cystic fibrosis.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Total lung capacity is decreased in which one of the following conditions?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pulmonary fibrosis is a restrictive lung disease that reduces total lung capacity (TLC < 80% predicted), whereas asthma, chronic bronchitis, and emphysema increase or preserve TLC.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the minimum spirometry criterion for diagnosis of bronchial asthma?
options: Decrease in FEV1 ≥ 20 % after 6 minutes of exercise
Increase in FEV1 ≥ 12 % following administration of inhaled bronchodilators
Increase in 500 ml of FEV1 after glucocorticoids inhalation
Less than 20 % diurnal variation on more than 3 days a week on PEF diary
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2019 Answer Key: Option (b) — Increase in FEV1 ≥ 12 % following administration of inhaled bronchodilators.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Modified Blatchford score is used for the risk stratification of:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Glasgow-Blatchford score risk-stratifies patients presenting with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding to predict need for clinical intervention.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text:
Long term use of proton pump inhibitor in elde rly puts the patient at risk of which of the following?
1. Community acquired pneumonia
2. Clostridium difficile associated disease
3. Urinary tract infection
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Long-term PPI acid suppression in the elderly increases the risk of community-acquired pneumonia (1) and Clostridioides difficile infection (2).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: Regardless of the infectious agent, the most characteristic symptom of infectious esophagitis is:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Odynophagia (painful swallowing) is the hallmark symptom of infectious oesophagitis (Candida, HSV, CMV) regardless of aetiology.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: The parameters used in modified Child-Pugh classification for staging cirrhosis are:
options: Serum albumin, serum bilirubin, prothrombin time only
Serum albumin, serum bilirubin, prothrombin time, ascities only
Serum albumin, Serum bilirubin, prothrombin time, ascities, hepatic encephalopathy
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2019 Answer Key: Option (d) — Serum albumin, Serum bilirubin, prothrombin time, ascities, hepatic encephalopathy.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are consistent with a diagnosis of Irritable Bowel Syndrome EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Unexplained weight loss is an 'alarm/red-flag' symptom that argues against functional irritable bowel syndrome and mandates workup for organic disease.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.text: A 26-year old HIV infected male presen ts with odynophagia. Upper GI endoscopy demonstrates serpiginous ulcers in a normal surrounding mucosa in distal esophagus. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Odynophagia in an HIV-positive patient with large linear/serpiginous distal oesophageal ulcers on normal mucosa is classic for CMV oesophagitis.
