upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the relative risk of developing pulmonary embolism in users of oral contraceptives as per the information given below? Women using OCs Pulmonary embolism Total Yes No Yes 120 80 200 No 10 70 80 Total 130 150 280
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Incidence in OC users = 120/200 = 0.60; incidence in non-users = 10/80 = 0.125. Relative Risk = 0.60 / 0.125 = 4.80.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following epidemiologic method s can be used to identify risk factors and estimate the degree of risk?
options: Cohort study and Randomized control trial
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Case-control (odds ratio) and cohort (relative risk) analytical studies are designed to identify risk factors and quantify the degree of risk.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following tests should be applied to compare mean haemoglobin level of two groups of antenatal mothers?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An unpaired (independent-samples) t-test compares the mean haemoglobin levels of two independent groups of antenatal mothers.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: In a population of 5000, there are 19 % eligible couples. To achieve a couple protection rate (CPR) of 60 %, how many of these should be covered for family planning services?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Eligible couples = 19% of 5000 = 950. To achieve 60% CPR, 0.60 × 950 = 570 couples must be covered.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: The drug of choice for chemoprophylaxis to health care personnel and close contacts of suspected or confirmed case of pandemic influenza A (H1N1) is:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Oral oseltamivir (75 mg once daily × 10 days) is the drug of choice for chemoprophylaxis of pandemic H1N1 influenza.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the recommended site for immunization with hepatitis B vaccine in young children for ensuring reliable absorption?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In young children and adults (beyond infancy), the deltoid muscle is preferred over the gluteal region for reliable Hepatitis B vaccine absorption.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Vaccine associated Paralytic Poliomyelitis is mo stly observed due to which of the following isolate type strain?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Among trivalent OPV strains, Type 3 (followed by Type 2 in immunodeficient recipients) has been a major cause of recipient VAPP in India.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: The specific goals for 2025 under the integrated Global Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Pneumonia and Diarrhea (GAPPD) are all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Reduce mortality from pneumonia in children less than 5 years of age to fewer than 3 per 1000 live births
Reduce mortality from diarrhea in children less than 5 years of age to fewer than 1 per 1000 live births
Reduce the incidence of severe pneumonia by 90 % in children less than 5 years of age compared to 2010 levels
Reduce incidence of severe diarrhea by 75 % in children less than 5 years of age compared to 2010 levels
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2019 Answer Key: Option (c) — Reduce the incidence of severe pneumonia by 90 % in children less than 5 years of age compared to 2010 levels.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Association between hardness of drinking water and death rate from cardiovascular diseases is:
options: Association is obtained in presence of confounders
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Epidemiological studies consistently show an inverse association between drinking water hardness (calcium/magnesium) and cardiovascular disease mortality.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regarding Magnesium is NOT true?
options: It is essential for normal metabolism of calcium and potassium
Human adult body contains about 50 g of Magnesium
Daily requirement of magnesium is estimated to be about 340 mg/day for adults
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The adult human body contains approximately 20–25 g of magnesium (not 50 g), mostly in bone and soft tissues.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following oil/fat contains high mono-unsaturated fatty acid and moderate linoleic acid?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Groundnut (peanut) oil is rich in monounsaturated fatty acids (~45–50% oleic acid) with moderate linoleic acid (~30%).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following trace elements if defi cient in the diet can lead to low birth weight, preterm delivery, spontaneous abortion or even congenital malformation like anencephaly?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Maternal zinc deficiency is associated with low birth weight, preterm delivery, spontaneous abortion, and neural tube defects such as anencephaly.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: An adult weighs 73 kgs and has a height of 1.75 meters. For the purpose of classification of overweight and obesity as per WHO recommendation, this person will be classified as:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: BMI = 73 / (1.75)² = 73 / 3.0625 = 23.84 kg/m², which falls within the WHO normal weight range (18.5–24.99 kg/m²).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regarding WHO Global Action Plan for the prevention and control of NCDs (2013–2020) is NOT correct?
options: At least 10 percent relative reduction in the harmful use of alcohol as appropriate within national context
A 20 percent relative reduction in prevalence of insufficient physical activity
A 10 percent relative reduction in mean population intake of salt/sodium
Halt the rise of diabetes and obesity
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2019 Answer Key: Option (b) — A 20 percent relative reduction in prevalence of insufficient physical activity.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: All are components of Jai Vigyan Mission Mode project on community control of RF/RHD in India EXCEPT:
options: To study the epidemiology of streptococcal sore throats
To establish registries for RF and RHD
Antibiotic treatment of streptococcal sore throats
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Jai Vigyan Mission Mode Project on RF/RHD focused on epidemiology, registries, and GAS vaccine development (not routine antibiotic treatment delivery).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text:
What type of indicator is Sustainable Development Goal target 3.4, which calls for a one third reduction in premature mortality from Non Communicable Diseases (NCD’s) by year 2030?
1. Impact
2. Coverage/risk factor
3. Risk factor/determinants
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: SDG Target 3.4 (one-third reduction in premature NCD mortality by 2030) measures long-term health outcome and is an Impact indicator.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following occupational diseases is the most common cause of permanent disability and mortality?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Silicosis causes progressive, irreversible nodular pulmonary fibrosis and is the leading occupational cause of permanent disability and mortality.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following conditions is NOT inborn error of metabolism?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Down's syndrome (Trisomy 21) is a chromosomal aneuploidy, whereas Tay-Sachs, maple syrup urine disease, and metabolic defects are inborn errors of metabolism.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Amniocentesis is called for in all of the following circumstances EXCEPT:
options: A mother aged 35 years or more
Mother who had a child with Down’s syndrome or other chromosomal anomalies
Parents who are known to have chromosomal translocation
A father aged 50 year or more
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Amniocentesis is indicated for advanced maternal age (≥35 years), prior trisomy child, or parental balanced translocation—not advanced paternal age alone.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: As per WHO recommendations which one of the following mumps vaccine strains should NOT be used in National Immunization Programme?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO advises against using the Rubini mumps vaccine strain in national immunization programmes due to its poor protective efficacy.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are mass approaches towards education of general public EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Internet, direct mailing, and posters/billboards are mass media communication approaches, whereas roleplaying is a group health education method.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following Ministries controls the Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS)?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS) is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is a contraindication for BCG vaccination in a newborn?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Symptomatic HIV infection (immunodeficiency) is a contraindication to live BCG vaccination in newborns due to risk of disseminated BCGosis.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) attempts to identify all of the following deficiencies in children in the age group 0–18 years EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: RBSK covers SAM, Vitamin A deficiency, Vitamin D deficiency (rickets), anaemia, and goitre—not isolated zinc deficiency.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Children of severe acute malnutrition discharged from Nutritional Rehabilitation Centres (NRCs) should be observed in the community by an Anganwari Worker (AWW) as per which one of the following schedules?
options: Once a week for first month and then twice weekly
Twice weekly in first month and then once a week
Once a week for first month and then once fortnightly
Twice weekly in first month and then once fortnightly
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: SAM children discharged from NRCs are followed up by the AWW once every week for the first month and then once fortnightly until full recovery.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: The facilities provided to pregna nt women under the Janani Shis hu Suraksha Karyakram are all EXCEPT:
options: All pregnant women delivery in public health institution to have absolutely free and no expense delivery including cesarean section
Free diet up to 3 days during normal delivery
Free diagnosis and free blood whenever required
Complications during ANC, PNC are not covered
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) covers free treatment for all pregnancy, delivery, and postnatal complications (Statement d is false).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following drugs are effective for treat ment of human reservoir for hookworm infection in single dose EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Piperazine is effective for Ascaris and Enterobius (pinworm), not hookworm (Ancylostoma/Necator), which responds to albendazole, levamisole, or pyrantel.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text:
A woman delivers a healthy baby with weight 2.2 kg at the time of birth. What measures are to be taken?
1. The baby should be exclusively breast fed for first six months
2. The vaccination with OPU and BCG should be delayed till the baby is 2.5 kg of weight
3. Baby should be kept with mother and kangaroo care to be given
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A healthy 2.2 kg newborn should be exclusively breastfed for 6 months (1) and kept with the mother for Kangaroo Mother Care (3) (BCG/OPV are given at birth regardless of 2.5 kg).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text:
LNG-20 (Mirena) is a third generation intra uterine device. What are the advantages of its use?
1. Low uterine pregnancy rates
2. Prevents anemia
3. Long effective life of 10 years
4. No effect on incidence of ectopic pregnancy
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: LNG-20 (Mirena) provides very low pregnancy rates (1), prevents iron-deficiency anaemia by reducing menstrual bleeding (2), and has an effective lifespan of 5–10 years in older/newer guidelines (official key marks 1, 2, 3).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: Open vial policy applies to which one of the following vaccines?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under India's Open Vial Policy, liquid Hepatitis B vaccine vials can be reused across sessions for up to 28 days (unlike lyophilized BCG, Measles, and JE).

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: A village ‘X’ has a population of 5000 with a birth rate of 25 per thousand. In any given month, how many pregnancies should be registered with the ANM of this village?
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Expected pregnancies in a year = 5000 × (25/1000) × 1.10 (10% pregnancy wastage) = 137.5; monthly active registered cohort ≈ 137.5 / 2 ≈ 69 pregnancies.

upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.text: In India, for providing HIV treatment services Link ART Centres are situated at:
options: Medical colleges and district level hospitals
Sub-district level hospitals and Community Health Centres
upsc-cms-2019-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under NACP, Link ART Centres (LACs) are located at sub-district hospitals and Community Health Centres (CHCs) to decentralize HIV care.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Most common valve involved in Carcinoid syndrome is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Carcinoid syndrome causes serotonin-mediated endocardial fibrosis on the right side of the heart, most commonly causing tricuspid regurgitation/stenosis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 70 year ol d man reports to the e mergency w ith acute chest pain. ECG shows inferior wall Myocardial Infarction (MI). He has recently been discharged 7 days back following thrombolysis with streptokinase for Acute Anterior wall MI. What will be the appropriate management?
options: Aspirin, Sublingual nitroglycerin, Clopidogrel, Primary PCI
Aspirin, Sublingual nitroglycerin, Clopidogrel, Beta blockers
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Re-administration of streptokinase within 5 days to 2 years is contraindicated due to neutralizing antibodies; primary PCI is the management of choice for acute inferior STEMI 7 days post-streptokinase.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The presence of a fusion beat on an Electrocardiogram is diagnostic of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fusion beats (hybrid QRS complexes from simultaneous supraventricular and ventricular depolarization) and capture beats are diagnostic of ventricular tachycardia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 64 year old man presents with chest pain of 24 hours duration. His ECG reveals ST elevation, Anterior Wall Myocardial Infarction. The preferred tr eatment modality for him is:
options: Nitroglycerin infusion , Aspirin and Beta blockers
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In acute STEMI presenting late (24 hours after symptom onset) without ongoing ischaemia/cardiogenic shock, thrombolysis is not indicated; medical therapy (nitroglycerin, aspirin, beta-blockers) is used.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The preferred anti hypertensive dru g for a 74 year old male with benign prostatic hypertrophy is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Alpha-1 blockers such as prazosin relax prostatic smooth muscle and lower blood pressure, making them useful in elderly hypertensive men with BPH.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The treatment of choice for a 32 year old male patient of severe mitral stenosis (Rheumatic) with thickened and calcified valves on echocardiography is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with heavily thickened, calcified, immobile valves is unsuitable for balloon valvotomy and requires surgical mitral valve replacement.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is an example of Type-IV respiratory failure?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Type IV respiratory failure results from hypoperfusion of respiratory muscles in circulatory shock (e.g., cardiogenic, septic, or hypovolaemic shock).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are seen in Polyarteritis Nodosa EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) is a medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis causing mononeuritis multiplex, mesenteric/bowel infarction, and pericarditis, while classically sparing the glomeruli (no glomerulonephritis).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are the pointers to organic cause of psychiatric disease EXCEPT:
options: Late age of onset of psychiatric illness
No previous history of psychiatric illness
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A positive family history of psychiatric illness points toward a primary functional psychiatric disorder rather than an organic medical cause.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are Long Acting Beta Agonists (LABA) EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Levosalbutamol (R-albuterol) is a short-acting beta-2 agonist (SABA), whereas salmeterol, formoterol, and indacaterol are LABAs.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Deficiency of which immune function results in tubercular infections?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Control of intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis depends critically on intact cell-mediated (T-cell / CD4+ Th1 / macrophage) immunity.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common agent responsible for community acquired pneumonia is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) is the single most common bacterial cause of community-acquired pneumonia worldwide.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 26 year old woman presents with fever, arthralgia and erythema nodosum. Her chest X -ray reveals bilateral hilar lymph adenopathy. Her mantoux test is negative. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fever, arthralgia, erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and a negative Mantoux test in a young woman represent Löfgren's syndrome (acute sarcoidosis).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the characteristics of Exudative pleural effusion?
1. Pleural fluid protein/serum protein > 0.5
2. Pleural fluid protein/serum protein < 0.5
3. Pleural fluid LDH/serum LDH > 0.6
4. Pleural fluid LDH/serum LDH < 0.6
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: By Light's criteria, exudative pleural effusions have pleural/serum protein > 0.5 (1) and pleural/serum LDH > 0.6 (3).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are seen in Whipple’s disease EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Whipple's disease presents with weight loss, steatorrhoea, migratory arthralgia, and CNS dementia/ophthalmoplegia, not haemolytic anaemia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A middle aged patient wit h chronic li ver di sease presents with pain abdomen and distension. He also has diarrhoea and fever si nce one day. On examination, he is hemodynamically stable with fever of 100 oF. There is jaundice, pall or, pedal edem a and ascites. A diagnostic paracentesis is done. Ascitic fluid protein is 0.8 gm%, sugar 100 mg%, total count 500/mm3 of which 85% are polymorphonuclear leaukocytes and 15% lymphocytes. Most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fever, abdominal pain, ascites with SAAG > 1.1 (low protein 0.8 g/dL), and ascitic neutrophil (PMN) count > 250 cells/mm³ (85% of 500 = 425/mm³) in cirrhosis confirm spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Herald patch followed by rash is characteristic of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pityriasis rosea classically begins with a solitary salmon-coloured oval 'herald patch' followed by a generalized 'Christmas-tree' eruption on the trunk.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A young male comes to the OPD with history of jaundice since many years. He has noted that the jaundice may fluctuate but is often aggravated when he is fasting. There is no history of hospitalisation, no drug use, alcoholism or blood transfusion. Family history is not significant. Clinical examination is unremarkable except for mild scleral icterus. What is the likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic intermittent mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia exacerbated by fasting or stress with normal LFTs and no haemolysis is diagnostic of Gilbert's syndrome.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are causes of anemia in a case of chronic kidney disease EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Anaemia of chronic kidney disease results from erythropoietin deficiency, shortened RBC survival, and uraemic/GI blood loss, not inherited haemoglobinopathy.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Characteristic feature of upper motor neuron lesion includes:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Clonus (along with spasticity, hyperreflexia, and Babinski sign) is a classic upper motor neuron sign, whereas fasciculations, hyporeflexia, and wasting are lower motor neuron signs.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following arteries is involved in causation of lateral medullary syndrome?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg's) syndrome is caused by occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) or vertebral artery.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A right handed 70 year old man has a brain s can which reveals a lesion that has damag ed his left angular and supramarginal gyr us. On examination, one would expect the following EXCEPT:
options: Difficulty with left to right discrimination
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Damage to the dominant (left) angular and supramarginal gyri produces Gerstmann syndrome (left-right disorientation, finger agnosia, agraphia, acalculia), not inappropriate affect (frontal lobe).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Total iron binding capacity of more than 360 µg/dl is seen in anemia due to:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Total iron-binding capacity (TIBC > 360 µg/dL) is characteristically elevated in iron-deficiency anaemia, whereas it is normal or low in chronic inflammation, haemoglobinopathies, and sideroblastic anaemia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Escape behaviour with paroxysmal occurrence is seen in:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Panic disorder is characterized by recurrent unexpected paroxysmal surges of intense fear/autonomic arousal leading to escape or agoraphobic avoidance.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following conditions are associated with prolonged prothrombin time?
1. Factor VIII deficiency
2. Factor VII deficiency
3. Heparin anticoagulation
4. Warfarin anticoagulation
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Prothrombin time (extrinsic/common pathway) is prolonged by Factor VII deficiency (2) and warfarin therapy (4) (Factor VIII and heparin primarily prolong aPTT).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Syndrome X includes:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Syndrome X (metabolic/insulin resistance syndrome) encompasses central obesity, hyperlipidaemia/atherogenic dyslipidaemia, Type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Growth hormone secretion is inhibited by:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hyperglycaemia (oral/IV glucose load) suppresses pituitary growth hormone secretion (the basis of the OGTT suppression test for acromegaly), whereas arginine, clonidine, and L-dopa stimulate GH.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following drugs causes hypercalcemia?
options: Furosemide All of the following insulins are longer acting EXCEPT: (a) Glargine (b) Degludec (c) Glulisine (d) Detemir
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic lithium therapy shifts the calcium-sensing set point of parathyroid cells, causing hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcaemia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following insulins are longer acting EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Insulin glulisine is a rapid-acting prandial insulin analogue, whereas glargine, degludec, and detemir are long-acting basal insulins.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The presence of vitiligo on examination suggests an associated:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Vitiligo is an autoimmune melanocyte-destructive disorder frequently associated with other autoimmune diseases such as autoimmune thyroiditis, pernicious anaemia, and Type 1 diabetes.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A mildy elevated TSH ( 5 -20 m U/L) along with a normal T3 and normal T4 levels is suggestive of :
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Mildly elevated TSH (5–20 mU/L) with normal free T3 and T4 levels defines subclinical hypothyroidism.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following suggests patient to be prediabetic?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: ADA defines prediabetes as HbA1c 5.7–6.4% or FPG 100–125 mg/dL (HbA1c 6.2% and FPG 105 mg/dL fall squarely in the prediabetic range; FPG ≥ 126 or HbA1c ≥ 6.5% is diabetes).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Cutaneous manifestations of tuberculosis includes:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cutaneous tuberculosis manifestations include erythema nodosum (hypersensitivity) and lupus vulgaris (chronic paucibacillary plaque).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Treatment of scrub typhus is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Doxycycline or azithromycin is the treatment of choice for scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi), with azithromycin preferred in pregnancy and children.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT correct regarding Clostridum tetani?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Clostridium tetani is an obligately anaerobic, Gram-positive, terminal spore-bearing ('drumstick') bacillus that IS motile via peritrichous flagella (not non-motile).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are extrapulmonary manifestations of mycoplasma infection EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes extrapulmonary arthritis, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and Stevens-Johnson syndrome, but does not cause dementia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A ‘slapped cheek rash’ is characteristic of infection with:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Parvovirus B19 causes erythema infectiosum ('fifth disease'), classically presenting with a bright red 'slapped-cheek' rash.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 34 week pregnant nurse comes in contact with a patient with chickenpox at her workplace. She has never had chickenpox in the past and is unvaccinated. The best option for her is:
options: Varicella zoster immunoglobulin to be given within 7 days
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A non-immune pregnant woman exposed to varicella should receive varicella-zoster immunoglobulin (VZIG) promptly (within 96 hours–7/10 days) to prevent severe maternal/fetal varicella.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following has the maximum diagnostic sensitivity for Leishmaniasis?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Splenic aspirate microscopy/culture has the highest diagnostic sensitivity (~95–98%) for visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar), followed by bone marrow and lymph node aspirates.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regarding cryptosporidiosis is NOT correct?
options: Infection is acquired by feco-oral route
It is usually a mild self limiting illness in immunocompetent patient
In HIV infected persons it is a serious opportunistic infection
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cryptosporidiosis is treated with nitazoxanide (and ART in HIV) and is notoriously unresponsive to metronidazole.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are live attenuated vaccines EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Human rabies vaccines are inactivated (killed) cell-culture vaccines, whereas MMR, OPV, and BCG are live attenuated.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are soil transmitted nematodes EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wait: hookworms (Ancylostoma, Necator) and Strongyloides penetrate skin from soil; Ascaris lumbricoides is also soil-transmitted (via eggs), though the official key marks (d) Ascaris lumbricoides.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
A veterinary doctor is bitten by a stray dog, which is classified as a category 3 bite. He has completed his pre -exposure prophy lactic vaccination with human diploid cell Rabies vaccine with three doses administered on day 0, 7, 28 about 1 year back. A ppropriate treatment would include which of the following?
1. Wound care
2. Antibiotics
3. Booster dose of Anti Rabies vaccine
4. Rabies immune globulin at wound site
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In a previously fully vaccinated individual bitten by a dog, PEP requires wound care (1), antibiotics if indicated (2), and 2 booster vaccine doses on Days 0 and 3 (3)—never RIG.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Loffler’s syndrome is caused due to infection by:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ascaris lumbricoides larval migration through the lungs is the classic cause of Löffler's eosinophilic pneumonitis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are the c ommon infectious syndrome(s) associated with klebsiella pneumoniae?
1. Pneumonia
2. Intra-abdominal infections
3. Hepatitis
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Klebsiella pneumoniae commonly causes severe necrotizing pneumonia (1) and intra-abdominal/liver abscesses (2), not viral-style hepatitis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Differential diagnosis of dysenteric syndrome includes which of the following?
1. Salmonella infection
2. Campylobacter infection
3. Shigella infection
4. Clostridium infection
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Salmonella (1), Campylobacter (2), Shigella (3), and Clostridioides difficile/perfringens (4) are all differential diagnoses of infectious dysentery/colitis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Antifungal agent of choice for the treatment of mucormycosis is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Liposomal Amphotericin B is the first-line antifungal agent of choice for mucormycosis (voriconazole, itraconazole, and fluconazole lack Mucorales activity).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: What drug therapy would be appropriate for management of UTI in a pregnant patient?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Beta-lactams such as ampicillin/amoxicillin (or cephalexin/nitrofurantoin) are safe in pregnancy, whereas fluoroquinolones and TMP-SMX (1st/3rd trimester) are avoided.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following conditions is NOT associated with lymphocytosis?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Leptospirosis classically causes neutrophilic leukocytosis (or normal WBC with thrombocytopenia), unlike infectious mononucleosis, viral fevers, and rickettsial fevers which feature lymphocytosis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a diagnostic criterion of Kwashiorkor?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Triceps skinfold thickness < 3 mm reflects severe subcutaneous fat depletion characteristic of marasmus, whereas kwashiorkor features oedema, hypoalbuminaemia (< 2.8 g/dL), and easy hair pluckability.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following drugs does NOT have any action against Salmonella typhi?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Doxycycline has no clinically useful activity against Salmonella typhi, unlike amoxicillin, co-trimoxazole, and azithromycin/macrolides.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following drugs are used for the treatment of influenza EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tenofovir is an NRTI used for HIV and Hepatitis B, not influenza (unlike neuraminidase inhibitors zanamivir/oseltamivir and adamantane rimantadine).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Diagnostic accuracy has been enhanced by the ability to detect specific DNA sequences in all of the following infectious micro-organisms EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: PCR/DNA detection has revolutionized diagnosis of CMV, HIV, and M. tuberculosis, whereas S. aureus is routinely diagnosed by rapid Gram stain and standard culture.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Hip Flexor Spasm is characteristic of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Irritation of the iliopsoas muscle by a psoas abscess produces painful hip flexion deformity and hip flexor spasm (psoas sign).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Gastroenteritis associated with eating raw eggs is usually attributed to:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Gastroenteritis after consuming raw or undercooked eggs/poultry is classically caused by non-typhoidal Salmonella enterica (e.g., S. Enteritidis).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following diseases is NOT caused by protozoa?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Schistosomiasis is caused by trematode helminths (blood flukes), whereas trypanosomiasis, leishmaniasis, and amoebiasis are protozoal infections.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: An adult with fever and right sided chest pain is found to have a moderate right sided pleural effusion. C hest X-Ray (PA view ) also shows a moderate ple ural effusion. A diagnostic thoracocentesis reveals straw coloured exudates with 50 mg% of sugar and lymphocytic pleocytosis. ADA levels are borderline. What investigation would be most likely to confirm a diagnosis of tuberculosis?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In tuberculous pleural effusion with borderline ADA and low bacillary load in fluid, closed needle pleural biopsy demonstrating caseating granulomas has the highest diagnostic yield.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to acute anterior poliomyelitis:
1. It is caused by a virus belonging to picornavirus family
2. Muscle pain and cramps may be associated with diffuse transient fasciculations at the onset
3. Tonsillectomy reduces the risk of bulbar poliomyelitis
4. Cerebrospinal fluid may show mild pleocytosis with increase polymorphonuclear cells in early course of disease
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Poliovirus is a picornavirus (1), early paralysis features myalgia/fasciculations (2), and early CSF shows neutrophilic pleocytosis before shifting to lymphocytes (4) (tonsillectomy increases bulbar polio risk).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT seen in case of Marasmus?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Easy hair pluckability ('flag sign') is a classic feature of kwashiorkor (protein deficiency), not marasmus.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Perception of an object in absence of stimulus is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A hallucination is a false sensory perception occurring in the absence of any external stimulus (whereas an illusion misinterprets a real stimulus).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following drugs can be used for the treatment for cessation of smoking EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Nicotine replacement, bupropion, and varenicline are evidence-based smoking cessation therapies; clonazepam is a benzodiazepine with no role in smoking cessation.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following features are present in Organophosphorus poisoning EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Organophosphate poisoning causes cholinergic crisis (bronchorrhoea, confusion, nicotinic fasciculations) leading to muscle weakness/flaccid paralysis rather than hypertonia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Small sized pupils are seen in poisoning with all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Organophosphates, opioids, and clonidine cause miosis (pinpoint pupils), whereas cocaine is a sympathomimetic causing mydriasis (dilated pupils).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 24 year old male presents with consumption of an unknown substance. His respiratory rate is 22/minute, pulse rate is 110/minute, BP is 150/94 mmHg and he has 2 episodes of seizures. There are tremors and hallucinations. The substance ingested most likely is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tachycardia, hypertension, tachypnoea, tremors, seizures, and hallucinations represent a sympathomimetic toxidrome typical of amphetamine intoxication.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The toxic effects of aluminium phosphide is due to the release of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Aluminium phosphide reacts with gastric moisture to liberate toxic phosphine (PH3) gas, which inhibits cytochrome c oxidase and causes refractory shock and myocarditis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: An 18 year old boy was brought to the emergency department after being bitten by a sa wscaled viper. The monitoring which is most crucial in this patient is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Saw-scaled viper (Echis carinatus) venom causes severe consumption coagulopathy; serial 20-minute whole blood clotting test (20WBCT) is the crucial bedside monitor.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Bite of cobra is likely to result in:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cobra (elapid) venom contains postsynaptic neurotoxins causing descending flaccid paralysis (ptosis, bulbar palsy, respiratory arrest).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Hematuria is a prominent symptom with infection due to:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Schistosoma haematobium inhabits the vesical venous plexus, causing terminal painless haematuria and chronic cystitis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Bite of the Tsetse Fly transmits:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness, Trypanosoma brucei) is transmitted by the bite of the tsetse fly (Glossina).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 60 year old man with pneumonia is unconscious and has a PaO 2 of 50 mm Hg. The preferred modality of treatment for him is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: An unconscious pneumonia patient with severe hypoxaemia (PaO2 50 mmHg) cannot protect their airway (contraindicating NIV) and requires endotracheal intubation with invasive mechanical ventilation.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Oliguria is defined as a reduction in urine output
options: Any decrease over previous urine output
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oliguria in adults is defined by KDIGO/clinical standards as urine output < 0.5 mL/kg/hour (or < 400 mL/24 hours).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are signs of Brain death EXCEPT:
options: Pupils fixed and unresponsive to light
Bilateral planter response – Mute or Absent
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Brain death criteria require absent brainstem reflexes (fixed pupils, absent corneal and gag reflexes); plantar responses may be absent or show spinal reflexes and are not a defining brainstem sign.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 35 year old man with history of alcoholism presents with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and global confusion. The treatment of choice for this patient is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and confusion in an alcoholic define Wernicke's encephalopathy, treated urgently with high-dose IV thiamine BEFORE IV glucose.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Most common form of paroxysmal supraventricular Tachycardia is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: AV nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT) is the most common mechanism (~60%) of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The primary therapeutic intervention in symptomatic Sino atrial node dysfunction is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Permanent pacemaker implantation is the definitive primary therapy for symptomatic sinoatrial node dysfunction (sick sinus syndrome).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the Indications for lung transplantation?
1. Emphysema
2. Primary pulmonary hypertension
3. Obliterative bronchiolitis
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: End-stage COPD/emphysema (1), idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (2), and obliterative bronchiolitis (3) are established indications for lung transplantation.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is used t o distinguish narrowing of large airway from small airway?
options: Peak expiratory flow rate is measured
Forced expiratory volume in one second is measured
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Flow-volume loops visually distinguish large central/upper airway obstruction (flattened inspiratory/expiratory plateau) from small-airway disease (coving of expiratory curve).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common cause of chronic relapsing diarrhoea is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is the most common functional cause of chronic relapsing diarrhoea in clinical practice.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common cause of severe acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (b) — Diverticular disease (diverticulosis) is the most common cause of severe acute lower GI bleeding in adults, closely followed by angiodysplasia (dropped by UPSC) [Harrison's Gastroenterology].

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Risk scoring system use d to stratify the patients of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding to predict the need for intervention to treat bleeding is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The modified/Glasgow-Blatchford score stratifies acute upper GI bleeding patients at presentation to predict the need for transfusion or endoscopic intervention.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Corkscrew hairs are seen due to deficiency of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Perifollicular haemorrhage and 'corkscrew' coiled body hairs are pathognomonic dermatologic signs of scurvy (vitamin C deficiency).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the indications of Renal biopsy?
1. Chronic Kidney disease with normal sized kidney
2. Nephrotic syndrome in adults
3. Nephrotic syndrome in children with atypical features
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Renal biopsy is indicated in unexplained CKD with normal-sized kidneys (1), adult nephrotic syndrome (2), and paediatric nephrotic syndrome with atypical/steroid-resistant features (3).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are common risk factors for contrast Induced Nephrotoxicity?
1. Use of high osmolality, ionic contrast media
2. Diabetes Mellitus
3. Myeloma
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: High-osmolality ionic contrast media (1), diabetes mellitus (2), and multiple myeloma with dehydration (3) are classic risk factors for contrast-induced nephropathy.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Presence of Dysmorphic Erythrocytes in urine analysis is suggestive of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Dysmorphic red blood cells (acanthocytes) on urine microscopy indicate glomerular basement membrane injury (glomerulonephritis).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) is usually associated with:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Small-cell lung carcinoma is the malignancy most frequently associated with paraneoplastic SIADH (ectopic ADH secretion).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A silent, resonant Hemithorax on examination is suggestive of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Absent breath sounds (silent chest) with hyperresonance on percussion over one hemithorax is classic for pneumothorax.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Gower’s sign is positive in:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Gower's sign (using hands to 'climb up' the thighs when rising from the floor due to pelvic-girdle weakness) is classic for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are the indications of renal replacement therapy EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Urgent dialysis (AEIOU) is indicated for refractory metabolic acidosis, hyperkalaemia (> 6 mmol/L), and diuretic-resistant fluid overload, not isolated hypercalcaemia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the bacterial diseases are exotoxin-mediated EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Botulism, diphtheria, and tetanus are mediated by potent bacterial exotoxins, whereas typhoid fever (Salmonella typhi) involves bacterial invasion and endotoxin.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: The following substances can cause dilated pupils EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: TCAs (anticholinergic), cocaine, and amphetamines (sympathomimetic) cause mydriasis, whereas clonidine (central alpha-2 agonist) causes miosis (small pupils).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following drugs can cause Pulmonary Eosinophilia?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (a) — Nitrofurantoin is a classic cause of drug-induced pulmonary eosinophilia (acute/chronic eosinophilic pneumonia) [Harrison's Respiratory Medicine].

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: CA 19-9 is a tumour marker used for the diagnosis of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: CA 19-9 is the primary serum tumour marker associated with pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Tinea versicolor is caused by:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pityriasis (tinea) versicolor is a superficial fungal infection caused by the lipophilic yeast Malassezia furfur.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Osborn wave in ECG is characteristic of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Osborn (J) waves are positive convex deflections at the J-point on ECG classically seen in hypothermia (< 32°C).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Disease modifying agent of choice for the peripheral manifestations of ankylosing spondylitis is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (c) — Sulfasalazine is the DMARD of choice for peripheral arthritis in ankylosing spondylitis [Harrison's Rheumatology].

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Drug of choice for treating hypertensive emergency in a case of Aortic dissection is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In acute aortic dissection, after rapid heart-rate/dP/dt control with an IV beta-blocker (esmolol/labetalol), IV sodium nitroprusside is added to lower systolic BP rapidly.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 5 year old boy is brought to the E mergency Room following a crushing injury. The ECG reveals peaked T waves, prolonged PR interval and widened QRS complexes. Which of the following treatments should be administered immediately?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Crush injury with peaked T waves, prolonged PR, and widened QRS indicates life-threatening hyperkalaemia; IV sodium bicarbonate (alongside calcium gluconate/insulin-dextrose) shifts potassium intracellularly and reverses acidosis.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A child with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia is started on chemotherapy. After 2 days he develops vomiting, decreased urine output abdominal pain and te tanic spasms . The ECG reveals QT C prolongation. Which one of the following therapies will be detrimental to his management?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In ALL tumour lysis syndrome, the child has hypocalcaemic tetany and QTc prolongation with hyperphosphataemia and oliguria; routine maintenance fluid (containing potassium) or inadequate/standard maintenance without aggressive TLS hydration/alkalinization is inappropriate—official key marks (a) Normal maintenance IV fluid.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following treatment modalities is NOT recommended for worsening respiratory distress in a child suspected to be suffering from acute croup?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sedation is strictly contraindicated in worsening acute croup because it depresses respiratory drive and masks impending airway obstruction.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following developmental skills will you expect a child to have acquired by 9 months?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Waving 'bye-bye' is a classic 9-month social/adaptive developmental milestone (cruising and mature pincer grasp appear at 10–12 months).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is physiological in a term neonate?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Erythema toxicum neonatorum is a benign, self-limiting papulopustular rash of healthy term newborns (unlike hypotonia, jaundice <24 h, or conjugated bilirubin 3.0 mg/dL).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A preterm neonate undergoes the initial steps of resuscitation. The clinician observes that the baby is breathing, has a heart rate of 80/minute and the baby is pink. What will be the next immediate step in management?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A neonate with heart rate < 100/min (80/min) after initial resuscitation steps requires immediate positive-pressure ventilation (PPV).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A child is able to copy a triangle, names 4 colours, dresses and undresses easily and is able to skip. What is the likely age of this child?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Copying a triangle, naming 4 colours, dressing/undressing independently, and skipping correspond to 60 months (5 years) of age.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following will be considered to be a ‘RED FLAG’ in child development?
options: Unable to sit without support by 10 months
Unable to walk independently by 15 months
Unable to speak a single word with meaning by 15 months
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Inability to sit without support by 9–10 months is a major gross-motor developmental 'red flag' (walking red flag is 18 months; single word is 18 months).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text:
Gastric lavage is contraindicated in which of the following?
1. Corrosive poisoning
2. Organophosphorus poisoning
3. Iron intoxication
4. Turpentine oil ingestion
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Gastric lavage is contraindicated in corrosive (acid/alkali; 1) and hydrocarbon/turpentine oil (4) ingestion due to perforation and aspiration pneumonitis risks.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 10-year old girl is brought to the emergency following a road traffic accident. The child is comatose with GCS score of 4. She is hypertensive, has bradycardia and extensor posturing. CT imaging reveals comminuted skull fractures and intraparenchymal hemorrhage. The initial management should include all of the following measures EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Corticosteroids (IV dexamethasone) are contraindicated/ineffective in acute traumatic brain injury (CRASH trial showed increased mortality), unlike head elevation, mechanical ventilation, and hypertonic saline.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 3-year old boy is brought with complaints of staying aloof. He also has delayed speech. Rest of the developmental milestones were attained normally. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Social aloofness and delayed speech with otherwise normal motor milestones in a 3-year-old boy point to Autism Spectrum Disorder.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements regarding HPV (Human Papilloma Virus) vaccine is NOT true?
options: It can be safely administered in pregnancy
The recommended age for initiation of vaccination is 10–12 years
Catch up vaccination may be permitted up to 26 yea rs of age, provided the woman is not sexually active
The vaccine is administered intramuscularly in deltoid region
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: HPV vaccine is not recommended during pregnancy (it should be deferred until postpartum; Statement a is false).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A 6 -year old boy comes to the immunization clinic having received all vaccines as per schedule till 18 months of age. Which vaccine should be administered now?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under India's National Immunization Schedule, a 5–6 year old child receives the second DPT booster (DTPw booster) if previously immunized up to 18 months.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: “Time-out” strategy is used for management of children having:
options: Breath holding spells 111 All of the following are included in the ‘Mission Indradhanush’ EXCEPT: (a) Japanese Encephalitis vaccine (b) Measles vaccine (c) Hepatitis A vaccine (d) Haemophilus influenza type B vaccine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Brief 'time-out' is the recommended behavioural technique for managing temper tantrums in young children.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: All of the following are included in the ‘Mission Indradhanush’ EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Mission Indradhanush includes BCG, OPV, DPT, HepB, Measles/MR, Hib (Pentavalent), JE (in endemic districts), and Rotavirus/PCV—not Hepatitis A.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is the best mode of management of a newborn born to a mother with Hepatitis B infection?
options: Hepatitis B Immunoglobulin (HBIG) and Hepatitis B vaccine at birth
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Newborns of HBsAg-positive mothers must receive both Hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) and the birth dose of Hepatitis B vaccine at separate sites within 12 hours of birth.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: At what age should a lateral neck radiograph be done for a child with Downs syndrome to rule out atlanto-occipital subluxation?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Children with Down syndrome should undergo cervical spine screening (lateral neck X-ray) around 3 years of age to rule out atlanto-axial/atlanto-occipital instability before sports participation.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which X ray will be used to evaluate the bone age (skeletal age)of a term newborn at birth?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: At birth in a term newborn, skeletal age is assessed on a knee X-ray by looking for distal femoral and proximal tibial epiphyseal ossification centres.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following permanent tooth eruption event has close correlation with menarche?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (d) — Eruption of the permanent second molar (~12–13 years) correlates closely with menarche [Forensic Medicine / Ghai Pediatrics].

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the ‘4 Ds’ that are the focus of the Rashtriya Bal Suraksha Karyakram’(RBSK)?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: RBSK's '4 Ds' are Defects at birth, Deficiencies, Diseases, and Developmental delays including disabilities (not 'Deficit').

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: In which one of the following age groups is the highest rate of drowning observed , worldwide?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Worldwide, the highest drowning mortality rate occurs among toddlers aged 1–4 years.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is the recommended initial intravenous therapy in a 2 -year old child with Severe Acute Malnutrition with Severe Dehydration and Shock?
options: Ringer Lactate(R) at the rate of 30 mL/kg over first 30 minutes
Half-normal saline (N/2) in 5% dextrose at the rate of 15 mL/kg over first 60 minutes
Normal saline(NS) at the rate of 20 mL/kg over the first 30 minutes
N/5 saline with 5% dextrose at the rate of 30 mL/kg over first 60 minutes
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2018 Answer Key: Option (b) — Half-normal saline (N/2) in 5% dextrose at the rate of 15 mL/kg over first 60 minutes.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: A female carrier for hemophilia A gene gets married to a genetically normal male. What are the chances of her delivering a male offspring with hemophilia?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Haemophilia A is X-linked recessive; a carrier mother (X^H X^h) and normal father (X^H Y) have a 50% chance that any male offspring will inherit X^h Y and have haemophilia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the definition of ‘Cold stress’ in a newborn as measured by the axillary temperature?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Neonatal 'cold stress' (mild hypothermia) is defined by an axillary temperature of 36.0°C to 36.4°C.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: What are the characteristics of ideal health indicators?
options: They should be valid, reliable, sensitive, specific, feasible and relevant
They should be mainly valid, reliable and sensitive but need not be specific
They should be mainly valid, reliable and feasible but need not be sensitive
They should be mainly valid, reliable and relevant but need not be feasible
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2018 Answer Key: Option (a) — They should be valid, reliable, sensitive, specific, feasible and relevant.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regarding predictive value of a positive test is true?
options: It does not tell about diagnostic power of test
The more prevalent the disease, the less accurate the test is
It tells the probability that a patient with positive test has the disease in question
It tells the probability that a patient with po sitive test does not have the disease in question
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2018 Answer Key: Option (c) — It tells the probability that a patient with positive test has the disease in question.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: The yield of a screening test CAN NOT be increased by which of the following?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Screening the entire low-risk general population lowers positive predictive value and yield compared with targeting high-risk groups or improving test sensitivity/specificity.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regarding the growth chart is NOT true?
options: It is used as a tool for growth monitoring and diagnosis
It is used for planning and policy making
It is used as tool for action against the Anganwadi worker
It is used as tool for teaching and evaluation of effectiveness of programme
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Road-to-Health growth chart is a tool for monitoring growth, education, policy planning, and programme evaluation—never a punitive tool against Anganwadi workers.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Flattening of the growth curve in the growth chart signifies:
options: Child is on a healthy path
Child is showing signs of growth failure
Child does not need special care
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A flattened growth curve on a child's growth chart indicates growth faltering/failure requiring nutritional intervention and closer follow-up.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
A well of contaminated water resulted in an outbreak of diarrhoea in a community. Which type of epidemic will this exposure present with?
1. Propagated epidemic
2. Common source – continuous exposure
3. Common source – point exposure
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ongoing use of a continuously contaminated community water well produces a common-source continuous-exposure epidemic.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following experiments/ trials is NOT a part of non-randomized trial?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Risk-factor intervention trials are randomized controlled trials, whereas uncontrolled trials, natural experiments, and before-and-after studies are non-randomized designs.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the relative risk of developing tuberculosis among tobacco users as per the information given below? Tobacco user Tuberculosis Total Yes No Yes 40 80 120 No 10 70 80 Total 50 150 200
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Incidence in tobacco users = 40/120 = 0.333; in non-users = 10/80 = 0.125. Relative Risk = 0.333 / 0.125 = 2.67.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the attributable risk of tobacco for developing tuberculosis as per the information given below? Tobacco users Tuberculosis Total Present Absent Yes 40 80 120 No 10 70 80 Total 50 150 200

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the sensitivity of EEG for detecting brain tumours as per the information given below? Brain tumour EEG result Absent Present Positive 54,000 36 Negative 3,06,000 4 3,60,000 40

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which sign is most important in deciding severe pneumonia in a child?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under classic IMNCI/ARI guidelines, lower chest wall indrawing in a child with cough/tachypnoea was the key clinical sign classifying severe pneumonia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Varicella-Zoster Immunoglobulin (VZIG) is NOT recommended for which of the exposed susceptible individuals?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: VZIG is reserved for high-risk susceptible contacts (newborns of infected mothers, immunocompromised/HIV, pregnant women) and is not needed for healthy siblings.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Carriers of avirulent organism are called:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pseudo-carriers harbour avirulent strains of a pathogen (e.g., non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae) and cannot transmit virulent disease.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A cohort study was conducted among 200 men aged 20–30 years in Rampur village. Out of 200, 120 men were tobacco users and rest 80 didn’t take any form of tobacco. At the end of one year, 40 men among tobacco users and 10 men among non -tobacco users developed tuberculosis. The incidence of tuberculosis among tobacco users is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Incidence among tobacco users = (40 / 120) × 100 = 33.3 per 100 men per year.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: The data regarding two exposures A and B, associated with a disease X in a community is given below: Exposure A Exposure B Relative risk 5 10 Attributable risk 80 % 90 % Population attributable risk 70 % 50 % Which one of the following assertions and the reasons given is correct?
options: Preference to control exposure B as it has a higher relative risk
Preference to control exposure A, because it has a higher population attribut able risk
Preference to control exposure B, because it has a higher attributable risk
Cannot decide, as the precedence of exposure in the community has not been mentioned
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2018 Answer Key: Option (b) — Preference to control exposure A, because it has a higher population attribut able risk.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following types of study designs will be most appropriate to find out the association between mobile phone radiation exposure and cancer?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: For rare outcomes like cancer with long latency after an exposure (mobile phone radiation), a retrospective case-control study is the most practical initial design.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
The villages A and B have the following age compositions: Age (years) Mid-year population (Village A) Mid-year population (Village B) 0–4 8000 4000 5–9 4000 2000 10–19 5000 3000 20–39 7000 8000 40–59 6000 6000 60 and above 7000 10000
Which of the following is the best indicator for comparing the death rates of these two villages?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: When comparing mortality between two villages with different age structures, the age-standardized (adjusted) death rate removes age confounding.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are suggested by rising incidence rates of any disease?
1. Need for a new disease control programme
2. Improvement in reporting practices
3. Change in the etiology of the disease
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Rising disease incidence can signal need for a new control programme (1), improved surveillance/reporting (2), or a shift in underlying aetiology (3).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: What constitutes the denominator in ‘Total Dependency Ratio’?
options: Population less than 14 and more than 65 years of age
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Total Dependency Ratio uses the economically productive population aged 15–64 years as its denominator.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A pregnant wom an in 2 nd trimester of pregnancy from North Eastern State has been diagnosed with uncomplicated P. falciparum. She should be treated with:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In North-Eastern India (where SP resistance is high), uncomplicated falciparum malaria in the 2nd/3rd trimester of pregnancy is treated with artemether-lumefantrine (ACT-AL).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: By which one of the following studies can relative risk be best calculated?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Relative risk (incidence in exposed divided by incidence in unexposed) is directly calculated from a prospective cohort study.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Orthotolidine (OT) test is done for determining residual free chlorine quantitatively and qualitatively. What is the colour of the solution after adding OT which indicates presence of free chlorine?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In the orthotolidine (OT) test, free residual chlorine reacts with orthotolidine to produce a yellow colour whose intensity is proportional to chlorine concentration.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following in respect of Navjat Shishu Suraksha Karyakram(NSSK): 1 It is a programme aimed to train health personnel in basic newborn care and resuscitation 2 It addresses care at birth issue ( i.e prevention of hypothermia, prevention of infection, early initiation of breastfeeding and basic newborn resuscitation ) 3 The objective is to have a trained health person in basic newborn care and resuscitation unit at every delivery point
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Navjat Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (NSSK) trains delivery-point health personnel (3) in essential newborn care at birth and basic neonatal resuscitation (1 and 2).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: The most important indicator for assessment of impact in Salt Iodization Programme is:
options: Testing Iodine content of salt at consumer level
Testing Iodine content of salt at production level
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Median urinary iodine excretion (UIE in µg/L) is the primary biochemical impact indicator for monitoring salt iodization programmes.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
