upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Caisson’s disease is usually seen in which group of workers?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Caisson's disease (decompression sickness / 'the bends') occurs in divers and compressed-air tunnel/caisson workers working below sea level.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: These toxic effects like abdominal colic, obstinate constipation, loss of appetite, anaemia, stippling of red cells and blue line on gums are due to exposure to:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Abdominal colic, obstinate constipation, anaemia, basophilic stippling of RBCs, and Burtonian blue gingival lines are classic for chronic lead poisoning (plumbism).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following conditions can be screened during neo natal screening by biochemical tests?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Congenital hypothyroidism is screened universally in newborns using dried blood-spot TSH/T4 biochemical testing.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a mass approach in health communication?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Folk methods, posters, and health exhibitions are mass communication approaches, whereas role play is a group/interpersonal teaching method.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are non –modifiable risk factors for hypertension?
1. Age
2. Sex
3. Genetic factors
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Age (1), sex (2), and genetic predisposition (3) are non-modifiable risk factors for systemic hypertension.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the correct daily dose of Iron and Folic acid to be prescribed to a child aged 12 years?
options: 20 mg elemental Iron and 100 mcg folic acid
30 mg elemental Iron and 250 mcg folic acid
60 mg elemental Iron and 300 mcg folic acid
100 mg elemental Iron and 500 mcg folic acid
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under WIFS/Anaemia Mukt Bharat for adolescents (10–19 years, here 12 years), the iron-folic acid tablet formulation is 100 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid (weekly prophylaxis; official key marks 100 mg + 500 µg).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: When should breastfeeding be initiated to an infant born via a normal delivery?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Breastfeeding should be initiated as soon as possible, within 1 hour of normal vaginal birth.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: As per biomedical waste management rule 2016 the metallic body implants should be discarded in which of the following?
options: Card board box with blue colored marking
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016, metallic body implants and glassware are segregated in puncture-proof boxes/containers with blue-coloured markings.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a quantitative method in the management of health services?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Management by Objectives (MBO) is a behavioural/qualitative management method, whereas network analysis (PERT/CPM), systems analysis, and PPBS are quantitative.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: India is in which stage of the demographic cycle?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: India is in the late expanding (third) stage of the demographic cycle, characterized by declining death rates and falling birth rates.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) that has been introduced in primary health centres helps in reducing which of the following indices?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) provides safe first-trimester abortion and post-abortion care at PHCs, directly reducing unsafe-abortion-related maternal mortality.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: The agreement (yes/no) between two observers is statistically measured by:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cohen's kappa (κ) coefficient measures inter-observer agreement for categorical (yes/no) ratings beyond chance.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: How many post natal visits should be made by the ANM to the house of a low birth weight baby?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under HBNC/IMNCI guidelines, 6 home visits (Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, and 42) are scheduled for institutional-born/LBW newborns (plus extra visits for LBW).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: The difference between Type A and Type B sub centre as per Indian Public Health standards is in terms of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under IPHS, Type B sub-centres have a labour room/MCH delivery facility (conducting ≥20 deliveries/month), whereas Type A sub-centres do not.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following Screening methods for Disease is the least useful?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Unselective mass screening of the entire general population has the lowest yield and highest cost-benefit inefficiency compared with high-risk or selective screening.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is an indicator for evaluation of impact of family planning?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Completed family size (alongside TFR/CBR/CPR) is a demographic impact indicator for evaluating family planning programmes.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following hemodynamic changes occurring during pregnancy:
1. Increase in cardiac output
2. Increase in stroke volume
3. Increase in colloid oncotic pressure
4. Increase in pulse rate
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Normal pregnancy increases cardiac output (1), stroke volume (2), and resting heart rate (4), while plasma colloid oncotic pressure decreases due to haemodilution.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the hypotheses for the onset of Labor?
1. Uterine distension
2. Activation of fetal hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis
3. Increase in prostaglandins
4. Increase in serum calcium levels
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hypotheses for labour onset include uterine stretch/distension (1), fetal HPA axis activation (2), and increased local prostaglandins (3).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of following statements regarding Puerperal sepsis are correct?
1. Multiple per vaginal examinations increase the risk
2. The responsible microorganisms are group A and B beta-haemolytic Streptococcus
3. Retained bits of placenta and membrane predispose
4. Vaginal packing can decrease the risk
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Puerperal sepsis is predisposed by multiple vaginal exams (1), retained placental/membrane bits (3), and Group A/B β-haemolytic streptococci (2) (vaginal packing increases infection risk).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
In case of Labour complicated with cord prolapse, which of the f ollowing statements are correct?
1. Reposition the patient in exaggerated Sims position
2. To replace the cord in the vagina
3. To replace the cord inside the uterus
4. Early amniotomy can prevent cord prolapse
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In umbilical cord prolapse, placing the mother in exaggerated Sims/Trendelenburg/knee-chest position (1) and keeping the cord moist in the vagina while elevating the presenting part (2) prevents compression until urgent CS.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: The following are the contents of broad ligament EXCEPT:
options: Uterine and ovarian arteries with their branches
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The broad ligament contains the fallopian tube, uterine/ovarian vessels, round ligament, ovarian ligament, and epoophoron—not the internal iliac artery (which lies retroperitoneally on the pelvic wall).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is true regarding normal menstrual physiology?
options: Ovulation occurs after 48 hours of LH surge
Oestradiol levels peak at 48 hours prior to ovulation
Ovulation occurs after 12 hours of LH peak
Threshold of LH surge generally persists for 48 hours
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ovulation occurs ~10–12 hours after the LH peak (and ~24–36 hours after the onset of the LH surge).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of Candida Vaginitis?
options: Pruritus is out of proportion to discharge
Yeast-buds and pseudohyphae forms can be seen under the microscope
Metronidazole is the treatment of choice
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Vulvovaginal candidiasis is treated with topical/oral azoles (clotrimazole, fluconazole), not metronidazole (which treats trichomoniasis and bacterial vaginosis).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a high risk factor for developing endometrial carcinoma?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Multiparity reduces lifetime unopposed oestrogen exposure and lowers endometrial carcinoma risk (unlike delayed menopause, obesity, and hypertension).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are the features of functional ovarian cyst EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Functional ovarian cysts (follicular/corpus luteum) are typically < 7 cm, unilocular, resolve spontaneously, and are usually asymptomatic (discovered incidentally).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Gestational trophoblastic disease is a spectrum comprising which of the following entities?
1. Complete Hydatidiform mole
2. Partial Hydatidiform mole
3. Invasive mole
4. Chorio carcinoma
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Gestational trophoblastic disease encompasses complete hydatidiform mole (1), partial mole (2), invasive mole (3), choriocarcinoma (4), and PSTT.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of Fothergill’s operation as a conservative surgery for uterovaginal prolapse?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Fothergill's (Manchester) operation comprises cervical amputation (1), cardinal ligament plication (2), and anterior/posterior colporrhaphy (3)—not abdominal cervicopexy.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT true regarding general physiological changes after delivery?
options: Pulse may be raised on first day
Blood volume returns to normal by second week
Cardiac output remains unchanged after delivery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cardiac output actually increases transiently immediately after delivery (due to autotransfusion from the contracted uterus and relieved IVC compression) before gradually returning to pre-pregnant levels.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider following statements regarding Beta Thalassemia in pregnancy:
1. There is low MCH and MCV
2. Total Iron binding capacity may be elevated or normal
3. HbA2 more than 3.5% is seen in Haemoglobin Electrophoresis
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Beta-thalassaemia trait in pregnancy shows low MCV/MCH (1), normal or elevated TIBC (2), and elevated HbA2 > 3.5% on electrophoresis (3).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A 20 year old Primigravida , comes at 35 weeks of gestation with complaints of swelling of feet. On examination her blood pres sure is 170/110 mm Hg on 2 occasions ; urine examination shows proteinur ia. Which one of the following statements regarding her management is NOT true?
options: Injection Dexamethasone is to be given for fetal lung maturity
Both maternal and fetal monitoring are required
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: At 35 weeks' gestation (≥34 weeks) with severe preeclampsia (BP 170/110 + proteinuria), prompt stabilization and delivery are indicated rather than delaying for antenatal corticosteroids (which are for < 34 weeks).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A 25 year old, G2P1L1 came with amenorrhoea of two and half months followed by bleeding PV and pain abdomen. On examination cervical OS is open with slight bleeding. The uterus is 10 weeks size with no tenderness in the fornices. The probable clinical diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Amenorrhoea of 10 weeks with vaginal bleeding, lower abdominal pain, and an open cervical os with a 10-week uterus indicates inevitable abortion.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statement s regarding intrauterine growth restriction is NOT correct?
options: There is danger of fetal asphyxia during delivery
Generally not seen in women with gestational diabetes
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: IUGR is defined by estimated fetal weight or abdominal circumference < 10th percentile for gestational age, not solely by biparietal diameter.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A 15 year old girl comes to the gynae casualty with a relative with complains of amenorrhoea 2 months. The urine pregnancy test is positive, ultrasound confirms 8 weeks pregnancy. The attendants are not willing to file a police case. What should the treating doctor do?
options: Take consent for abortion and proceed
Inform the police and make MLC
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under India's POCSO Act, pregnancy in a minor (< 18 years, here 15 years) mandates medico-legal case (MLC) documentation and reporting to the police alongside clinical care.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for use of oral contraceptive pills?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Migraine with aura / focal neurological symptoms ('focal migraine') is an absolute (WHO MEC Category 4) contraindication to oestrogen-containing combined oral contraceptives due to ischaemic stroke risk.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: The amount of Ethinyl Estradiol in third generation combined oral contraceptive pills is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Third-generation low-dose combined oral contraceptive pills contain 20–30 µg of ethinyl oestradiol.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following clinical situation s is NOT ideal to perform female sterilization procedure?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Postpartum tubal sterilization is ideally performed within 24–48 hours (up to 7 days max, though 7 days postpartum uterus is involuting/suboptimal; official key marks 7 days postpartum as not ideal).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Cardiac diseases in pregnancy which have major risk of maternal mortality are
1. Pulmonary hypertension
2. Aortic coarctation with valvular involvement
3. Atrial septal defect
4. Mitral stenosis
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (1) and coarctation of the aorta with valvular/aortic involvement (2) carry the highest maternal mortality (mWHO Class IV).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Pregnancy can be terminated at any gestation if the fetus is diagnosed to have:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Anencephaly is an invariably lethal neural tube defect compatible with termination at any gestation under medical/legal provisions.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a cause of recurrent spontaneous abortion?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chromosomal abnormalities, antiphospholipid syndrome, and thrombophilias cause recurrent spontaneous abortion, whereas acute rubella causes sporadic miscarriage/CRS rather than recurrent abortion.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
The congenital abnormality which is invariably lethal is:
1. Anencephaly
2. Transposition of great vessel
3. Down Syndrome
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Anencephaly (absence of forebrain and calvarium) is invariably lethal in the perinatal period (unlike TGA and Down syndrome).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
For vaginal breech delivery, ideal selection criteria would include:
1. Fetus not compromised
2. Adequate pelvis
3. Extended breech presentation
4. Estimated fetal weight < 3.5 kg
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Safe vaginal breech delivery requires a non-compromised fetus (1), clinically adequate pelvis (2), frank/extended breech (3), and estimated fetal weight < 3.5 kg (4).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following presentations:
1. Brow presentation
2. Left mento anterior position
3. Occipito posterior position
4. Breech presentation In which of the above Vaginal delivery is NOT possible?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Persistent brow presentation engages the mentovertical diameter (13.5 cm), making vaginal delivery impossible in a term average-sized fetus (unlike mentoanterior face, OP, or selected breech).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
The blood supply of uterus is from:
1. Uterine artery
2. Ovarian artery
3. Pudendal artery
4. Superior vesical artery
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The uterus receives its arterial blood supply from the uterine arteries (1; main) and ovarian arteries (2; anastomosing via the utero-ovarian arcade).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following regarding amniotic fluid is true?
options: The volume is highest at 28 weeks
It reveals information about fetal lung maturity and wellbeing
It is decreased in duodenal atresia in baby
It is decreased in gestational diabetes
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Amniotic fluid assessment (lecithin/sphingomyelin ratio, phosphatidylglycerol, AFI) provides key information on fetal lung maturity and fetal well-being (peaks at ~34–38 weeks and increases in duodenal atresia/GDM).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding changes in pregnancy:
1. Plasma volume increases up to 30–50%
2. Pregnancy is a hypercoagulable state
3. Hematocrit is decreased
4. Total plasma proteins increases
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In normal pregnancy, plasma volume expands 30–50% (1), clotting factors rise creating a hypercoagulable state (2), haematocrit falls due to haemodilution (3), and total circulating plasma protein mass increases (4).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements regarding anatomy of fetal head is NOT true?
options: Coronal suture separates frontal bones from parietal bones
Lambdoid suture separates the two parietal bones
Bregma is a diamond shaped space at junction of coronal and sagittal sutures
Frontal suture separates the two frontal bones
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2018 Answer Key: Option (b) — Lambdoid suture separates the two parietal bones Bregma is a diamond shaped space at junction of coronal and sagittal sutures.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
A 30 year old lady, mother of 3 children presents with mass descending per vaginum. On examination it is found to have stage 3 prolapse, moderate cystocele, no posterior vaginal wall prolapse. The recommended surgery would be:
1. Cystocele repair
2. Rectocele repair
3. Manchester operation
4. Vaginal hysterectomy
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a young 30-year-old woman wishing to preserve her uterus with Stage 3 prolapse and moderate cystocele, Manchester (Fothergill's) operation (3) with anterior colporrhaphy/cystocele repair (1) is recommended.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A 50 year old post menopausal woman comes with complaints of bleeding per vaginum . Which one of the following investigations is NOT required?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Postmenopausal bleeding requires Pap smear, endometrial biopsy, and hysteroscopy to exclude endometrial/cervical malignancy, not diagnostic laparoscopy.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements regarding β -Human chorionic Gonadotropin are NOT correct?
1. It is a glycoprotein hormone.
2. Serum levels increase in pregnancy, germ cells tumor and gestational t rophoblastic disease
3. Its levels are same in single and multiple pregnancy
4. It has common and Alpha-sub unit with other hormones FSH, LH and TSH.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Serum β-hCG levels are significantly higher (not the same) in multiple gestation compared with singleton pregnancy (and note official key marks 1, 2 and 3).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT an emergency contraception method?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Norplant (levonorgestrel subdermal implant) is a long-acting reversible contraceptive, not an emergency postcoital contraceptive method.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following statements are correct about vasectomy EXCEPT:
options: No Scalpel Vasectomy (NSV) was first developed in China.
It increases the incidence of testicular cancer
It is less time consuming than tubectomy
Addition contraception should be used for 3 months after vasectomy
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Vasectomy has no causal association with testicular or prostate cancer (Statement b is false).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the statement regarding anemia in pregnancy is NOT true?
options: Iron deficiency anemia is most common in Tropics
Faulty dietary habit is one of the factors responsible for anemia
II mother is severely anemic, the fetus is also severely anemic
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The fetus acts as an efficient parasite for maternal iron via active placental transfer, so even when the mother is severely anaemic, the newborn's haemoglobin is usually normal at birth.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements about male sterilization is NOT true?
options: It is safer and less expensive
It has a low failure rate
It is performed under general anaesthesia
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: No-scalpel vasectomy is routinely performed as an outpatient procedure under local infiltration anaesthesia, not general anaesthesia.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a method of second Trimester abortion?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intra-amniotic KCl injection is used for feticide in multifetal pregnancy reduction or late termination, not as a standard standalone second-trimester abortion method.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: In the process of MTP ( Medical Termination of Pregnancy) done by suction and evacuation, it was realized that perforation of uterus occurred with cannula. The next step should be:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Suspected uterine perforation with a suction cannula during MTP risks bowel or vascular injury and requires immediate diagnostic laparoscopy/laparotomy with bowel exploration.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding MTP (Medical Termination of Pregnancy):
1. Suction and evacuation can be done up till 12 weeks.
2. Medical methods can be used up till 10 weeks
3. Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) syringe can be used up to 6 weeks
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Suction and evacuation is safely performed up to 12 weeks' gestation (1); medical abortion is approved up to 7–9 weeks (not 10), and MVA up to 12 weeks.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Cellulitis is:
options: A suppurative invasive infection of skin and subcutaneous tissues
A nonsuppurative invasive infection of tissues
Infection caused by Gram negative bacilli
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cellulitis is an acute, spreading, non-suppurative bacterial infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue (usually caused by Streptococcus pyogenes).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Following are the factors for increased risk of wound infection EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Good local blood supply promotes healing and resists infection, whereas malnutrition, diabetes/uraemia, and immunosuppression increase SSI risk.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A 25 year old lady underwent exploratory laparotomy for bowel injury which happened while she underwent medical termination of pregnancy 2 days back. 24 hours after exploratory laparotomy her pulse is 106/m, respiratory rate 26/m, total leucocyte count 14000/cumm with blood urea 84 mg% and serum creatinine 2.0 mg/dL. The lady is having:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Postoperative bowel-injury peritonitis with SIRS (HR 106, RR 26, WBC 14,000) plus acute kidney injury (urea 84, creatinine 2.0) defines sepsis syndrome (severe sepsis).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A 22 year old young man came with history of occasional bleeding per rectum. On colonoscopy, numerous sessile polyps were seen in descending and sigmoid colon. On family history his elder brother was operated for thyroid malignancy. The young man should be advised:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Numerous colonic polyps with a family history of thyroid cancer suggest familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), warranting prophylactic panproctocolectomy to prevent inevitable colorectal cancer.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A 47 year old post menopausal lady was on adjuvant hormonal treatment with T amoxifen for 3 years for Carcinoma Breast. She came to O utpatient Department with history of passing blood clots per vagina. She is probably suffering from:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Tamoxifen exerts partial oestrogenic agonist effects on the endometrium, increasing the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial carcinoma presenting with postmenopausal bleeding.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following regarding blood supply of rectum is NOT true?
options: Superior rectal artery is a direct continuation of Inferior mesenteric artery
Middle rectal artery arises from external iliac artery and passes through the lateral ligaments into rectum
Inferior rectal artery arises from internal pudendal artery
Inferior rectal artery traverses the Alcock’s canal into rectum
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2018 Answer Key: Option (b) — Middle rectal artery arises from external iliac artery and passes through the lateral ligaments into rectum.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Gastric conduit after oesophageal resection is based upon:
options: Short gastric vessels and Vasa brevia
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: During oesophagectomy with gastric pull-up, the mobilized gastric conduit relies primarily on the right gastroepiploic artery arcade.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: A 70 year old male having comorbidities present with benign appearing parotoid tumour. The best option is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a 70-year-old comorbid patient with a benign-appearing parotid mass, fine-needle aspiration cytology (aspiration biopsy) confirms the histology before deciding on surgery or observation.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Fine Needle A spiration Cytology (FNAC) is NOT conclusive in which one of the following thyroid swellings?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: FNAC cannot distinguish benign follicular adenoma from follicular carcinoma because malignancy requires demonstrating capsular or vascular invasion on histopathology.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Patients with phlebographically confirmed deep vein thrombosis of the calf:
options: can expect asyptomatic recovery if treated promptly with anticoagulant
may be effectively treated with low-dose heparin
may be effectively treated with pneumatic compression stockings
are at risk for significant pulmonary embolism
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Confirmed deep vein thrombosis (including calf DVT) carries a risk of proximal propagation and potentially fatal pulmonary embolism, requiring full therapeutic anticoagulation.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Herceptin (Trastuzumab) is an immunotherapeuctic agent used for:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Trastuzumab (Herceptin) is a humanized anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody used in HER2-positive breast cancer (and gastric cancer).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Mainstay of an accurate diagnosis of pancreatic injury following blunt abdominal trauma is:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen is the mainstay for diagnosing and grading pancreatic injury in haemodynamically stable blunt trauma patients.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Pancreatic pseudocysts developing complications are best managed by:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Complicated pancreatic pseudocysts (bleeding, rupture, infection, or refractory obstruction) traditionally require surgical internal drainage/intervention (or endoscopic/IR drainage).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following regarding absorbable meshes is NOT true?
options: They are made of polygycolic acid fibre
They are used in temporary abdominal wall closure
They are used to buttress sutured repair
They show very good results as collagen deposition is maximum
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Absorbable meshes (polyglactin/polyglycolic acid) dissolve rapidly and do not promote durable collagen scar strength, leading to high hernia recurrence rates (Statement d is false).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT a surgical modality for management of femoral hernia?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Lytle's operation (narrowing the deep inguinal ring) is used for indirect inguinal hernia, whereas Lotheissen's, McEvedy's, and Lockwood's are classic femoral hernia repairs.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: “Triangle of Doom” dissected and seen during Laparoscopic inguinal hernia r epair is bounded by all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The 'triangle of doom' is bounded by the vas deferens medially, spermatic vessels laterally, and peritoneal reflection inferiorly—not the inferior epigastric artery.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Antro-chonal polyp always arises from:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An antrochoanal (Killian) polyp originates from the mucosa of the maxillary antrum/sinus and extends posteriorly through the ostium into the nasopharynx.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Paralytic ileus is a type of:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Paralytic ileus is a functional, adynamic intestinal obstruction caused by impaired neuromuscular peristalsis without a mechanical blockage.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Indication of Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is:
options: More than 25% stenosis of critical left main stem
More than 25% stenosis of proximal left anterior interventricular artery
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Significant triple-vessel coronary artery disease (and >50% left main stenosis) is a classic Class I indication for CABG.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Normal anatomical narrowing of ureter are present in all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The three normal anatomical constrictions of the ureter are the pelvi-ureteric junction, the pelvic brim (crossing the common/external iliac vessels, not the abdominal aorta), and the ureterovesical junction/orifice.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is NOT correct regarding Adenocarcinoma of the kidney ?
options: It is also called Grawitz tumour
It may be associated with Pyrexia of unknown origin
Renal vein extention may embolize to lungs
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Renal cell carcinoma (Grawitz tumour) presents with the classic triad (haematuria, flank pain, mass) in only ~10% of cases and does not always present with haematuria.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following regarding abdominal paediatric surgery is correct?
options: Transverse abdominal incision is always used
Incision can be closed with absorbable suture
Bowel must be always anastomosed in double layer
Skin over abdomen can never be closed with subcuticular sutures
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In paediatric abdominal surgery, fascial incisions can be closed cleanly with delayed-absorbable sutures (e.g., PDS/Vicryl), and single-layer anastomosis and subcuticular skin closure are standard.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Genetic disorder predisposing patients to develop Berry aneurysm includes all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: ADPKD, fibromuscular dysplasia, and Marfan/Ehlers-Danlos syndromes predispose to intracranial berry aneurysms, unlike Neurofibromatosis Type II.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following regarding Nasal polyps is NOT true?
options: Nasal polyps are very painful to touch
Meningocele must be excluded in children with polyps
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Simple ethmoidal nasal polyps are insensitive/painless to touch (not very painful), bilateral, pale, and mobile.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Allen’s test is used in Cardiac surgery:
options: To select finger prick for blood glucose estimation
When radial artery harvest is planned
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The modified Allen's test confirms adequate ulnar collateral palmar blood flow before harvesting the radial artery for CABG or arterial cannulation.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: In a lateral facial wound, if facial nerve injury is suspected, it should be:
options: Skin and subcutaneous flaps to be raised to cover the cut ends
Secondary repair using microscope gives best result
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Suspected facial nerve transection in a fresh lateral facial wound should undergo immediate primary microsurgical neurorrhaphy (within 72 hours while distal ends can still be stimulated).

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Radiologic views used for fracture Mandible (body and Ramus) are all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mandibular body and ramus fractures are evaluated with OPG, lateral oblique, and occlusal views, whereas submentovertex view evaluates the zygomatic arches and skull base.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Mallory-Weiss tear causing haematemesis is seen over:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mallory-Weiss syndrome is a longitudinal mucosal laceration at the gastro-oesophageal junction (cardia) caused by forceful retching/vomiting.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following factors is NOT involved in the pathogenesis of Systematic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS)?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: SIRS pathogenesis is driven by cytokine release, abnormal nitric oxide synthesis, and free radical injury—not primary microvascular occlusion.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Sleeve Gastrectomy done for Morbid obesity is a:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy is a restrictive bariatric procedure that reduces gastric volume by ~80% without intestinal bypass.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Pre-operative Nutrition Screening in a patient with morbid obe sity planned for Gastric Bypass includes all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Preoperative nutritional screening before gastric bypass checks magnesium, calcium/vitamin D, vitamin B12, iron, and folate—not routine serum insulin.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: In postoperative care the long term risks after Bariatric Surgery include all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Long-term bariatric surgery complications include protein-calorie malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies, and weight regain, whereas DVT is an acute/early postoperative complication.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Hilton’s method of Incision and drainage of abscess has the advantage of:
options: Avoids injury to underlying vessels and nerves
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hilton's method (blunt sinus-forceps opening after skin incision) safely drains deep abscesses in neurovascularly dense areas (neck, axilla, groin) without injuring underlying vessels or nerves.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Indications of computed tomography after head injury include all EXCEPT:
options: Glasgow Coma Scale < 13 at any point
Mild head injury in a 50 year old man
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: GCS < 13, open depressed skull fracture, and post-traumatic amnesia > 30 min are NICE indications for head CT, whereas mild head injury without risk factors in a 50-year-old (< 65 years) does not require CT.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Mondor’s disease is:
options: Thrombophlebitis of superficial veins of the breast and anterior chest wall
Other name for tuberculosis of breast
Rare type of chronic intramammary abscess
Named after the scientist who first coined the term “Actinomycosis of Breast”
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2018 Answer Key: Option (a) — Thrombophlebitis of superficial veins of the breast and anterior chest wall.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Sengstaken-Blakemore tube is used to control bleeding in:
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Sengstaken-Blakemore (or Minnesota) balloon tamponade tube is used as a temporizing measure to control life-threatening bleeding oesophageal/gastric varices.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following regarding Pancreatic effusion is correct?
options: Free fluid collection in Pleural cavity
Pancreatic stenting is to be done
Percutaneous drainage under image guidance is necessary
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Large symptomatic pancreatic fluid/effusion collections are drained percutaneously under ultrasound or CT image guidance.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following bone is affected in Keinbock’s disease?
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Kienböck's disease is idiopathic avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) of the carpal lunate bone.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following regarding management of acute wounds is NOT true?
options: The whole patient should be examined according to ATLS principles
Wounds should be examined, taking into consideration site and structures damaged
Bleeding wounds should be elevated and a pressure pad applied
Clamps should be used to stop all bleeding vessels
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Blindly applying haemostatic clamps inside acute wounds risks crushing adjacent nerves and vessels; direct pressure and elevation should be used first.

upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.text: Risk Scoring System which can be used post operatively is:
options: POSSUM → Physiologic and operative severity Score for enUmeration of Mortality and Morbidity
upsc-cms-2018-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2018 Answer Key: Option (d) — POSSUM → Physiologic and operative severity Score for enUmeration of Mortality and Morbidity.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT correct?
options: Hepatitis A does not lead to massive hepatic necrosis
Hepatitis B vaccination is part of universal childhood vaccination
Hepatitis C is commonest cause of transfusion transmitted hepatitis
Hepatitis E carries very high mortality in pregnant women
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hepatitis A can rarely cause fulminant hepatic failure with massive hepatic necrosis (especially in older adults or chronic liver disease; Statement a is false).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following antihypertensive drugs is contraindicated in pregnancy?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: ACE inhibitors like ramipril are teratogenic (fetal renal dysplasia, oligohydramnios) and strictly contraindicated throughout pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following least predisposes to infective endocarditis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Low-pressure secundum atrial septal defects (ASD) have minimal turbulence across the defect and carry the lowest risk of infective endocarditis compared with VSD, PDA, and TOF.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 60 year old male with Marfan’s syndrom e comes to emergency department with severe generalised tearing pain localised to chest anteriorly and in ter scapular region, sweating and weakness. On examination, his BP is 200/140 mm Hg. X ray chest shows widening of superior mediastinum. EC G shows sinus tachycar dia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Severe tearing interscapular chest pain, hypertension (200/140 mmHg), and widened superior mediastinum on CXR in a Marfan's patient are classic for acute aortic dissection.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient who is allergic to penicillin can be prescribed which of the following drugs for prophylaxis of acute rheumatic fever?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Erythromycin (or sulfadiazine) is the recommended alternative for secondary prophylaxis of rheumatic fever in penicillin-allergic patients.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: QT interval is prolonged in:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypocalcaemia prolongs the ST segment and the QT interval on ECG (whereas hyperkalaemia, hypermagnesaemia, and digoxin shorten QT).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Differential cyanosis is seen in:
options: Atrial septal defect with pulmonary arterial hypertension
Ventricular septal defect with pulmonary arterial hypertension
Patent ductus arteriosuswith pulmonary arterial hypertension
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Patent ductus arteriosus with Eisenmenger pulmonary hypertension reverses shunting distal to the left subclavian artery, producing cyanosis and clubbing in the toes but not the fingers (differential cyanosis).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Wilson’s disease is characterised by all EXCEPT:
options: Deposition of copper in Descemet’s membrane
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wilson's disease features decreased (not increased) serum caeruloplasmin along with elevated hepatic copper, increased urinary copper, and corneal Kayser-Fleischer rings.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Following drugs are used for H.Pylori eradication EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: H. pylori eradication regimens combine PPIs with amoxicillin, clarithromycin, metronidazole, tetracycline, or bismuth—never first-generation cephalosporins like cephalexin.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 45 year old female comes to you with dysphagia. She is found to have anaemia and koilonychia. Most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Middle-aged woman with dysphagia, iron-deficiency anaemia, and koilonychia (spoon nails) is classic for Plummer-Vinson (Paterson-Kelly) syndrome.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Chest tube insertion should be considered in a patient with parapneumonic effusion include the following EXCEPT:
options: Positive Gram stain/culture of pleural fluid
Pleural effusion is less than 10 mm thickness on decubitus
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Small parapneumonic effusions (< 10 mm thickness on lateral decubitus X-ray) resolve with antibiotics alone and do not require chest tube insertion.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient underwent hip replacement surgery. On fourth post-operative day, he had dyspnoea, pleuritic pain and haemoptysis. Most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, and haemoptysis on postoperative day 4 after hip replacement surgery indicate acute pulmonary embolism.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 55 year old male with a history of ch ronic obstructive pulmonary disease was rushed to emergency department with in creasing shortness of breath, fever and a productive cough with yellow green sputum . He has difficulty in communicating because of his inability to complete a se ntence. Measurement of arterial blood gas shows pH 7.3, PaCO 2 68 mmHg, HCO3 28 mmol/L, and PaO 2 60 mmHg. How would you interpret this?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: pH 7.30 (acidaemia), PaCO2 68 mmHg (elevated), and mildly elevated HCO3- 28 mmol/L indicate partially compensated respiratory acidosis in acute-on-chronic COPD exacerbation.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 40 years old woman presents with hematu ria, ecchymoses and menorrhagia of six months duration. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Mucocutaneous bleeding (ecchymoses, menorrhagia, haematuria) for 6 months in a 40-year-old woman points to idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following heavy metal poisoning strictly affects motor nerve ?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic lead toxicity classically causes a pure motor peripheral neuropathy (wrist drop and foot drop) without sensory loss.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient develops skin necrosis 3 days af ter being started on warfarin for deep vein thrombosis. What is the most likely cause?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis occurring 3–5 days after starting warfarin without heparin bridging is caused by underlying inherited Protein C deficiency (rapid drop in short-half-life Protein C).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 15 year old boy is brought to emergenc y with two days history of headache, vomiting and altered sensorium. His BP is 70 mmHg systolic and he has ecchymoses on his skin. Most likely organism causing his condition is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Headache, vomiting, altered sensorium, septic shock (BP 70 systolic), and cutaneous ecchymoses/purpura in a teenager are diagnostic of meningococcaemia (Neisseria meningitidis).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A child presents with episode of hematuria soon after respiratory tract infection. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Synpharyngitic gross haematuria occurring within 1–3 days of an upper respiratory tract infection in a child is classic for IgA nephropathy (Berger's disease).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: In microalbuminuria, 24 hours urinary albumin is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Microalbuminuria (moderately increased albuminuria) is defined as 24-hour urinary albumin excretion of 30–300 mg/day.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Following are complications of acute renal failure EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute renal failure causes intravascular volume overload, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis (not metabolic alkalosis).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Deficiency of which vitamin causes subacute combined degeneration of spinal cord?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) deficiency causes demyelination of the dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts, known as subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Obstructive lung function tests are seen in which of the following conditions?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Bronchial asthma produces an obstructive ventilatory defect (reduced FEV1/FVC), whereas obesity, kyphoscoliosis, and pleural effusion cause restrictive defects.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: In which of the following conditions is there an increase in lung diffusion capacity?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is spuriously increased in alveolar haemorrhage because intra-alveolar haemoglobin binds inhaled CO.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Omalizumab is a blocking antibody that neutralises circulating IgE
Omalizumab is a newer long acting anticholinergic agent
Omalizumab is once a day long acting beta-2 agonistic
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Omalizumab is a humanized anti-IgE monoclonal antibody that binds free circulating IgE, preventing mast cell and basophil sensitization.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Widespread concave ST segment elevation and PR depression in most leads except aVR lead favours the diagnosis of:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Diffuse concave-upward ST-segment elevation with PR-segment depression (and opposite changes in aVR) is diagnostic of acute pericarditis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A known case of lepromatous leprosy wa s initiated on treatment. She developed painful erythmatous papules with fever and lymphadenopathy. What is the likely reactional state?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 lepra reaction) is an immune-complex-mediated reaction in lepromatous leprosy causing tender erythematous nodules/papules, fever, and lymphadenopathy.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not true regarding congestive cardiac failure in the elderly?
options: Common causes include coronary artery disease and hypertension
Loop diuretics are usually well tolerated
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Elderly heart failure patients are prone to electrolyte disturbances, orthostatic hypotension, and prerenal azotaemia from aggressive diuresis—making loop diuretics poorly tolerated if overused (Statement d is false).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Multidrug resistant tuberculosis is defined as:
options: At least resistance to three or more antitubercular drugs
At least resistance to Isoniazid, Streptomycin and Ethambutol
At least resistance to Isoniazid and Rifampicin
At least resistance to Streptomycin and Rifampicin
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) is defined by resistance to at least the two most potent first-line drugs: isoniazid and rifampicin.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Aortic stenosis is associated with:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Severe aortic stenosis produces a slow-rising, delayed, low-volume carotid pulse known as pulsus parvus et tardus.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following is associated with hypercoagulable state?
1. Protein C deficiency
2. Antiphospholipid syndrome
3. Homocysteinemia
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Protein C deficiency (1), antiphospholipid syndrome (2), and hyperhomocysteinaemia (3) are all established thrombophilias causing a hypercoagulable state.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 20 year old male walked into outpatient department with high grade fever, cough and chest pain for one day. Chest X-ray show ed consolidation of left upper zone. His respiratory rate is 22/minute, pulse rate 96/minute, BP systolic 120 mmHg and blood urea 18 mg/dl. What is his CURB score?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: CURB-65/CURB score: no Confusion (0), Urea 18 mg/dL (<42 mg/dL = 0), RR 22 (<30 = 0), BP 120 systolic (>90 = 0), age 20 (<65 = 0) → Total CURB score = 0.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following conditions is an autosomal dominant disorder?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Marfan syndrome (FBN1 mutation) is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait (G6PD is X-linked; sickle cell and Fanconi anaemia are autosomal recessive).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the treatment of bronchial asthma:
1. Tablets of β2 adrenoceptor agonist are better than aerosol therapy
2. Inhaled corticosteroids are contraindicated in acute severe asthma
3. Oral steroids may be necessary for severe acute asthma
4. Anticholinergic bronchodilators are muscarinic antagonists 5. Salmeterol and formoterol are hi ghly selective and potent long acting β2 adrenoceptor agonists
Which of the statements given above are true?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In asthma, systemic oral steroids are needed for severe exacerbations (3), anticholinergics are muscarinic antagonists (4), and salmeterol/formoterol are potent LABAs (5) (aerosol therapy is superior to tablets, and ICS are not contraindicated).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Acute massive pulmonary embolism is manifested by the following EXCEPT:
options: Pulmonary opacities in chest X ray
Reduced cardiac output and acute right heart failure
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The chest X-ray in acute pulmonary embolism is frequently normal or shows oligaemia (Westermark sign) rather than pulmonary opacities.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: The side effects of isoniazid include the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Isoniazid causes hepatitis, rash, and peripheral neuropathy (prevented by pyridoxine), whereas hyperuricaemia is caused by pyrazinamide and ethambutol.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
A patient of COPD develops a large pneum othorax during a violent bout of coughing. The most appropriate management would be:
1. Simple aspiration
2. Tube thoracostomy
3. Pleurodesis
Which of the above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A large secondary spontaneous pneumothorax in COPD requires tube thoracostomy (2) and pleurodesis (3) to prevent fatal recurrence.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Carbon dioxide tension (PaCO2) in arterial blood at sea level is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Normal arterial carbon dioxide tension (PaCO2) at sea level is 35–45 mmHg.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: The volume of fresh air entering the alveoli each minute is called as:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Alveolar ventilation is the volume of fresh inspired air reaching the gas-exchanging alveoli per minute: (Tidal Volume − Dead Space) × Respiratory Rate.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Exacerbations of bronchial asthma that occur with little or no warning are called:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Brittle asthma is characterized by sudden, severe, life-threatening asthma exacerbations occurring with little or no warning despite therapy.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following constituents of antacid can cause constipation?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Aluminium hydroxide antacids delay gastric emptying and classically cause constipation (whereas magnesium salts cause diarrhoea).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: “TIPS” procedure in the treatment of cirrhosis liver stands for:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: TIPS stands for Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt, creating a conduit between the hepatic vein and portal vein to relieve portal hypertension.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: The drug of choice in the treatment of oesophageal candidiasis is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oral/IV fluconazole is the systemic antifungal of choice for oesophageal candidiasis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding neuroleptic malignant syndrome?
options: Characterized by muscle rigidity and hyperthermia
There is stimulation of central dopamine receptors in hypothalamus
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is caused by blockade (not stimulation) of central D2 dopamine receptors by antipsychotics like haloperidol.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Type IV renal tubular acidosis may be caused by all of the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Type IV (hyperkalaemic) renal tubular acidosis is caused by hypoaldosteronism from heparin, NSAIDs, and trimethoprim/ACE inhibitors—not penicillin.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Treatment options available for management of renal artery stenosis is/are:
options: Medical treatment for hypertension by antihypertensive drugs
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Renal artery stenosis can be managed medically with antihypertensives, via percutaneous angioplasty/stenting (especially in fibromuscular dysplasia), or surgical revascularization.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A reversible cause of dementia is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic subdural haematoma is a classic treatable/reversible cause of dementia, unlike neurodegenerative Alzheimer's, Huntington's, and Parkinson's diseases.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: In Wallenberg syndrome, where is the site of lesion?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wallenberg's (lateral medullary) syndrome results from infarction of the lateral medulla (usually PICA/vertebral artery occlusion).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: The following are features of polycythaemia vera EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In polycythaemia vera, autonomous erythropoiesis suppresses plasma erythropoietin (EPO is low, not elevated).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following conditions is associated with cigarette smoking?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Desquamative interstitial pneumonia (DIP) and respiratory bronchiolitis-ILD are smoking-related interstitial lung diseases.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT true of Wilson disease?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In Wilson's disease, defective ATP7B impairs copper incorporation into apocaeruloplasmin, causing low (not increased) serum caeruloplasmin.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 55 year old patient on treatment for pul monary tuberculosis with Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide and Ethambutol complain of pain in large and small joints. Which one of the following investigations will you order?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pyrazinamide inhibits renal tubular urate excretion, causing hyperuricaemia and gouty arthralgia; serum uric acid should be checked.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: The following diseases can cause bullous lesions in the skin EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pemphigus, bullous impetigo, and toxic epidermal necrolysis cause blistering/bullous skin lesions, whereas pityriasis rosea presents with non-bullous scaly oval plaques.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following disorder is autosomal recessive?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cystic fibrosis is autosomal recessive, whereas nail-patella syndrome, myotonic dystrophy, and Huntington disease are autosomal dominant.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the most a ppropriate treatment for overdose aspirin ingestion?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Intravenous sodium bicarbonate alkalinizes both serum (limiting CNS salicylate entry) and urine (enhancing renal salicylate excretion) in aspirin overdose.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Killer T cells which are responsible for de fence against intracellular pathogen are expressed by which of the following CD phenotypes?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cytotoxic (killer) T lymphocytes express the CD8 surface co-receptor and recognize antigen presented on MHC Class I.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Intravenous immunoglobulin therapy is approved in the following conditions EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: IVIg is established/approved for Kawasaki disease, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and dermatomyositis, but has no role in severe rheumatoid arthritis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following does NOT cause small vessel vasculitis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Kawasaki disease is a medium-vessel vasculitis (affecting coronary arteries), whereas EGPA (Churg-Strauss), IgA vasculitis (HSP), and GPA are small-vessel vasculitides.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Most common cells in peripheral blood smear of chronic myeloid leukemia are:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic myeloid leukaemia shows marked leukocytosis with the entire myeloid maturation spectrum on peripheral smear, dominated by mature neutrophils and myelocytes.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements about infective endocarditis:
1. Modified Duke criteria are used for clinical diagnosis
2. Echocardiographic findings form one of the major Duke criteria
3. Presence of one major and two minor criter ia is considered as diagnostic of endocarditis
4. Presence of glomerulonephritis is a minor Duke criterion
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Modified Duke criteria diagnose definite infective endocarditis with 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor (not 2 minor), or 5 minor criteria; echocardiography is major (2) and glomerulonephritis is minor (4).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 16 year old had an acute episode of dyspnoea, wheezing and coughing during early morning hours. The episode resolved spontaneously. What is the likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Recurrent early-morning dyspnoea, wheezing, and cough that resolves spontaneously in a 16-year-old is classic for bronchial asthma.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
An elderly patient had cerebrovascular accid ent which was diagnosed as ischaemic in nature. Which of the following is a contraindication for thrombolysis?
1. Onset of symptoms to time of drug administration is ≤ 4.5 hours
2. Gastrointestinal bleeding in preceding 21 days
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Recent gastrointestinal bleeding within the preceding 21 days is an absolute contraindication to IV thrombolysis in acute ischaemic stroke (4.5 hours is within the therapeutic window).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following insulin preparations:
1. Aspart
2. Glulisine
3. Detemir
4. Regular
Which of the above are considered short acting insulin?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Aspart (1), glulisine (2), and regular insulin (4) are rapid/short-acting insulins, whereas detemir is a long-acting basal analogue.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A middle aged male known smoker presente d with recurrent sinusitis, haemoptysis, haematuria, arthralgia and palpable purpura. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Recurrent sinusitis, haemoptysis, haematuria (glomerulonephritis), arthralgia, and palpable purpura in a middle-aged man are classic for granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener's).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient presents with diarrhoea, steatorrhea and weight loss. Which of the following diseases is LEAST possible?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Whipple's disease, tropical sprue, and coeliac disease cause small-bowel malabsorption with steatorrhoea, whereas Ménétrier's disease is a protein-losing gastropathy without steatorrhoea.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN) :
1. Immunosupressive therapy is effective
2. PSGN develops one to three weeks after streptococcal pharyngitis
3. PSGN develops two to six weeks after impetigo
4. The classic presentation is acute nephritis
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: PSGN follows pharyngitis by 1–3 weeks (2) or impetigo by 2–6 weeks (3) and presents as acute nephritic syndrome (4); treatment is supportive (immunosuppression is ineffective).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient with long term impl antable cardioverter defibrillator device developed neck and facial swelling, hoarseness of voice, nasal congestion, dysphagia and haemoptysis. The facial swelling increased on supine position. This patient most likely developed:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Face/neck swelling worsened when supine, hoarseness, and venous congestion in a patient with a long-term transvenous ICD lead indicate superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient of AIDS developed ophthalmopleg ia, ataxia and global confusion. He is likely to have the deficiency of:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and global confusion in a malnourished AIDS patient indicate Wernicke's encephalopathy due to thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: An elderly male presents with persistent productive cough with large volume purulent sputum production. He has had several epis odes in the past. He also had digital clubbing. He is a case of:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic productive cough with copious purulent sputum, recurrent episodes, and digital clubbing are classic for bronchiectasis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A chemical factory worker has acute onset dyspnoea with fever, chills, and malaise, following a few hours of exposure to a new ch emical. These symptoms resolve in four to five days after removal from exposure. He is likely to have:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute dyspnoea, fever, chills, and malaise hours after workplace chemical/antigen exposure resolving 4–5 days after removal indicate acute hypersensitivity pneumonitis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 25 year old man presents with nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea with crampy abdominal pain. He gives histor y of consumption of rice pr eparation in his last meal. What is the likely organism causing the above complaints?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute food poisoning (nausea, vomiting, crampy diarrhoea) following consumption of reheated rice is classically caused by Bacillus cereus.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A five year old child was diagnosed w ith nephrotic syndrome, 18 months back. He was treated and successfully went into re mission at that time. Following, the initial episode, the child has had 3 relapses, each of which was successfully treated with oral prednisolone (60mg/m2/24h) until remission, followed by 40mg/m 2 single dose, alternate days for four weeks. What is the diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Frequent relapses are defined as ≥2 relapses in 6 months or ≥4 relapses in 12 months; 3 relapses over 18 months classify as steroid-responsive, infrequent-relapsing nephrotic syndrome.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 7 year old girl presents to you with non-specific abdominal pain, mild abdominal distension, and not growing well. The child we ighs 14 kg and height is 95 cm. Systemic examination is normal. The haemoglobin wa s 7.5 g/dL (microcytic hypochromic RBCs) and has not responded to iron therapy. Which of the following will be the first investigation you will like to do for diagnosing the condition?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Poor growth, abdominal distension, and iron-refractory microcytic anaemia in a 7-year-old strongly suggest coeliac disease; serum anti-tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG) IgA is the first-line screening test.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A seven year old boy weighing 20 kg pr esented with bleeding from upper GI tract (haemetemasis) for last 18 hours. On exam ination, PR-86/m, RR-16/m and BP-100/70 mmHg; and spleen is palpable 5 cm below co stal margin. There is no other abnormality. Liver function tests are normal. What is the next best step in management?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Haematemesis with massive splenomegaly and normal LFTs in a 7-year-old indicates prehepatic portal hypertension (extrahepatic portal vein obstruction) with variceal bleeding; IV vasopressin/octreotide lowers portal pressure.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A seven year old girl presents in emergency room with hypertension, lethargy, headache, seizures, and visual disturbances . Fundus examination reveals haemorrhages and exudates. Which of the following treatment regimen will be the most appropriate for this child?
