upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypertensive emergency with encephalopathy (seizures, visual changes, papilloedema/exudates) in a child is treated with controlled IV labetalol (or nicardipine) infusion (sublingual nifedipine causes precipitous drops).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: On routine newborn screening at day 3 of life, the baby was found to have TSH level 40mU/L. What should be the next step?
options: Repeat thyroid profile within one week
Repeat thyroid profile after four weeks
Repeat thyroid profile/ start thyroxine, if the child has clinical features of congenital hypothyroidism, otherwise wait and watch
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: An elevated newborn screening TSH of 40 mU/L at Day 3 requires urgent confirmatory venous thyroid profile (TSH and free T4) within 1 week before/when starting levothyroxine.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A five year old girl is brought to you with history of fever for se ven days associated with rash, anorexia, myalgia and petechia l haemorrhages. Which of the following investigations will be most appropriate for making a diagnosis of dengue fever?
options: Detection of IgM antibodies for dengue
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: On Day 7 of dengue illness (after the initial 1–5 day viraemic NS1 phase), IgM capture ELISA is the diagnostic test of choice.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: An eight year old boy was diagnosed to have P.vivax malaria and was treated with appropriate dosages of chlor oquine. The fever subsided but recurred after 3 weeks. Peripheral smear was again positive for P.viva x. This child should now be treated as a case with
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Recurrence of P. vivax parasitaemia 3 weeks after appropriate chloroquine therapy (before primaquine radical cure) may represent either chloroquine-resistant recrudescence or early hepatic hypnozoite relapse.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A two day old neonate is brought with cyanosis, single s econd heart sound, and pansystolic murmur on the left sternal border. ECG reveals left axis deviation, right atrial overload and left ventricular hypertrophy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cyanotic newborn with single S2, pansystolic murmur (VSD), and left axis deviation with LVH on ECG is pathognomonic of tricuspid atresia.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A three year old girl is brought with complaint of not being able to ever stand or walk. She achieved head control at one year of ag e. Examination reveals generalised hypotonia, brisk knee jerk, and ankle clonus. What is the likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Delayed milestones with brisk knee jerks and ankle clonus (upper motor neuron signs despite truncal hypotonia) indicate spastic cerebral palsy.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A child presents with se nsations of itching, burning and a probable foreign body beneath the eyelids. Examination reveals photophobia, large oval fo llicles within the conjunctiva and preauricular adenopathy. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Foreign-body sensation, photophobia, large oval conjunctival follicles, and preauricular lymphadenopathy are classic for adenoviral epidemic keratoconjunctivitis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A seven year old boy presents with acute on set of mild intermittent pain in the right groin and a limp. Abduction and internal rotation of the hip were restricted on the affected side. There was no fever. Radiographs of the pelvis were normal. The most likely diagnosis is :
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute groin pain and limp with restricted hip abduction/internal rotation, no fever, and normal pelvic radiographs in a 7-year-old boy indicate transient monoarticular synovitis (irritable hip).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A child is brought with history of ingestion of an unknown substance. On examination child has excess salivation, lacrimation, miosis, gastrointestinal cramps and emesis. What was the most likely substance ingested?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Excess salivation, lacrimation, miosis, abdominal cramps, and vomiting represent a cholinergic toxidrome caused by carbamate or organophosphate poisoning.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A term newborn presents with respiratory failure which is refractory to mechanical ventilation, surfactant replacement therapy, glucocorticoid administration and extra corporeal membrane oxygenation. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lethal neonatal respiratory failure in a term infant refractory to ventilation, surfactant, steroids, and ECMO is classic for congenital surfactant protein B deficiency.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A child after snake bite develops petech iae and ecchymosis on the skin. In addition, child develops bleeding from venipuncture site and oliguria. The most likely snake species is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Petechiae, ecchymoses, persistent venipuncture bleeding (coagulopathy), and oliguria (AKI) after a snakebite are classic for viper (pit viper / Russell's viper) envenomation.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A six year old boy presents with short neck, low hairline and restriction of neck movements. The child also has Sprengel anomal y, scoliosis, and fused cervical vertebrae. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Short neck, low posterior hairline, restricted neck motion, Sprengel shoulder deformity, and fused cervical vertebrae constitute the classic triad of Klippel-Feil syndrome.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A 10 year old boy presents with recurrent bouts of nasal congestion, itching, sneezing, clear rhinorrhoea and conjunctival irritati on. On examination he has conjunctival hyperaemia, allergic gape and a transverse nasal crease. Wh ich of the following drugs is preferred for management of this child?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic allergic rhinitis (nasal congestion, clear rhinorrhoea, allergic salute/transverse nasal crease, conjunctivitis) is most effectively treated with intranasal corticosteroids such as fluticasone.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A two year old child presents with partia l albinism and susceptibility to infection. Peripheral smear examination reveals giant peroxidise positive lysosomal granules in granulocytes. Which of the following is most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oculocutaneous partial albinism, recurrent pyogenic infections, and giant peroxidase-positive lysosomal granules in neutrophils are pathognomonic of Chédiak-Higashi syndrome.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A one year old child on exclusive milk feeds presents w ith constipation. On examination there is no fecal impaction. What is the next step in management?
options: Increasing intake of vegetables and cereals
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Functional constipation in a 1-year-old fed exclusively milk without faecal impaction is managed first-line by dietary modification—increasing fibre-rich vegetables and cereals and reducing excessive cow's milk.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: A six year old boy presents with generalized seizure disorder and hypo pigmented skin lesions. On examination he has tiny red nodules over the nose and cheeks. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Seizures, hypopigmented ash-leaf macules, and facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum—tiny red nodules on nose/cheeks) are diagnostic of tuberous sclerosis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following can cause bilateral sensorineural hearing loss?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid) are ototoxic and can cause bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (cholesteatoma and glomus tumours cause conductive/unilateral loss).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: The joint sitting of Parliament for transacting a legislative business is presided over by:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under Article 118(4) of the Indian Constitution, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Recently, a massive coral bleaching has been re ported in the ‘Great Barrier Reef’. It is located near the coast of:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef lies in the Coral Sea off the coast of Queensland, north-eastern Australia.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Who is the first Law Officer of the Government of India?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Attorney General for India (Article 76) is the highest/first law officer of the Government of India.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: In the context of Geneti c Engineering, scientists have developed a new computational method called ‘Target Finder’ which can predict where non- coding DNA interacts with genes. Which of the following is a likely advantage of this?
options: Artificial induction of beneficial mutations so as to develop high-yielding varieties
Finding new drug targets to treat some genetic diseases
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Predicting enhancer-promoter interactions of non-coding DNA with target genes helps uncover disease mechanisms and identify novel therapeutic drug targets.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Gold
2. Platinum
3. Silver
Which of the above is/are found in e-waste?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Electronic waste (e-waste) printed circuit boards and components contain recoverable precious metals including gold, platinum, and silver (1, 2, and 3).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: “Boil a small quantity of khoya with some water, cool and add a few drops of iodine solution and see the formation of blue colour”. This is the test to find the presence of which of the following?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Adding iodine solution to boiled, cooled khoya produces a deep blue colour if adulterated with starch.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following CANNOT be used as a biofertilizer in rice cultivation?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Rhizobium forms symbiotic root nodules exclusively in leguminous plants, whereas Azolla, Azospirillum, and blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) fix nitrogen in flooded rice paddies.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Groundwater in many areas in West Bengal has been contaminated leading to a large number of cases of poisoning. What is the substance responsible for such cases?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Naturally occurring arsenic contamination of groundwater in the Gangetic delta of West Bengal has caused widespread chronic arsenicosis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: For acquiring ethanol for blending with petrol, the oil companies in India depend on:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ethanol for India's Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) programme is produced primarily from sugarcane molasses by sugar mills.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements: Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services Act, 2016 aims to strengthen the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana provide funds for the relief of farmers
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 provides statutory backing for Aadhaar-based DBT delivery—neither PMJDY nor farmer relief specifically.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojna aims to promote:
options: Collateral security in housing for rural and urban poor
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is India's flagship national mission for universal financial inclusion (bank accounts, RuPay cards, insurance).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: The objective of the ‘’Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana” is to promote:
options: Cultivation of wild varieties of cereal crops
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) promotes cluster-based organic farming without synthetic chemical pesticides or fertilizers.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Which among the following is a very water intensive crop?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sugarcane is a long-duration (12–18 month) tropical crop with the highest total water requirement among the listed crops.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following does nanoscience have applications?
1. Drug delivery
2. Electronics
3. Food processing
4. Water purification
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Nanotechnology has broad applications across targeted drug delivery (1), nanoelectronics (2), food packaging/processing (3), and membrane/nanoparticle water purification (4).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are the exclusiv e powers of the Lok Sabha as compared to Rajya Sabha?
1. Introducing money bills
2. Passing a motion of no-confidence against the Council of Ministers
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Exclusive powers of the Lok Sabha include introducing Money Bills (1) and passing a motion of no-confidence against the Council of Ministers (2).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Who among the following do not participate in the election of the President of India?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Electoral College for the President of India includes elected MPs (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha) and elected MLAs (Vidhan Sabhas)—not members of State Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishads).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: There is a popular opposition to the use of ‘’plastic microbeads”. In the manufacture of which of the following are they used?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Non-biodegradable plastic microbeads are widely used as exfoliants in personal care cosmetics and scrubs, polluting marine ecosystems.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. In certain parts of India, the cu ltivation of opium is legally allowed.
2. Opium gum is mixed with cluster b ean gum in fracking technology that is used in the shale gas extraction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Licensed medicinal opium poppy cultivation is legally permitted in parts of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh (1); guar (cluster bean) gum—not opium gum—is used in fracking (2 is false).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: There is a worldwide protest against the use of hydrofluorocarbons. In which of the following household things are they used?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) are potent greenhouse gases used primarily as refrigerants in air conditioners and refrigerators.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
What is/are the objectives of Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety?
1. Establishing or promoting in-situ conservation facilities for rare and endangered organisms
2. Maintaining the worldwide network of gene banks for all the known flora and fauna
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety governs the safe transboundary movement and handling of Living Modified Organisms (LMOs), not in-situ conservation or gene banks.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following animals:
1. Sloth bear
2. Jaguar
3. Hoolock gibbon
Which of the above is/are found in India in their natural habitat?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sloth bears (1) and Hoolock gibbons (3; India's only ape in Northeast India) are native to India, whereas jaguars are native to the Americas.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Biodiversity is normally greater in th e lower latitude as compared to higher latitudes.
2. Along the mountain gradient, biodivers ity is normally greater in the lower altitudes as compared to higher altitudes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Species biodiversity follows the latitudinal and altitudinal gradients, being richest in lower (tropical) latitudes (1) and lower mountain altitudes (2).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Aflatoxins are formed by:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Aflatoxins (hepatocarcinogenic mycotoxins contaminating stored groundnuts and grains) are produced by Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following districts:
1. Munnar
2. Mandi
3. Krishna
Which of the above districts is/are well known for tea plantations?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Munnar (Idukki, Kerala; 1) and Mandi (Himachal Pradesh; 2) are known tea-growing districts, unlike Krishna (coastal Andhra).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: ‘Fly ash’ is emitted from:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fly ash is the fine mineral particulate residue generated from burning pulverized coal in thermal power plants.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: Calcium carbide is used
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Calcium carbide reacts with moisture to release acetylene gas and is illegally used for artificial ripening of fruits (mangoes, bananas).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
With reference to food additives, consider the following statements:
1. Benzoic acid and sorbic acid function as antimicrobial agents.
2. Citric acid is used to suppre ss browning of fruits and vegetables.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Benzoic acid and sorbic acid inhibit microbial growth as preservatives (1), while citric acid lowers pH and chelates copper in polyphenol oxidase to prevent enzymatic browning (2).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
With reference to the use of microorganisms in food processing, consider the following statements:
1. Lactic acid bacteria can ferment any monosaccharide or polysaccharide into lactic acid.
2. Baker’s yeast is manufactured fr om single cell isolates of Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is used as baker's yeast (2), whereas lactic acid bacteria ferment specific simple sugars rather than any polysaccharide (1 is false).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following chemicals is/are used in food preservation?
1. Calcium propionate
2. Potassium metabisulphite
3. Lecithin
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: None of them is used in food preservation
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Calcium propionate (antimicrobial in bread), potassium metabisulphite (antioxidant/antimicrobial), and lecithin (emulsifier/stabilizer) are all used in food processing and preservation.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.text: What is ‘M-cessation’, sometimes seen in news?
options: An initiative to help tobacco users to quit tobacco
A mobile phone service that delivers audio messages on pregnancy, child birth and child care
An app to learn all the methods of cashless financial transactions
A government initiative to eradicate the availability of narcotics to general public
upsc-cms-2017-paper-1-authentic.explanation: mCessation is a Government of India mobile SMS/missed-call initiative supporting tobacco users to quit smoking and smokeless tobacco.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: The external opening of branchial fistula is present in :
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A second branchial cleft fistula typically opens externally along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle at the junction of its middle and lower thirds (lower third of the neck).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A eight year old male child complains of severe pain in right testes. The most probable diagnosis is
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sudden-onset severe testicular pain in an 8-year-old boy is testicular torsion until proven otherwise and requires urgent surgical exploration.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Gastroschisis?
options: Gut has herniated through a defect to right of umbilicus
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Gastroschisis is a congenital paraumbilical abdominal wall defect (usually to the right of the umbilicus) with herniated midgut and no covering sac—it is distinct from an omphalocele/exomphalos.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Heineke‐Mikulicz operation is done for:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Heineke-Mikulicz pyloroplasty enlarges a narrowed pyloric outlet by a longitudinal incision closed transversely (used in peptic pyloric stenosis/truncal vagotomy drainage).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 32 year old female underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy which was difficult. On her second post operative day, she develops jaundice. Her LFT parameters show serum bilirubin 6.8 mg/dL; direct bilirubin 5.6 and indirect bilirubin 1.2 mg/dL; and serum alkaline phosphatase 1226 IU/L. She is most likely suffering from obstructive jaundice due to:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Early postoperative obstructive jaundice (high direct bilirubin and markedly elevated ALP) after a difficult laparoscopic cholecystectomy indicates iatrogenic bile duct injury.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 60 year old man presents with painless progressive jaundice for two months. He has a history of weight loss. On examination, his gallbladder is palpable which is smooth, non‐tender and globular. His serum bilirubin is 18.2 mg/dL. He is most likely suffering from:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Painless progressive jaundice with weight loss and a palpable, smooth, non-tender gallbladder (Courvoisier's law) in a 60-year-old man is classic for carcinoma of the head of the pancreas.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A young 23 year old male riding his motorcycle meets with a road accident. He is tachypnoeic with HR 110/m and BP 112/74 mmHg. On examination, he has tenderness over left side of chest with decreased air entry. His trachea is pushed to opposite side. Abdominal examination is unremarkable. Most probably he is suffering from:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chest trauma with tachypnoea, ipsilateral chest tenderness, decreased air entry, and contralateral tracheal shift indicates a large haemothorax (or pneumothorax) compressing the lung.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Mondor’s disease is
options: Thrombophlebitis of superficial veins of breast
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mondor's disease is a benign, self-limiting superficial thrombophlebitis of the thoracoepigastric veins of the breast and anterior chest wall.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT true regarding ‘Renal Carbuncle’?
options: It is an abscess in renal parenchyma
It is a type of renal tuberculosis
It occurs in intravenous drug abusers
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A renal carbuncle is a multiloculated cortical renal abscess (typically due to Staphylococcus aureus haematogenous spread in diabetics or IV drug users)—it is not a form of renal tuberculosis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Anderson‐Hynes operation is performed for:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty is the gold-standard surgical procedure for pelvi-ureteric junction (PUJ) obstruction.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT correct for ‘strawberry gall bladder’?
options: It is a malignant condition of gall bladder
It has sub mucous aggregation of cholesterol crystals
It may be associated with cholesterol Stones
Simple cholecystectomy is the treatment of choice
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: 'Strawberry gallbladder' (cholesterolosis) is a benign condition caused by submucosal accumulation of cholesterol esters/macrophages, often associated with cholesterol gallstones and treated by cholecystectomy if symptomatic.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Treatment of choice for Recurrent Thyrotoxicosis after surgery is
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Recurrent thyrotoxicosis after subtotal thyroidectomy is best treated with radioactive iodine (I-131) to avoid the high complication risk of re-operative neck surgery.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: All the following are features of Polycystic disease of kidneys EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Polycystic kidney disease causes haematuria, hypertension, and progressive renal failure (and occasionally erythrocytosis from erythropoietin, though UPSC key for this item marked (d) Erythrocytosis).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the most important selection criteria for obesity surgery ?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Standard bariatric surgery selection criteria require a BMI > 40 kg/m² alone, or BMI > 35 kg/m² with significant obesity-related comorbidities.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 45 year old underwent abdominal rectal prolapse surgery. At present, he complains of sexual dysfunction which is probably due to the injury of:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Deep pelvic dissection during abdominal rectopexy/prolapse surgery can injure the pelvic autonomic nerves (hypogastric/nervi erigentes), causing postoperative sexual dysfunction.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: In endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography endoscope used is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: ERCP uses a side-viewing duodenoscope to visualize the ampulla of Vater on the medial wall of the second part of the duodenum.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Oliguria is defined as:
options: More than 900 ml of urine excreted in a day
600 ml to 700 ml of urine excreted in a day
Less than 300 ml of urine excreted in a day
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Oliguria in adults is defined as a urine output of less than 300–400 mL in 24 hours (<0.5 mL/kg/hr).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 40 year old man, with a history of a reducible left groin swelling of two years, comes with severe pain over left groin. The swelling is now non‐reducible and is very tender to touch. The most probable treatment plan for this patient would be:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A previously reducible groin hernia that becomes acutely irreducible, severely painful, and very tender indicates strangulation and requires immediate preparation for emergency surgery.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: During laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair, in the ‘triangle of doom’, the following are true EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In the laparoscopic 'triangle of doom', the apex is superior, the vas deferens is medial, the spermatic vessels are lateral, and the base is formed by the peritoneal reflection (covering the external iliac vessels).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: All are rare type of lateral Hernia of abdominal wall, EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Spigelian, superior lumbar (Grynfeltt), and inferior lumbar (Petit) hernias are rare lateral abdominal wall hernias, whereas an obturator hernia occurs through the pelvic obturator foramen.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 35 year old female had laparoscopic ventral hernia repair using polypropylene mesh in January 2015. In June 2015, she is again admitted with features of subacute intestinal obstruction and is managed conservatively. She continues to have recurrent colicky pain after that. Most probably she is suffering from:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intraperitoneal polypropylene mesh placed during laparoscopic ventral hernia repair directly contacts bowel loops and commonly causes dense bowel adhesions and recurrent subacute intestinal obstruction.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT correct for breast abscess?
options: Drainage of abscess by a radial incision
Antibiotic is given if pus is already present
A counter‐incision is made in the dependant part
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Once pus has formed in a breast abscess, antibiotics alone are inadequate—surgical incision and drainage (or USG-guided aspiration) is mandatory.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Important landmark in submandibular gland dissection is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The posterior border of the mylohyoid muscle is the key surgical landmark in submandibular gland dissection, around which the deep lobe and Wharton's duct wrap.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: SIRS criteria include fever (>38°C) or hypothermia (<36°C), tachypnoea, leukocytosis/leukopenia, and tachycardia (heart rate >90/min)—not bradycardia.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 35 year old man presents to Emergency with acute onset pain abdomen radiating to whole abdomen and abdominal distension for one day. On examination, he has tenderness and guarding all over abdomen with pulse rate of 100/m and BP 116/84 mmHg. Chest X‐ray erect position shows gas under bilateral domes of diaphragm. Probably he is suffering from:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Massive pneumoperitoneum (gas under both domes of the diaphragm) with generalized peritonitis is characteristic of hollow viscus (peptic ulcer or colonic) perforation.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 70 year old man comes to Emergency with pain lower abdomen and not passing urine for eight hours. He has a past history of urgency, hesitancy and frequency of urine. On examination, he has a lump up to the umbilicus which is slightly tender. What is the next step of management?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An elderly man with chronic LUTS (urgency, hesitancy, frequency) presenting with acute urinary retention and a palpable bladder up to the umbilicus requires immediate per-urethral catheterization.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: ‘Swiss cheese defects’ of anterior abdominal wall after exploratory laparotomy is best seen while doing:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Laparoscopic ventral hernia repair provides a panoramic view of the entire anterior abdominal wall, readily identifying multiple small 'Swiss-cheese' fascial defects.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 35 year old male patient comes to casualty with acute pain abdomen; and on examination found to have cold, clammy extremities, sunken eyes, dry tongue, thready pulse, drawn and anxious face with abdominal guarding and rigidity. This clinical picture indicates:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cold clammy extremities, sunken eyes, dry tongue, thready pulse, Hippocratic facies, and generalized rigidity indicate diffuse late peritonitis with septic shock.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following statements are true for keloids EXCEPT:
options: It is rarely seen in white skinned persons and is more common over the sternum
True keloid continues to become worse even after one year
True keloid does not spread into surrounding tissue
The maturation and stabilization of the collagen fibrils is inhibited
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Unlike hypertrophic scars, true keloids characteristically invade and spread beyond the boundaries of the original wound into surrounding normal skin.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of these is a palliative shunt procedure created between the left subclavian artery and pulmonary artery to treat cyanotic congenital heart disease?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Blalock-Taussig shunt anastomoses the subclavian artery to the ipsilateral pulmonary artery to increase pulmonary blood flow in cyanotic congenital heart disease (e.g., Tetralogy of Fallot).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A young male is undergoing emergency surgery for a clinical diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Intraoperatively minimal pus was found but the appendix was normal. What is the next step of management?
options: Close the abdomen without doing anything
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: When a normal appendix is found during emergency appendicectomy for suspected appendicitis, the surgeon must inspect the terminal ileum (2 feet proximal to ileocaecal valve) for a perforated or inflamed Meckel's diverticulum.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT considered as an indicator of adequate fluid resuscitation?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Adequacy of fluid resuscitation in shock is monitored primarily by urine output (≥0.5 mL/kg/hr), pulse rate, and blood pressure—not respiratory rate.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: In a 65 year old, double contrast barium enema shows cancer of colon with an apple core appearance. Colonoscopic biopsy shows adenocarcinoma. What will be the next step of management?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: After histological confirmation of colon adenocarcinoma on colonoscopic biopsy, contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) of the chest/abdomen/pelvis is the next step for preoperative staging before surgery.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 35 year old woman presented with a lump in her upper abdomen for two months which was slightly increasing. She also complained of early satiety. She gave a history of acute severe pain in upper abdomen for which she was admitted in hospital for 10 days, about three months ago. On examination, the mass was firm, smooth surfaced and not moving with respiration. She was most likely suffering from:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A smooth, fixed upper abdominal mass causing early satiety 3 months after an episode of acute severe epigastric pain (acute pancreatitis) is classic for a pancreatic pseudocyst.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: While working in a primary health centre, an elderly patient presents with a history of  sudden  loss  of  vision  and  curtain  falling  sensation  in  one  eye.  This  symptom  is highly suggestive that the patient has the following condition:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sudden painless vision loss preceded by a 'curtain falling' across the visual field in an elderly patient is classic for retinal detachment.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Pringle’s manoeuvre is done to stop bleeding at:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Pringle manoeuvre compresses the hepatoduodenal ligament (containing the hepatic artery and portal vein) to temporarily control bleeding from the liver.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the most common malignant tumour of eyelid?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Basal cell carcinoma (rodent ulcer) is the most common malignant tumour of the eyelid (~90% of cases, most often on the lower lid).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is NOT a symptom of atherosclerotic occlusive disease at the bifurcation of aorta (Leriche syndrome)?
options: Claudication of the buttock and thigh
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Leriche syndrome (aortoiliac occlusive disease) presents with the classic triad of buttock/thigh/calf claudication, erectile impotence, and absent femoral pulses—isolated distal foot gangrene is not typical.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following factors is labelled as cytokine in the pathogenesis of Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS)?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukins (IL-1, IL-6) are key pro-inflammatory cytokines driving the pathogenesis of SIRS.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Vocal cord palsy after thyroid surgery is due to injury to:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Post-thyroidectomy vocal cord paralysis results from iatrogenic injury to the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A infertile woman presents with yellow or green vaginal discharge, bartholin cyst and proctitis. What is the most probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Purulent yellow-green vaginal discharge, Bartholin gland abscess/cyst, proctitis, and tubal infertility are characteristic of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Absolute contraindication to combined oral contraceptive is:
options: History of previous two caesarean section
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A personal history of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary thromboembolism is an absolute contraindication to combined oral contraceptive pills.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 28 year old P1L1 presents with severe pain in her abdomen and is taken for laparotomy. On opening the abdomen pseudomyxoma of the peritoneum is present. What should be the probable reason?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Rupture of a mucinous cystadenoma/cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary (or appendiceal mucinous neoplasm) seeds mucin-producing epithelium throughout the peritoneal cavity, causing pseudomyxoma peritonei.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: In a 40 year old woman, pap smear shows atypical glandular cells. The next step of management should be:
options: Repeat pap smear after three months
Colposcopy, cervical biopsy, endocervical curettage and endometrial biopsy
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2017 Answer Key: Option (c) — Colposcopy, cervical biopsy, endocervical curettage and endometrial biopsy.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 50 year old P4L4 has a simple left ovarian cyst of 10cm. Ca 125 is 30u/ml. Treatment of choice would be:
options: TAH + BSO (Total abdominal hysterectomy + Bilateral salpingo‐oopherectomy)
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2017 Answer Key: Option (a) — TAH + BSO (Total abdominal hysterectomy + Bilateral salpingo‐oopherectomy).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A seven year old girl with precocious puberty is found to be having a 10 cm. ovarian cyst on USG. The most likely etiology is
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An oestrogen-secreting juvenile granulosa cell tumour of the ovary is the most common ovarian neoplasm causing isosexual precocious puberty in a young girl.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 17 year old girl presents with an ovarian cyst of 5cm. The cyst is echo free, unilocular and CA 125 of 8U/ml. What is most appropriate management?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A 5 cm simple, unilocular, echo-free ovarian cyst with normal CA-125 (8 U/mL) in an adolescent girl is likely a functional follicular cyst and is managed conservatively with follow-up ultrasound.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: The contraceptive choice for a 38 year old P1L1 woman having chronic hypertension, dysmenorrhoea and menorrhagia is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a 38-year-old woman with chronic hypertension (contraindicating COCs), dysmenorrhoea, and menorrhagia, the levonorgestrel-releasing IUD (LNG-IUS) provides contraception while treating heavy bleeding and pain.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Most probable cause of heavy bleeding in a P2L2 during tenth day post partum is:
options: Retained bits of cotyledons and membranes
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Secondary postpartum haemorrhage occurring around the 10th postpartum day is most commonly caused by retained placental cotyledons or membranes (often with endometritis).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman with which of the following health problems should avoid centchromen?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Centchroman (ormeloxifene, a SERM) is contraindicated in women with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), as it can worsen ovarian cyst formation and menstrual irregularity.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Combined contraceptive pills give protection from the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Combined oral contraceptives protect against ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer, and ectopic pregnancy, whereas long-term use does not protect against cervical cancer.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman presents with heavy foul smelling discharge with sharply demarcated ulcers without induration on the perineum and the labia majora. Inguinal lymphadenopathy is also present. What is the most probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) presents with painful, non-indurated, sharply demarcated genital ulcers with foul-smelling discharge and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 28 year old woman develops amenorrhoea after having dilatation and curettage. The most likely diagnosis is :
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Secondary amenorrhoea developing after uterine curettage (D&C) is classic for Asherman's syndrome (intrauterine adhesions/synechiae).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the  following tests is NOT used for diagnosing syphilis?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Frei's intradermal test was historically used to diagnose lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV), whereas DFA, FTA-ABS, and TPHA are diagnostic tests for syphilis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Fitz‐Hugh‐Curtis syndrome involving perihepatitis is present in the following:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome (violin-string perihepatic adhesions causing RUQ pain) complicates pelvic inflammatory disease caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae or Chlamydia trachomatis.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following cause/causes bacterial vaginosis?
1. Gardnerella
2. Mycoplasma
3. Ureaplasma urealyticum
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bacterial vaginosis is a polymicrobial syndrome characterized by overgrowth of Gardnerella vaginalis, Mycoplasma hominis, Ureaplasma urealyticum, and anaerobes replacing lactobacilli.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Where are antisperm antibodies usually present?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wait—no, cms17-p2-057: Antisperm antibodies in infertile women are predominantly found in cervical mucus (cervix), impairing sperm penetration.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Modified Bishop’s score includes all EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The modified Bishop score evaluates five parameters: cervical dilatation, cervical length (effacement), consistency, position, and fetal head station—not position of the occiput.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: The engaging diameter of brow presentation is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In brow presentation, the largest anteroposterior diameter—the mento-vertical diameter (~13.5–14 cm)—attempts to engage the pelvic brim.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Intramuscular injection of iron dextran is given by ‘Z’ technique to:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intramuscular iron dextran is administered using the Z-track technique to seal the needle track and prevent subcutaneous leakage and permanent skin staining.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are the risk factors for acute pelvic inflammatory disease in women?
1. Intercourse during menstruation
2. Multiple sex partners
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intercourse during menstruation (loss of cervical mucus plug barrier) and multiple sexual partners are major risk factors for acute pelvic inflammatory disease.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: The umbilical cord normally contains:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A normal umbilical cord contains two umbilical arteries (carrying deoxygenated fetal blood) and one umbilical vein (carrying oxygenated blood).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Painless genital ulcer is found in which one of the following genital infections?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV, caused by Chlamydia trachomatis L1–L3) begins as a transient, painless genital ulcer/papule followed by painful inguinal buboes.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Medical management of tubular ectopic pregnancy can be done in the following EXCEPT:
options: β HCG level more than 10,000 IU
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Medical management of tubal ectopic pregnancy with methotrexate is contraindicated when serum beta-hCG is very high (>5,000–10,000 IU/L), fetal cardiac activity is present, or sac diameter exceeds 3.5–4 cm.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Cholestasis may lead to the following complications EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (IHCP) increases the risk of preterm labour, meconium-stained liquor, and sudden intrauterine fetal death—it does not directly cause neonatal jaundice.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following genital infections is associated with preterm labour?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bacterial vaginosis is an established infectious risk factor for spontaneous preterm labour and preterm premature rupture of membranes.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Multiple pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of the following EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wait—no, cms17-p2-067: Multiple pregnancy increases the risk of hyperemesis gravidarum, congenital malformations, and pre-eclampsia (PIH), and predisposes to preterm (not post-date) delivery.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following conditions of the endometrium is associated with a significantly increased risk of development of cancer?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Complex endometrial hyperplasia with cellular atypia carries the highest risk (~25–30%) of progression to or coexistence with endometrial adenocarcinoma.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Surgical staging is done for all the genital malignancies EXCEPT:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ovarian, endometrial, and fallopian tube carcinomas are staged surgically (FIGO), whereas gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) is staged clinically/radiologically without routine surgical staging.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: B‐Lynch suture for atonic postpartum haemorrhage
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The B-Lynch brace suture is a vertical compression suture placed around the uterus to mechanically compress the uterine walls and control atonic postpartum haemorrhage.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Regarding ‘Delancy’s levels of vaginal support’, consider the following pairs:
1. Level I .......... Supports distal urethra perineal body
2. Level II .......... Supports mid-vagina
3. Level III .......... Supports apical defect Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In DeLancey's levels of vaginal support, Level I (uterosacral-cardinal ligament complex) provides apical support, Level II (paravaginal attachments) supports the mid-vagina, and Level III (perineal body/pubourethral ligaments) supports the distal vagina and urethra; hence only Level II is correctly matched.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Regarding “conjoined twins”, which of the following statements is/are true?
1. These are always monozygotic
2. These result when division occurs before the embryonic disc is formed
3. Most common variety is thoracopagus
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Conjoined twins are always monozygotic resulting from incomplete division of the embryonic disc after day 13 post-fertilization, and thoracopagus (joined at the chest) is the most common variety.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: The appropriate treatment for the baby of a woman who is HBsAg positive but HBeAg negative is
options: Both active and passive immunisation soon after birth
Passive immunisation soon after birth but active immunisation after one year of age
Only active immunisation soon after birth
Only passive immunisation soon after birth
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Newborns of HBsAg-positive mothers (regardless of HBeAg status) require both passive immunoprophylaxis with Hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) and active immunization with the Hepatitis B vaccine soon after birth (within 12 hours) at different sites.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following pairs regarding foetal heart during labour: Term .... Description
1. Early decelerations .... Most common during labour and are due to cord compression
2. Late decelerations .... Result due to any process leading to maternal hypotension, placental insufficiency or excessive uterine activity
3. Variable decelerations .... Are due to head compression leading to vagal stimulation Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency (from maternal hypotension, placental insufficiency, or tachysystole), whereas early decelerations are caused by fetal head compression and variable decelerations by umbilical cord compression.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 26 year old woman P1L1 reports with High Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (HGSIL) on Pap smear (Papanicolaou smear). Further management for her is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A Pap smear showing High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (HSIL) requires colposcopy and directed biopsy to histologically confirm or rule out CIN 2/3 or invasive carcinoma before definitive excisional therapy.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: With reference to the displacement of uterus, the treatment of choice for genuine stress urinary incontinence is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mid-urethral sling procedures such as tension-free vaginal tape obturator (TVT-O) are the surgical treatment of choice for genuine stress urinary incontinence.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Regarding placental separation in III stage of labour, consider the following statements:
1. Separation of placenta occurs at deciduas spongiosa
2. In Shultz method, separation of placenta starts at centre
3. In Mathew Duncan’s method, separation begins at margin
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Placental separation occurs through the decidua spongiosa; in the Schultze mechanism separation begins centrally (fetal surface presents first), whereas in the Matthews Duncan mechanism separation begins at the margin (maternal surface presents first).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 16 year old girl presents with primary amenorrhea with absent vagina, cervix and uterus in the presence of normal secondary sexual characteristics. Ovaries are present on USG. The most probable diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome presents in phenotypic 46,XX females with normal ovaries and secondary sexual characteristics, primary amenorrhea, and congenital absence of the uterus and upper vagina.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A 32 year old woman is noted to have 1200 cc of blood loss following a spontaneous vaginal delivery and delivery of placenta. The uterine fundus is palpated and noted to be firm. Which of the following is the most likely treatment for this patient?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Postpartum haemorrhage with a firm, well-contracted uterine fundus points to genital tract trauma rather than uterine atony; inspecting and surgically repairing a cervical or vaginal laceration is indicated.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding physiology of menstruation?
1. LH surge precedes ovulation
2. There are two peaks in serum estradiol levels, first in follicular and second in luteal phase
3. Serum progesterone has only one peak i.e., in luteal phase
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a normal menstrual cycle, the LH surge precedes ovulation, serum estradiol has two peaks (late follicular and mid-luteal), and serum progesterone has a single peak during the mid-luteal phase.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are the measure(s) of dispersion ?
1. Mode
2. Median
3. Standard Deviation
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Standard deviation is a measure of dispersion (spread of data around the mean), whereas mode and median are measures of central tendency.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which among the following is/are the examples of primordial prevention ?
1. Adopting healthy lifestyles from childhood
2. Immunization of infants
3. Screening of cervical cancer
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Primordial prevention aims to prevent the emergence of risk factors in the first place (such as adopting healthy lifestyles from childhood), whereas immunization is primary prevention and screening is secondary prevention.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: The appropriate statistical test to find out obesity as a significant risk factor for breast cancer is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Chi-square test is used to test the statistical significance of association between two categorical (qualitative) variables, such as obesity (present/absent) and breast cancer (present/absent).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: In a case control study, confounding factors can be minimized by the following EXCEPT:
options: Matching of variables such as age and sex
Increasing sample size for cases and controls
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Increasing the sample size reduces random sampling error (increases precision) but does not eliminate systematic confounding bias, which is controlled by matching, randomization, or stratification.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is FALSE regarding confounding factor in epidemiological studies ?
options: Associated both with exposure and disease
Distributed equally between study and control groups
Independent risk factor for disease in question
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A confounding factor is unequally distributed between study and control groups, is associated with both the exposure and the disease, and is an independent risk factor for the disease.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Denominator in calculation of case fatality rate is:
options: Total number of deaths due to all causes
Total number of cases due to the disease concerned
Total number of deaths due to the disease concerned
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Case fatality rate (CFR) is calculated as the number of deaths due to a specific disease divided by the total number of cases of that disease, expressed as a percentage.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A well of contaminated water resulting in an epidemic of acute watery diarrhoea is a typical example for
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A contaminated well used repeatedly by a community produces a common-source, continuous (or repeated) exposure epidemic with cases occurring over an extended period.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: An important measure of communicability of a disease is
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Secondary attack rate measures the proportion of susceptible contacts who develop the disease within one incubation period after exposure to a primary case, making it a key measure of communicability.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding case fatality rate?
options: Very useful indicator for both acute and chronic diseases
One of the measures related to virulence
It is the ratio of deaths to cases expressed as percentage
Variation can occur for the same disease because of changes in the agent factors
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Case fatality rate (CFR) is primarily useful for acute infectious diseases rather than chronic diseases because chronic diseases have prolonged, variable courses where death may occur years later or from other causes.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Farmer’s lung is caused by the inhalation of:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Farmer's lung is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by inhaling moldy hay or grain dust containing thermophilic actinomycetes (e.g., Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Suraksha Clinics are conducted under the aegis of which National Health Programme?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Suraksha Clinics are STI/RTI clinics established under the National AIDS Control Programme (NACP) to provide standardized syndromic management and counseling.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Mean + 2 S.D. contains
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a normal (Gaussian) distribution, Mean ± 1 SD covers 68.3% of values, Mean ± 2 SD covers 95.4% of values, and Mean ± 3 SD covers 99.7% of values.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Infant Mortality Rate is expressed per:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is defined as the number of infant deaths (under 1 year of age) in a year per 1,000 live births in the same year.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following tests is NOT used for checking quality of pasteurisation of milk?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Phosphatase test, standard plate count, and coliform count assess the adequacy of milk pasteurization, whereas the orthotolidine test measures residual chlorine in water.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following are components of epidemiological triad?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The classical epidemiological triad of disease causation consists of three interacting components: Agent, Host, and Environment.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
By applying the principles of ergonomics which of the following can be improved?
1. Designing of equipment and tools
2. Human efficiency
3. Layout of place of work
4. Reduction in industrial accidents
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ergonomics ('fitting the job to the worker') optimizes equipment design, workplace layout, human efficiency, and comfort while reducing occupational fatigue and industrial accidents.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: The risk of disease is measured by
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Incidence rate measures the number of new cases arising in a population at risk over a specified period, directly quantifying the risk of developing a disease.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Tetanus spores can only be killed by
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Tetanus spores are highly resistant to heat and antibiotics; among the listed options, gamma irradiation (along with autoclaving) reliably destroys bacterial spores.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which is/are the correct statements regarding the cut off points for the diagnosis of anaemia?
1. Haemoglobin for adult males is 13 g/dl
2. Haemoglobin for adult non-pregnant female is 12 g/dl
3. Haemoglobin for adult pregnant female is 11 g/dl
4. Haemoglobin for children six months to six years of age is 11 g/dl
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO haemoglobin cutoffs for diagnosing anaemia are <13 g/dL in adult males, <12 g/dL in non-pregnant adult females, <11 g/dL in pregnant women, and <11 g/dL in children aged 6 months to 6 years.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Health functionary at PHC level is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the Indian rural health care system, the Health Assistant (Female) / Lady Health Visitor (LHV) is posted at the Primary Health Centre (PHC) level to supervise Health Workers (Female) at Sub-Centres.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Due to a measles outbreak in a community, a medical officer decided to immunize a child aged seven months with measles vaccine. When should the next measles vaccine be administered?
options: When the child completes nine months of age
When the child completes fifteen months of age
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: If a measles vaccine is given before 9 months of age (such as at 7 months during an outbreak), it does not count as a routine dose due to maternal antibody interference, so the child must be revaccinated at 9 months of age.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are the methods of assessment of nutritional status?
1. Clinical examination
2. Anthropometry
3. Biochemical evaluation
4. Orthotolidine test
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Nutritional status assessment includes clinical examination, anthropometry, and biochemical evaluation, whereas the orthotolidine test is used for residual chlorine testing in water.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Retrospective cohort studies have the following features EXCEPT:
options: Outcomes have occurred before the start of the study
Generally more expensive than prospective studies
Investigator goes back in time to select study groups
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Retrospective cohort studies are generally less expensive and quicker than prospective cohort studies because the exposure and outcomes have already occurred in existing records.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
What is the correct sequence of the following levels of prevention?
1. Specific protection
2. Early diagnosis and prompt treatment
3. Disability limitation and rehabilitation
4. Health promotion Select the correct sequence from the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The chronological sequence of preventive interventions across the natural history of disease is: Health promotion (4), Specific protection (1), Early diagnosis and prompt treatment (2), and Disability limitation and rehabilitation (3).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following items are among the uses of epidemiology?
options: To study historically the rise and fall of the diseases
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Epidemiology is used to study historical disease trends, make a community diagnosis, identify syndromes, and evaluate health services.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding folic acid:
1. It is needed for normal development of blood cells in the marrow
2. It has a role in synthesis of nucleic acids
3. It is resistant to boiling
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Folic acid is essential for nucleic acid synthesis and normal erythropoiesis in bone marrow, but it is heat-labile and easily destroyed by boiling/overcooking.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: The maternal and child health care indicator that gives a good indicator of the extent of pregnancy wastage as well as the quantity and quality of health care available to the mother and new born is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Perinatal Mortality Rate (late fetal deaths plus early neonatal deaths per 1,000 total births) reflects both the extent of pregnancy wastage and the quality of maternal and newborn care.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: To control Mansonoides mosquitoes, the most effective method is:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mansonoides mosquitoes breed in water bodies with aquatic vegetation (like Pistia) to which larvae attach for oxygen; removing aquatic plants is the most effective control method.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the fertility indicator that gives the approximate magnitude of completed family size?
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Total Fertility Rate (TFR) represents the average number of children a woman would bear if she experienced current age-specific fertility rates throughout her reproductive life, approximating completed family size.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: For a child aged four years, an Anganwadi Worker detects that the weight is lower than expected. What should the Anganwadi Worker do first regarding the malnutrition detected in the child?
options: Refer the child to the nearby Health Centre
Refer the child a nearby nutritional rehabilitation centre
Give nutritional counselling to the mother
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: When a 4-year-old child has mild-to-moderate growth faltering (weight lower than expected) detected during growth monitoring, the Anganwadi Worker's first step is nutritional counselling to the mother (along with supplementary nutrition).

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following anthropometrical measurements is/are carried out to assess the growth of children under five years of age?
1. Weight measurement
2. Height measurement
3. Mid upper arm circumference
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Weight, height/length, and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) are standard anthropometric measurements used to assess growth and nutritional status in under-five children.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following is included in detecting a child with severe acute malnutrition?
1. Weight for age Z-score less than minus three SD
2. Bilateral pitting oedema
3. Weight for height Z-score less than minus three SD
4. Mid upper arm circumference of less than 12 cm.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO criteria for Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in children aged 6–59 months include weight-for-height Z-score < -3 SD, MUAC < 11.5 cm (not <12 cm), or bilateral pitting oedema.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Essential Obstetric Care under the Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn and Child Health care Programme?
1. Early registration of pregnancy
2. Provision of first referral units
3. Provision of safe delivery practices
4. Provision of at least four postnatal checkups
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under RMNCH+A, Essential Obstetric Care includes early registration of pregnancy and provision of safe delivery practices, whereas First Referral Units (FRUs) provide Emergency Obstetric Care.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: A pregnant woman visits a medical officer for an antenatal check up. The woman mentions that she had received two doses of Tetanus Toxoid vaccine four years ago. Which of the following steps should the medical officer take with regard to administration of Tetanus Toxoid vaccine as per the Government of India recommended schedule?
options: Tetanus Immunoglobulin should be administered in the third trimester of pregnancy
Two doses of Tetanus Toxoid vaccine should be administered with an interval of four weeks between the two doses
Only one dose of Tetanus Toxoid vaccine is required
No Tetanus Toxoid vaccine is required
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: If a pregnant woman received two doses of Tetanus Toxoid (TT) within the preceding 3–5 years (or 4 years ago per older GOI/UPSC guidelines for previously immunized mothers), only a single booster dose of TT is required during the current pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text:
With reference to quarantine measures to prevent the spread of a disease, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. In addition to human beings, quarantine measures are at times also applied to an aircraft or a train or a container etc.
2. The duration of the quarantine period is equivalent to the minimum incubation period for the disease
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Quarantine applies not only to humans but also to ships, aircraft, trains, or containers from infected areas; its duration equals the maximum (not minimum) incubation period of the disease.

upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2017-paper-2-authentic.text: Which is the first step in carrying out an Adverse Event Following Immunization (AEFI)?
options: Observe the immunization service in action
Collect data about the suspected vaccine
