upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Classical radical neck dissection removes cervical lymph nodes levels I–V along with the sternocleidomastoid muscle, internal jugular vein, and spinal accessory nerve, while preserving the trapezius muscle.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Mousseau-Barbin Tube (M.B.Tube) is used for:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Mousseau-Barbin tube is a palliative pulsion endoprosthesis used to maintain luminal patency in advanced, inoperable oesophageal carcinoma.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the investigation of choice in a patient with haematemesis?
options: Barium meal for stomach and duodenum
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Flexible upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (oesophagogastroduodenoscopy) is the investigation of choice in haematemesis for both diagnosis and endoscopic haemostasis.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: The two important values necessary for describing the variation in a series of observations are:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: For a symmetrical/normally distributed series of observations, mean (central tendency) and standard deviation (dispersion) are the two essential summary parameters.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: The time period between entry of infective agent in a host and maximal infectivity of that host is:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Generation time is defined as the interval between the entry of an infectious agent into a host and the time of maximal infectivity of that host.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements: Symposium is a method of health education characterised by a series of speeches on a selected topic presentation of different aspects of a topic by 3 or 4 experts.
3. a discussion among the symposium member s the chairperson making a comprehensive summary at the end of the session Which of these statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A symposium consists of a series of short speeches by 3–4 experts on different aspects of a topic followed by a chairperson's summary, without formal debate/discussion among the panel members.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-I (Major Group of Insecticides)
List-II (Name of Insecticide)
A. Stomach poison
1. Temephos
B. Organo-chlorine compound
2. Propoxur
C. Organo-phosphorous compound
3. Sodium fluoride
D. Carbamates
4. Dieldrin
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sodium fluoride is a stomach poison (A-3), dieldrin is an organochlorine (B-4), temephos is an organophosphate (C-1), and propoxur is a carbamate insecticide (D-2).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following diseases:
1. Rift valley fever
2. Yellow Fever
3. Chickungunya fever
4. West Nile fever
Which of the above diseases are transmitted by Aedes mosquito?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Yellow fever, chikungunya, and Rift Valley fever are transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, whereas West Nile fever is primarily transmitted by Culex mosquitoes.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Consider the following statements: Prophylactic disinfection includes disinfection of urine specimen of patient with enteric fever pasteurization of milk disinfection of contaminated linen disinfection of water by chlorine Which of these statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Prophylactic (precurrent) disinfection includes milk pasteurization and water chlorination, whereas disinfecting urine or linen of an infected patient is concurrent disinfection.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Registration of birth, even if the child is born in a hospital, is essentially the responsibility of parents only.
2. At present, the registration of birth has to be done not more than 15 days after the birth. Which of these statements is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under India's Registration of Births and Deaths Act, institutional births must be reported by the hospital medical officer/head, and the statutory period for birth registration is 21 days (not 15 days).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Sullivan Index is the measure of which of the following?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sullivan's index measures disability-free life expectancy by subtracting the duration of bed-disability and inability to perform major activities from total life expectancy.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Con sider the following statements: The strategy to eradicate poliomyelitis in India comprised of conducting national immunisation days mopping up rounds with OPV
3. acute flaccid paralysis surveillance public awareness through multimedia Which of these statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: India's polio eradication strategy combined National Immunization Days (NIDs), house-to-house mop-up OPV rounds, acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) surveillance, and multimedia public awareness.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: In the estimation of statistical probability, Z score is applicable to:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Z-score (standard normal deviate) is specifically applicable to a normal (Gaussian) probability distribution.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following vectors:
1. Aedes mosquito
2. Flea
3. Ticks
4. Itchmite Transovarian transmission is demonstrated in
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Transovarial transmission (passage of pathogens from female vector to offspring via eggs) is classically demonstrated in Aedes mosquitoes (e.g., dengue/yellow fever) and ticks (e.g., KFD, rickettsiae).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: The most sensitive indicator of the health status of a community is the:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is widely regarded as the most sensitive indicator of a community's overall health status and socioeconomic conditions.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Chemoprophylaxis is an example of:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chemoprophylaxis (using drugs to prevent a specific disease before onset) is an example of specific protection under primary prevention.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A rapid mass screening method that can be employed by a paramedical worker for detecting malnutrition in pre - school (age: 1 to 5 years) children is:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) is age-independent between 1 and 5 years and is ideal for rapid mass screening of malnutrition by paramedical workers.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: The most important single determinant of infant mortality is:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Low birth weight is the single most important biological determinant of infant mortality.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: The immunoglobulins that can be transported across the placenta include:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Only IgG crosses the placenta (note: the official UPSC key for this paper marked (b) IgA only in error, though physiologically IgG is the sole immunoglobulin transported across the placenta).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. The duration of immunity is longer when live vaccine is administered as compared to the administration of killed vaccine.
2. In the case of killed vaccine, single dose is sufficient whereas multiple doses are always required in the case of live vaccines. Which of these statements is/are corr ect?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Live attenuated vaccines generally induce longer-lasting immunity than killed vaccines and often require only a single dose, whereas killed vaccines typically require multiple doses.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-I (Disease)
List-II (Incubation Period)
A. Measles
1. 6 weeks to 6 months
B. Diphtheria
2. 15 to 50 days
C. Hepatitis A
3. 10 to 14 days
D. Hepatitis B
4. 2 to 6 days
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Incubation periods: measles 10–14 days (A-3), diphtheria 2–6 days (B-4), Hepatitis A 15–50 days (C-2), and Hepatitis B 6 weeks to 6 months (D-1).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Throat swab positive and Schick test negative indicate that the person is:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A positive throat swab for Corynebacterium diphtheriae with a negative Schick test (indicating circulating antitoxin immunity) suggests either an immune carrier or a person immune to toxin.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: The following are manifestations of psychosis except:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Schizophrenia, manic-depressive psychosis, and paranoia are psychotic disorders, whereas psychoneurosis (neurosis) preserves reality testing and is not a psychosis.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following definitions: ‘Effectiveness measures the extent to which predetermined objectives are achieved. Efficiency measures how well the resources are utilized.’ In view of these definitions, which of the fol lowing assertions are true ?
1. Percentage of bed occupancy measures effectiveness
2. Immunization coverage rate measures efficiency
3. Cost per patient treated measures efficiency
4. Reduction in mo rtality measure s effectiveness
Select the correct answer u sing the code given below:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Effectiveness measures goal achievement (e.g., reduction in mortality), whereas efficiency measures resource utilization (e.g., cost per patient treated, immunization coverage per unit resource).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
With reference to the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme, c onsider the following statements:
1. Active case finding is pursued under this Programme.
2. Microscopy centres are established in the districts for every one lakh population and in hilly and tribal areas for every 50,000 population. Which of these statements is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under RNTCP, passive (not active) case finding was the primary strategy, and Designated Microscopy Centres (DMCs) were established at 1 per 100,000 population (1 per 50,000 in hilly/tribal areas).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Districts are classified into different categories regarding neonatal tetanus risk. Which one of the following correctly describes ‘Neonatal Tetanus Elimination‘ status?
options: Incidence rate more than 2/1000 births, two do ses of TT vaccine coverage less than 70%, attended deliveries between 60% and 70%
Incidence rate between 1 to 2/1000 births, three doses of TT vaccine coverage 70%, attended deliveries more than 75%
Incidence rate 0.5 to 1 /1000 births, three doses of TT vaccine coverage between 70% and 80%, attended deliveries between 65% and 70%
Incidence rate less than 0.1/1000 births, two doses of TT vaccine coverage more than 90%, attended deliveries more t han 75%
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: WHO defines Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus Elimination (MNTE) as an annual incidence of <0.1 neonatal tetanus cases per 1,000 live births in every district, supported by high TT2+ coverage.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Influenza vaccine is recommended for:
1. Elderly
2. Persons with underlying chronic diseases
3. HIV infected
4. General population
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Seasonal influenza vaccination is specifically prioritized for high-risk groups including the elderly, individuals with chronic medical conditions, and HIV-infected patients.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
With reference to mumps, consider the following statements:
1. The average age of incidence of mumps is higher than that of measles and chicken pox.
2. The mumps disease tends to be more severe in adults than in children.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mumps has a higher average age of incidence than measles or chickenpox and tends to run a more severe course with complications (e.g., orchitis) in adults.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements about content/yield of 100 gm of some foodstuffs:
1. Fat content of Bengal gram is less than that of maize
2. Protein content of maize is more than that of rice
3. Calorie yield of fish and egg is same
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Per 100 g, maize (~11.1 g) has a higher protein content than milled rice (~6.8 g), whereas Bengal gram has more fat than maize and fish yields fewer calories than eggs.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements :
1. Protein content of soyabean is more than that of meat (per 100 gm)
2. Fat content of fish is more than that of soyabean (per 100 gm)
3. Calorie yield for each 100 gm of fish is almost the same as for 100 gm of banana
4. Fat content of soyabea n is more than that of eggs (per 100 gm)
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Per 100 g, soybean (~43 g protein, ~19.5 g fat) contains more protein than meat and more fat than eggs (~13 g), and fish (~100–115 kcal) yields roughly similar calories to banana (~116 kcal).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following features of food poisoning: ‘Incubation period less than 24 hours, source of infection is milk products , and symptoms include diarrhoea and vomiting.’ To which of the following does the above description apply?
1. Staphylococcal food poisoning
2. Salmonella food poisoning
3. Botulism
Select the correct answer using the code gi ven below:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Both staphylococcal food poisoning (1–6 hours) and Salmonella food poisoning (12–24 hours) can have incubation periods under 24 hours and present with vomiting and diarrhoea from contaminated milk products.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: For adolescents, what is the weekly iron and folic acid supplementation dose?
options: 60 mg elemental iron and 400 microgram folic acid
100 mg elemental iron and 500 microgram fo lic acid
120 mg elemental iron and 400 microgram folic acid
150 mg elemental iron and 500 microgram folic acid
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) programme for adolescents in India, the weekly tablet contains 100 mg elemental iron and 500 µg folic acid.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following statements is/are true about proportional case rate of malaria?
1. This indicator is used since morbidity rate is difficult to determine
2. This is defined as the number of cases of malaria for every 100 patients seen in hospital OPDs
3. It is a crude index since cases are not related to their time and space distribut ion
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Proportional case rate of malaria is the number of malaria cases per 100 OPD patients; it is a crude index used when population-based morbidity rates are unavailable, as it ignores time and space distribution.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Type 2 poliovirus was eliminated in India in 2005.
2. Main cause of vaccine derived poliovir uses (VDPV) is Type 2 component of OPV.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wild poliovirus type 2 was last detected globally in India in 1999 (not 2005), and the Type 2 Sabin component of OPV is responsible for the vast majority of circulating vaccine-derived polioviruses (cVDPV2).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is true about hydatid disease?
options: It is rare in sheep rearing countries
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hydatid disease (Echinococcus granulosus) is a cestode zoonosis endemic in sheep-rearing regions where dogs are definitive hosts and humans are accidental dead-end intermediate hosts.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is true about direct age standardization?
options: A stan dard population is used
Age specific death rates are not known
Number of people in each age group is not known
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Direct age standardization applies the observed age-specific death rates of the study population to a chosen standard population with known age distribution.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:
List I (Disease)
List II (Example)
A. Nosocomial
1. Cytomegaloviral infection
B. Opportunistic
2. Hepatitis B viral infection
C. Iatrogenic
3. Aplastic anemia
D. Epornithic
4. Influenza
Code : A B C D
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hepatitis B from needle-stick/blood is nosocomial (A-2), CMV in immunocompromised hosts is opportunistic (B-1), drug-induced aplastic anaemia is iatrogenic (C-3), and influenza is classically associated with avian/animal epornithics (D-4).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: With reference to International Certificate of Vaccination for Yellow Fever, t he validity of the certificate begins how many days after the vaccination?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under International Health Regulations, the Yellow Fever International Certificate of Vaccination becomes valid 10 days after vaccination.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
With reference to dengue virus, consider the following statements:
1. In India, all the four serotypes are found.
2. The reservoir of infection is both man and mosquito.
3. Adults usually have a milder disease than children.
4. Dengue hemorrhagic fever is caused by infection with more than one dengue virus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: All four dengue serotypes circulate in India, both humans and Aedes mosquitoes act as reservoirs, and sequential infection with a different serotype increases the risk of dengue haemorrhagic fever (adults often have severe disease too).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the window period for HIV infection?
options: None of these Among the following foodstuffs, which one has the highest protein content per 100 gm? (a) Black gram (b) Egg (c) Ragi (d) Wheat
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The serological window period for HIV antibody detection typically ranges from 6 to 12/24 weeks (with older ELISA assays taking up to 6–24 weeks).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Among the following foodstuffs, which one has the highest protein content per 100 gm?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Per 100 g, black gram (urad dal, ~24 g protein) has a higher protein content than egg (~13 g), wheat (~12 g), or ragi (~7 g).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Smoking is associated with all the following diseases except:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Smoking is a major risk factor for emphysema, cardiovascular disease, and lung cancer, whereas sarcoidosis is negatively associated with (less common in) smokers.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Skin
2. Water
3. Faeces
4. Urine Bleaching powder can be used for disinfection of wh ich of the above?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bleaching powder (chlorinated lime) is used to disinfect water, faeces, and urine, but it is caustic and not used on human skin.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A 35 year old nulliparous woman complains of menorrhagia and mass per abdomen. On examination, the positive findings are: she is anaemic, has a pelvic mass of 16-weeks size, firm in consistency which moves with the movement of cervix. What is the most likely clinical diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Menorrhagia, anaemia, and a firm 16-week pelvic mass that moves with the cervix in a 35-year-old nulliparous woman are classic for a uterine leiomyoma (fibroid).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Abundant cornified cells in vaginal exfoliative cytology indicate:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Peak oestrogen levels in the late proliferative phase produce maximal maturation of vaginal epithelium with abundant superficial cornified (eosinophilic) cells on exfoliative cytology.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statem ents:
1. Carbon dioxide is the safest gas for creating pneumoperitoneum in operative laparoscopy.
2. Laparoscopic sterilization is not recommended during the period of immediate postpartum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Carbon dioxide is the safest insufflation gas for laparoscopy (non-combustible and rapidly absorbed), and laparoscopic tubal sterilization is avoided in the immediate postpartum period due to the enlarged uterus and increased risk of perforation.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Polyhydramnios at term is diagnosed when AFI is more than:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Polyhydramnios at term is defined ultrasonographically as an Amniotic Fluid Index (AFI) > 24–25 cm (or deepest vertical pocket > 8 cm).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the foll owing is not a potentially teratogenic infection if contracted in pregnancy?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Rubella, CMV, and varicella-zoster (chickenpox) are established teratogenic congenital infections, whereas seasonal influenza virus is not classically teratogenic.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Active management of 3 rd stage of labour includes the following except:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Active management of the third stage of labour (AMTSL) includes 10 IU intramuscular oxytocin (or slow IV infusion, not routine 10 IU IV bolus), controlled cord traction, and uterine massage.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Regarding hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, the following are true except:
options: Significant proteinuria is more than/equal to 0.3 g/24hr
Eclampsia may present in the absence of hypertension
A protein:creatinine ratio more than 30 mg/mmol is considered significant
Urinary dipstick result of +1 is equivalent to urinary prote in concentration of 300 mg/dl
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A +1 urine dipstick corresponds to approximately 30 mg/dL (0.3 g/L) of protein, not 300 mg/dL (which corresponds to +3).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of Mayer Rokitansky Kuster Hauser syndrome?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: MRKH syndrome (Müllerian aplasia) is frequently associated with renal (e.g., renal agenesis) and skeletal (vertebral) anomalies, whereas cardiac anomalies are not a characteristic feature.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a contraindication for prescribing combined oral contraceptive pills?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Thromboembolic disease, active viral hepatitis, and rheumatic heart disease with valvular/thrombotic risk contraindicate combined oral contraceptives, whereas PID does not (COCs actually reduce PID risk).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: The following are used in the staging of carcinoma of the cervix except :
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under classical clinical FIGO staging of cervical carcinoma, vaginal involvement, parametrial extension, and hydronephrosis/hydroureter are included, whereas pelvic lymph node status was excluded until the 2018 revision.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Presence of signet-ring cells in a cellular or myxomatous stroma is diagnostic of:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Krukenberg tumour is a metastatic ovarian tumour (most commonly from gastric signet-ring cell carcinoma) characterized histologically by mucin-filled signet-ring cells in a cellular stroma.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A 58 year old woman, post menopausal for last 8 years comes with history of spotting per vaginum. What is the most likely cause?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Atrophic endometritis/vaginitis is the most common cause of postmenopausal spotting or bleeding in a 58-year-old woman (though endometrial carcinoma must be ruled out).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A diabetic obese patient comes with history of post-menopausal bleeding. On examination, there is a supra pubic mass and per vagina there is purulent discharge. The probable diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Obesity and diabetes are classic risk factors for endometrial carcinoma, which presents with postmenopausal bleeding, an enlarged uterus (suprapubic mass), and sometimes pyometra causing purulent vaginal discharge.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: An adolescent girl with stage 1a dysgerminoma is managed by:
options: Total abdominal hysterectomy with unilateral salpingo - oophorectomy
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Stage Ia dysgerminoma in an adolescent wishing to preserve fertility is managed conservatively with unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy alone (plus staging).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following conditions is best treated by a posterior colpotomy?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A pelvic abscess pointing into the pouch of Douglas is best drained surgically via posterior colpotomy.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following suture materials has the least tissue reaction?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Monofilament metallic sutures like stainless steel elicit the least tissue inflammatory reaction among the listed suture materials.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Menopause is associated with the following except:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Menopause increases the risk of osteoporosis, ischaemic heart disease, and decreased libido due to oestrogen deficiency, but does not cause delusions.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following conditions simulates the menstrual pattern of pain?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Haematometra (retention of menstrual blood in the uterine cavity due to outflow obstruction) causes cyclic, crampy pain that mimics the menstrual pattern.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the undermentioned conditions does not cause postmenopausal vaginal bleeding?
options: Prolapse of uterus with decubitus ulcer
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Senile vaginitis, cervical carcinoma, and decubitus ulcer on a prolapsed uterus cause postmenopausal bleeding, whereas a benign cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) of the ovary is hormonally inactive and does not.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Defective fusion of the Mullerian ducts may give rise to which of the following?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Incomplete fusion of the two Müllerian (paramesonephric) ducts results in uterine duplication anomalies such as uterus bicornis unicollis.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: For a woman who has had unprotected intercourse two days ago, which one of the following emergency contraceptive methods cannot be suggested?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine device (LNG-IUD) is not recommended for emergency contraception (unlike the copper IUD, ulipristal acetate, levonorgestrel 1.5 mg, or Yuzpe regimen).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Deep transverse arrest of head in labour occurs in:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An android pelvis (funnel-shaped with prominent ischial spines and narrow transverse diameter) predisposes to occipitoposterior position and deep transverse arrest.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Early deceleration of foetal heart rate in labour is du e to:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Early decelerations mirror uterine contractions and are caused by vagal stimulation secondary to fetal head compression.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: McRoberts manoeuvre is used during labour for management of:
options: Normal labour to assist extension of head
Extended arms of breech during assisted breech delivery
Delivery of after coming head of breech
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The McRoberts manoeuvre (hyperflexion of maternal hips onto the abdomen) flattens the sacral promontory and rotates the symphysis pubis to relieve shoulder dystocia.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a suitable condition for outlet forceps application?
options: Head is above ischial spine level
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Outlet forceps require the fetal scalp to be visible at the introitus (head on the perineum, well below the ischial spines); a head above the ischial spines is a strict contraindication.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Polyhydramnios is not caused by which one of the following?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Anencephaly, spina bifida, and oesophageal atresia cause polyhydramnios (impaired fetal swallowing or CSF transudation), whereas renal anomalies (like single kidney/renal agenesis) reduce fetal urine output and cause oligohydramnios.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is the type of antepartum haemorrhage where blood loss is foetal?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Vasa previa involves rupture of unprotected fetal umbilical vessels crossing the internal os, resulting in rapid, life-threatening fetal blood loss.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following conditions is not associated with oligohydramnios during pregnancy?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Post-term pregnancy, PPROM, and IUGR are associated with oligohydramnios, whereas oesophageal atresia impairs fetal swallowing and causes polyhydramnios.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A 23 year old presents with recurrent abortions at 16 weeks gestation. She should be investigated for:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Painless second-trimester pregnancy losses (around 16 weeks) are classically caused by cervical incompetence.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is the most common cause of abortion during first trimester?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Fetal chromosomal abnormalities (most commonly autosomal trisomies) account for over 50% of first-trimester spontaneous abortions.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Abnormally low alpha-fetoprotein in maternal serum indicates:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Abnormally low maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP) is a screening marker for Down syndrome (trisomy 21), whereas elevated MSAFP suggests open neural tube defects.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Umbilical cord blood stem cells are used to treat all the following diseases except :
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Umbilical cord blood stem cells are established/investigated for haematological malignancies (leukaemia) and regenerative/autoimmune conditions, but not for routine treatment of osteoporosis.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A patient of ectopic pregnancy had beta-hCG less than 6000 IU/ml. Medical management was done by single dose methotrexate. Beta-hCG repeated after 48 hours was found 7000 IU/ml. What will you do further?
options: Follow up with Beta - hCG after one week
Follow up with Beta - hCG after 72 hours
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: After single-dose methotrexate for ectopic pregnancy, beta-hCG commonly rises slightly by day 4 (48–72 hours) due to trophoblast lysis; therefore, management is to recheck beta-hCG at 72 hours/day 4–7 rather than immediately operating or repeating the dose.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A 35 year old married woman with no risk factors for cervical cancer is having Pap smear showing ‘atypical squamous cells of under mined significance (ASCUS)’ for the first time. What is the further step in the management?
options: Large loop excision of the transformation zone
To follow up with Pap test at 6 months
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In low-risk women with a first-time ASCUS Pap smear (when HPV DNA testing is not done), repeating the Pap smear at 6 months is an appropriate follow-up step.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: For a primary amenorrhoea in dividual having an XY karyotype, normal infantile female external and internal genitalia fibrous bands in place of gonad, lack of development of secondary sexual characters, what is the most probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Swyer syndrome (46,XY pure gonadal dysgenesis) presents with primary amenorrhoea, streak gonads, absent secondary sexual characteristics, and normal infantile female internal/external genitalia due to absent AMH and testosterone.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A lady who is using oral contraceptive pills comes with a complaint of vaginal discharge and pruritus vulvae. On local examination, there is curdy white discharge from the vagina. W hat is the most likely clinical diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Curdy white vaginal discharge with intense pruritus vulvae in an OCP user is classic for vulvovaginal candidiasis (monilial vaginitis).

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: Antisperm antibodies are usually present in:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In immunological infertility, antisperm antibodies in women are most commonly secreted in the cervical mucus (cervix), causing sperm agglutination or immobilization.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: For a woman who has been operated for chocolate cyst with normal menstrual cycle, any of the following may be prescribed except:
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: GnRH analogues (leuprolide), dienogest, and oral progestogens suppress endometriotic implants after surgery, whereas tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic used for heavy menstrual bleeding and has no role in suppressing endometriosis.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: For a 40 year old hypertensive woma n, which one of the following is not recommended for contraception?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: NuvaRing is a combined oestrogen-progestogen vaginal ring and is contraindicated in a 40-year-old woman with hypertension due to thromboembolic and cardiovascular risks.

upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.text: A 30 year old female has severe dysmenorrhoea and dyspareunia. On examination , uterus is 8 weeks size, uniformly enlarged and there i s tenderness in posterior fornix. What is the most probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2016-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Severe dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia, and a uniformly enlarged, tender uterus (~8 weeks size) in a 30-year-old woman are classic clinical features of adenomyosis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The following statements in relation to right ventricular myocardial infarction are correct except:
options: It may occur along with inferior wall myocardial infarction
The ECG shows segment elevation in right precordial leads
Prognosis in right ventricular infarction is worse than the left ventricular myocardial infarction
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Right ventricular myocardial infarction is preload-dependent, so negative inotropes and vasodilators like intravenous diltiazem or nitrates are contraindicated; management relies on IV fluids and maintaining AV synchrony.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Atrial myxoma is associated with the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Left atrial myxoma causes constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss), embolic phenomena (splinter haemorrhages), and a mid-diastolic rumble ('tumour plop') mimicking mitral stenosis rather than a systolic murmur.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Unable to speak in sentences
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wide fixed split S2 is classic for atrial septal defect (A-2), continuous machinery murmur for patent ductus arteriosus (B-3), muffled heart sounds for pericardial effusion (C-4), and wide variable split S2 for pulmonary hypertension (D-1).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Diarrhoea present in upto 50% cases
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Amiodarone is used for ventricular tachycardia (A-3), adenosine for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (B-4), digoxin for atrial fibrillation (C-2), and atropine for Mobitz type II AV block (D-1).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Klebsiella pneumonia has the following characteristics except:
options: Lung abscess formation is very uncommon
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Klebsiella pneumonia classically causes upper-lobe consolidation ('bulging fissure' sign), empyema, pneumatoceles, and frequent lung abscess formation (not uncommon).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-I (Disease)
List-II (Antigen leading to hypersensitivity pneumonitis)
A. Bagassosis
1. Oak, Cedar, Pine dust
B. Byssinosis
2. Moldy hay
C. Farmer’s lung
3. Cotton
D. Wood worker’s lung
4. Sugarcane dust
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Bagassosis is caused by moldy sugarcane dust (A-4), byssinosis by cotton dust (B-3), farmer's lung by moldy hay (C-2), and woodworker's lung by oak/cedar/pine dust (D-1).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not likely to be associated with pulmonary fibrosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Coal worker's pneumoconiosis, asbestosis, and ankylosing spondylitis (apical fibrosis) cause pulmonary fibrosis, whereas primary biliary cirrhosis is an autoimmune cholestatic liver disease.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are a feature/features of severity in immediate assessment of acute severe asthma?
1. Pulse rate >110 per min
2. Pulsus paradoxus
3. Unable to speak in sentences
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Inability to speak in sentences, heart rate >110/min, and pulsus paradoxus are established clinical indicators of acute severe asthma.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Cavitating pulmonary lesions can be seen in the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tuberculosis, bronchogenic carcinoma, and histoplasmosis frequently produce cavitating pulmonary lesions, whereas sarcoidosis typically causes bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and parenchymal infiltrates without cavitation.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A 35 year old 40 kg male patient was diagnosed to be a case of pulmonary tuberculosis. The appropriate conventional regimen of antitubercular drugs would be:
options: Rifampicin 450 mg + Isoniazid 300 mg + Pyrazinamide 1500 mg
Rifampicin 600 mg + Isoniazid 300 mg + Pyrazinamide 1000 mg
Rifampicin 450 mg + Isoniazid 200 mg + Pyrazinamide 1000 mg
Rifampicin 450 mg + Isoniazid 200 mg + Pyrazinamide 1500 mg
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: For a 40 kg adult with pulmonary tuberculosis under conventional weight-banded dosing, the appropriate daily regimen is rifampicin 450 mg, isoniazid 200 mg, and pyrazinamide 1000 mg.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the auscultatory signs is absent in mitral stenosis in the presence of atrial fibrillation?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pre-systolic accentuation of the mitral stenosis murmur is produced by vigorous atrial contraction at end-diastole and therefore disappears in atrial fibrillation.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not recommended in immediate treatment of acute severe asthma?
options: High doses of inhaled B2 –adrenoreceptor agonists
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Immediate management of acute severe asthma relies on high-flow oxygen, high-dose inhaled beta-2 agonists, and systemic corticosteroids; IV aminophylline is no longer recommended routinely due to narrow therapeutic index and toxicity.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a feature of type 2 respiratory failure ?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Type 2 (hypercapnic) respiratory failure is defined by elevated PaCO2 (>45–50 mmHg) with hypoxaemia (causing asterixis and papilloedema); a PaCO2 of 38 mmHg with PaO2 50 mmHg represents Type 1 respiratory failure.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following drugs is not given in dilated cardiomyopathy?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and spironolactone improve survival in dilated cardiomyopathy/HFrEF, whereas non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers have negative inotropic effects and are avoided.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following features are related to Zollinger Ellison syndrome?
1. Aggressive and refractory peptic ulceration
2. Unregulated gastrin release
3. Beta islet cell tumour of pancreas
4. Diarrhoea present in upto 50% cases
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome features refractory peptic ulcers, unregulated gastrin secretion, and diarrhoea (up to 50%); it arises from non-beta islet cell (G-cell) gastrinomas, not beta-cell tumours.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: In which of the following diseases, primary skin lesions are not seen?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: SLE (malar/discoid rash), infectious mononucleosis (maculopapular rash), and leptospirosis (pretibial/petechial rash) can present with primary skin lesions, whereas Hepatitis B does not typically produce primary skin lesions.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a common feature of hypersensitivity pneumonitis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is a Type III/IV immune reaction characterized by neutrophilia/lymphocytosis and raised CRP rather than peripheral eosinophilia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to duodenal ulcers:
1. They occur most often in the second part of duodenum.
2. Infection with H. pylori and NSAID–induced injury account for the majority of duodenal ulcers.
3. Malignant duodenal ulcers are extremely rare.
4. Eradication of H. pylori has greatly reduced the recurrence rates in duodenal ulcers.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Duodenal ulcers occur most commonly in the first part (not second part) of the duodenum, are mainly caused by H. pylori and NSAIDs, are rarely malignant, and show markedly reduced recurrence after H. pylori eradication.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Carcinoid tumours commonly arise from:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Carcinoid tumours arise from enterochromaffin (argentaffin/Kulchitsky) cells, most commonly in the gastrointestinal tract (small intestine/appendix).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following viral markers signifies the ongoing viral replication in the case of Hepatitis-B infection?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) is a soluble viral protein that correlates directly with active viral replication and high infectivity.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The following may result in polyuria except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic renal failure, hypercalcaemia, and lithium toxicity impair urinary concentrating ability and cause polyuria, whereas hypoadrenalism (Addison's disease) causes volume depletion and oliguria.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Regarding adult polycystic kidney disease, which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: Inherited as autosomal dominant with 100% penetrance
Associated with increased incidence of subarachnoid haemorrhage
Renal cell carcinoma is a frequent association
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) has nearly 100% penetrance, hepatic cysts, and berry aneurysms (subarachnoid haemorrhage), but does not have a frequent association with renal cell carcinoma.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a feature of chronic renal failure?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic renal failure causes reduced 1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D3 synthesis, osteomalacia/renal osteodystrophy, and secondary hyperparathyroidism, but not hyperthyroidism.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient with past history of recurrent headache, presents with irregular, dazzling, enlarging visual phenomena that obstructs vision in the affected region and remains for several minutes. The symptoms are indicative of:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Irregular, dazzling, enlarging visual disturbances (scintillating scotoma/fortification spectra) preceding or accompanying recurrent headaches are classic for migraine aura.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-I (Disease)
List-II (Cause)
A. Macrocytic anaemia
1. Iron deficiency
B. Microcytic anaemia
2. Hypothyroidism
C. Hemolytic anaemia
3. Vitamin B12 deficiency
D. Megaloblastic anaemia
4. Alpha methyldopa
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Matched List-I and List-II pairs correspond to the disease-cause code A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Haemolysis in G6PD (glucose 6 phosphate dehydrogenase) enzyme deficiency may occur with all of the following drugs except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Primaquine, phenacetin, and probenecid can trigger oxidative haemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals, whereas penicillin is safe.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-I (Blood picture)
List-II (Type of Anaemia)
A. Microcytic, hypochromic red cells
1. Vitamin B12 deficiency anaemia
B. Macrocytic, hypochromic red cells
2. Thalassemia major
C. Large number of early, intermediate and late erythroblasts
3. Aplastic anaemia
D. Low reticulocyte count
4. Iron-deficiency anaemia
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Iron-deficiency anaemia shows microcytic hypochromic cells (A-4), B12 deficiency shows macrocytic cells (B-1), thalassaemia major shows abundant erythroblasts (C-2), and aplastic anaemia shows a low reticulocyte count (D-3).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following conditions does not cause pancytopenia?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypersplenism, aplastic anaemia, and marrow infiltration cause pancytopenia, whereas G6PD deficiency causes isolated haemolytic anaemia with reticulocytosis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following drugs does not cause oedema?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Growth hormone, anabolic steroids, and dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers cause fluid retention and peripheral oedema, whereas beta-blockers do not.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient of hypoglycemia fails to regain consciousness after blood glucose is restored to normal. The complication that carries high mortality and morbidity is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Prolonged severe hypoglycaemia can lead to irreversible neuronal injury and cerebral oedema, explaining failure to regain consciousness after normoglycaemia is restored.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: An adult patient presents with systemic hypertension, renal calculus disease and peptic ulcer disease. Which one of the following is most likely occurrence in this case?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Primary hyperparathyroidism causes hypercalcaemia, predisposing to nephrolithiasis ('stones'), peptic ulcer disease ('groans'), and systemic hypertension.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-I (Types of hyperlipidemia)
List-II (Feature)
A. Hyperchylomicronaemia
1. Palmar plantar xanthoma
B. Hyperbetalipoproteinaemia
2. Subcutaneous extensive tendon xanthoma
C. Type III hyperlipoproteinaemia
3. Eruptive xanthoma over buttocks
D. Familial LPL deficiency
4. Triglyceride level above 1000 mg %
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hyperchylomicronaemia has triglycerides >1000 mg% (A-4), hyperbetalipoproteinaemia has tendon xanthomas (B-2), Type III hyperlipoproteinaemia has palmar/plantar xanthomas (C-1), and familial LPL deficiency has eruptive xanthomas (D-3).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is least suggestive of poliovirus infection?
options: Low grade fever and malaise with complete resolution in 2 to 3 days
Biphasic illness with several days of fever, then meningeal symptoms and asymmetric flaccid paralysis 5 to 10 days later
Descending motor paralysis with preservation of tendon reflexes and absent sensation
Failure to isolate a virus from the CSF in the presence of marked meningismus
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (c) — Descending motor paralysis with preservation of tendon reflexes and absent sensation.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The following conditions can cause interstitial nephritis except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Infections, lymphoma, and sarcoidosis can cause interstitial nephritis, whereas hepatorenal syndrome is functional renal vasoconstriction with normal renal histology.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are characteristics features of tuberculoid leprosy?
1. Type 2 lepra reaction
2. A few lesions with well demarcated edges
3. Early and marked nerve damage
4. Tendency to heal spontaneously
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tuberculoid leprosy presents with a few well-demarcated lesions, early severe nerve involvement, and spontaneous healing; Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL) occurs in lepromatous/borderline lepromatous leprosy.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following immunological reactions occurs in Goodpasture syndrome ?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Goodpasture's syndrome is a Type II cytotoxic hypersensitivity reaction (note: the official UPSC key for this paper marked (c) Type III immune complex).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Regarding erythema nodosum leprosum, which one of the following is not correct?
options: It is usually during initiation of treatment
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 lepra reaction) typically occurs after several months (not usually at initiation) of multidrug therapy in multibacillary leprosy, presenting with tender nodules, lymphadenopathy, and iridocyclitis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common microorganism known to cause tropical pyomyositis is :
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the causative organism in over 80–90% of cases of tropical pyomyositis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Following are the common features of Cushing’s syndrome except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cushing's syndrome features truncal obesity, osteoporosis, glucose intolerance, and proximal (not distal) muscle weakness/myopathy.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A farmer presents with history of fever and chills, severe bodyache, headache, conjuctival suffusion and jaundice. He has severe muscle tenderness, leukocytosis and mild uraemia. The most likely diagnosis would be:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fever, severe myalgia with muscle tenderness, conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, leukocytosis, and uraemia in a farmer are classic for severe leptospirosis (Weil's disease).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding falciparum malaria:
1. The mortality rises steeply when the proportion of infected erythrocytes increases above 3 percent.
2. The patient may develop hypoglycemia even when not treated with quinine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In falciparum malaria, mortality rises steeply when parasitaemia exceeds 2–3%, and severe malaria itself causes hypoglycaemia via parasite glucose consumption and impaired gluconeogenesis even without quinine.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: “Loeffler’s syndrome” is characterized by:
options: Fibrosis in the base of one or both lungs
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Loeffler's syndrome (simple pulmonary eosinophilia) is characterized by transient, migratory pulmonary infiltrates on chest X-ray with peripheral eosinophilia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Keyboard operators and typists are especially susceptible to injury of the
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Repetitive wrist flexion/extension in keyboard operators and typists predisposes to carpal tunnel syndrome due to compression of the median nerve.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a clinical feature of Kwashiorkor?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Kwashiorkor is characterized by bipedal oedema, hypoalbuminaemia, and moon face, whereas visible severe wasting is the hallmark of marasmus.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Clinical features)
List II (Deficiency of)
A. Flaky paint rashes of lower extremity
1. Niacin
B. Goose-hump skin lesion
2. Thiamine
C. Confabulation
3. Zinc
D. Dementia
4. Vitamin A
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Flaky-paint rash occurs in zinc deficiency (A-3), phrynoderma/goose-bump skin in vitamin A deficiency (B-4), confabulation (Korsakoff) in thiamine deficiency (C-2), and dementia (pellagra) in niacin deficiency (D-1).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Psoriasis
2. Atopic dermatitis
3. Leprosy
4. Vitiligo PUVA therapy can be used to treat which of the above?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: PUVA (psoralen + UVA) photochemotherapy is used for psoriasis, vitiligo, and severe atopic dermatitis, but has no role in treating leprosy.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The cutaneous viral infection which is commonly seen in children and characterized by single or multiple pearly -white skin colored smooth dome shaped papules with central pitting is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Molluscum contagiosum (caused by a poxvirus) presents in children as pearly-white, dome-shaped papules with characteristic central umbilication (pitting).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements about polyarticular juvenile rheumatoid arthritis:
1. It is more common in girls
2. Five or more joints are affected within the first six months of onset
3. Uveitis occurs in 95% patients
4. Rheumatoid factor may be negative
Which of the statements given above are true ?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Polyarticular juvenile rheumatoid arthritis is more common in girls, involves ≥5 joints within the first 6 months, and can be RF-negative; chronic uveitis is much more common in oligoarticular (pauciarticular) JRA than in 95% of polyarticular cases.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding schizophrenia:
1. Patient feels that other persons put thoughts into his mind
2. Patient feels that he is being punished for his wrong doings
3. He may be in a state of catatonia
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Schizophrenia features thought insertion and catatonia, whereas delusions of guilt/punishment for wrongdoings are characteristic of severe psychotic depression.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Lithium carbonate is employed in the following conditions except:
options: To treat acute episodes of mania
To prevent depression in bipolar disorders
To prevent depression in unipolar disorders
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lithium carbonate is used to treat acute mania, prevent manic relapses, and prevent bipolar depression (or augment resistant depression), but is not a first-line monotherapy to prevent unipolar depression.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The following conditions can cause protein-losing enteropathy except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ulcerative colitis, celiac disease, and intestinal lymphoma can cause protein-losing enteropathy, whereas irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a functional disorder without mucosal protein loss.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following ocular findings is a component of Foville syndrome?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Foville syndrome (inferior medial pontine syndrome) causes ipsilateral lateral conjugate gaze palsy, facial nerve palsy, and contralateral hemiplegia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The following features are suggestive of Behcet’s syndrome except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Behçet's syndrome is characterized by recurrent oral and genital aphthous ulcers, uveitis, and polyarthritis; livedo reticularis is typical of antiphospholipid syndrome or PAN.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-I (Drug)
List-II (Side effect)
A. Phenytoin sodium
1. Hypothyroidism
B. Para aminosalicylic acid
2. Hepatotoxicity
C. Rifampicin
3. 8th nerve damage
D. Streptomycin
4. Cerebellar dysfunction
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Phenytoin causes cerebellar ataxia/dysfunction (A-4), PAS causes hypothyroidism (B-1), rifampicin causes hepatotoxicity (C-2), and streptomycin causes 8th cranial nerve ototoxicity (D-3).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-I (Disease state)
List-II (Clinical feature)
A. Pemphigus vulgaris
1. Acro-osteolysis
B. Psoriasis
2. Brachydactyly
C. Turner syndrome
3. Koebner phenomenon
D. Primary hyperparathyroidism
4. Nikolsky sign
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pemphigus vulgaris shows Nikolsky's sign (A-4), psoriasis shows Koebner phenomenon (B-3), Turner syndrome shows brachydactyly/short 4th metacarpal (C-2), and primary hyperparathyroidism shows acro-osteolysis (D-1).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A 10 year old child “blank s out” in class (e.g. stops talking midsentence and then continues as if nothing had happened). During spells there is slight quivering of lips. What is the most probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Brief staring spells ('blanking out' mid-sentence) with subtle lip-smacking or eyelid fluttering and immediate return to baseline in a 10-year-old child are classic for absence seizures.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A 45 year old man presents with hematuria. Renal biopsy demonstrates a focal necrotizing glomerulitis with crescent formation. The patient gives history of intermittent hemoptysis and intermittent chest pain of moderate intensity. A previous chest X -ray had demonstrated multiple opacities, some of which were cavitated. The patient also has chronic cold like nasal symptoms. What is the most probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic sinonasal symptoms, cavitating pulmonary nodules, and crescentic necrotizing glomerulonephritis with haematuria are classic for Wegener's granulomatosis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A 28 year old woman presented with high grade fever, cough, diarrhea and mental confusion for 4 days. X-ray chest revealed bilateral pneumonitis. Search for etiology will most likely reveal
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: High-grade fever, cough, bilateral pneumonia, watery diarrhoea, and confusion (encephalopathy) strongly point to Legionella pneumophila pneumonia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Congenital heart disease associated with pre-excitation is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ebstein's anomaly (downward displacement of the tricuspid valve) is classically associated with accessory conduction pathways and Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) pre-excitation.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Hockey-stick appearance in echocardiography is a feature of:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A 'hockey-stick' appearance of the anterior mitral leaflet during diastole on echocardiography is characteristic of rheumatic mitral stenosis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Hutchinson sign is a feature of ocular involvement by which of the following viruses?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hutchinson's sign (vesicles on the tip or side of the nose indicating nasociliary nerve involvement) predicts ocular involvement in herpes zoster ophthalmicus.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Well recognised side-effects of prolonged phenytoin use may result in all except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Long-term phenytoin therapy causes hirsutism, gingival hyperplasia, lymphadenopathy, and cerebellar ataxia, whereas it tends to cause hyperglycaemia rather than hypoglycaemia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: First order neurons in the visual pathway are constituted by:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In the visual pathway, retinal bipolar cells constitute the first-order neurons (connecting photoreceptors to retinal ganglion cells, which are second-order neurons).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Level of which hormone is likely to increase after hypothalamic ablation?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Prolactin secretion is under tonic inhibitory control by hypothalamic dopamine; therefore, hypothalamic ablation removes this inhibition and increases serum prolactin levels.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A 50 year old patient with signs of peripheral ne uropathy is found to have diabetes mellitus. He has no ocular symptoms. When would you refer this patient for retina evaluation?
options: If he needs insulin for blood sugar
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Patients with newly diagnosed Type 2 diabetes mellitus (especially with microvascular complications like neuropathy) must be referred for a dilated retinal examination immediately at diagnosis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following tests has the highest chance of detecting HIV infection in a blood donor during the window period?
options: Demonstration of antibody to HIV by ELISA
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: During the HIV window period before seroconversion, p24 antigen is detectable in blood earlier than anti-HIV antibodies detected by ELISA or Western blot.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The following are exotoxin-mediated infections except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cholera, botulism, and tetanus are mediated by potent bacterial exotoxins, whereas typhoid (Salmonella Typhi) is an invasive infection involving endotoxin.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The following tests can be used for diagnosing celiac disease except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG), anti-endomysial, and anti-gliadin antibodies are used to diagnose celiac disease, whereas antinuclear antibodies (ANA) are not.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not an early complication of acute myocardial infarction?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Dressler's syndrome (post-MI autoimmune pericarditis) is a late complication occurring weeks after acute myocardial infarction, unlike papillary muscle dysfunction, VSD, or early fibrinous pericarditis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following conditions:
1. Thyrotoxicosis, phaeochromocytoma and acromegaly
2. Haemochromatosis
3. Conn’s syndrome (primary hyperaldosteronism)
4. Pancreatic carcinoma
Which of the above may result in secondary diabetes mellitus?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Secondary diabetes mellitus occurs in acromegaly, thyrotoxicosis, phaeochromocytoma, haemochromatosis, and pancreatic carcinoma, whereas Conn's syndrome causes hypokalaemia and hypertension.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements: Gastric lavage is contraindicated in children in case of iron poisoning kerosene poisoning corrosive poisoning aspirin poisoning
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Gastric lavage is strictly contraindicated in corrosive and hydrocarbon (kerosene) poisoning because of the risk of oesophageal perforation and chemical pneumonitis from aspiration.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Visible gastric peristalsis
2. Bilious vomiting
3. Palpable mass
4. Melena
Which of the above is/are the feature/features of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis presents with non-bilious projectile vomiting, visible gastric peristalsis, and a palpable olive-shaped epigastric mass (not bilious vomiting or melena).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A very large ventricular septal defect should be operated :
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A large ventricular septal defect causing significant left-to-right shunt and pulmonary hypertension should be surgically closed before 6 months of age (or early infancy) to prevent irreversible pulmonary vascular disease.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A 2 year old boy is being evaluated for se verity of malnutrition. The child weighs 7 kg and measures 74 cm in length. Expected (median) weight for height, and height for age for this child are 9 kg and 86 cm respectively. According to WHO classification of undernutrition, which of the following is the correct category for this child?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Here weight-for-height is 7/9 = 77.8% (70–80%, wasted) and height-for-age is 74/86 = 86.0% (85–90%, stunted), classifying the child as wasted and stunted.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Catch-up diet for treatment of severe malnutrition in children should achieve the following:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: During the catch-up growth (rehabilitation) phase of severe acute malnutrition, children require high energy (150–220 kcal/kg/day) and high protein (4–6 g/kg/day).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a feature of vitamin D deficiency rickets?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency rickets causes reduced gut calcium absorption, hypocalcaemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism (increased, not decreased, PTH), renal phosphate wasting, and elevated alkaline phosphatase.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: A child presents with moderate fever for tw o months. On examination, she had moderate anaemia and a few petechia. All the following can be the diagnosis except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Prolonged moderate fever (2 months) with anaemia and petechiae can occur in acute leukaemia, disseminated tuberculosis, and systemic JRA, whereas untreated typhoid does not typically run a 2-month chronic petechial course.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding juvenile chronic myeloid leukemia?
options: The prognosis is better than the adult form of chronic myeloid leukemia.
Single agent chemotherapy with busulfan or hydroxyurea can achieve remission.
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Juvenile chronic myeloid leukaemia (juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia) is Philadelphia chromosome-negative, features thrombocytopenia, and carries a poorer prognosis than adult CML.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following features:
1. X-linked recessive inheritance
2. Atopic dermatitis
3. Low serum levels of IgA
Which of the above is/are the characteristic features of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is an X-linked recessive immunodeficiency triad of thrombocytopenia, eczema (atopic dermatitis), and recurrent infections, with elevated (not low) serum IgA and IgE.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Lisch nodules are seen in which of the following conditions?
