upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lisch nodules (pigmented iris hamartomas) are a characteristic diagnostic feature of neurofibromatosis type 1 (von Recklinghausen's disease).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
A 5 year old c hild presented with microcytic hypochromic anaemia. Serum ferritin is low.
Which of the following is least likely?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Thalassemia major is characterized by iron overload and elevated serum ferritin, making a low serum ferritin least likely (unlike celiac disease, nutritional iron deficiency, or PNH).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: An infant can sit l eaning forward on his hands. He bounces actively when made to stand. He laughs aloud and becomes concerned when the mother moves away. What is his most likely age?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sitting leaning forward on hands (tripod position), bouncing when held standing, laughing aloud, and stranger anxiety are classic developmental milestones at 28 weeks (~7 months).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Association with hepatomegaly)
List II (Presentation)
A. Skin lesion
1. Histiocytosis
B. Engorged neck veins
2. Galactosemia
C. Cataract
3. Toxoplasmosis
D. Hydrocephalus
4. Constrictive pericarditis
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hepatomegaly with skin lesions occurs in Langerhans cell histiocytosis (A-1), engorged neck veins in constrictive pericarditis (B-4), cataract in galactosaemia (C-2), and hydrocephalus in congenital toxoplasmosis (D-3).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The most common type of juvenile rheumatoid arthritis is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oligoarticular (pauciarticular) juvenile rheumatoid arthritis is the most common subtype of JRA (~50% of cases).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: An 8 year old boy presented to the Emergency Department on the fourth day of fever during a dengue epidemic. He ha d a mild erythematous rash on his body and no bleeding from any site. His BP was 110/70 mmHg and pulse was 94/minute. Hess test was positive. Dengue serology report is awaited. Platelet count is 30,000/cm3 and PCV: 36%. What is the treatment of choice?
options: Plenty of oral/ IV fluids and observation
Emergency platelet transfusion to raise platelets above 50,000/ cm3
Give antipyretic and wait for dengue serology report
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In dengue without active bleeding or shock (stable BP 110/70, PCV 36%), management is adequate oral/IV hydration and close monitoring; prophylactic platelet transfusion is not indicated.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the Code given below the lists:
List I ( Antidote)
List II (Poison/Drug)
A. Calcium sodium edetate
1. Cyanide
B. Sodium nitrite
2. Nitrobenzene
C. Methylene blue
3. Lead
D. Atropine
4. Organophosphate 5. Kerosene
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Calcium sodium edetate chelates lead (A-3), sodium nitrite treats cyanide poisoning (B-1), methylene blue treats nitrobenzene-induced methaemoglobinaemia (C-2), and atropine treats organophosphate poisoning (D-4).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Diseases)
List II (Laboratory parameters)
A. Thalassemia major
1. Increased serum iron, decreased TIBC, increased serum ferritin
B. Iron deficiency anaemia
2. Decreased serum iron, increased TIBC, decreased serum ferritin
C. Nephrotic syndrome
3. Decreased serum iron, decreased TIBC, increased serum ferritin
D. Acute iron poisoning
4. Increased serum iron, normal TIBC, normal serum ferritin
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Thalassemia major shows high serum iron, low TIBC, and high ferritin (A-1); iron deficiency shows low iron, high TIBC, and low ferritin (B-2); nephrotic syndrome shows low iron and TIBC (C-3); acute iron poisoning shows markedly elevated iron and TIBC (D-4).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
A previously well 2 year old boy presents with a brief generalized seizure. There is no past or family history of seizures. On examination, child is alert, active, febrile with axillary temperature of 39.4 0C. Except for bilateral tonsillar enlargement and congestion, systemic examination is normal. Management at this time may include:
1. Immediate reduction of body temperature
2. Intravenous diazepam and phenytoin, followed by a lumbar puncture
3. Institution of phenytoin for maintenance therapy for at least one year
4. Rectal diazepam every 8 hourly for 2-3 days to reduce the risk of recurrence
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A brief generalized seizure with high fever (39.4°C) and tonsillitis in an alert 2-year-old is a simple febrile seizure; immediate management includes antipyretics/cooling and treating the underlying infection, without routine diazepam/phenytoin or LP.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Endocrinological disorders)
List II (Results of investigations)
A. Hypothyroidism
1. Increased urinary excretion of catecholamines
B. Cushing’s syndrome
2. Increased urinary 17-ketosteroids
C. Pheochromocytoma
3. Hypocalcaemia and hyperphosphataemia
D. Hypoparathyroidism
4. TSH levels are increased and T3, T4 levels are decreased
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypothyroidism shows high TSH and low T3/T4 (A-4), Cushing's syndrome shows elevated urinary steroids (B-2), pheochromocytoma shows high urinary catecholamines (C-1), and hypoparathyroidism shows hypocalcaemia and hyperphosphataemia (D-3).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the Code given below the lists:
List I ( Clinical presentation)
List II (Disease pathology)
A. Extrapyramidal cerebral palsy
1. Stroke
B. Spastic quadriplegia
2. Multicystic encephalomalacia
C. Spastic hemiplegia
3. Periventricular leukomalacia
D. Spastic diplegia
4. Bilirubin encephalopathy
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Extrapyramidal cerebral palsy is linked to bilirubin encephalopathy/kernicterus (A-4), spastic quadriplegia to multicystic encephalomalacia (B-2), spastic hemiplegia to perinatal stroke (C-1), and spastic diplegia to periventricular leukomalacia (D-3).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following pairs: National Park State
1. Keoladeo Ghana National Park ...... Rajasthan
2. Sultanpur National Park ...... Uttar Pradesh
3. Valley of Flowers National Park ...... Himachal Pradesh Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Keoladeo Ghana National Park is in Rajasthan (correct), whereas Sultanpur National Park is in Haryana (not UP) and Valley of Flowers National Park is in Uttarakhand (not Himachal Pradesh).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The Himalayas have snowline at higher altitude compared to that in the Alps mountains. This is because
options: Himalayas are higher than the Alps
Himalayas are located in lower latitudes
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Because the Himalayas lie at much lower latitudes (closer to the equator) than the Alps, they receive more solar insolation and have a higher snowline altitude.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
The knowledge of genome sequence is important to understand how genes work together in the growth and development of an entire organism.
2. study the regulatory regions in the genome outside the gene that controls expression of genes.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Knowing an organism's genome sequence reveals both how genes interact during growth and development and how non-coding regulatory regions control gene expression.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Besides the Sunderbans, mangrove forests are also to be found in
1. Bhitarkanika
2. Godavari delta
3. Pichavaram
4. Kaveri (Cauvery) delta
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In addition to the Sundarbans, major Indian mangrove forests are found in Bhitarkanika (Odisha), the Godavari delta (Andhra Pradesh), and Pichavaram/Cauvery delta (Tamil Nadu).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: In the preparation of vinegar in the households, dried fruits can be used.
Vinegar making involves fermentation by yeast.
A fruit juice containing 5% or more sugar cannot be made into vinegar in the households.
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (d) — A fruit juice containing 5% or more sugar cannot be made into vinegar in the households..

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following viruses was exploited to create genetically engineered virus “onyx-15”, an oncolytic virus to target and eliminate cancer cells?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: ONYX-015 is a genetically engineered oncolytic adenovirus with an E1B-55kD deletion designed to selectively replicate in and lyse p53-deficient cancer cells.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not included in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Preamble of the Constitution of India declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic; the word 'Federal' does not appear in the Preamble.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following milk borne diseases:
1. Brucellosis
2. Listeriosis
3. Salmonellosis
Which of the above can be controlled by pasteurization?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pasteurization effectively destroys non-spore-forming milk-borne pathogens including Brucella, Listeria monocytogenes, and Salmonella.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Who of the following is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under Article 64 of the Indian Constitution, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fly ash can be added to agricultural soil to enhance its water holding capacity.
2. Fly ash can be used in the manufacture of bricks and blocks for construction purposes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fly ash improves the water-holding capacity of sandy agricultural soils and is widely used to manufacture fly-ash bricks and construction blocks.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: “Ecological niche” refers to the
options: amount of autotrophs available for consumption of the grazing population.
relationship of an animal with the surrounding animals.
position of an animal with reference to its species composition.
positional and functional relationship of an organism in an ecosystem.
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: An ecological niche describes both the physical habitat (position) and the functional role of a species within an ecosystem.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one the following is not required for the formation of photochemical smog?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Photochemical smog forms when nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds react in the presence of sunlight and oxygen; carbon monoxide is not required.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The ‘Nirbhaya Fund’ set up by the Government of India is for:
options: Promoting the financial literacy of rural poor
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Nirbhaya Fund was established by the Government of India in 2013 to support initiatives aimed at enhancing the safety and security of women.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: What is “Solar Impulse 2”, which was recently in the news?
options: A Central Government sponsored scheme to promote the production of solar energy
A spacecraft sent by NASA to study a comet moving towards Sun
A project of India in collaboration with NASA to study the impact of solar flares on Earth
A round-the-world flight powered only by the solar energy
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Solar Impulse 2 was a Swiss experimental solar-powered aircraft that completed a round-the-world flight powered solely by solar energy.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. In food preservation by irradiation, ionising rays are used.
2. Irradiation does not affect the colour, odour, taste, pH and levels of vitamin contents in the foods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Food irradiation uses ionizing radiation (gamma rays, X-rays, or electron beams) to kill microbes, and it can alter colour, odour, taste, or vitamin levels depending on dose.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Kutch (in Gujarat) has the existence of a large number of salt pans. What could be the most valid reason/reasons for this?
1. Existence of creeks and mudflats
2. Higher evaporation rate
3. Presence of vast intertidal zone
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Rann/coast of Kutch supports extensive salt pans due to its network of creeks and mudflats, vast intertidal zone, and high evaporation rates.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Most of the ozone in the atmosphere is concentrated in the:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: About 90% of atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere (the ozone layer).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Lactic acid
2. Sorbic acid
3. Sulphurous acid
Which of the above are food preservatives?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lactic acid, sorbic acid, and sulphurous acid (sulfites) are all widely used antimicrobial and antioxidant food preservatives.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
With reference to “DNA Microarray” technology, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It helps in identifying the genes involved in a disease by comparing the gene expressions between the tissues from a healthy and an infected person.
2. It allows visualizing the activity of hundreds of genes simultaneously.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: DNA microarray technology allows simultaneous profiling of the expression levels of hundreds to thousands of genes and compares healthy versus diseased tissue.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Artemesinin is a drug derived from a:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Artemisinin is an antimalarial sesquiterpene lactone extracted from the plant Artemisia annua (sweet wormwood).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following can be used to extract heavy metals from water?
1. Aluminium oxide
2. Cellulose
3. Silica
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Aluminium oxide (alumina), modified cellulose, and silica-based adsorbents are all used to extract heavy metal ions from contaminated water.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following represents the correct sequence of vegetational transitions with increasing latitude?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Moving from the equator toward higher latitudes, terrestrial vegetation transitions from tropical rainforest to temperate deciduous forest and then boreal coniferous forest (taiga).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. LED lamps have shorter life span as compared to incandescent bulbs.
2. LED lamps are made by using semi-conductor material.
3. LED lamps are more expensive than conventional sources of lighting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: LED lamps are made from semiconductor materials, cost more upfront than incandescent bulbs, and have a much longer (not shorter) lifespan than incandescent lamps.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: In India, ecologists consider “sacred groves” very valuable because of their role in
options: meeting fuelwood and medicinal needs of local people.
protection of biodiversity that has vanished from surrounding areas due to exploitation by man.
stabilization of climate and reduction of global warming.
socio-cultural and religious interactions among traditional communities of different regions.
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (b) — protection of biodiversity that has vanished from surrounding areas due to exploitation by man..

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: The “Cry1Ac”, often in news is
options: a gene that enables some crop plants to fight pests.
another strain of virus responsible for bird-flue that occurred in China.
a gene used in making the transgenic rice known as “golden rice”.
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cry1Ac is a Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) delta-endotoxin gene inserted into transgenic crops (such as Bt cotton and Bt brinjal) to confer resistance against insect pests.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
Excessive accumulation of nitrates in water bodies can result in:
1. Proliferation of biodiversity
2. Algal blooms
3. Acidification
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Excessive nitrate runoff into water bodies causes eutrophication with algal blooms and subsequent acidification/hypoxia, reducing rather than proliferating biodiversity.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
According to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, which of the following is/are the right/rights of the children?
1. Right to expression
2. Right to recreation
3. Right to name and nationality
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: None of these is a Right of the children
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) guarantees children the right to freedom of expression, the right to rest and recreation, and the right to a name and nationality.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text:
In the context of genetic engineering, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Vector mediated recombinant gene transfer can be done from one eukaryote to another eukaryote only.
2. Vector mediated recombinant gene transfer can be done from animal cell to plant cell.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Vector-mediated recombinant gene transfer can cross kingdom boundaries—for example, transferring genes between animals, bacteria, and plants (not restricted to eukaryote-to-eukaryote).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the importance of a plant named jatropha that is frequently in the news?
options: It is a wild variety of rice of North-east India rich in vitamin A and iron.
it is a bio-diesel yielding plant that can grow well in areas of low rainfall.
It is a genetically modified pest-resistant potato plant.
It is a highly drought-resistant wild variety of pearl millet adopted for cultivation in dry areas of South India.
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (b) — it is a bio-diesel yielding plant that can grow well in areas of low rainfall..

upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.text: Gene silencing means a gene which would be expressed under normal circumstances is switched off by cell machinery. Which one of the following cellular components is not involved in gene silencing?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-1-authentic.explanation: RNA interference (gene silencing) involves double-stranded RNA, small interfering RNA (siRNA), and microRNA (miRNA), whereas ribosomal RNA (rRNA) forms part of the ribosome and does not mediate gene silencing.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 20 year old female was operated for perforation peritonitis and after closing the rectus sheet her abdominal wound was left open to heal with proliferative granulation tissue which contracted and epithelized to form a scar. This patient had undergone healing by:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Leaving a contaminated surgical wound open to heal by granulation tissue formation, contraction, and epithelialization represents healing by secondary intention (or tertiary/delayed closure per this key; note classic secondary intention vs delayed primary closure).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 50 year old patient had a haematoma in his left gluteal region which was large, painful and causing some neural deficit. The next plan of management will be to:
options: Apply some superficial ointment for it to subside
Get an CECT or MRI done
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A large, painful gluteal haematoma causing neurological deficit requires urgent decompression by incision or aspiration to relieve pressure on the sciatic nerve.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: An 18 year old boy had a closed lower limb injury while riding his motorbike. H e was brought to hospital where on examination he had severe pain which increased on passive movement of effected limb with distal sensory disturbances. What is the probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Severe pain out of proportion to injury, worsened by passive stretching, with distal sensory deficits after a closed lower-limb trauma is classic for acute compartment syndrome.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A surgeon told the patient’s attendant that his patient has “flesh eating bug” which is the cause of such severe infection in his dirty wound on his lower limb. Which organism was the surgeon referring to?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Necrotizing fasciitis ('flesh-eating bacteria') is most classically caused by Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A beta-haemolytic streptococcus).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: In Hernia repair, polypropylene suture is used because
options: It is a synthetic braided dyed absorbable suture with low tissue reaction and high tensile strength
It is synthetic monofilament dyed non absorbable suture with low tissue rea ction and high tensile strength
It is a synthetic monofilament undyed absorbable suture with high tissue re action and low tensile strength
It is a synthetic monofilament undyed non absorbable suture with high tissue reaction and which degrades at 15-20% per year
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (b) — It is synthetic monofilament dyed non absorbable suture with low tissue rea ction and high tensile strength.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 60 year old lady had a pyothorax which was treated with an intercostal chest drain. After two days, the meniscus of the fluid in the tube was not swinging during her respiratory process. What could be the likely problem?
options: No fluid in the chest drain bag
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Loss of respiratory swing (tidaling) of the fluid meniscus in an intercostal chest drain indicates either full lung re-expansion or blockage/kinking of the chest tube.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The main principle regarding removal of drain after surgery is
options: Keep drains as long as possible to prevent complications
Drains kept for colo -rectal anastomosis should be removed within 2 days as they can cause complications
Suction drains can be removed early
Drain should be removed as soon as it is no longer required
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Surgical drains act as potential conduits for infection and mechanical irritation, so the fundamental principle is to remove them as soon as they are no longer serving their purpose.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The Chief of laparoscopic surgery asked his assistant to giv e him a laparoscopic port which has absolutely no chance of “capacitance coupling” during laparoscopic surgery. Which port should the assistant give to the Chief?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An all-plastic laparoscopic cannula/port eliminates conductive metal components and completely prevents capacitive coupling burns during monopolar electrosurgery.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Southampton wound grading system and ASEPSIS wound score is used for
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Southampton wound grading system and the ASEPSIS scoring system are standardized tools used to grade the severity of surgical site (wound) infections.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 75 year old diabetic man had surgery for perforated colonic diverculitis . In his post operative period he complained of severe wound pain and had signs of spreading inflammation with crepitus with subdermal spread of gangrene. He is likely to be suffering from
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Postoperative severe wound pain with spreading subdermal gangrene and crepitus in an elderly diabetic patient after bowel surgery indicates synergistic necrotizing cellulitis / Meleney's synergistic gangrene.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are congenital sinuses except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Preauricular, urachal, and coccygeal sinuses are congenital, whereas pilonidal sinus is predominantly an acquired condition caused by hair penetration in the natal cleft.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: An obese 45 year lady who is a chronic smoker came with tender subcutaneous nodules with chronic inflammation with scarring under her left axilla. She is likely to be suffering from:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Tender, recurrent subcutaneous nodules with chronic suppuration and scarring in the axilla of an obese female smoker are classic for hidradenitis suppurativa.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The priority in management of supracondylar fracture of humerus in a child is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a child with a supracondylar fracture of the humerus, assessing and preserving the brachial artery (preventing Volkmann's ischaemia) takes immediate priority.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are premalignant lesions except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Actinic keratosis, Bowen's disease, and giant hairy naevus are premalignant lesions, whereas rhinophyma (sebaceous hyperplasia of the nose in rosacea) is benign.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 50 year old man with long history of swelling in his right parotid region had sudden history of occasional pain, nerve weakness along with paresthesia. His fine needle aspiration cytology was inconclusive. What should be the next step?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sudden pain, facial nerve weakness, and paraesthesia in a long-standing parotid mass strongly suggest malignant transformation; when FNAC is inconclusive, superficial parotidectomy provides definitive histological diagnosis and treatment.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 70 year old man with history of smoking has a 1 cm ulcerative lesion over the vermilion of his upper lip. What is he likely to be suffering from?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Upper lip skin/cutaneous lesions in elderly sun-exposed smokers are commonly basal cell carcinoma (whereas lower lip vermilion lesions are predominantly squamous cell carcinoma).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 55 year old male came with history of hoarseness of voice for which direct laryngoscopy was done and the lesion was biopsied to detect squamous cell carcinoma. He now requires investigation to detect extent of cartilage involv ement, imaging of pre and paraglottic spaces and any extension to deep neck structures. Most appropriate investigation of choice will be:
options: Repeat direct laryngoscopy under general anaesthesia
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the neck is the investigation of choice to evaluate laryngeal cartilage invasion, pre-epiglottic/paraglottic space involvement, and nodal spread in laryngeal carcinoma.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Breast imaging reporting and data system (BI -RADS): Final assessment categorized a 45 year old female to have Category 5 disease. What does the report signify?
options: Negative- Annual screening can be recommended.
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under BI-RADS final assessment categories, Category 5 signifies findings 'highly suggestive of malignancy' with a ≥95% probability of cancer.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: In a male patient of road traffic accident with blood at the tip of external meatus, the likely injury is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Blood at the external urethral meatus following pelvic trauma or a road traffic accident is the classic sign of urethral injury (contraindicating blind catheterization).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 35 year old female has inflammatory carcinoma of left breast, with clinically palpable two left axillary lymph nodes and no clinically or radiologically detectable metastasis. Her TNM staging will be:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Inflammatory breast carcinoma is staged as T4d, clinically palpable ipsilateral mobile axillary lymph nodes as N1, and absence of distant metastasis as M0 (T4d N1 M0).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Milan trial, NSABP trial and EORTC trial in breast cancer compared:
options: Chemotherapy vs Radiotherapy in breast cancer
Neo adjuvant chemotherapy vs Adjuvant chemotherapy
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The landmark Milan, NSABP B-06, and EORTC trials demonstrated equivalent overall survival between breast-conserving surgery (plus radiotherapy) and mastectomy.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Regarding breast conservative therapy and issue of post operative local recurrence, all are true except:
options: Lumpectomy can be considered in any size provided the tumour can be excised with clear margins and acceptable cosmetic results
Margins should be clear for invasive cancer
Margins should be clear for ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS)
Margins should be clear for lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS)
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In breast-conserving therapy, surgical margins must be clear of invasive carcinoma and DCIS, whereas lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS) is a risk marker rather than an obligate precursor and does not require clear margins.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 75 year old lady came with an incidentally diagnosed splenic artery aneurysm which after radiological investigation confirmed to be calcified. She should be offered:
options: Laparoscopic splenic artery ligation and splenectomy
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An asymptomatic, calcified splenic artery aneurysm in a 75-year-old woman (outside pregnancy and <2 cm) carries a low rupture risk and is managed conservatively with observation.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Regarding choledochal cysts following features are true except:
options: Older presentations have an acquired variant
Increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma in older presentations
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Choledochal cysts are congenital biliary dilatations (60% diagnosed before age 10) that carry an increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma in adults; late presentations are congenital cysts presenting late rather than an acquired variant.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 55 year old gentleman presented with history of right upper quadrant discomfort, jaundice, pruritis, fever, fatigue and weight loss. His serum bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase levels are raised and he also gives history of treatment for inflammatory bowel disease. He is most likely to be suffering from:
options: Benign bile duct stricture with cholangitis
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cholestatic jaundice, pruritus, raised alkaline phosphatase, and a history of inflammatory bowel disease (especially ulcerative colitis) strongly indicate primary sclerosing cholangitis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Regarding carcinoma gall bladder following features are true except:
options: One can have similar presentation with benign biliary disease
Squamous cell carcinoma is 40% of all cases
Most patients present with advanced disease
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Over 80–90% of gallbladder carcinomas are adenocarcinomas, whereas squamous cell carcinoma accounts for less than 5% (not 40%).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 45 year old female presented with a cystic lesion in the lesser sac on CT s can. Endoscopic ultrasound guided aspiration showed amylase to be 500 IU and carcinoembryonic antigen as 500ng/ml. What was she suffering from?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A pancreatic cystic lesion with markedly elevated cyst fluid CEA (>192–500 ng/mL) is diagnostic of a mucinous cystic neoplasm of the pancreas.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: During Pylorus preserving pancreatico -duodenectomy (PPPD) the following organs are removed except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy (PPPD) resects the pancreatic head, duodenum, gallbladder, and distal common bile duct while preserving the entire stomach and pylorus.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: In Crohn’s disease all are true except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Crohn's disease involves the full thickness of the bowel wall anywhere in the GI tract with frequent fistulae, whereas crypt abscesses are far more characteristic of ulcerative colitis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Glasgow Coma Score Scale pertains to:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale was originally designed to assess the depth and duration of impaired consciousness specifically in head injury patients.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Muscle relaxant ideal for rapid intubation and short procedures is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Suxamethonium (succinylcholine) is an ultra-short-acting depolarizing muscle relaxant with rapid onset (~45–60 s) and brief duration (~5–10 min), ideal for rapid sequence intubation.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 22 year old male addicted to alcohol and abused with pan -masala-arecanut comes to the clinic with limited mou th opening and restricted tongue movement. The clinical suspicion will be of:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Progressive trismus (limited mouth opening) and restricted tongue protrusion in a chronic pan-masala/areca-nut chewer are classic for oral submucous fibrosis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 56 year old male comes with history of claudication pain in both buttocks, thighs and calves. He also gives history of impotence. The probable site of arterial occlusion is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bilateral buttock, thigh, and calf claudication combined with erectile dysfunction (Leriche syndrome) indicates aortoiliac arterial occlusion.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The earliest clinical sign of an impending burst abdomen is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Serosanguinous ('salmon-pink' serous) discharge from an abdominal incision around postoperative days 5–8 is the earliest warning sign of impending wound dehiscence (burst abdomen).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Most common neoplasm of thyroid gland is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is the most common malignant neoplasm of the thyroid gland (~80% of thyroid cancers).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following blood components has the shortest shelf life?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Stored at 20–24°C with continuous agitation, platelet concentrates have the shortest shelf life (5 days) among blood components.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following features:
1. Visible gastric peristalsis
2. Bilious vomiting
3. Palpable tumour
4. Melena Which of these is/are feature/features of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis presents with visible gastric peristalsis and a palpable pyloric 'olive' tumour, with non-bilious vomiting and no melena.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 24 year old married lady presents with sudden onset right iliac fossa pain. On examination she has marked pallor and is hypotensive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sudden-onset right iliac fossa pain with marked pallor and hypotension in a young married woman is a ruptured ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following layers is most important in intestinal anastamosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The submucosa contains dense collagen and elastin fibres and provides the primary tensile strength for holding sutures in an intestinal anastomosis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The best cure rates for keloids are achieved by:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Because simple excision of a keloid has high recurrence rates, intralesional excision combined with postoperative radiotherapy (or intralesional steroids) achieves the highest cure rates.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 30 year old G2P1L0 with history of anencephaly in previous pregnancy has a nuchal fold thickness of 2.5 mm with other normal fetal parameters. She may be having:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A nuchal translucency/fold thickness of 2.5 mm with normal fetal parameters is within normal limits (cutoffs >3 mm for NT or ≥6 mm for second-trimester nuchal fold), indicating a normal pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 26 year old primigravida presents with blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg, proteinurea and congestive heart failure. Which drug is not useful in this situation?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Methyldopa is a slow-acting oral antihypertensive unsuitable for acute hypertensive crisis with congestive heart failure, where rapid-acting agents (labetalol, nifedipine, diuretics) are needed.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A pregnant woman with 30 weeks gestation presents with BP 166/110 mmHg with pulmonary edema with convulsions. The woman is given magnesium sulphate. The following drug should be avoided:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wait—no, cms15-p2-043: Sublingual nifedipine causes unpredictable, precipitous hypotension and should be avoided—especially alongside magnesium sulphate—in severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman undergoing treatment of infertility presents with triplet pregnancy. The most probable drug given to her for treatment of infertility would have been:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Injectable human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG) carries a much higher risk of ovarian hyperstimulation and multiple (triplet or higher-order) pregnancies than clomiphene citrate.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman presents with abdominal pain and nausea with amenorrhea of 5-6 weeks. Ectopic pregnancy can be diagnosed if:
options: Beta hCG < 1000 IU/L with endometrial thickness of 14mm
Beta hCG > 2000 IU/L with no gestational sac in the uterus on transvaginal sonography
Beta hCG > 3000 IU/L with empty uterus on transvaginal sonography
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (c) — Beta hCG > 2000 IU/L with no gestational sac in the uterus on transvaginal sonography.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman suffering from active tuberculosis not on ATT has a full term vaginal delivery. All the following should be done except:
options: BCG should be given to the neonate
Neonate should be isolated from mother
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: If a mother has untreated active sputum-positive tuberculosis at delivery, the neonate should be temporarily separated from the mother (if open/infectious), given INH prophylaxis, and vaccinated with BCG (with expressed breast milk or supervised feeding per older guidelines).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman with post-term pregnancy with unripe cervix should not be induced with misoprostol if she has:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Misoprostol (PGE1) can cause uterine hyperstimulation, tachycardia, and haemodynamic instability, making it contraindicated in women with decompensated heart disease.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: An overweight, hirsuit woman of 30 years, with one live issue presented to the family planning clinic for advice for contraception. The best suited oral contraceptive will contain the following:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cyproterone acetate is an anti-androgenic progestin combined with ethinylestradiol (co-cyprindiol) that is specifically suited for women with hirsutism and PCOS needing contraception.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Contraceptive options for a 28 year old woman who is breastfeeding a six week old baby, wanting to avoid pregnancy for a longer interval are the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Combined oral contraceptives contain oestrogen, which suppresses lactation and is avoided at 6 weeks postpartum in breastfeeding mothers; progestin-only methods and IUDs are safe.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman using combined oral contraceptive has the following non contraceptive benefits except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Combined oral contraceptives protect against PID, ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer, and colorectal cancer, whereas long-term use slightly increases the risk of cervical cancer.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 40 year old lady is examined and found to have uterovaginal prolapse. What is the appropriate surgery to prevent recurrence?
options: Vaginal hysterectomy with anterior and posterior colporrhaphy and McCall culdoplasty
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Vaginal hysterectomy combined with McCall culdoplasty obliterates the pouch of Douglas and suspends the vaginal vault to prevent post-hysterectomy vault prolapse.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Cervical mucus examination of a 22 year old infertile woman is done to look for all the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cervical mucus evaluation in infertility assesses spinnbarkeit, ferning, and cellularity (Insler score) for oestrogenic effect and ovulation, not HPV presence.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: In a 28 year old infertile woman with anovulation ,the following parameters will indicate ovulation except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Urinary LH surge, cervical mucus Insler score, and progesterone-induced vaginal smear changes indicate ovulation, whereas a single serum oestradiol level alone does not confirm ovulation.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Therapeutic options for a 30 year old woman suffering from severe pain due to endometriosis are the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mirena (LNG-IUS), oral contraceptives, and aromatase inhibitors (letrozole) treat endometriosis-related pelvic pain, whereas sildenafil is a PDE5 inhibitor with no role in endometriosis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Waste disposal of placenta after delivery is done by
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under Biomedical Waste Management rules, anatomical waste such as the placenta is placed in yellow bags and disposed of by incineration.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Features of Janani Suraksha Yojana are the following except:
options: ASHA is a link between woman and Government
Cash assistance is given to mothers for high and low performing states
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a 100% centrally sponsored scheme promoting institutional deliveries via ASHA workers; cash assistance amounts differ between Low Performing States (LPS) and High Performing States (HPS) (with restricted eligibility in HPS).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Ideal time to perform post partum sterilization as per Government of India guidelines is:
options: From 12 hours to 7 days of delivery
From 24 hours to 7 days of delivery
From 48 hours to 7 days of delivery
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: As per Government of India family planning guidelines, postpartum sterilization (minilap) is ideally performed between 24 hours and 7 days after delivery.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Regimen for medical abortion upto 7 weeks of gestation as per Government of India guidelines includes:
options: 200 mg of misfepristone on D1 followed by 800 µg of misoprostol on D3
200 mg of misfepristone on D1 followed by 400 µg of misoprostol on D3
400 mg of misfepristone on D1 followed by 800 µg of misoprostol on D3
400 mg of misfepristone on D1 followed by 400 µg of misoprostol on D3
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Government of India medical abortion regimen up to 7 weeks (49 days) gestation is 200 mg oral mifepristone on Day 1 followed by 400 µg misoprostol on Day 3.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The most common sign of rupture of previous LSCS scar during labour is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A non-reassuring fetal heart rate pattern (fetal bradycardia or prolonged decelerations) is the earliest and most common sign of uterine scar rupture during a trial of labour after caesarean.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Serum CA-125 levels can be raised in all the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Serum CA-125 is elevated in epithelial ovarian cancer, endometriosis, and tuberculous peritonitis/ascites, but is typically normal in benign mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 30 year old healthy woman presents with decreased bleeding during menstruation. The cause could be all of the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Genital tuberculosis, Asherman's syndrome (intrauterine adhesions), and lactation cause hypomenorrhoea/amenorrhoea, whereas endometriosis typically causes dysmenorrhoea and menorrhagia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: For the treatment of a woman with frothy vaginal discharge with fishy smell the following are essential except:
options: Washing of private parts with antiseptics /disinfectants
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Frothy, foul-smelling vaginal discharge indicates trichomoniasis, treated with metronidazole, partner treatment, and condom use; antiseptic douching disrupts normal vaginal flora and is contraindicated.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: During immediate puerperium,
options: the number of white cells decreases
the number of white cells increases
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: During the immediate puerperium, physiological leukocytosis occurs (total WBC count rises up to 20,000–25,000/mm³) due to neutrophilia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the best contraceptive for a newly married couple who wants to postpone pregnancy for one year?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Combined oral contraceptives offer high contraceptive efficacy, cycle control, and rapid reversibility, making them ideal for a newly married couple wishing to delay pregnancy for a year.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a branch of internal iliac artery?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The superior gluteal, inferior gluteal, and uterine arteries are branches of the internal iliac artery, whereas the ovarian artery arises directly from the abdominal aorta.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 30 year old multiparous woman comes with an ultrasound report of fibroid uterus measuring 3 x 3 cm. Her only complaint is mild pain during menstruation. The best management in this would be:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A small (3×3 cm), asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic uterine fibroid in a 30-year-old woman requires only reassurance and periodic follow-up.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The most accurate method to diagnose adenomyosis is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the most accurate non-invasive imaging modality for diagnosing adenomyosis (showing junctional zone thickening ≥12 mm).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: On ultrasonography low-lying placenta is labelled when implantation in the lower uterine segment is such that:
options: Placental edge does not reach the internal os and remains 2 cm wide perimeter around the os
Placental edge does not reach the internal os and remains 3 cm wide perimeter around the os
Placental edge does not reach the internal os and remains 4 cm wide perimeter around the os
Internal os is covered partially or fully by the placenta
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (a) — Placental edge does not reach the internal os and remains 2 cm wide perimeter around the os.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following cardiovascular parameters decreases during pregnancy?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: During normal pregnancy, systemic vascular resistance falls markedly, leading to a decrease in arterial blood pressure (especially in the second trimester) despite increased cardiac output and blood volume.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A multipara with 8 gm% haemoglobin at 30 weeks’ gestation should be treated by:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A pregnant woman at 30 weeks with mild-to-moderate anaemia (Hb 8 g/dL) and adequate time before term is initially treated with oral iron therapy (or parenteral iron if intolerant/non-compliant).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The progress of labour can be monitored by observing the following except:
options: The intensity of uterine contractions by abdominal examination
The descent of foetal head by abdominal examination
The formation of caput by vaginal examination
Gradual increase in cervical dilatation by vaginal examination
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Labour progress is monitored by uterine contractions, fetal head descent, and cervical dilatation; caput succedaneum reflects moulding/prolonged labour rather than normal progress.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Prophylactic intravenous methergin should not be given in cases of:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intravenous methylergometrine (Methergin) causes intense vasoconstriction and hypertension, and is contraindicated in patients with heart disease or severe hypertension.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: During labour, which one of the foetal heart patterns is ominous?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency and fetal hypoxia, making them an ominous fetal heart rate pattern during labour.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A case of ante-partum haemorrhage is seen at a Primary Health Centre. The treatment will consist of:
options: Assessment of general condition of the patient, intravenous drip and reference to a hospital
Vaginal examination and reference to a hospital only if diagnosed as placenta praevia
Packing the vagina to stop the bleeding and then reference to a hospital
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (a) — Assessment of general condition of the patient, intravenous drip and reference to a hospital.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 20 year old full term primigravida is admitted with full dilatation of the cervix and breech presentation. Breech is not engaged. Foetal heart is normal. The proper procedure for the management would be:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An unengaged breech at full cervical dilatation in a primigravida indicates cephalopelvic disproportion or inadequate descent, for which Caesarean section is the safest management.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following factors is the most significant as a risk factor for post-partum psychosis?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A previous history of postpartum psychosis (or bipolar disorder) is the single strongest risk factor for recurrence of postpartum psychosis.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The main cause of perinatal mortality in ‘Frank breech presentation’ is:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In breech delivery, rapid compression and decompression of the unmoulded aftercoming head can cause tentorial tears and intracranial haemorrhage, the leading cause of perinatal mortality.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 45 year old woman presents with continuous vaginal bleeding for 15 days. Her bleeding should be controlled by:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a 45-year-old perimenopausal woman with prolonged abnormal uterine bleeding (15 days), dilatation and curettage (to exclude endometrial hyperplasia/carcinoma and arrest bleeding) followed by progestogens is indicated.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The treatment of primary spasmodic dysmenorrhoea in a young girl as a first measure would be:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: First-line treatment for primary spasmodic dysmenorrhoea in young women is NSAID analgesics (prostaglandin synthetase inhibitors) and antispasmodics.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 44 year old woman presents with polymenorrhoea for one year. Clinical examination reveals bulky uterus with no other abnormality. D & C report is simple hyperplasia. What is the treatment of choice?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Simple endometrial hyperplasia without atypia in a 44-year-old woman is treated medically with cyclic or continuous progestogen therapy.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Health Education
2. Treatment of hypertension
3. Screening for cervical cancer
4. Changing lifestyles to prevent stress Which are the examples of primordial prevention?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Primordial prevention prevents the development of risk factors in healthy populations via health education and lifestyle modification (preventing stress/obesity), whereas treatment and screening are secondary prevention.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: When the prevalence rate is used without any qualification, it is taken to mean as
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: When 'prevalence rate' is stated without qualification, it conventionally refers to point prevalence rate (cases at a single point in time).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: An outbreak of viral hepatitis A was reported from a town between June and August of a particular year. Of total cases, 60% occurred in July. Exposure of the community to infection is from
options: a common single source for a short period
a common single source for a prolonged period
multiple sources for a short period
multiple sources for a prolonged period
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A sharp cluster where 60% of cases occur within a single month (July) points to a point-source (common single source for a short period) epidemic.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Rheumatic Heart Disease can be prevented by:
options: Treatment of respiratory infections in children
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Preventing rheumatic heart disease involves prompt treatment of streptococcal pharyngitis, school-based screening for early detection, and research into streptococcal vaccines.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The addition of killed Bordetella pertusis microorganisms to diphtheria toxoid enhances the antibody response of the latter because of
options: additive action of the two antigens
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In the DPT vaccine, the endotoxin/cell-wall components of killed Bordetella pertussis act as an immunological adjuvant that enhances the antibody response to diphtheria toxoid.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Post exposure prophylaxis against HIV infection should not be delayed beyond:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) is most effective when initiated as early as possible (ideally within 2–4 hours, and no later than 72 hours).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: With reference to meningococcal meningitis, which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: Disease spreads mainly by droplet infection
Treatment of cases has no significant effect in epidemiological pattern of disease
Mass chemoprophylaxis causes immediate drop in incidence rate of cases
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In untreated meningococcal meningitis, the case fatality rate approaches 50–80% (often cited as ~80% rather than 60%), whereas droplet spread and rapid drop in cases with mass chemoprophylaxis are true.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following vaccines is/are contraindicated in pregnancy?
1. Rubella
2. Hepatitis-B
3. Diphtheria
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Live attenuated vaccines such as Rubella (MMR) are contraindicated during pregnancy due to theoretical risk of fetal infection, whereas killed/recombinant vaccines like Hepatitis B and diphtheria toxoid can be given.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: In a case of paucibacillary leprosy, treatment is considered adequate if the patient has received the six monthly doses of combined therapy within:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under WHO/NLEP guidelines, paucibacillary (PB) leprosy multidrug therapy is considered adequate when 6 monthly blister packs are completed within a maximum period of 9 months (or 6 months per strict schedule).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Chemoprophylaxis is indicated in the following conditions except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chemoprophylaxis is indicated for close contacts of cholera, meningococcal meningitis, and plague, whereas it is not recommended for typhoid fever.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Chandler’s index is used in the epidemiological studies of
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chandler's index measures the average number of hookworm eggs per gram of faeces to assess the community intensity of hookworm infection.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following diseases:
1. Measles
2. Polio
3. Staphylococcal food poisoning
4. Typhoid
Which of the above are the correct examples for incubation period of 10-14 days?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Both measles (10–14 days) and typhoid fever (typically 10–14 days) have a classical incubation period of 10 to 14 days.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is the most common malignant tumour in adult males in India?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Oral and oropharyngeal cancers (strongly linked to tobacco and betel nut use) represent the most common malignancy among adult males in India.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Eight months old child had history of unusual crying and convulsions following previous vaccination after BCG, DPT & OPV ( first dose), and Hepatitis B. Now parents have brought child for next doses of vaccination. Which vaccine is contraindicated in this situation?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Inconsolable crying and convulsions following a previous DPT dose are contraindications to the pertussis component, so subsequent DPT doses are contraindicated (switch to DT).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The clinical features of Turner Syndrome in girls include the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Turner syndrome (45,XO) presents with short stature, webbed neck, and delayed puberty/streak gonads, while intelligence is typically normal (severe mental retardation is not a feature).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Occupational exposure to Benzol may lead to :
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chronic occupational exposure to benzene (benzol) is a well-established cause of bone marrow suppression and acute myeloid leukaemia.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Marriage between two heterozygous individuals for the same disorder is prevented by:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Prospective genetic counselling identifies heterozygous carriers before marriage or reproduction to prevent high-risk matings and genetic disease in offspring.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The benefits of ESI Act include the following except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Act provides medical, sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants', funeral, and rehabilitation benefits, but not a nutritional allowance.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The following are the group health education approaches except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Lectures, demonstrations, and role play are group health education methods, whereas documentaries (films/TV) are mass media communication approaches.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Current WHO recommendations for initiating Antiretroviral treatment (ART) in HIV +ve individuals is:
options: CD4 cells less than or equal to 350 cells/mm3
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Per the 2010/2013 WHO guidelines referenced by this exam, ART was recommended for all HIV-positive adults with CD4 count ≤350 cells/mm³.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The following are the principles of Primary Health Care except:
options: Provision of specialist services at Primary Health Centres
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The four principles of Primary Health Care (Alma-Ata) are equitable distribution, community participation, intersectoral coordination, and appropriate technology; specialist services are provided at CHC/referral levels, not PHCs.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is a quantitative method of health management?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cost-effectiveness analysis is a quantitative health management technique comparing programme costs against health outcomes.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Acute Respiratory Infections (ARI) are important causes of under-five mortality in India. In remote areas, children develop frequent episodes of ARI. What measures will you take for prevention and control of ARI amongst under-five children in that area?
options: Case management and Health education to mothers
Controlling malnutrition, Promoting breast feeding and vitamin A supplementation
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Reducing under-five ARI mortality requires integrated case management, maternal education, immunization (measles, Hib, pertussis, pneumococcal), nutrition, breastfeeding, and Vitamin A.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The following are objectives of Indian Public Health Standards for Primary Health Centres except:
options: Provision of comprehensive primary health care
Achievement of an acceptable quality of health care
Provision of accident and emergency care
Making services more responsive to the needs of the community
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) for PHCs aim for comprehensive primary care, quality assurance, and community responsiveness, whereas dedicated accident and emergency/trauma care is a CHC/district hospital objective.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A pregnant woman in third trimester having fever was diagnosed as a case of Falciparum malaria. Under the National Health Programme, which drug is recommended?
options: ACT accompanied by single dose of Primaquine on day 2
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under India's National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme, falciparum malaria in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy is treated with ACT alone (primaquine is contraindicated in pregnancy).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following genetic disorders leads to mental retardation?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Untreated phenylketonuria (PKU) leads to toxic phenylalanine accumulation in the developing brain, causing severe intellectual disability (mental retardation).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Biomedical waste from a yellow plastic bag is disposed by:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under Biomedical Waste Management rules, infectious anatomical and soiled waste collected in yellow plastic bags is disposed of by incineration (or deep burial).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a feature of heat stress?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Heat stress manifests as heat cramps, heat syncope, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke/hyperpyrexia, whereas numbness is not a typical feature.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: The denominator for calculating proportional mortality rate from a specific disease is:
options: Population at risk in that particular area
Attributable deaths of a particular disease
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Proportional mortality rate from a specific disease is calculated as deaths from that disease divided by total deaths from all causes in that year (×100).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a measure of dispersion?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mean is a measure of central tendency, whereas range, mean deviation, and standard deviation are measures of dispersion.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Analytical studies include the following methods of studies except:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Case-control, cohort, and analytical cross-sectional studies are observational analytical studies, whereas randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are experimental/interventional studies.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is false?
options: Gestational diabetes can lead to Type-II diabetes after delivery.
Gestational diabetes is always transient and cured after delivery.
Gestational diabetes is a risk factor for diabetes in children born to mothers with GDM.
Screening for gestational diabetes should be included in antenatal care.
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: While gestational diabetes often resolves after delivery, it is not always transient—affected women carry a high lifelong risk of developing Type 2 diabetes mellitus.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Cu-T-380 A IUCD should be replaced in:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Copper-T 380A intrauterine contraceptive device has an approved effective lifespan of 10 years before replacement.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Coconut oil
2. Groundnut oil
3. Mustard oil
Which of the above is/are dietary sources of linoleic acid?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Groundnut oil, mustard oil, and coconut oil all contain linoleic acid (an essential omega-6 fatty acid, highest in groundnut/mustard and small amounts in coconut).

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: A 20 year old male is diagnosed as a case of dengue fever at a Primary Health Centre. What are the suitable measures to be taken for the prevention and control of dengue in that area?
options: Case management for DF and DHF and vaccination
Case management for DF and DHF, isolation and individual protection from mosquitoes
Case management for DF and DHF, isolation and individual protection from mosquitoes and vaccination
Case management for DF and DHF, isolation and individual protection from mosquitoes and environmental measures for elimination of breeding places
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (d) — Case management for DF and DHF, isolation and individual protection from.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: WHO defines a multi-drug resistant (MDR) Tuberculosis strain as one that is:
options: Resistant to INH and Rifampicin with or without resistant to other anti TB drugs
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (c) — Resistant to INH and Rifampicin with or without resistant to other anti TB drugs.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the characteristic features of screening tests?
1. Done on healthy people
2. Done on unhealthy people
3. More accurate
4. Less accurate 5. Less expensive 6. More expensive 7. Not a basis for treatment 8. Used as a base for treatment
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Screening tests are applied to apparently healthy populations; they are relatively inexpensive, less accurate than diagnostic tests, and are not a direct basis for treatment without diagnostic confirmation.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which National Programe came into existence during 11th Five Year Plan?
options: National Cardiovascular diseases & Stroke control programme
National Diabetes and Cancer control programme
National Programme for prevention and control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular diseases and Stroke
