upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (d) — National Programme for prevention and control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular diseases and Stroke.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text: Which states are qualified as high prevalence states in the context of HIV/AIDS?
options: When prevalence in high risk groups is more than 5%, and less than 1% in antenatal women
When prevalence in high risk groups is more than 5%, and 1% or more in antenatal women
When prevalence in high risk groups is less than 5%, and more than 1% in antenatal women
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2015 Answer Key: Option (b) — When prevalence in high risk groups is more than 5%, and 1% or more in antenatal women.

upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following diseases:
1. Yellow fever
2. Q fever
3. Chikungunya fever
4. Relapsing fever 5. Japanese encephalitis 6. Sleeping sickness
Which of the above are transmitted by mosquitoes?
upsc-cms-2015-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Yellow fever (Aedes), chikungunya (Aedes), and Japanese encephalitis (Culex) are mosquito-borne, whereas Q fever is airborne/tick-borne, relapsing fever is louse/tick-borne, and sleeping sickness is tsetse-fly-borne.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient with small cell lung carcinoma has symptomatic hyponatraemia (serum sodium 127 mmol/ L). The most likely etiology is:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Small cell lung carcinoma frequently causes ectopic ADH secretion (SIADH), leading to euvolaemic symptomatic hyponatraemia.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Regarding Gilbert’s syndrome, which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: Inheritance of disease is autosomal dominant.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Gilbert's syndrome causes mild, fluctuating unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia exacerbated by fasting or illness; liver histology is normal and jaundice does not progressively worsen.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is an uncommon cause of autonomic dysfunction?
options: Neuropathy associated with Vitamin B12 deficiency.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Guillain-Barré syndrome, acute intermittent porphyria, and diabetes mellitus commonly cause autonomic neuropathy, whereas Vitamin B12 deficiency primarily affects dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Peripheral Eosinophilia is not a characteristic feature of:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, tropical pulmonary eosinophilia, and Loeffler's syndrome feature marked peripheral eosinophilia, whereas hypersensitivity pneumonitis does not.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Salicylate intoxication in adults usually causes:
1. Severe respiratory alkalosis.
2. Mixed metabolic acidosis respiratory alkalosis.
3. Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.
Select the correct answer using the code given below
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Salicylate toxicity in adults initially stimulates the medullary respiratory centre causing respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation causing a mixed metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: With reference to psoriatic arthritis, which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: Distribution of arthritis is mainly asymmetrical.
Involvement of PIP joints is more than DIP joints.
Cup like erosions are seen on X ray.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Psoriatic arthritis classically affects the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joints predominantly—more than the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints—and produces 'pencil-in-cup' erosions.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding rheumatic heart disease:
1. Rheumatic carditis is a pancarditis.
2. Carey–Coombs murmur is a delayed systolic murm ur heard during the course of acute rheumatic fever.
3. Mitral regurgitation is the most co mmon manifestation of acute rheumatic carditis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Rheumatic carditis is a pancarditis, most commonly causing mitral regurgitation; the Carey-Coombs murmur is an apical mid-diastolic (not delayed systolic) murmur.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: The extra cellular fluid deficit in a comatose patient of diabetic ketoacidosis is replenished by:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Initial resuscitation of extracellular fluid deficit in diabetic ketoacidosis is performed with isotonic 0.9% normal saline (NaCl).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not associated with a high reticulocyte count?
options: Response to treatment in ‘nutrition – deficiency’ anaemia
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Megaloblastic anaemia causes ineffective erythropoiesis with intramedullary haemolysis and therefore presents with a low (inappropriately reduced) reticulocyte count.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: What happens when normal erythrocytes (blood – group matched) are transfused into a patient with anaemia secondary to an intracorpuscular defect?
options: Depends on the severity of anaemia.
Depends on whether the donor cells are fresh or stored (older than a week).
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: When the defect is intrinsic (intracorpuscular) to the patient's own red cells (e.g., G6PD deficiency, spherocytosis), transfused normal donor erythrocytes have a normal lifespan.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase is seen in all except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Osteomalacia, Paget's disease of bone, and cholestatic jaundice elevate serum alkaline phosphatase, whereas uncomplicated osteoporosis has normal ALP.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Starvation ketosis is treated with intravenous glucose/dextrose and nutrition—not glucagon, which would worsen ketogenesis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: In a young epileptic woman wishing to use oral contraceptive agents, which of the following drugs is not an ideal agent?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Carbamazepine is a potent hepatic CYP450 enzyme inducer that accelerates the metabolism of oral contraceptive steroids and can cause contraceptive failure.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not true about alcoholic cirrhosis?
options: On many occasions alcoholic hepatitis and alcoholic cirrhosis coexist.
Starts with macronodular and later on changes to micronodular cirrhosis.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2014 Answer Key: Option (c) — Starts with macronodular and later on changes to micronodular cirrhosis..

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Cardiac arrest may be due to all of the following except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ventricular fibrillation, acute MI, and massive pulmonary embolism can cause sudden cardiac arrest, whereas atrial fibrillation alone does not directly cause cardiac arrest.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not useful in the management of status epilepticus?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Status epilepticus is treated acutely with IV benzodiazepines (lorazepam), phenytoin/fosphenytoin, or phenobarbitone; carbamazepine is only an oral maintenance drug and has no role in status epilepticus.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: The following are indications for renal replacement in ARF except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Refractory hyperkalaemia, fluid overload, and uraemic pericarditis are indications for dialysis in acute renal failure, whereas metabolic alkalosis is not (severe metabolic acidosis is).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Biphasic defibrillation in case of ventricular fibrillation is first done with:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Biphasic defibrillation for ventricular fibrillation is typically initiated at 150–200 Joules (200 J per standard ACLS protocols).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Gastric erosions are likely to be associated with the following conditions except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cor pulmonale, polycythaemia vera, and hepatic cirrhosis are associated with peptic ulceration/gastric erosions, whereas pernicious anaemia causes autoimmune gastric atrophy and achlorhydria.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Wegener’s granulomatosis is characterized by all of the following except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wegener's granulomatosis (GPA) affects the upper/lower respiratory tract, kidneys (glomerulonephritis), and eyes (uveitis/scleritis), whereas granulomatous hepatitis is not a characteristic feature.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: An 11 year old boy has elevated prothrombin and activated partial prothrombin time . What is the most likely defect?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Prolongation of both PT and aPTT indicates a defect in the common coagulation pathway (Factors X, V, II, or I) or multiple factor deficiencies.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: The radiological findings in chest X ray in sarcoidosis includes the following except:
options: Bilateral symmetrical lymphadenopathy on chest X ray is commonly seen.
Upper lobe involvement is more than that of lower lobe.
Egg shell calcification is seen on X ray.
Pleural effusion is a common finding.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sarcoidosis typically shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, upper-lobe parenchymal predominance, and occasional eggshell nodal calcification; pleural effusion is uncommon (<5%).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Acute rheumatic fever is caused by:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute rheumatic fever is a nonsuppurative immune-mediated sequela following pharyngitis caused by Group A beta-haemolytic Streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a complication of peptic ulcer?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Bleeding, perforation, and gastric outlet obstruction are major complications of peptic ulcer disease, whereas simple indigestion is a symptom.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Rickettsial infection)
List II (Means of transmission to humans)
A. Rocky mountain spotted fever.
1. Tick bite.
B. Q fever.
2. Mite bite.
C. Rickettsial pox.
3. Infected louse passes feces into broken skin.
D. Epidemic typhus.
4. Inhalation of dried infected material.
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is transmitted by ticks (A-1), Q fever by inhalation of dried infected material (B-4), rickettsialpox by mites (C-2), and epidemic typhus by body louse faeces (D-3).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Clinical features)
List II (Diagnosis)
A. Osler’s node
1. Patent ductus arteriosus with reversal of shunt.
B. Differential cyanosis
2. Aortic stenosis with aortic regurgitation.
C. Bisferiens pulse
3. Pulmonary hypertension
D. Graham Steel murmur
4. S ubacute bacterial endocarditis
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Osler's nodes occur in subacute bacterial endocarditis (A-4), differential cyanosis in PDA with shunt reversal (B-1), pulsus bisferiens in AS+AR (C-2), and Graham Steell murmur in pulmonary hypertension (D-3).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Normal anion gap
2. Hyperchloraemic acidosis
3. Inappropriately high urinary pH (>5.4)
Which of the above are the characteristic features of renal tubular acidosis (RTA)?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Renal tubular acidosis is characterized by normal anion-gap, hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis with an inappropriately high urinary pH (>5.4–5.5 in distal RTA).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are typical features of Parkinsonism?
1. Failure to swing the arms while walking
2. Nystagmus
3. Cogwheel rigidity
4. Festinating gait
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Parkinsonism features reduced arm swing, cogwheel rigidity, and festinating gait; nystagmus is not a typical feature.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements about acromegaly:
1. Fibroma molluscum and acanthosis nigricans are common findings.
2. Paradoxical growth hormone response to TRH administration is observed.
3. Acro-osteolysis is a common radiological finding.
4. Diabetes mellitus may be associated in nearly 25 % of acromegalics. Which of these statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acromegaly features fibroma molluscum, acanthosis nigricans, paradoxical GH rise to TRH, and diabetes mellitus (~25%), whereas acro-osteolysis is not a feature (tufting of phalanges occurs).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Ability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Of all the types of lupus nephritis, the worst outcome is seen in:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis (WHO/ISN Class IV) carries the worst renal prognosis among the lupus nephritis classes.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a cause of hypomagnesemia?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chronic pancreatic insufficiency, poorly controlled diabetes, and alcoholism cause hypomagnesemia, whereas beta-blockers do not.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Among the following, which one is not a good dietary source of iron?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Liver, fish, and jaggery are good dietary sources of iron, whereas milk is notoriously poor in iron.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List I (Poison)
List II (Antidote)
A. Benzodiazepine
1. D-penicillamine
B. Copper sulphate
2. Flumazenil
C. Opiates
3. N–acetyl cysteine
D. Paracetamol
4. Naloxone
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Specific antidotes: benzodiazepines–flumazenil (A-2), copper sulphate–D-penicillamine (B-1), opiates–naloxone (C-4), and paracetamol–N-acetylcysteine (D-3).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: An elderly male presented with unilateral headache, fever and high ESR (110 mm). What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Unilateral headache, fever, and markedly elevated ESR (>50–100 mm/hr) in an elderly male are classic for giant cell (temporal) arteritis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a defect in calcium channels?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis is caused by mutations in the skeletal muscle voltage-gated sodium channel (SCN4A), whereas episodic ataxia-2, SCA-6, and hypokalemic periodic paralysis (CACNA1S) involve calcium channels.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is a loop diuretic?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ethacrynic acid is a loop diuretic acting on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle; spironolactone is potassium-sparing and thiazide/indapamide act on the DCT.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: The classical features of Wernicke’s encephalopathy are the following except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Wernicke's encephalopathy presents with the classic triad of confusion/encephalopathy, ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus, and ataxia; extensor plantar response is not a classical feature.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not seen in hepatorenal syndrome?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hepatorenal syndrome presents with hypotension, progressive azotaemia, and very low urinary sodium (<10 mEq/L); serum potassium is normal or elevated, not low.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Common sites of involvement of Takayasu’s arteritis are the following except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Takayasu's arteritis classically involves the aortic arch, subclavian, carotid, and abdominal aorta/renal arteries; wait—UPSC key marked (a) Subclavian artery (though clinically subclavian is the most common; pulmonary artery is less common).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
In which of the following is clubbing a common occurrence?
1. Infective endocarditis
2. Congestive cardiac failure
3. Pulmonary thromboembolism
4. Ebstein anomaly
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Clubbing is a classic feature of infective endocarditis and cyanotic congenital heart diseases (such as Ebstein's anomaly with right-to-left shunt), unlike CCF or pulmonary embolism.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the most common lobe involved in Herpes Simplex virus encephalitis?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) encephalitis characteristically localizes to the temporal and inferior frontal lobes.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements about staphylococcal pneumonia:
1. Three-fourth of the patients are below the age of one year.
2. Pneumatoceles are common.
3. It is the commonest cause of empyema in a child below two years of age.
4. The condition is easily amenable to treatment in the outdoors.
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Staphylococcal pneumonia predominantly affects infants (<1 year), frequently causes pneumatoceles and empyema in children under 2, and requires urgent inpatient IV antibiotics rather than outpatient therapy.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: In carcinoid syndrome, the most common valvular lesion is:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Carcinoid heart disease involves right-sided endocardial plaques causing tricuspid regurgitation (most common) and pulmonary stenosis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Na+ is reabsorbed in which part/parts of kidney ?
1. Proximal convoluted tubule
2. Distal convoluted tubule
3. Thick ascending limb of loop of Henle
4. Collecting duct
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Major Na+ reabsorption occurs in the proximal convoluted tubule (~65%) and the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle (~25%) via NKCC2.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A 40 year old female presented with dysphagia and inability to open the mouth fully. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Microstomia (inability to open the mouth fully due to perioral skin tightening) and oesophageal dysmotility/dysphagia in a middle-aged woman are classic for systemic sclerosis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following tests is best for measuring glomerular function?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Creatinine clearance rate provides a direct clinical estimate of the glomerular filtration rate (GFR), making it superior to serum creatinine or blood urea alone.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Optic chiasmal lesion commonly produces:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Compression of decussating nasal retinal fibres at the optic chiasm produces bitemporal hemianopia.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Adult hemoglobin consists of the following chains:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Normal adult haemoglobin A (HbA, ~97%) is a tetramer composed of two alpha and two beta globin chains (α2β2).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding rheumatoid arthritis:
1. The synovial fluid looks cloudy.
2. Synovial fluid viscosity is reduced.
3. Synovial fluid complement levels are markedly decreased.
4. Lymphocytes predominate in the differential white blood cell count in the synovial fluid.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In rheumatoid arthritis, synovial fluid is cloudy/turbid with reduced viscosity and markedly decreased complement levels due to immune complex consumption, while neutrophils (not lymphocytes) predominate.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the commonest organism for prosthetic valve endocarditis?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Coagulase-negative staphylococci, particularly Staphylococcus epidermidis, are the most common cause of prosthetic valve endocarditis (especially early-onset).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Tuberculoid leprosy is likely to have:
options: Abundant lepra bacilli in the skin lesion
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tuberculoid leprosy features thickened peripheral nerves, strong cell-mediated immunity (positive lepromin test), and scanty bacilli, whereas leonine facies occurs in lepromatous leprosy.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: The following are true regarding Henoch Schonlein purpura except:
options: 2/ 3rd cases are preceded by viral upper respiratory tract infection.
Renal involvement is seen in around 40 % of cases.
Purpura is seen all over the body especially the upper limbs.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Henoch-Schönlein purpura is a small-vessel IgA vasculitis often preceded by URI, with renal involvement in ~40% and palpable purpura distributed predominantly over the buttocks and lower limbs (not upper limbs).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct regarding cluster headache?
options: Females are more commonly affected than males.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cluster headache has a strong male predominance (male-to-female ratio ~3–4:1), making 'females more commonly affected' incorrect.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Maturity onset diabetes of the young (MODY) is inherited as:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY) is a monogenic form of diabetes inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Ghon’s complex is not characterized by:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A Ghon complex consists of a peripheral subpleural parenchymal focus, draining lymphatics, and ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy; pleural effusion is not a component of the Ghon complex itself.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match list I with list II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Urine exam)
List II (Disease)
A. Red cell casts.
1. Nephrotic syndrome.
B. Microscopic haematuria.
2. Chronic renal failure.
C. Proteinuria.
3. Polycystic kidney disease.
D. Broad cell casts.
4. Glomerulonephritis.
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Red cell casts indicate glomerulonephritis (A-4), microscopic haematuria is seen in polycystic kidney disease (B-3), heavy proteinuria in nephrotic syndrome (C-1), and broad waxy casts in chronic renal failure (D-2).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a feature of Gullain-Barre syndrome?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Guillain-Barré syndrome is a lower motor neuron demyelinating polyneuropathy causing areflexia, albuminocytologic dissociation, and occasional transient autonomic/bladder symptoms; an extensor Babinski response is an UMN sign and is absent.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: With reference to Marfan’s syndrome, which one of the following is not correct?
options: Lens of the eye is dislocated downward
Aorta regurgitation is present in many patients
Ratio of upper segment to lower segment is less than 1
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In Marfan syndrome (FBN1 mutation), ectopia lentis is classically upward and outward (superotemporal), not downward (downward/inferonasal dislocation suggests homocystinuria).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Tetany may be a feature of the following except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hyperventilation (respiratory alkalosis), hypokalaemic alkalosis, and hypomagnesaemia reduce ionized calcium or increase neuromuscular excitability causing tetany, whereas hyponatraemia does not.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Regarding vitamin “K”, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: It is a water soluble vitamin
Its body stores can last more than 8 years
Its routine prophylaxis in newborn children is recommended to prevent early haemorrhagic disease
It is the treatment of choice in patients with acute severe haemoptysis
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2014 Answer Key: Option (c) — Its routine prophylaxis in newborn children is recommended to prevent early haemorrhagic disease.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following clinical features:
1. Impaired judgement
2. Impaired memory
3. Alteration of personality
4. Clouding of consciousness
Which of the above are characteristics of dementia?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Dementia is characterized by progressive impairment of memory, judgement, and personality with a clear sensorium; clouding of consciousness is the hallmark of delirium, not dementia.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Koebner’s phenomenon is seen in:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Koebner's isomorphic phenomenon (appearance of new skin lesions along sites of cutaneous trauma) is classically seen in psoriasis, lichen planus, and vitiligo.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which hepatitis marker can be used to diagnose Acute Hepatitis B?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: IgM anti-HBc antibody is the definitive serological marker for diagnosing acute Hepatitis B infection (including during the core window period).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not an example of metabolic acidosis with high anion gap?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lactic acidosis, ketoacidosis, and methanol poisoning cause high anion-gap metabolic acidosis, whereas renal tubular acidosis causes normal anion-gap (hyperchloraemic) metabolic acidosis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a vector - borne disease?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Japanese encephalitis (Culex), dengue (Aedes), and kala-azar (sandfly) are vector-borne, whereas meningococcal meningitis spreads directly from person to person via respiratory droplets.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Regarding management of Myxoedema coma, which of the following is not true?
options: Treatment must begin after biochemical confirmation of the diagnosis
Levothyroxine usually given by I/V route
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Myxoedema coma is a life-threatening emergency in which IV levothyroxine, hydrocortisone, passive rewarming, and cautious fluids must be started immediately on clinical suspicion without waiting for lab confirmation.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is the major determinant of plasma osmolality?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Sodium (and its accompanying anions) is the principal extracellular cation and accounts for over 90% of plasma osmolality.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Acute aortic regurgitation occurs in:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Infective endocarditis causes rapid cusp destruction leading to acute aortic regurgitation, unlike ankylosing spondylitis, Marfan syndrome, or rheumatoid arthritis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause the following except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes subacute combined degeneration of the cord (myelopathy), peripheral neuropathy, and optic atrophy, but not primary myopathy.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A patient with cirrhosis develops oliguria and worsening azotemia. Urinary sediment is normal. Urinary sodium concentration is 5 meq/ L. The most likely cause could be:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oliguria and worsening azotaemia in cirrhosis with normal urine sediment and urinary sodium <10 mEq/L (here 5 mEq/L) indicate hepatorenal syndrome.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A 6 week old infant presents with recurrent nonbilious vomiting with some dehydration. A mass is palpable in right upper quadrant of abdomen with visible peristalsis. The most likely diagnosis is :
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Recurrent non-bilious vomiting, visible peristalsis, and a palpable RUQ/epigastric olive mass in a 6-week-old infant are diagnostic of congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A 2 year old previously healthy child develops abrupt onset high grade fever, drooling of saliva and respiratory distress. He has a toxic look and becomes severely ill within few hours. What is the most likely clinical diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Abrupt high fever, toxic appearance, drooling of saliva, and rapidly progressive respiratory distress in a 2-year-old child are classic for acute epiglottitis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A 6 year old child presents with oliguria, haematuria, puffiness of face. He has a convulsion and blood pressure is found to be 200/100 mm of Hg. Laboratory tests reveal hemoglobin: 12g/dl, total leucocyte count: 7200/mm 3, platelet count: 3.1 lakhs/mm3, blood urea: 80 mg/dl and serum creatinine: 1.1 mg/dl. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Oliguria, haematuria, facial puffiness, severe hypertension (200/100 mmHg), and convulsions with normal platelet count (excluding HUS) indicate acute glomerulonephritis with hypertensive encephalopathy.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A two year old child with acute watery diarrhea and severe dehydration presents to the emergency. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
options: Ringer lactate at 30ml/kg given intravenously in 30 minutes
Oral rehydration solution through nasogastric tube
Ringer lactate at 10ml/kg given intravenously in 2 hours
Normal saline at 10ml/kg given intravenously in 2 hours
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: For a 2-year-old child with severe dehydration (WHO Plan C), initial IV resuscitation is Ringer's lactate at 30 mL/kg over 30 minutes, followed by 70 mL/kg over 2.5 hours.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A diagnosis of steroid dependent nephrotic syndrome is made in a 5 year old male child and he is initiated on a drug. After 6 weeks of therapy, he develops nausea, vomiting, neutropenia and gross hematuria. Which of the following is the most likely drug used?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is used in steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome and causes bone marrow suppression (neutropenia), nausea/vomiting, and acrolein-induced haemorrhagic cystitis (gross haematuria).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding distal renal tubular acidosis:
1. Blood biochemistry reveals normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
2. There is defective secretion of H+ in the distal tubule.
3. There may be associated muscle weakness and rickets.
4. Children may present with polydipsia and polyuria.
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Distal (Type 1) RTA results from impaired distal H+ secretion, causing normal anion-gap metabolic acidosis, polyuria/polydipsia, growth failure, muscle weakness (hypokalaemia), and rickets.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A one year old male child presents with poor urinary stream and dribbling of urine since birth. A mass is palpable mass just above the symphysis pubis. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Poor urinary stream, dribbling since birth, and a palpable distended bladder above the symphysis pubis in an infant boy are classic for posterior urethral valves.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A 4 years old child presents with rash on lower limbs, arthritis, and abdominal pain. Urine examination reveals microscopic hematuria. The most likely diagnosis is:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Lower-limb palpable purpura/rash, arthritis, abdominal pain, and microscopic haematuria in a 4-year-old child represent the classic tetrad of Henoch-Schönlein purpura.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: The following milestones can be achieved by a 12 month old infant except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A 12-month-old infant can stand alone, say 'mama/dada', and wave bye-bye; building a tower of 6 blocks is a 24-month (2-year) milestone.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not a feature of severe combined immunodeficiency in children?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) features profound T- and B-cell defects, low immunoglobulins, recurrent severe infections, and thymic hypoplasia/aplasia (not an enlarged thymus).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Children with an autosomal recessive condition have partial albinism, susceptibility to infections and presence of giant peroxidase positive lysosomal granules in granulocytes. What is the most probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chédiak-Higashi syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by partial oculocutaneous albinism, recurrent pyogenic infections, and giant peroxidase-positive lysosomal granules in neutrophils.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A 50 hours old full term breast – fed newborn boy weighing 3100 g presents with jaundice. Physical examination is normal. The total serum bilirubin is 11.0 mg/ dL with a direct bilirubin of 0.4 mg/ dL. The correct treatment would be to:
options: Continue breast feeds and review after 48 hours
Stop breast feeds and review after 24 hours
Continue breast feeds and start blue – light phototherapy
Arrange for a double volume exchange transfusion
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In a healthy, well-appearing 50-hour-old term newborn with total bilirubin of 11.0 mg/dL (well below the phototherapy threshold for age), physiological jaundice is managed by continuing breastfeeding and reviewing after 48 hours.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
options: Vitamin B12 -------- Subacute combined degeneration of cord.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Beriberi is caused by Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency, not Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) deficiency.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Congenital malformation syndrome)
List II (Congenital heart defect)
A. Foetal alcohol syndrome
1. Bicuspid aortic valve
B. Turner’s syndrome
2. Endocardial cushion defect
C. Down syndrome
3. Pulmonary stenosis
D. Congenital rubella syndrome
4. Ventricular septal defect
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Fetal alcohol syndrome is associated with VSD (A-4), Turner syndrome with bicuspid aortic valve/coarctation (B-1), Down syndrome with endocardial cushion/AVSD defect (C-2), and congenital rubella syndrome with pulmonary stenosis/PDA (D-3).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A 12 months old baby boy weighs 4.5 kg and measures 60 cm. He has marked loss of subcutaneous fat and has no edema. What fo rm of protein energy malnutrition does the baby have?
options: Grade IV protein energy malnutrition with K
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A 12-month-old weighing 4.5 kg (<60% of expected ~10 kg) with severe loss of subcutaneous fat and no oedema has marasmus.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder (FBN1 mutation) with a normal 46,XY or 46,XX karyotype—not 47,XYY.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is the most reliable test for screening hemophilia?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Haemophilia A (Factor VIII) and B (Factor IX) affect the intrinsic coagulation pathway, making activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT/PTT) the most reliable screening test.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: A child with poliomyelitis in acute phase can have all the following except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Poliomyelitis selectively destroys anterior horn motor neurons, causing asymmetric flaccid paralysis, hypotonia, myalgia, and diminished reflexes, while sensory function remains completely intact.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following antibodies is most specific in children with systemic lupus erythematosus?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies (along with anti-Smith) are highly specific for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and correlate with lupus nephritis activity.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Vaccine)
List II (Type of vaccine)
A. Hepatitis B vaccine
1. Live attenuated vaccine
B. Diphtheria vaccine
2. Sub unit vaccine
C. Haemophilus influenzae vaccine
3. Toxoid
D. Measles vaccine
4. Polysaccharide vaccine
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hepatitis B is a recombinant subunit vaccine (A-2), diphtheria is a toxoid (B-3), Haemophilus influenzae type b is a polysaccharide conjugate vaccine (C-4), and measles is a live attenuated vaccine (D-1).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following are the gases whose presence in high concentration in the lower strata of atmosphere, is chiefly responsible for causing the Greenhouse effect?
1. Sulphur dioxide
2. Carbon dioxide
3. Chlorofluorocarbons
4. Nitrogen
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO2) and chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are potent greenhouse gases in the lower atmosphere that trap outgoing infrared radiation, whereas nitrogen and SO2 are not primary greenhouse gases.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following electric lamps:
1. C F L
2. Incandescent bulb
3. L E D lamp Indiscriminate or improper disposal of which of the above causes/ cause mercury pollution in the environment?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Compact fluorescent lamps (CFLs) contain small amounts of mercury vapour, so improper disposal releases mercury into the environment (unlike incandescent or LED lamps).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following substances:
1. Acesulfame potassium
2. Polyethlene glycol
3. Saccharin
4. Sucralose
Which of the above are used as sugar substitutes in foods?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acesulfame potassium, saccharin, and sucralose are non-nutritive artificial sweeteners used as sugar substitutes, whereas polyethylene glycol is a polymer/laxative.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Ozone is
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ozone (O3) is a triatomic allotrope of the element oxygen.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following contributes/contribute to the burst of monsoon in India?
1. Intense heating of th e north-west part of Indian sub-continent during summer
2. Steep pressure gradient between th e Indian Ocean and the Indian landmass
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Intense summer heating of northwestern India creates a low-pressure trough and a steep pressure gradient from the Indian Ocean, driving the southwest monsoon burst.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: In India, which one of the following determines the principles that should govern the grants- in-aid to the States?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under Article 280 of the Constitution of India, the Finance Commission recommends the principles governing grants-in-aid to the States from the Consolidated Fund of India.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is a Human Right as well as a Fundamental Right under the Constitution of India?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Right to Education (Article 21A, for children aged 6–14 years) is both a Fundamental Right under the Indian Constitution and an internationally recognized Human Right.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not used as a food preservative?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Benzoic acid, citric acid, and sodium chloride are common food preservatives, whereas ethylene dichloride is an industrial solvent/fumigant, not a food preservative.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is located in Bastar region?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Indravati National Park (a Project Tiger reserve) is located in the Bijapur/Bastar region of Chhattisgarh.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Water hyacinth is generally perceived as a notorious aquatic weed, but it can be a useful plant. Which of the following statements is/ are correct in this context?
1. This plant contains certain substances which can be extracted and used as medicines, herbicides and pesticides.
2. This plant can be used to remove many heavy metals like Cadmium, Lead and Mercury from water bodies.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) has high phytoremediation capacity and can bioaccumulate heavy metals such as cadmium, lead, and mercury from polluted water bodies.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Use of calcium carbide for the artificial ripening of fruits is banned but it is often reported to be illegally used. What is/are the likely health hazards of exposure to this chemical?
1. Permanent damage to the eyes
2. Pulmonary edema
3. Irritation of mouth, throat and nose
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Calcium carbide used for artificial fruit ripening releases acetylene and phosphine/arsine impurities that can cause severe eye damage, mucosal irritation of the mouth/throat/nose, and pulmonary oedema.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Malachite that is used as food adulterant?
options: It is used for ripening of mangoes and custard apple.
It is used to make green vegetables shiny.
It is added to sugar to increase its volume and weight.
It is added to tea dust to improve its flavour.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Malachite green is an industrial dye illegally used to give green vegetables (like peas, okra, and bitter gourd) a bright, shiny green appearance.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following organs from a brain dead person can be used as donated organs?
1. Heart
2. Kidney
3. Liver
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A brain-dead (heart-beating) donor can donate vital solid organs including the heart, kidneys, and liver (as well as lungs, pancreas, and corneas).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following can be a threat to Biodiversity?
1. Global climate change
2. Pests and Pathogens
3. Invasive species
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Global climate change, emerging pests/pathogens, and invasive alien species are all major threats to global biodiversity.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following can be used in biomass power plants to produce electricity?
1. Cow dung
2. Rice husk
3. Stalks of wheat
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
options: None of these can be used in biomass power plants.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cow dung (biogas/combustion), rice husk, and wheat stalks (agricultural residues) can all be utilized in biomass power plants to generate electricity.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Why are phosphates added to soft drinks?
options: To give the drinks a tangy taste.
To add sparkle to the drinks.
To supplement the drinks with certain mineral nutrients.
To give dark brown or chocolate colour to the drinks.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Phosphoric acid/phosphates are added to cola and soft drinks primarily as acidulants to impart a sharp, tangy taste.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
With reference to electrical and electronic equipment or components, the e–waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011 apply to:
1. Consumers
2. Producers
3. Collection centres
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: India's E-Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011 apply to producers, consumers, bulk consumers, collection centres, dismantlers, and recyclers.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following can be made by using biodegradable polymers?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Biodegradable polymers (such as polyglycolic acid and polylactic acid scaffolds) are used in tissue engineering to fabricate bioresorbable artificial blood vessels.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: The Eastern Ghats and Western Ghats meet at
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Eastern Ghats and Western Ghats converge at the Nilgiri Hills in southern India.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Panchayati Raj is a four tier system of governence.
2. There is a reservation of seats fo r women in Panchayati Raj elections.
3. Members of Gram Panchayat can convene Lok Adalat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Panchayati Raj is a three-tier (not four-tier) system with constitutional reservation of at least one-third of seats for women; Lok Adalats are convened by Legal Services Authorities, not Gram Panchayat members.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: If you wish to see Pandas and Gibbons in their natural habitat in India, which of the following regions do you have to travel to?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In India, red pandas and hoolock gibbons are found in their natural habitat in the Eastern Himalayas and northeastern states.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following provisions of the Constitution of India:
1. Directive Principles of State Policy
2. Rural and Urban Local Bodies
3. Centre–State Relations
Which of the above has/ have a bearing on education?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Education is addressed in the Directive Principles of State Policy (Article 45), the 11th/12th Schedules for Rural and Urban Local Bodies, and Centre-State legislative relations (Concurrent List).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: In which of the following cancers is it shown initially that the disruptive micronuclei can trigger DNA damage on chromosomes and can be a potential biomarker for genetic instability
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chromothripsis and disruptive micronuclei triggering DNA damage on chromosomes were linked to genetic instability in non-small cell lung cancer.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Who is the President of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)?
options: Union Minister of Science and Technology
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-officio President of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following animals are found in India in their natural habitat?
1. Flying fox
2. Puma
3. Snow Leopard
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Flying foxes (fruit bats) and snow leopards are native to India, whereas pumas (cougars) are native only to the Americas.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are used as decoloring agent in the refinement of sugar?
1. Dimethylamine epichlorohydin copolymer
2. Sodium stearoyl lactylate
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Dimethylamine-epichlorohydrin copolymer is a cationic decolorizing polymer used in sugar refining, whereas sodium stearoyl lactylate is a food emulsifier.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following crops of India:
1. Groundnut
2. Sesamum
3. Pearl millet
Which of the above is/are predominantly rainfed crops?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Groundnut, sesame (sesamum), and pearl millet (bajra) are predominantly rainfed Kharif crops in India.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Araku valley is in:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Araku Valley is a hill station located in the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one among the following types of forests exhibits highest biodiversity?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tropical rainforests exhibit the highest species richness and biodiversity of any terrestrial biome.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following best describes the phenomenon of El Nino?
options: The anomalous widespread warming of the sea surface of tropical east and central Pacific Ocean
The revolving tropical storms of the Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico.
The deflection of the ocean currents in the northern and southern hemisphere due to the rotation of Earth.
A violent rotating column of air extending from a thunderstorm to the ground.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2014 Answer Key: Option (a) — The anomalous widespread warming of the sea surface of tropical east and central Pacific Ocean.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: A 40 year old man presented with a flat 1x1cm. scaly, itchy black mole on the front of thigh. Examination did not reveal any inguinal lymphodenopathy. The best course of management would be:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A suspicious pigmented skin lesion (1×1 cm black mole) without regional lymphadenopathy should be evaluated by complete excision biopsy with a narrow margin to allow accurate Breslow thickness staging.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Residual volume of urine >100cc
3. Serum level of prostatic specific antigen>10nmol/L
4. Trabeculated Urinary bladder
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bladder outlet obstruction from BPH is indicated by post-void residual urine >100 mL, trabeculated bladder, and obstructive urinary symptoms (PSA >10 nmol/L is not a direct measure of obstruction).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Ankyloglossia in a patient with carcinoma tongue is staged as
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ankyloglossia (fixation/tethering of the tongue due to invasion of extrinsic tongue muscles or floor of mouth) in carcinoma of the tongue stages the primary tumour as T4.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Which is the most commonly used chemothe rapy regimen in the adjuvant treatment following modified radical mastectomy in the estrogen receptor negative 35 year old female with breast cancer?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The CAF/FAC regimen (Cyclophosphamide, Adriamycin/Doxorubicin, and 5-Fluorouracil) is a standard anthracycline-based adjuvant chemotherapy regimen for node-positive or high-risk ER-negative breast cancer.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements: The clinical features of tension pneumothorax include tracheal shift to contralateral side absent breath sounds on the affected side low output circulatory failure peripheral cyanosis
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Tension pneumothorax causes mediastinal/tracheal shift to the contralateral side, absent breath sounds on the affected side, and obstructive low-output shock (central, rather than isolated peripheral, cyanosis).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: The following procedures are recommended for palliation in a patient with obstructive jaundice due to unresectable carcinoma of head of pancreas except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Palliative surgery for unresectable pancreatic head carcinoma bypasses biliary and gastric obstruction (hepaticojejunostomy/choledochoduodenostomy + gastrojejunostomy); pancreaticojejunostomy is only done after Whipple resection.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Which of the following are cont raindications to salvaging accidentally injured spleen during operation?
1. Labile blood pressure
2. Presence of intraperitoneal infection
3. Pre-existing splenic disease
4. Age below 50 years
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intraoperative splenic salvage is contraindicated in haemodynamically unstable patients (labile BP), gross intraperitoneal contamination/infection, or pre-existing splenic pathology.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Match List 1 (Condition) with List II (Presentation) and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists
List I (Condition)
List II (Presentation)
A. Caroli’s disease
1. Abdominal pain, Biliary sepsis
B. Budd-Chiari Syndrome
2. Hepatomegaly, Pain
C. Polycystic Liver Disease
3. Ascites
D. Primary sclerosing cholangitis
4. Abdominal Liver Function Test (LFT) or jaundice
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Caroli's disease causes biliary sepsis/pain (A-1), Budd-Chiari syndrome causes ascites (B-3), polycystic liver disease causes hepatomegaly/pain (C-2), and primary sclerosing cholangitis causes cholestatic LFTs/jaundice (D-4).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Treatment of choice for annular pancreas is
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Annular pancreas encircling the second part of the duodenum is treated by bypassing the obstruction via duodenoduodenostomy (diamond-shaped) rather than resecting pancreatic tissue.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: In a patient of gastric outlet obstruction nutritional support is best delivered by:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In severe gastric outlet obstruction where enteral access beyond the pylorus is unavailable, total parenteral nutrition (TPN) is used to correct malnutrition.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: The following nerves are blocked for repairing inguinal hernia by local anaesthetic except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Local anaesthetic field block for inguinal hernia repair blocks the ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric, and genitofemoral nerves, not the femoral nerve.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements: Venacaval opening of the diaphragm, situated at the level of T8 transmits inferior vena cava vagus nerve branches of the right phrenic nerve thoracic duct
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The vena caval hiatus of the diaphragm lies at T8 and transmits the inferior vena cava along with branches of the right phrenic nerve.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Traumatic haemothorax is best managed by:
options: Aspiration of blood from pleural cavity
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Traumatic haemothorax is initially and definitively managed by closed tube thoracostomy (intercostal chest tube drainage).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements about mesh skin grafts is not correct?
options: They permit coverage of large areas.
They allow egress of fluid collections under the graft.
They contract to the same degree as a grafted sheet of skin.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Meshed split-thickness skin grafts cover larger surface areas, allow drainage of seroma/haematoma, and take well on granulating beds, but they contract more—not to the same degree—as unmeshed sheet grafts.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: An 8 year old girl sustained a fall on the outstretched right hand 6 hours ago and was treated with egg albumen bandages by a village bone setter. She presented with gross swelling of the right elbow and forearm. The first essential intervention in this case would be to
options: order urgent radiographs of both elbows.
immerse the hand in warm water to increase the circulation.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a child with gross forearm swelling after tight village bandages (risk of compartment syndrome/Volkmann's ischaemia), the immediate first step is to completely remove all constricting bandages.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Sprain of the ankle joint results from an injury to:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Inversion ankle sprains most commonly injure the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL), the weakest component of the lateral collateral ligament complex.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following are the most common forms of cardiac tumors seen in clinical practice ?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Atrial myxoma is the most common primary cardiac tumour encountered in clinical practice (~50% of benign primary heart tumours).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: The following operative procedure can result in neurogenic voiding dysfunction except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Radical hysterectomy, abdominoperineal resection, and retroperitoneal lymph node dissection can injure pelvic autonomic nerves causing neurogenic bladder, whereas ureterolithotomy does not.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: In diabetes mellitus the following findings are seen in ophthalmoscopy except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Diabetic retinopathy features microaneurysms, dot-and-blot haemorrhages, and flame-shaped haemorrhages (note: official UPSC key marked (b) Flame shaped haemorrhage, though flame haemorrhages can also occur in hypertensive/diabetic retinopathy; 'wet sponge' is an archaic/rare term).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following structures in the femoral triangle:
1. Femoral canal
2. Femoral Nerve
3. Femoral artery
4. Femoral vein What is the correct sequence of the above from medial to lateral ?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: From medial to lateral in the femoral triangle, the structures are arranged as: Femoral canal (1) → Femoral vein (4) → Femoral artery (3) → Femoral nerve (2).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: A female patient aged 30 years with bilateral conductive deafness is wearing a hearing aid. What is the probable diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Painless, progressive bilateral conductive hearing loss in a young adult female (around 30 years) is classically due to otosclerosis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (Operative procedure)
List II (Complication)
A. Highly selective vagotomy
1. Metabolic bone disease
B. Vagotomy with Gastrojejunostomy
2. Post Prandial gas bloat
C. Subtotal Gastrectomy
3. Lesser curve necrosis
D. Nissen’s Fundoplication
4. Diarrhea
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Highly selective vagotomy risks lesser curve necrosis (A-3), vagotomy + gastrojejunostomy causes post-vagotomy diarrhoea (B-4), subtotal gastrectomy causes metabolic bone disease (C-1), and Nissen fundoplication causes gas-bloat syndrome (D-2).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
options: Krukenberg tumour ……… Peritoneal seeding involving ovaries
Blumer’s shelf ……… Secondary deposits in pelvic cul-de-sac
Virchow’s node ……… Palpable node in left supraclavicular space
Sister Joseph’s nodule ……… Solitary secondary deposit in the liver
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sister Mary Joseph's nodule is a metastatic umbilical nodule from intra-abdominal malignancy, not a solitary secondary deposit in the liver.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Optimum age for surgery for a child with cleft lip is:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cleft lip repair (cheiloplasty) is optimally performed between 3 and 6 months of age (following Millard's 'rule of 10s': 10 weeks, 10 lb, Hb 10 g/dL).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: An electrical contact burn is considered to be:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Electrical contact burns generate intense heat along deep tissues and are classically classified as full-thickness (third-degree) burns.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: In a fracture of shaft of longbone, the component which contributes least in fracture healing is:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Fracture healing relies on vascular supply, periosteum, and endosteum for osteoprogenitor cells and callus formation, whereas bone matrix itself contributes least.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: A 52 year old male patient comes with history of rectal bleeding, alteration in bowel habits and tenesmus. The ideal investigation would be:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a 52-year-old male with rectal bleeding, altered bowel habits, and tenesmus (red-flag symptoms for colorectal cancer), full colonoscopy with biopsy is the investigation of choice.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: 28 What is the treatment of choice in a patient with Crohn’s case, where inflamed appendix was found on exploration?
options: Closing the abdomen and starting medical treatment
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: When exploration in a patient with Crohn's disease reveals an acutely inflamed appendix (and a normal caecal base), appendicectomy is performed; ileocaecal resection is reserved for terminal ileal complications.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: In an unconscious patient with multiple injuries, what is the best and reliable modality for assessment of cervical spine injury?
options: Full AP and lateral radiographs of spine
While doing CT scan of brain take extra cuts at the cervical spine region
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2014 Answer Key: Option (c) — While doing CT scan of brain take extra cuts at the cervical spine region.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: The following are features of hypovolemic shock except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hypovolaemic shock causes oliguria, hypotension, metabolic acidosis, and compensatory tachycardia—not bradycardia.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: A 45 year old man sustains trauma in a road traffic accident and develops engorgement of neck veins, pallor, rapid pulse rate, and chest pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Thoracic trauma with distended neck veins, hypotension/pallor, tachycardia, and chest pain (Beck's triad) indicates cardiac tamponade.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct regarding trichobezoar ( hair balls)?
options: It is more common in females.
It is associated usually with psychiatric illness.
It is more common in young.
It is usually associated with pyloric stenosis.
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Trichobezoars (swallowed hairballs) are most common in young females with trichotillomania/psychiatric disorders, and are not typically associated with pyloric stenosis.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following conditions:
1. Otitis media
2. Speech problems
3. Dentition abnormalities
Which of the above is/are associated with cleft palate?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cleft palate is classically associated with Eustachian tube dysfunction (recurrent otitis media), hypernasal speech problems, and dental/occlusal abnormalities.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: On second day following femoral embolectomy, the leg is found to be tender, tense and dusky with feeble dorsalis pedis. The most appropriate management would be:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A tense, tender, dusky calf with feeble distal pulses after revascularization (femoral embolectomy) indicates reperfusion compartment syndrome, requiring urgent fasciotomy.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: An air fluid level with dilated oesophagus and “bird beak” appearance in a barium swallow is diagnostic of:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A dilated oesophagus with an air-fluid level and smooth distal tapering ('bird's-beak' appearance) on barium swallow is diagnostic of achalasia cardia.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: A colonic carcinoma involving muscularis propria, with one or two nodes involved with a solitary metastasis in the liver, the TNM stage would be:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In colorectal cancer TNM staging, invasion of muscularis propria is T2, 1–3 regional lymph nodes is N1, and distant liver metastasis is M1 (T2 N1 M1).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: After undergoing surgery, for carcinoma of colon, a patient developed single liver metastasis of 2 cm. What would be the next treatment?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A solitary, resectable 2 cm metachronous hepatic metastasis from colon cancer is best treated with surgical resection (hepatic metastasectomy) for potential cure.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is given a score of two in Alvarado score?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In the Alvarado score for acute appendicitis, migration of pain, anorexia, nausea/vomiting, rebound tenderness, and fever each score 1 point, whereas RLQ tenderness and leukocytosis (>10,000/mm³) each score 2 points.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following parts of intussception is susceptible for ischaemia and perforation?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The apex (leading point) of the intussusceptum suffers the earliest and most severe mesenteric vascular compression, making it most susceptible to ischaemia and perforation.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: A 30 year old lady comes with history of bloody discharge from her right nipple while taking bath. On examination, there is a cystic swelling in the subareolar region. The clinical diagnosis would be:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bloody nipple discharge with a palpable subareolar mass/cystic swelling in a 30-year-old woman (note: intraductal papilloma is classic, though UPSC key marked (d) Intraductal carcinoma).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Match List I (sign) with List II (description) and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List I (sign)
List II (description)
A. Palmer’s sign
1. Bluish coloration of vagina in pregnancy
B. Braxton Hicks sign
2. Rhythm ic painless uterine contractions felt per abdomen in second trimester
C. Goodell’s sign
3. Softening of cervix in pregnancy
D. Chadwick sign
4. Rhythmic uterine contractions felt in first trimester
Code: A B C D
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Palmer's sign is rhythmic uterine contractions in the first trimester (A-4), Braxton Hicks are painless second-trimester contractions (B-2), Goodell's sign is cervical softening (C-3), and Chadwick's sign is bluish vaginal discolouration (D-1).

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: HELLP syndrome includes the following except:
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: HELLP syndrome stands for Haemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, and Low Platelets; leukocytosis is not a defining component.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Predisposing factors of puerperial sepsis are following except:
options: Repeated internal examinations specially in the case of premature rupture of membrane
Cases of manual removal of placenta
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Repeated vaginal examinations after PROM, manual removal of placenta, and placenta praevia predispose to puerperal sepsis, whereas multiparity alone is not a direct risk factor.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Fetal pulmonary hypoplasia
2. Fetal chromosomal anomalies
3. Prostaglandin synthetase inhibitors
4. Amniotic fluid index of 15 cm
Which of the above are asso ciated with oligohydramnios?
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Oligohydramnios is associated with fetal pulmonary hypoplasia, fetal renal/chromosomal anomalies, and maternal NSAID (prostaglandin synthetase inhibitor) use; an AFI of 15 cm is normal.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: Surgical treatment of choice for a 20 year old woman with nulliparous uterine prolapsed is:
options: Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair
Abdominal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In a young 20-year-old nulliparous woman with uterine prolapse, uterus-preserving sling surgery (e.g., Shirodkar/Purandare cervicopexy) is the treatment of choice.

upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2014-paper-2-authentic.text: A 32 years old woman with two live children was brought to emergency with history of missed period for 15 days, spotting since 7 days and pain abdomen since 6 hours. Her pulse was 120 per minute, pallor + +, systolic B.P. 80 mm Hg. There was fullness and tenderness on per abdomen examination. Copper T thread was seen through external os on per speculum examination. On p/ v examination, cervical movements were tender, uterus was anteverted, bulky and soft.
