upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hypothyroidism shows hung-up ankle jerk (A-4), rheumatic carditis shows prolonged PR interval (B-1), subarachnoid haemorrhage shows subhyaloid haemorrhage (C-3), and morphine poisoning shows pinpoint pupils (D-2).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Each of the following is a sign of impaired ventricular function except
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Raised JVP, narrow pulse pressure, and basal crepitations indicate ventricular dysfunction/failure, whereas a tapping apical impulse is a classic sign of mitral stenosis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements regarding coarctation of aorta:
1. It may be associated with Turner syndrome
2. It most commonly occurs near the insertion of the ligamentum arteriosum
3. It is twice as common in females than males
4. It may be associated with bicuspid aortic valve
Which of the statements given above are correct?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Coarctation of the aorta commonly occurs near the ligamentum arteriosum and is strongly associated with Turner syndrome and bicuspid aortic valve; it is more common in males (not females).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following ECG findings is most likely to be seen at the time of cardiac arrest ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is the most common initial shockable arrhythmia recorded at the time of sudden cardiac arrest.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: The most reliable indicator of recent Hepatitis-B infection in a convalescing patient is
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: IgM anti-HBc is the most reliable marker of acute/recent Hepatitis B infection, especially during the convalescent window period when HBsAg has cleared.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: A 2-year old child presents with generalized muscle hypotonia and weakness. Distal muscles are affected more than the proximal muscle groups. Facial muscles are spared. Deep tendon reflexes are diminished. Electromy graphy reveals fibrillation pattern. The most likely site of involvement is
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Generalized hypotonia with distal-greater-than-proximal weakness, spared facial muscles, diminished DTRs, and fibrillations on EMG localizes to a peripheral neuropathy.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Confirmation of the diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease is by
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Full-thickness or suction rectal biopsy demonstrating absence of ganglion cells in the myenteric and submucosal plexuses is the gold-standard confirmatory test for Hirschsprung disease.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis is associated with which of the following viral infections ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a fatal late complication of persistent measles virus infection.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists:
List I
List II (Disease) (CSF analysis)
A. Acute pyogenic
1. Normal CSF meningitis
2. Elevated
B. Tubercular proteins with meningitis no cells
C. Gullian-Barre
3. Elevated syndrome protein and cells (mainly
D. Neurocyst cercosis polymorphs)
4. Elevated proteins and cells (mainly (ymphocytes)
Code : A B D
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute pyogenic meningitis shows polymorphs and high protein (A-3), TBM shows lymphocytes and high protein (B-4), GBS shows albuminocytologic dissociation (C-2), and neurocysticercosis typically shows normal CSF (D-1).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Pseudotumour cerebri is characterized y allof the following except acterized
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pseudotumour cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension) causes raised ICP, headache, papilloedema, and diplopia (6th nerve palsy), without focal parenchymal neurological deficits.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Vitamin K-dependant clotting factors include all the following except
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Vitamin K-dependent clotting factors are II, VII, IX, and X (plus Proteins C and S); Factor VIII is not vitamin K-dependent.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: A mother brings her 2-yeal old boyns Guide with short history of pallor. Examination reveals pallor, petechiae and splen megaly. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A 2-year-old child with acute-onset pallor, petechiae (thrombocytopenia), and splenomegaly most likely has acute leukaemia.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
Match List I with List Il and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists:
List I
List II (Disease) (Clinical feature)
A. Acute
1. Recurrent lymphoblastic knee joint leukaemia swelling
B. Juvenile
2. Lymphaden rheumatoid pathy with ersona arthritis petechiae
C. Thalassaemia
3. Swelling of small joints
D. Haemophilia of hands
4. Hepatosplen megaly with severe pallor
Code : A B C D
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia presents with lymphadenopathy and petechiae (A-2), JRA with small-joint swelling (B-3), thalassaemia with hepatosplenomegaly and severe pallor (C-4), and haemophilia with recurrent knee haemarthrosis (D-1).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following cells in per pheral blood smear are necessarily increased in all haemolytic anaemias?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Increased reticulocyte count (reticulocytosis) is a universal bone marrow compensatory response seen in all haemolytic anaemias.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following is not a naturally occurring anticoagulant in the body?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Protein C, Protein S, and Antithrombin III are endogenous anticoagulants, whereas von Willebrand factor promotes platelet adhesion and stabilizes Factor VIII (procoagulant).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the earliest gestational age at which iodine trapping occurs in foetal thyroid?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The fetal thyroid gland begins trapping iodine and synthesizing thyroid hormones around 8–10 (to 12) weeks of gestation.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following inborn errors of metabolisin can give rise to thromb embolic manifestation in a child?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Homocystinuria causes endothelial damage and platelet aggregation, predisposing children to arterial and venous thromboembolic events alongside marfanoid habitus and downward lens dislocation.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: In an infant bom to a mother, at what age of child the ELISA test can reliably diagnose HIV infe tion ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Maternal transplacental anti-HIV IgG antibodies persist in infants until about 15–18 months, so ELISA antibody testing is only reliable for diagnosing HIV at or after 18 months of age.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: The most likely diagnosis in a 2-day old neonate with indirect hyperbilirubin mia, positive direct Coombs' test and spherocytes on peripheral blood smear is
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: A 2-day-old neonate with indirect hyperbilirubinaemia, positive direct Coombs test, and prominent spherocytes on peripheral smear is classic for ABO haemolytic disease of the newborn.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: The triad of 'diarrhoea, dementia and dermatitis' is characteristically seen in the deficiency of vitamin
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Pellagra, characterized by the classic triad of dermatitis, diarrhoea, and dementia, is caused by niacin (Vitamin B3) deficiency.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Hyperkalaemia can occur in all the following except
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Crush injuries, renal failure, and intravascular haemolysis release intracellular potassium causing hyperkalaemia, whereas Cushing's syndrome causes mineralocorticoid-mediated hypokalaemia.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: An asymptomatic 3-year old girl is brought to the emergency department after 2 hours of accidental kerosene ingestion. The appropriate management
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In accidental kerosene ingestion, gastric lavage and emesis are contraindicated due to aspiration risk; an asymptomatic child is managed with observation and a chest X-ray (after 4–6 hours) to exclude chemical pneumonitis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: A 28-year old woman suffering from sickle cell anaemia marries a 31-year old with no abnormality. What are the respective probabilities to have (i) sickle cell disease and (ii) sickle cell trait in their offspring?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: If one parent has sickle cell anaemia (HbSS) and the other is completely normal (HbAA), 100% of their children will inherit HbAS (sickle cell trait) and 0% will have sickle cell disease.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: What is the naturally occurring form of vitamin D in the human skin?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: 7-Dehydrocholesterol (provitamin D3) is the naturally occurring precursor in human skin that is converted to previtamin D3 upon UVB exposure.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Warthin-Finkelday giant cells in ly phoid tissue are characteristic of which of the following infections?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Multinucleated Warthin-Finkeldey giant cells in lymphoid tissues (tonsils, appendix, lymph nodes) are pathognomonic of measles.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Some antibioties act as ionophores, which means that they
options: interfere directly with bacterial cell wall synthesis
increase cell membrane perme bility to specific ions
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Ionophore antibiotics (e.g., valinomycin, monensin) incorporate into lipid bilayers and selectively increase membrane permeability to specific ions, collapsing electrochemical gradients.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Polymerase Chain Reaction technique is used for
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a molecular biology technique used to exponentially amplify specific target DNA segments in vitro.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: In the hills, the soil erosion takes place due to rapid flow of rain water. It can be most effectively controlled by
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Terrace cultivation breaks long mountain slopes into flat steps, slowing surface water runoff and effectively controlling soil erosion in hilly terrain.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: The chemical substance "Taxol" is said to have curative value for malignant tumours. It is obtained from the
options: roots and fruits of Taxodium sp.
bark from stem of Tuxus sp.
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Taxol (paclitaxel), a potent mitotic inhibitor used in cancer chemotherapy, was originally isolated from the bark of the Pacific yew tree (Taxus brevifolia).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Greenhouse gases are called as such because they
options: are used in warming plant growth chambers
help in maintaining atmospheric 02 and CO2 balance
are produced by green phot synthesizing plants and are trapped in the Earth's atmosphere
prevent the escape of heat waves reradiated from the Earth's surface
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Greenhouse gases absorb and trap outgoing long-wave infrared (heat) radiation emitted from the Earth's surface, warming the lower atmosphere.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: General Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Bacillus thuringiensis is used to control
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) produces crystal delta-endotoxins that are toxic to larvae of specific insect pests and is widely used as a biological insecticide.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which group of algae can provide nitr genous nutrients to paddy cultivation under natural field conditions?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc) fix atmospheric nitrogen in flooded paddy fields, naturally enriching rice crops.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Tissue culture technique can be used for developing virus-free plants multiplication of elite genotypes of useful trees production of secondary metab lites of plants
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Plant tissue culture (micropropagation and meristem culture) is used to produce virus-free plants, rapidly multiply elite genotypes, and synthesize valuable secondary metabolites.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following is an appropriate description of mangrove plants ?
options: Large wood-yielding trees of the tropical forests
Plants in marshy areas with breathing roots
Succulent plants that can thrive in arid/desert areas
Vast grassland areas interspersed with deciduous trees and thorny bushes
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees and shrubs growing in coastal intertidal marshy areas, equipped with specialized aerial breathing roots (pneumatophores).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following :
1. Ethylene dibromide
2. Potassium meta-bisulphate
3. Sodium benzoate
Which of the above is/are used as food preservatives ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Potassium metabisulphite and sodium benzoate are standard chemical food preservatives, whereas ethylene dibromide is a banned grain fumigant/pesticide.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Rayon fibre is made from
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Rayon is a semi-synthetic regenerated fibre manufactured from purified plant cellulose.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following parts/spectra of solar radiation is/are mostly absorbed by the leaves of green plants?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Chlorophyll a and b in green plant leaves maximally absorb red and blue wavelengths of visible solar radiation for photosynthesis (reflecting green).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Other than nitrogen and oxygen, which one of the following is the most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: After nitrogen (~78%) and oxygen (~21%), argon (~0.93%) is the third most abundant gas in Earth's dry atmosphere.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Among the following regions of India, which one receives the highest annual average monsoon rainfall from June to September ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Among the listed regions, Gangetic West Bengal receives the highest average southwest monsoon rainfall (June–September) due to proximity to the Bay of Bengal.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: In which one of the following types of forests is teak a dominant tree species?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Teak (Tectona grandis) is a characteristic dominant tree species of tropical moist and dry deciduous forests in India.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Carbon dioxide is released from the interior of the Earth during volcanic eruption.
2. Carbon dioxide corrodes the metal surfaces.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Volcanic eruptions release large quantities of CO2 from the Earth's interior, and dissolved CO2 forms weak carbonic acid that accelerates metal corrosion.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
With reference to the 'Protected Areas in India, consider the following stat
1. In a Wildlife Sanctuary, limited biotic interference is permitted.
2. A Biosphere Reserve is declared to conserve a few specific species of flora and fauna.
3. The boundaries of a National Park are defined by legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/ are correct ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In India, Wildlife Sanctuaries permit limited regulated human/biotic activity, National Park boundaries are fixed by state legislation, and Biosphere Reserves conserve entire ecosystems rather than a few specific species.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following pollutants causes surface deterioration of leather goods ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (d) — Sulphur dioxide (SO2) reacts with moisture to form sulfurous/sulfuric acid, causing surface deterioration of leather goods, paper, and marble [Park's PSM Environment].

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: The Finance Commission derives its authority from the
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: The Finance Commission of India is a constitutional body deriving its authority directly from Article 280 of the Constitution of India.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which of the following regions has the lowest atmospheric humidity?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cold polar air holds very little water vapour, giving polar regions the lowest absolute atmospheric humidity on Earth.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety deals with
options: establishing or promoting in situ conservation facilities for rare and endangered organisms
maintaining the worldwide network of gene banks for all the known flora and fauna
monitoring and regulating the development of living modified organisms
ensuring safe handling, safe use and safe trans-boundary movement of living modified organisms
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2013 Answer Key: Option (d) — ensuring safe handling, safe use and safe trans-boundary movement of living modified organisms B-BNT-M-HHQ-A - A prepp Your Persondl Exms Guide.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Which one of the following 1S secondary pollutant?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Tropospheric ozone is a secondary air pollutant formed photochemically from primary pollutants (NOx and VOCs) in sunlight, unlike primary pollutants SO2, NO, and benzene.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: A transition zone or region separating two biomes is known as
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: An ecotone is a transitional zone or boundary region between two adjacent ecological communities or biomes.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: Eutrophication of water bodies is mainly caused by
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Cultural eutrophication of lakes and rivers is primarily driven by excessive nutrient enrichment with phosphates and nitrates from agricultural runoff and sewage.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following:
1. Coal pits
2. Sewers
3. Volcanic eruptions
Which of the above is/are the source/ sources of HS in the environment?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Hydrogen sulphide (H2S) is released into the environment from anaerobic decomposition in sewers, coal pits/mines, and volcanic emissions.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
Which of the following is/are the source/sources of methane. a gree house gas ?
1. Cattle
2. Rice fields
3. Wetlands
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Enteric fermentation in cattle, anaerobic flooded rice paddies, and natural wetlands are all major sources of atmospheric methane (CH4).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: As per the Constitutional provisions, if a Panchayat is dissolved, elections are to be held within
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Under Article 243E (73rd Constitutional Amendment), if a Panchayat is dissolved prematurely, fresh elections must be held within 6 months.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: The release of which one of the following into ponds and wells helps in controlling the mosquitoes?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Gambusia affinis (mosquitofish) is a larvivorous fish introduced into ponds and wells for biological control of mosquito larvae.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Infant mortality rate takes into account the death of infants within a month after birth.
2. Infant mortality rate is the number of infant deaths in a particular year per 100 live births during that year.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: Infant mortality rate counts deaths under 1 year of age (not 1 month) and is expressed per 1,000 live births (not per 100 live births).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.subject: Pediatrics
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.text: In India, sovereignty resides in the
upsc-cms-2013-paper-1-authentic.explanation: In India's democratic republic ('We, the People of India...'), ultimate popular sovereignty resides in the people of India.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: L The commonest site for thyroglossal cyst 1S :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A thyroglossal duct cyst is a midline neck swelling that moves with swallowing and tongue protrusion; its most common anatomical location is subhyoid (~60–65%).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Factors important in the formation of gall stones include all of the following except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cholesterol supersaturation in bile, gallbladder hypomotility, and obesity promote gallstone formation, whereas micelle size itself is not a primary factor (bile salt-phospholipid ratio maintains cholesterol solubility).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Universal precautions to be followed by the surgical team include all of the following except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Universal precautions for surgical teams include barrier protection (double gloves, water-repellent gowns, protective boots/eyewear), whereas prophylactic antimicrobials are patient-directed rather than universal precautions.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The clinical signs of brain-stem death include all of the following except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Brain-stem death is diagnosed by irreversible coma, apnoea (absent spontaneous respiration), and absent brainstem reflexes (oculovestibular, pharyngeal/gag, pupillary, corneal); profound hypotension is not a diagnostic criterion.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Non-cardiac cause of raised central venous pressure include all of the following except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Tension pneumothorax, positive-pressure ventilation, and hypervolaemia raise central venous pressure (note: abdominal compartment syndrome also raises intrathoracic/CVP clinically, though UPSC key marked (a)).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following fractures i most often complicated by fat embolism?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Fractures of the shaft of the femur (and pelvis/long bones) carry the highest risk of fat embolism syndrome.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A 25-years old patient has 5 × 5 cm. amoebic abscess in right lobe of liver. He is febrile and has pain right hypochondrium. His primary management would include:
options: Ultra-sound guided placement of pigtail catheter
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess (5×5 cm without impending rupture) is primarily managed medically with metronidazole (plus luminal amoebicide) and clinical observation.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The surgical complications of typhoid fever include all of the following except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Typhoid fever can cause ileal perforation peritonitis, acute acalculous cholecystitis, and splenic abscess, whereas acute pancreatitis is not a typical surgical complication.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The complications of ascaris lumbricoides infestation include all of the following except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ascaris lumbricoides can cause bolus intestinal obstruction, biliary colic/cholangitis, and pancreatitis, whereas lower gastrointestinal bleeding is not a typical complication.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Treatment of choice for acute femoral artery embolism is :
options: Embolectomy after rest for few days
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Acute femoral artery embolism threatening limb viability is definitively treated with urgent surgical (Fogarty catheter) embolectomy.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Most common manifestation of Wilm's tumour is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wilms' tumour (nephroblastoma) most commonly presents in young children as an asymptomatic, smooth, unilateral abdominal mass.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The most common early sign of increasing intracranial pressure in the victim of head injury is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Alteration in the level of consciousness (agitation, drowsiness, falling GCS) is the earliest and most sensitive clinical sign of rising intracranial pressure.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Protein metabolism after trauma is characterized by all of the following excpt :
options: Inhibition of skeletal muscle brea down by interleukin I and tumour necrosis factor
Hepatic synthesis of acute phase reactants
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2013 Answer Key: Option (b) — Inhibition of skeletal muscle brea down by interleukin I and tumour necrosis factor.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Deep vein thrombosis of calf is best managed by :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Calf deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is primarily managed with systemic anticoagulation (LMWH/UFH followed by warfarin/DOAC) to prevent propagation and pulmonary embolism.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following cranial nerves pass through the jugular foramen except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The glossopharyngeal (IX), vagus (X), and spinal accessory (XI) nerves exit through the jugular foramen, whereas the hypoglossal nerve (XII) exits through the hypoglossal canal.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Most common cause obstruction in childhood is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Intussusception (typically ileocolic in infants 6–18 months) is the most common cause of acute intestinal obstruction in early childhood.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Surgical treatment for a 40-years old lady with 3 × 3 cm. papillary carcinoma thyroid with level III enlarged lymph nodes is :
options: Total thyroidectomy with excision of involved nodes
Total thyroidectomy with radical neck dissection
Total thyroidectomy with functional neck dissection
Total thyroidectomy with pos operative radio-iodine ablation
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (3×3 cm) with ipsilateral level III cervical lymph node metastasis is treated with total thyroidectomy and functional (modified radical) neck dissection.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: To differentiate pancreatic ascites from ascites secondary to cirrhosis of the liver, the most important test is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Diagnostic abdominal paracentesis showing markedly elevated ascitic fluid amylase (>1,000 IU/L) and high protein differentiates pancreatic ascites from cirrhotic ascites.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following ligaments contains splenic artery ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The splenorenal (lienorenal) ligament transmits the splenic artery, splenic vein, and tail of the pancreas to the splenic hilum.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Splenectomy is best indicated for :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hereditary spherocytosis is the classic haematological indication for splenectomy, which eliminates the site of red cell destruction and cures anaemia.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A retained stone in CBD (common bile duct) diagnosed by T-tube cholangeogram is best treated by :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A retained common bile duct stone detected postoperatively on a T-tube cholangiogram is best removed non-operatively via endoscopic papillotomy/ERCP (or Dormia basket extraction through the T-tube tract).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following statements regarding gallstones are true except :
options: Mixed stones are the commonest type
They can lead to acute cholangitis
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mixed stones are the commonest type of gallstones (~80%), and only ~10–15% of gallstones are radio-opaque on plain X-ray (most are radiolucent).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Pancreatic calculi are composed of :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pancreatic calculi (as seen in chronic calcific pancreatitis) are predominantly composed of calcium carbonate.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The nerve most likely to get injured in patients with fracture of upper end of radius is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Fracture of the proximal/upper end of the radius (or Monteggia fracture-dislocation) places the posterior interosseous nerve (winding around the radial neck) at highest risk of injury.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A 65-year old patient presents with obstructive jaundice and 15 kg weight loss. An ultrasound shows a 4 cm mass in the head of the pancreas with dilated bile ducts. Further work up includes a helical CT scan. The study shows several lesions consistent with metastasis in the right and left lobes of the liver and encasement of gastro duodenal artery. The most appropriate treatment would be :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In unresectable pancreatic head carcinoma with hepatic metastases and vascular encasement, palliative endoscopic biliary stenting is preferred over major surgery to relieve obstructive jaundice.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Laparoscopic instruments are best sterilized by :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Heat-sensitive optical laparoscopic instruments are best sterilized by low-temperature ethylene oxide gas (or plasma/2% glutaraldehyde soaking).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Primary hyper-aldosteronism presents with all of the following except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's syndrome) causes hypertension, renal potassium wasting with hypokalaemia (not hyperkalaemia), and periodic muscle weakness/paralysis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider following statements in respect of parenteral nutrition : indicated in patients when enteral nutrition cannot be given parenteral route is a better choice than enteral route abnormalities of liver functions can occur on prolonged use hyperglycemia is common
Which of the above statements are correct?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Total parenteral nutrition is indicated when the gut cannot be used, and can cause hyperglycaemia and cholestatic liver dysfunction; however, enteral nutrition is always preferred over parenteral whenever the gut works.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The 'claw sign' in barium enema study favours the diagnosis of :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The 'claw sign' (contrast outlining the rounded apex of the intussusceptum) on barium enema is classic for intussusception.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A 32 year-old male patient presents in casualty department with history of RTA one hour back; on examination is found that BP is 90/50 mm Hg, pulse rate 110 beats per minute, with fracture left lower ribs, and generalized distension of abdomen with guarding and rigidity. He also complained of pain on the tip of the left shoulder. As a casualty Medical Officer you must exclude which one of the following clinical conditions on the primary basis ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Left lower rib fractures, hypovolaemic shock, abdominal guarding/rigidity, and referred left shoulder-tip pain (Kehr's sign) after blunt trauma strongly indicate splenic rupture.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The treatment of choice for congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ramstedt's pyloromyotomy (longitudinal splitting of the hypertrophied circular pyloric muscle down to the submucosa) is the definitive surgery for congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Carcinoma of pyriform fossa usually presents with :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pyriform fossa carcinoma often remains silent locally and most commonly presents first with a metastatic cervical lymph node lump in the neck.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Pelvic abscess can presentpewith symptoms except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A pelvic abscess presents with fever, lower abdominal pain, and mucous diarrhoea/tenesmus from rectal irritation, but not frank rectal bleeding.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Femoral hernias are more common in females because :
options: ligaments of femoral canal neck are weak
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Femoral hernias are more common in females because the wider female pelvis gives a broader femoral ring/canal.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The most common ocular lesion peculiar to HIV infection in early stage is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cotton-wool spots (soft retinal exudates) due to focal nerve-fibre layer microinfarcts are the most common early ocular finding in HIV retinopathy.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text:
Consider the following statements in respect of prostatic carcinoma : Most originate from peripheral zone
2. Prostatic needle biopsy is better performed under trans rectal ultrasound
3. Prostate specific antigen is the specific test
4. L.H.R.H. analogues are used as medical treatment for metastatic disease
Which of the statements given above is/ are correct ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Prostate carcinoma mostly arises in the peripheral zone, is biopsied under TRUS guidance, and responds to LHRH analogues in metastatic disease; PSA is tissue-specific (also raised in BPH/prostatitis), not cancer-specific.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Regarding varicocele, all of the following are true except :
options: Feels like a bag of worms
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Varicocele is a dilatation/varicosity of the pampiniform venous plexus (not cremasteric veins), usually left-sided, feeling like a 'bag of worms' and associated with male subfertility.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The commonest complication of fracture of clavicle is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Malunion (cosmetic deformity without functional deficit) is the most common complication of clavicular fractures.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The most frequent complication of fracture pelvis is injury to :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Pelvic fractures most frequently injure the posterior (membranous) urethra at the urogenital diaphragm.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: General Surgery
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Burns involving the head and neck region are particularly dangerous because :
options: Face is a very vascular area
There may be thermal damage to the respiratory passage
Blood loss may be more severe
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Head and neck burns carry a high risk of inhalational thermal injury and rapid upper airway oedema/obstruction.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Pregnancy is characterized by the following physiological changes except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: During normal pregnancy, renal plasma flow and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) increase by ~40–50% (not decrease), alongside delayed gastric emptying, ureteric dilatation, and increased tidal volume.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Donovan bodies are associated with:
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Donovan bodies (intracellular Klebsiella granulomatis within macrophages) are pathognomonic of granuloma inguinale (donovanosis).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: During pregnancy, vaccination can be given against all these diseases except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Live attenuated vaccines such as mumps (MMR) are contraindicated during pregnancy, whereas tetanus toxoid, Hepatitis A, and Hepatitis B vaccines can be safely administered.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the likely cause of primary amenorrhoea together with retention of urine in an adolescent girl ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Imperforate hymen/transverse vaginal septum in an adolescent girl causes primary amenorrhoea with haematocolpos, which compresses the urethra and causes acute urinary retention.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Histological type of endometrium that is suggestive of ovulation is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Secretory-phase endometrium (driven by corpus luteum progesterone) provides histological confirmation that ovulation has occurred.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The ferning of cervical mucous is due to the high concentration of :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Oestrogen-driven ferning (arborization) of dried cervical mucus results from crystallization of sodium chloride around mucin.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A pregnant woman in Ill trimester has normal blood pressure in the arms when standing and sitting but drops to 90/50 when lying down. What is the likely cause ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Supine hypotension syndrome in the third trimester occurs when the gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava against the spine, reducing venous return and cardiac output.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct about foetal circulation ?
options: Umbilical artery carries oxygenated blood to the fetus
Umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood to the fetus
Umbilical artery carries deoxygenated fetal blood to the placenta
Two umbilical arteries and one umbilical vein traverse through
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In fetal circulation, the two umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the placenta, whereas the single umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood to the fetus.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is a contr indication for breast feeding?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Maternal diarrhoea, post-caesarean state, and treated/non-infectious maternal tuberculosis are not contraindications to breastfeeding.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Meconium aspiration syndrome can be prevented by taking the following measures except :
options: Suctioning of trachea through laryng scope
Delivering the baby by emergency caesarean section
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Amnioinfusion (for thick meconium) and selective airway management help prevent meconium aspiration syndrome, whereas routine emergency Caesarean section for meconium-stained liquor alone is not indicated.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A 15-year old unmarried gift comes withuide history of dysmenorrhea. Age of menarche is 12 years. Per abdominal and per rectum examination reveal nothing abnormal. You will treat the patient with :
options: Reassurance and giving antispasmodics throughout the month
Reassurance and giving antispasmodics during menses
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Wait—no, cms13-p2-051: Primary dysmenorrhoea in a 15-year-old with normal pelvic/rectal findings is managed with reassurance and analgesics/antispasmodics during menstruation.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A pregnant lady with 37 weeks gestation has been admitted with history of premature rupture of membranes for 6 hours. She is best treated with :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A term pregnant woman (37 weeks) with premature rupture of membranes for 6 hours should receive prophylactic antibiotics and prompt labour induction (steroids are for <34 weeks).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Use of ventose is preferred over forceps in the delivery of :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Vacuum extraction (ventouse) allows autorotation of the fetal head and is preferred over forceps in occipitoposterior malposition (contraindicated in breech and face presentation).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Normal pH of foetal scalp blood is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Normal fetal scalp blood pH during labour is 7.25–7.35 (with ≥7.20–7.25 considered reassuring/normal; <7.20 indicates acidosis).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Face to pubis delivery is common in which type of pelvis ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An anthropoid pelvis (long anteroposterior diameter) predisposes to direct occipitoposterior position and face-to-pubes delivery.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The following are the signs of placental separation except :
options: The uterus becomes hard and globular
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Signs of placental separation include a hard globular uterus, apparent lengthening of the cord, a gush of fresh blood, and a rise (not decrease) in fundal height.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The following conditions are associated with molar pregnancy except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Hydatidiform mole is associated with hyperemesis gravidarum, early-onset pre-eclampsia (PIH), and thyrotoxicosis (from high hCG), but not gestational diabetes.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the commonest cause of retention of urine at 12-14 weeks of pregnancy?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: An incarcerated retroverted gravid uterus at 12–14 weeks pushes the cervix anteriorly beneath the symphysis pubis, compressing the urethra and causing acute urinary retention.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is a uterine compression suture during management of atonic post partum haemorrhage?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The B-Lynch brace suture is a vertical uterine compression suture used to control refractory atonic postpartum haemorrhage.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following anti-hypertEnsims Guide drugs is/are best avoided during pregnancy?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: ACE inhibitors (and ARBs) are teratogenic (causing fetal renal dysgenesis, oligohydramnios, and skull hypoplasia) and are strictly contraindicated in pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The hormone Relaxin of pregnancy is secreted by :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: During pregnancy, the peptide hormone relaxin is primarily secreted by the corpus luteum of the ovary (and placenta/decidua).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Complications of heparin therapy in pregnancy include all except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Heparin does not cross the placenta and is therefore non-teratogenic (unlike warfarin), though prolonged use can cause bleeding, thrombocytopenia (HIT), and maternal osteoporosis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Misoprostol can be used during pregnancy by the following routes except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Misoprostol (PGE1 analogue) is administered orally, vaginally, sublingually, or rectally, never intravenously.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Following are the contraindications for laparoscopic female sterilization except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Severe cardiac disease, respiratory dysfunction, and diaphragmatic/hiatus hernia are contraindications to laparoscopic pneumoperitoneum and Trendelenburg positioning, whereas obesity is not an absolute contraindication.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Mifepristone used for inducing abortion acts on :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mifepristone (RU-486) is a competitive progesterone receptor antagonist that blocks endometrial progesterone receptors, increases uterine contractility/prostaglandin sensitivity, and causes decidual necrosis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A man underwent vasectomy. but 6 months later his wife was 16 week pregnant. What is the most likely cause ?
options: Failure to use additional contraception in postoperative period
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: After vasectomy, spermatozoa remain viable in the distal vas and seminal vesicles for ~3 months/20 ejaculations; failure to use backup contraception until azoospermia is confirmed is the commonest cause of early pregnancy.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which method of vasectomy has the highest failure rate?
options: Open ended vasectomy with granulation formation
Cutting and ligating vas to occlude the proximal and distal lumen
Use of hemoclips with 1-4 cm gap after cutting proximal and distal ends
Cutting the vas and turning the ends backwards and ligating with suture material
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Open-ended vasectomy (leaving the testicular end open) allows sperm granuloma formation, which is associated with a higher risk of spontaneous recanalization and failure.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: All of the following are eligibility criteria for female sterilization except :
options: Client's age should not be less than 22 years or more than 49 years
Client or her spouse must not have undergone sterilisation in the past
At least two living children should be present
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under Government of India sterilization guidelines, the client must have at least one living child (preferably over 1 year old), not necessarily two living children.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: During the first 6 months of the gestionxams Guide which amongst the following contraceptives is not advisable ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC Answer Key: Not Given / Dropped — Suggested Best Answer (AI + Textbook): Option (b) — Combined oral contraceptive pills (estrogen-containing) are not advisable in lactating women during the first 6 months postpartum as estrogen suppresses lactation and increases VTE risk [Park's PSM / Williams Obstetrics].

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text:
Oral contraceptives may provide protection against the following malignancies except :
1. Cervical cancer
2. Endometrial cancer Ovarian cancer
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Combined oral contraceptives protect against ovarian and endometrial cancers, whereas long-term use does not protect against (and slightly increases risk of) cervical cancer.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The following drugs are effective in the management of menorrhagia except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: NSAIDs, progestogens, and antifibrinolytics (tranexamic acid) reduce menstrual blood loss in menorrhagia, whereas prostaglandins increase uterine bleeding/cramping.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Out of the following. select the histologic type of cancer endometrium which has the worst prognosis:
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Among the listed endometrial cancers, serous/clear cell carcinomas (Type II non-oestrogen-dependent) carry a much worse prognosis than endometrioid or mucinous adenocarcinomas (note: UPSC key marked (c) Clear cell carcinoma).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the commonest cause of Vulv Vaginal Fistula in developing countries ?
options: Radiotherapy for treatment of carcinoma cervix
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In developing countries, prolonged obstructed labour causing pressure necrosis of the vesicovaginal septum is the most common cause of vesicovaginal fistula.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A 28-year old woman comes with infertility. Husband's semen analysis is normal. Endometrial biopsy shows secretary changes with no evidence of tuberculosis. On hysterosalpingography both tubes show tubal blockage. What should be the next step in management?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bilateral cornual/tubal block on HSG (which can be due to tubal spasm) should be confirmed by diagnostic laparoscopy with chromopertubation before planning tuboplasty or IVF.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following statements is true for maternal rubella infection ?
options: It leads to abortions before 16 weeks of gestation
24% incidence of congenital infection if acquired during the last month of pregnancy
It causes blindness with recurrent infection
The primary infection is responsible for birth defects
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Congenital rubella syndrome (cataracts, deafness, PDA) results from primary maternal rubella infection during pregnancy (especially in the first trimester).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Contraindications for medical abortions are all except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Severe anaemia (Hb <8 g/dL), undiagnosed adnexal mass (possible ectopic), and uncontrolled seizures are contraindications to medical abortion, whereas maternal age >35 years alone is not.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: In an Rh negative mother delivered an Rh positive baby, prophylactic anti-D is indicated:
options: As a routine procedure in all cases
II indirect Coombs' test is positive
II indirect Coombs' test is negative
II direct Coombs' test is positive
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Note: clinically anti-D is given if ICT is negative, though the official UPSC key for this question marked (a) As a routine procedure in all cases.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A woman dies from a heart disease six days after delivery. This would come under the category of :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Death of a pregnant or recently delivered woman from a pre-existing medical condition aggravated by pregnancy (such as heart disease 6 days postpartum) is classified as an indirect maternal death.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: In a woman using an intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) an intrauterine pregnancy occurs and the IUCD threads are visible. What is the reason to recommend removal of the device ?
options: To prevent the risk of subsequent septic abortion and preterm labour
To prevent congenital abnormality of the newborn
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Leaving an IUD in situ during an intrauterine pregnancy markedly increases the risk of septic abortion, chorioamnionitis, and preterm labour; therefore, it should be removed early if the strings are visible.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Success of tubal re-canalization is best with :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Laparoscopic Falope ring (or Hulka clip) sterilization destroys the shortest segment of the fallopian tube and yields the highest success rate for surgical tubal recanalization.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The amount of previously unrecognized disease that is diagnosed as a result of the screening effort is known as :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Yield of a screening test refers to the amount of previously unrecognized disease detected and diagnosed as a result of the screening effort.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The total osmolarity of new oral rehydration solution formulation is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The WHO/UNICEF reduced-osmolarity oral rehydration solution (ORS) has a total osmolarity of 245 mmol/L.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which one of the following is not consistent with Aedes egypti's life cycle?
options: Breeds in artificial collection of water
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Aedes aegypti lays single, cigar-shaped eggs without lateral floats (Anopheles eggs are boat-shaped with lateral air floats).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The National Health Policy 2002 target to be achieved by the year 2010 is :
options: Achieve zero level growth of HIV/
Reduce infant mortality rate 30/1000 live births
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: India's National Health Policy 2002 targeted reducing the Infant Mortality Rate to 30 per 1,000 live births by 2010.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: One of the following is not a characteristic of causal association :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Bradford Hill criteria for causal association include coherence, specificity, and biological plausibility—not sensitivity (which is a screening test metric).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Discarded tablets are disposed in:
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under the older 1998 Biomedical Waste Rules referenced by this exam, discarded medicines and cytotoxic drugs were disposed of in black plastic bags (updated to yellow/cytotoxic in 2016).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: In a village of 5,000 population, 50 persons suffered from cholera and 10 persons died. What will be the case fatality ratio?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Case fatality ratio = (Deaths due to disease / Total cases of disease) × 100 = (10 / 50) × 100 = 20.0%.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: One of the following diseases has more than one route of transmission:
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Leprosy (Mycobacterium leprae) can be transmitted via both respiratory droplets (nasal secretions) and prolonged skin-to-skin contact.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Serial interval is the gap between :
options: Introduction of infection and development of maximum infectivity
Transmission of infection from patient to another susceptible host
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Serial interval is the time gap between the onset of symptoms in a primary case and the onset of symptoms in a secondary case.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The best indicator for a potential explosiv ness of plague outbreak is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The Xenopsylla cheopis index (average number of X. cheopis fleas per rat) is the best indicator of the potential explosiveness of a bubonic plague outbreak.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Tuberculous pericarditis is included in which treatment category of DOTS strategy ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Severe extrapulmonary tuberculosis such as tuberculous pericarditis or TB meningitis is treated under Category I of the DOTS strategy.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Vision 2020 India includes all of the following except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Vision 2020 India targets major causes of avoidable blindness including cataract, refractive errors, glaucoma, corneal blindness, and diabetic retinopathy—not epidemic conjunctivitis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The most sensitive index for surveillance of malaria transmission is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Infant parasite rate (percentage of infants aged 0–11 months with malaria parasites) is the most sensitive index of recent/ongoing malaria transmission in a community.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Chandler's index is used in :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chandler's index estimates the average hookworm egg count per gram of stool to measure hookworm endemicity.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Integrated management of neonatal and childhood illness includes all except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: IMNCI (Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness) covers acute respiratory infections (pneumonia), diarrhoea, malaria, measles, and malnutrition, but not tuberculosis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Toxic shock syndrome occurs after one of the following vaccinations:
options: Recombinant DNA Vaccine against Hepatitis B
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Reconstituted measles vaccine contaminated with Staphylococcus aureus and kept beyond 4 hours can cause fatal toxic shock syndrome in infants.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The health indicator obtained By dividing de height by cube root of weight is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Ponderal index is calculated as height (cm) divided by the cube root of body weight (kg).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: What is the method of sampling in which the units are picked up at regular intervals from the universe ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Systematic random sampling selects every k-th unit at regular intervals from an ordered sampling frame.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Child starts speaking short sentences by the age of :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A normal child begins speaking in simple 2–3 word short sentences by 24 months (2 years) of age.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: A village has a total of 100 under-five children. The coverage with measles vaccine in these age groups is 60%. Following the occurrence of a measles case in a child after a visit outside, twenty six children developed measles later. The secondary attack rate of measles is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Of 100 children, 60% (60) are vaccinated/immune, leaving 40 susceptible; 1 is the primary case, leaving 39 exposed susceptibles. Secondary attack rate = 26 / 39 × 100 = 66.6%.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The method of choice for purification of highly polluted water on a large scale is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Highly polluted water on a large scale is treated by super-chlorination (high chlorine dose to destroy pathogens and oxidize organics) followed by dechlorination.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Dehydration is not a feature of one of the following diseases :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Cholera (profuse diarrhoea), pertussis (post-tussive vomiting/poor intake), and cerebral malaria (hyperpyrexia/coma) can cause dehydration, whereas MDR-TB does not acutely cause dehydration.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The useful fertility indicator where birth registration statistics do not exist or are inadequate is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Child-woman ratio (number of children 0–4 years per 1,000 women aged 15–49 years) is derived from census data and is useful when birth registration is incomplete.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The Disability Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) lost due to neuropsychiatric disorders is highest in :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Unipolar depressive disorders account for the largest share of Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) lost among all neuropsychiatric conditions.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Direct mailing as a means of communication, is an example of :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Direct mailing (pamphlets, letters, newsletters sent to large populations) is classified under the mass approach of health communication.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Autosomal recessive disorders except :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Sickle cell anaemia, albinism, and Hirschsprung disease (some forms) follow autosomal recessive/multifactorial inheritance, whereas retinoblastoma (RB1) is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is X-linked dominant trait?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: X-linked hypophosphataemic (vitamin D-resistant) rickets is a classic X-linked dominant disorder (whereas haemophilia A, colour blindness, and DMD are X-linked recessive).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Mansonoides mosquito transmits the following disease :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Mansonoides mosquitoes are the principal vectors of Brugian filariasis (Brugia malayi) in India.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Kuppu Swamy Socio-economic Status Scale comprises of :
options: Income. family size and land holding
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Kuppuswamy's Socioeconomic Status Scale for urban families uses three parameters: education of head of family, occupation of head of family, and monthly family income.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Failure rate of contraceptive method is determined by :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Contraceptive failure rate is quantified by the Pearl Index (failures per 100 woman-years).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following drugs is not used for chemo prophylaxis of malaria?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Chloroquine, proguanil, and mefloquine are used for malaria chemoprophylaxis, whereas artesunate has a very short half-life and is used for treatment, not prophylaxis.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The net reproduction rate of 1 can be achieved only if the following rate exceeds 60% :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A Net Reproduction Rate (NRR) of 1 (replacement-level fertility) is achieved when the Couple Protection Rate (CPR) exceeds 60%.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: According to the new guidelines, the Body Mass Index cut off for overweight is :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Under WHO international criteria, overweight in adults is defined as a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 25 kg/m² (and obesity as ≥ 30 kg/m²).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Horrock's apparatus is used to measure :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Horrock's apparatus is used in the field to determine the chlorine demand (dose of bleaching powder needed to disinfect 455 L of water).

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Among the causes of maternal mortality. which of the following is correct in descending order of maternal deaths in India ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Official UPSC CMS 2013 Answer Key: Option (d) — Haemorrhage, sepsis, abortion, obstructed labour prepp Your Personal Exms Guide.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The order of priority of immunization strategy to prevent congenital rubella infection from first to last is :
options: Infants → children 1-14 years → women of reproductive age group
Infants → women of reproductive age group → children 1-14 years
Women of reproductive age group → Infants → children 1-14 years
Women of reproductive age group → children 1-14 years → Infants
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: To prevent congenital rubella syndrome, priority targets women of reproductive age first (immediate protection), followed by children aged 1–14 years, and finally infants.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The attitude is a domain of :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: In Bloom's taxonomy of educational objectives, attitudes, values, and feelings belong to the affective domain of learning.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Diethyltoluamide is an effective :
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: Diethyltoluamide (DEET) is the most widely used topical insect repellent against mosquitoes and ticks.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: The term Perinatal covers the period from :
options: 28 weeks gestation to one week after birth
28 weeks gestation to one month after birth
24 weeks gestation to one week after birth
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: The perinatal period extends from 28 weeks of gestation (or ≥1,000 g birth weight) to 7 completed days (1 week) after birth.

upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.subject: Preventive & Social Medicine
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.text: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for combined contraceptive oral pills ?
upsc-cms-2013-paper-2-authentic.explanation: A previous history of venous or arterial thromboembolism is an absolute contraindication to combined oral contraceptive pills.

ST segment elevation is an integral part of LBBB
Cardiomyopathy is another possible aetiology of LBBB

While hormonal imbalances and systemic diseases can cause growth issues, they are generally less common than a specific pattern of delayed development.
